title: Add the Grasshopper components for the ten uncovered commands
body:
The 1.5.9 commands shipped in the Add-On without their Grasshopper counterparts, so they were reachable only through the JSON interface. This adds one component each:

  General   GetPointFromUser
  Project   CreateHotlinkNodes, CreateHotlinkInstances,
            ChangeHotlinkInstances, SaveAsModuleFile
  Library   SetLibraries, AddLibraries
  Solid ops TrimElements, RemoveElementTrims, GetElementTrims

Every command registered in AddOnMain.cpp now has a component except the six that deliberately have none: GenerateDocumentation (developer only), GetNavigatorItemTree, the two element notification clients (they need a callback the plugin cannot receive) and the ShowScriptUI / GetScriptUIResult pair.

CreateHotlinkNodes hands out node identifiers, so it needs a type for them: HotlinkNodeGuid, which CreateHotlinkInstances takes back. Like every other GuidObject it also accepts a bare guid string, so the two components can be wired to each other or fed from text.

The optional per-item inputs follow the CreateLayers convention - empty, one value for all, or one per item, with the size checked before the request rather than letting Archicad answer with a mismatch.

Icons are derived from their closest existing sibling plus a corner badge, so they read as part of the same set.
author: tlorantfy

title: `SetPropertyValuesOfElements`: one failing entry silently fails all later entries for the same element
body:
# `SetPropertyValuesOfElements`: one failing entry silently fails all later entries for the same element

## Summary

In `SetPropertyValuesOfElements`, the error code of one entry leaks into all following
entries **for the same element** in the same call. As soon as one property value cannot be
written, every remaining property of that element is reported as
`Failed to get property values for element` and is **never even attempted** — although
those properties are perfectly writable on their own.

The most common trigger is a property whose *availability for classifications* is set to
**none**: writing to it fails (correctly), and that single failure then takes down every
value that comes after it for the same element.

Entries for *other* elements are not affected.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Tapir add-on | 1.5.8 |
| Archicad | 26, German localisation |
| OS | macOS (Darwin 24.6.0) |
| Client | Python, `multiconn_archicad` 0.6.1 (any JSON client will do) |

## Impact

This is easy to miss because the command still reports partial success. In a real project
(a room-book tool writing 385 values to 11 zones), **exactly one** property had been set to
availability "none" by hand in the Property Manager. Result of one
`SetPropertyValuesOfElements` call:

* 209 values written
* 143 values reported as failed — 11 of them the genuinely unwritable property, **132 of
  them perfectly writable values that were dropped because of the cascade**

Splitting the payload into smaller batches only reduced the damage (batches of 20 → 83
failures instead of 143), it does not avoid it, and it makes the loss look like a random
flake rather than a deterministic bug.

## Root cause

`archicad-addon/Sources/PropertyCommands.cpp`,
`SetPropertyValuesOfElementsCommand::Execute` (line numbers from the 1.4.0 sources; the
behaviour is unchanged in the 1.5.8 binary I tested):

```cpp
GSErrCode err = ACAPI_Element_GetPropertyValuesByGuid (elemGuid, properties, propertyValues);

for (API_Property& propertyValue : propertyValues) {
    ...
    if (err != NoError) {
        result = CreateFailedExecutionResult (err, "Failed to get property values for element");
        continue;
    }

    err = ACAPI_Property_SetPropertyValueFromString (...);   // overwrites err
    ...
    err = ACAPI_Element_SetProperty (elemGuid, propertyValue);   // overwrites err
```

`err` is declared **outside** the inner loop and is reused for the per-property calls.
It is never reset at the start of an iteration, so after the first failing property every
later iteration takes the `err != NoError` branch — and reports it as a *get* failure even
though the get succeeded.

### Suggested fix

Keep the result of the get in its own variable and use a fresh error variable per
iteration, e.g.

```cpp
const GSErrCode getErr = ACAPI_Element_GetPropertyValuesByGuid (elemGuid, properties, propertyValues);

for (API_Property& propertyValue : propertyValues) {
    ...
    if (getErr != NoError) {
        result = CreateFailedExecutionResult (getErr, "Failed to get property values for element");
        continue;
    }

    GSErrCode err = ACAPI_Property_SetPropertyValueFromString (...);
    ...
}
```

## Steps to reproduce

Fully scriptable — no manual dialog steps. The script creates a property group with two
string properties: one available for **no** classification (equivalent to choosing
"None" under *Availability for Classifications*), one available for all of them.

```python
from multiconn_archicad import MultiConn

h = MultiConn().primary
T = lambda c, p=None: h.core.post_tapir_command(c, p or {})

DEFAULT = {"basicDefaultValue": {"status": "normal", "type": "string", "value": "-"}}

# every classification in the project, so that NormalProp is available on any element
def collect(nodes, out):
    for n in nodes:
        item = n["classificationItem"]
        out.append(item["classificationItemId"]["guid"])
        collect(item.get("children", []), out)

classifications = []
for system in h.standard.commands.GetAllClassificationSystems():
    tree = h.core.post_command(
        "API.GetAllClassificationsInSystem",
        {"classificationSystemId": {"guid": str(system.classificationSystemId.guid)}})
    collect(tree["classificationItems"], classifications)

T("CreatePropertyGroups", {"propertyGroups": [{"propertyGroup": {"name": "TapirBugRepro"}}]})
T("CreatePropertyDefinitions", {"propertyDefinitions": [
    {"propertyDefinition": {"group": {"name": "TapirBugRepro"}, "name": "HiddenProp",
                            "description": "", "type": "string",
                            "availability": [],                      # <- "None"
                            "defaultValue": DEFAULT}},
    {"propertyDefinition": {"group": {"name": "TapirBugRepro"}, "name": "NormalProp",
                            "description": "", "type": "string",
                            "availability": [{"classificationItemId": {"guid": g}}
                                             for g in classifications],
                            "defaultValue": DEFAULT}}]})

props = {p["propertyName"]: p["propertyId"]["guid"]
         for p in T("GetAllProperties")["properties"]
         if p["propertyGroupName"] == "TapirBugRepro"}
hidden, normal = props["HiddenProp"], props["NormalProp"]
zones = [z["elementId"]["guid"]
         for z in T("GetElementsByType", {"elementType": "Zone"})["elements"]]

def run(title, entries):
    payload = [{"elementId": {"guid": e}, "propertyId": {"guid": p},
                "propertyValue": {"value": "X"}} for e, p in entries]
    results = T("SetPropertyValuesOfElements",
                {"elementPropertyValues": payload})["executionResults"]
    print(title)
    for (e, p), r in zip(entries, results):
        name = "HiddenProp" if p == hidden else "NormalProp"
        zone = "zone1" if e == zones[0] else "zone2"
        print(f"   {zone} / {name:11} -> " + ("success" if r.get("success")
              else "FAILED: " + r.get("error", {}).get("message", "?")))

run("A) [HiddenProp, NormalProp]  on one element", [(zones[0], hidden), (zones[0], normal)])
run("B) [NormalProp, HiddenProp]  on one element", [(zones[0], normal), (zones[0], hidden)])
run("C) [NormalProp]              on one element", [(zones[0], normal)])
run("D) HiddenProp on zone1, NormalProp on zone2", [(zones[0], hidden), (zones[1], normal)])
```

(The project needs at least two Zones; any element type works.)

### Expected

`HiddenProp` fails in every case — it is available for no classification. `NormalProp`
succeeds in every case, regardless of the order of the entries.

### Actual

```
A) [HiddenProp, NormalProp]  on one element
   zone1 / HiddenProp  -> FAILED: Failed to set property value for element
   zone1 / NormalProp  -> FAILED: Failed to get property values for element   <-- wrong
B) [NormalProp, HiddenProp]  on one element
   zone1 / NormalProp  -> success
   zone1 / HiddenProp  -> FAILED: Failed to set property value for element
C) [NormalProp]              on one element
   zone1 / NormalProp  -> success
D) HiddenProp on zone1, NormalProp on zone2
   zone1 / HiddenProp  -> FAILED: Failed to set property value for element
   zone2 / NormalProp  -> success
```

`NormalProp` is written or not depending purely on whether it is listed **before or
after** a failing entry of the same element (A vs. B). D shows the cascade is limited to
one element.

The reported message is also misleading: the *get* did succeed; it is the previous
entry's *set* error being re-reported.

## Cleanup for the reproduction

```python
T("DeletePropertyDefinitions",
  {"propertyIds": [{"propertyId": {"guid": g}} for g in props.values()]})
c = h.standard.commands
group = [g.propertyGroup for g in c.GetPropertyGroups(c.GetAllPropertyGroupIds())
         if g.propertyGroup.name == "TapirBugRepro"][0]
T("DeletePropertyGroups",
  {"propertyGroupIds": [{"propertyGroupId": {"guid": str(group.propertyGroupId.guid)}}]})
```

## Workaround for API users

Until this is fixed, query `API.GetPropertyDefinitionAvailability` before writing and drop
every property whose `availableClassifications` is empty — those writes cannot succeed
anyway, and leaving them in the payload silently discards the values that follow them.

That only covers this one trigger, though. Any other per-entry failure causes the same
cascade, so the general workaround is one `SetPropertyValuesOfElements` call per element,
or retrying failed entries individually.

title: Feature/text label full support + GetAutoTextKeys  and GetAutoTextName
body:
Summary
This PR adds dedicated ModifyTexts/ModifyLabels commands with full style/leader-line/symbol-style/multi-run editing — going beyond the plain-field editing already available via SetDetailsOfElements (merged in #611/a2a111b/54cbd36) — plus two new commands for AutoText key discovery. Nothing in main is modified; this is fully additive. Rebased onto current upstream/main (this branch was 297 commits behind).

New: ModifyTexts/ModifyLabels — dedicated commands for editing content, style, leader-line and symbol-style, complementing the generic SetDetailsOfElements path.
New: GetAutoTextKeys/GetAutoTextName — discover and name-resolve autotext keys, to make use of the <KEY> embedding SetTextContentAndParagraphs (from #611) already supports.
Fixed before submitting: a bug in this PR's own new ModifyTexts/ModifyLabels code that silently no-op'd every content edit — never present in main.
Tests: exhaustive Text/Label suite, 67 passing checks.
The bug (in this PR's own code, not in main)
While building ModifyTexts/ModifyLabels, explicitContent was computed with the wrong ObjectState::Get overload:


const bool explicitContent = (item.Get ("text") != nullptr || item.Get ("runs") != nullptr);
The pointer-returning overload never matches a plain scalar/array field, only nested objects — so this was always false, and the whole content-rebuild block was silently skipped on every call. Fixed with the value-returning overloads:


GS::UniString explicitContentTextCheck;
GS::Array<GS::ObjectState> explicitContentRunsCheck;
const bool explicitContent = item.Get ("text", explicitContentTextCheck) || item.Get ("runs", explicitContentRunsCheck);
The memo handling for the actual write follows the same technique already established in main by #611: build the new memo from a blank API_ElementMemo{} instead of one fetched via ACAPI_Element_GetMemo first, and write it with the non-Uni APIMemoMask_TextContent | APIMemoMask_Paragraph.

New commands
ModifyTexts/ModifyLabels — content (plain or multi-run), style (font/bold/italic/justification/anchor/frame/etc.), leader-line (arrow/shape/anchor) and symbol-style, none of which SetDetailsOfElements currently exposes for Text/Label.
GetAutoTextKeys — lists the available autotext keys (name + embeddable key), generic or scoped to one element's own properties.
GetAutoTextName — resolves one or more keys back to their display name in a single batched call; PROPERTY-<guid> keys are looked up directly via ACAPI_Property_GetPropertyDefinition instead of enumerating every property definition in the project.
Live-verified end to end, including a Label associatively bound to a real Wall correctly resolving that wall's own thickness / Element ID via a PROPERTY- autotext key — not just a standalone element.

Tests
Extended the exhaustive Text/Label test suite — 67 passing checks.

Three edge cases could not be made to work despite investigation; they're tracked as documented known issues rather than failures — it's possible a workaround exists that wasn't found, rather than a hard Archicad limitation:

arrowVisible changes silently dropped by ModifyLabels, even with every arrowData sub-field masked together in the same call
A lone justification change ignored by ACAPI_Element_Change
Multi-run content collapsing to its flattened text on ACAPI_Element_Create (but not on ACAPI_Element_Change)
author: MathiasJon

title: Text/Label full support + GetAutoTextKeys/GetAutoTextName, with the review fixes of #630
body:
## Summary

This carries [#630](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/pull/630) by @MathiasJon (ModifyTexts / ModifyLabels with full style, leader-line, symbol-style and multi-run editing, plus GetAutoTextKeys / GetAutoTextName) unchanged, and adds commits on top that work through the review findings, add the Grasshopper components, pick up the open review threads of the merged #627, and fix #634. The original branch lives on a fork, hence the new PR.

Fixes #634.

## What the extra commits change

**Compatibility, checked against the AC25 to AC29 DevKit headers**
- `GetAutoTextKeys` works on AC25 and AC26 as well: `APIAny_GetPropertyAutoTextKeyTableID` exists in `APIdefs_Goodies.h` from AC25, so `MigrationHelper.hpp` wraps it like the other `ACAPI_AutoText_*` calls. The table is name → key per the DevKit doc.
- `kArrowTypeNames` matches `API_ArrowID` in every supported DevKit; `arrowVisibility` is AC29-only and `textFrame` exists from AC28, so the gates are right.
- Before AC29 a label's arrow head is `begArrow` (the DevKit's own label example sets it), so `arrowVisible` reads and writes that flag.

**Memo handling**
- Paragraph handles are disposed with `ACAPI_DisposeParagraphsHdl`; a pre-AC28 `textContent` handle is freed before being replaced; the pre-AC28 read stops at the first terminator and is bounded by the handle size.
- Every paragraph is read back, with run offsets relative to their paragraph (DevKit `Element_Test` layout), so a style-only modify cannot truncate a multi-paragraph text. Every run is reported, a single one too. Runs round-trip their effects; a failed memo read fails the item instead of rebuilding from empty content.
- A style change rebuilds the content only when it touches a run-level field (pen, font, faces, height, effects), merging those into every run; element-level fields (angle, anchor, justification, frame, ...) apply through their masks and leave the content, and any autotext reference in it, untouched. A rebuild is refused when a read-back run is an autotext run (protected), so a reference cannot be turned into static text. Each text-frame sub-field is masked on its own.

**Response shape, schemas, errors**
- `GetDetailsOfElements` keeps the flat Text fields (`text`, `position`, `angle`, `height`, `pen`, `justification`, `zCoordinate`) next to `style`, `paragraphCount` and `runs`, and still emits `text`/`paragraphCount` when the memo cannot be read.
- `TextStyleDetails` and `LabelLeaderLineDetails` are plain objects (the `allOf` branches were unsatisfiable). `TextRunDetails` carries the effect flags. The text-frame fields say they need Archicad 28.
- Per-item errors are `FailedExecutionResult`s (`success: false`); an unresolvable `lineTypeId`, an unparseable `elementId`, the other label class's fields, and a failed autotext list fetch are reported instead of ignored.
- `ModifyTexts` honours the `z` of its `Coordinate3D` and an optional `floorIndex`; a content rebuild is documented as making the element auto-width, as SetDetailsOfElements does.

**Grasshopper**
- New components: ModifyTexts, ModifyLabels (on the Modify* base, which now takes dotted JSON keys for nested `style`/`leaderLine` fields), GetAutoTextKeys (optional element, embeddable keys) and GetAutoTextName (per-key errors), with icons.
- #634: CreateDesignOptionCombinations read its generic tree input as `GH_ObjectWrapper`, which Grasshopper refuses for a generic parameter (it hands out `IGH_Goo`); the tree is read as `IGH_Goo` and converted item by item, as CreateAssociativeDimensions does. CreateGroups had the same reader and is fixed alongside.
- Follow-ups of #627's post-merge review: Hotlinks outputs the node ids, names and types (appended, so saved definitions keep their wiring), so CreateHotlinkInstances can be wired from it; ChangeHotlinkInstances' Origins states its broadcast; GetPointFromUser asks for the point only on Refresh and says Escape is an error; GetElementTrims reports per-element errors; CreateHotlinkInstances has its own icon; `Resources.Designer.cs` layout restored.

**Examples, goldens, docs**
- `modify_texts.py`, `modify_labels.py` and `get_autotext_keys.py` print locale-independent, deterministic results; their goldens get recorded on the next `test_examples.py` run. `get_autotext_keys.py` prints each check as OK or FAILED, so a wrong name/key direction would show in the golden. The shared test masks hide the font-metric dependent `boxWidth`/`boxHeight`.
- `create_texts.py` sets every field it prints and its golden was rewritten to match. That golden was written by hand from the expected shape, not recorded from a live Archicad.
- `docs/archicad-addon/*.js` regenerated from the sources (same output as `GenerateDocumentation`); this also picks up the description changes of #588 and #621.

## Not verified here (no Archicad, no DevKit toolchain on this runner)
- What the memo returns for an autotext run (its key or its resolved value); the rebuild refusal above covers the case either way.
- Whether `API_ParagraphType::just` fixes the known "lone justification change ignored" case.
- The Grasshopper changes compile in CI but were not exercised in Rhino.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI build checks on AC25 to AC29, Windows and macOS, and the Grasshopper build
- [ ] `Test/test_examples.py` against a running Archicad, recording the three new goldens (check `get_autotext_keys.py`'s lines all read OK)
- [ ] `Examples/manual_tests/test_text_label_exhaustive.py` on a live Archicad
- [ ] A UI-placed multi-paragraph, multi-run text: GetDetailsOfElements, then a style-only ModifyTexts with `bold`, on AC25 and AC29; the content must come back unchanged
- [ ] A text with an embedded `<PROJECTNAME>`: a style-only ModifyTexts with `angle` keeps the reference; one with `bold` is refused
- [ ] The new and changed Grasshopper components in Rhino, including CreateDesignOptionCombinations from #634

title: RoofDetails has no typed Grasshopper getter
body:
The roof details added in #625 are readable through `GetDetailsOfElements`, but on the Grasshopper side `ElementsComponents/GetDetailsOfElementsComponent.cs` holds a typed getter per element type: `WallDetails`, `BeamDetails`, `ColumnDetails`, `SlabDetails`, `PolylineDetails`, `ZoneDetails`, `TextDetails`, `LabelDetails`. There is no `RoofDetails` sibling, so the data is not reachable on a canvas.

It sits outside the sweep in #627 because it is not a command registered in `AddOnMain.cpp`.

title: Try to Create associative Dimensions with tapir and claude
body:
Hi there !

I'm trying to Create associative Dimensions with tapir and claude.

But Claude told he than was impossible for now. 

Here is his report :

CreateAssociativeDimensions: witness points never resolve for Zone/Slab elements, and CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection always fails to find a valid section
Tapir version: 1.5.5 Archicad version: 29 Tested via: archicad-mcp (wraps TapirCommand.CreateAssociativeDimensions / CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection / GetDimensionData)

Summary
Two related issues with associative dimension creation:

CreateAssociativeDimensions witness points resolve correctly (real coordinates, correct dimensionValue) when elementId points to a Wall, Line, or Polyline, using only elementId + inIndex (1 or 2 — the two endpoints of the element's own reference line). However, witness points never resolve when elementId points to a Zone or a Slab — every combination of inIndex / nodeId / special / nodeType / nodeStatus I tried returns a witness coordinate of {0, 0} (and the created Dimension element is visually degenerate / invisible), even though the command itself reports success and returns a valid element GUID.

CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection fails with "The referenced 'sectionElementId' is not a valid section element" for every CutPlane element in the project I tested against — including sections that existed in the file before any scripting (not just ones created via CreateSections), and regardless of which ID I passed (the elementId returned by CreateSections, the navigatorItemId found via GetNavigatorItemTree, the databaseId returned by GetDatabaseIdFromNavigatorItemId, and the elementId returned by GetElementsByType("CutPlane") — all four candidates fail identically).

Issue 1: witness points on Zone/Slab
Repro steps
Create or select a Wall, and a Zone, in the same project.
Call CreateAssociativeDimensions with witnessPoints referencing the Wall's elementId, inIndex: 1 and inIndex: 2 (no other witness fields set). → Works. GetDimensionData on the result shows the witness coordinate matching the wall's begCoordinate/endCoordinate exactly, and dimensionValue equals the true distance.
Repeat the exact same call, but pointing elementId at a Zone instead (inIndex: 1 / inIndex: 2, referencing the zone's first two polygonOutline vertices). → The command reports success and returns a valid Dimension GUID, but GetDimensionData shows both witness points with coordinate: {x: 0, y: 0}. The resulting Dimension is not visible in the model (confirmed via Get2DBoundingBoxes returning "Element not supported", and FitInWindow on the element falling back to a whole-project zoom instead of centering on any real geometry).
Same result for a Slab element (tested with a slab whose polygonOutline matches the zone's, confirmed via GetDetailsOfElements).
What I tried on Zone/Slab witness points, all resulting in {0,0}
elementId only (all other fields omitted/null)
inIndex 0, 1, 2 (matching real vertex positions in polygonOutline)
inIndex + nodeId (1, 2)
inIndex + special (1, 2)
inIndex + nodeType (1, 2)
inIndex + line: true
Additional confirmation this is Zone/Slab-specific, not a general witness bug
The exact same payload shape (elementId + inIndex only) works reliably and repeatedly on Wall, Line, and Polyline elements.
A manually-drawn dimension (native ArchiCAD dimension tool, snapped to a wall corner where two walls meet) resolves to the walls' real footprint corner (not the reference-line endpoint) — proving ArchiCAD itself can address that corner internally — but GetDimensionData does not expose the underlying witness parameters used, so this couldn't be reverse-engineered from an existing working dimension.
On the same wall used in that manually-drawn dimension, testing inIndex values up to 12 still only resolves for 1 and 2 (the reference-line endpoints) — never the real footprint corner.
Expected behavior
Either: witness points should resolve for Zone/Slab elements the same way they do for Wall/Line/Polyline (ideally addressing each polygon vertex via inIndex), or the command/docs should clearly state that only certain element types support witness point addressing, and which inIndex/nodeType/etc. values are valid for each.

Issue 2: CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection never finds a valid section
Repro steps
In a project with existing Section views (created natively, long before any scripting) and/or new ones created via CreateSections, call CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection with preset: "WallCompositeFaces" and a sectionElementId.
Tried as sectionElementId:
The elementId returned directly by CreateSections
The navigatorItemId of the matching SectionItem found via GetNavigatorItemTree
The databaseId returned by GetDatabaseIdFromNavigatorItemId for that navigator item
The elementId of every CutPlane-type element returned by GetElementsByType("CutPlane") (7 sections in the test file, including natively pre-existing ones)
All of the above return: {"error": {"code": -2130313112, "message": "The referenced 'sectionElementId' is not a valid section element."}}
Expected behavior
At least one of these four natural ID candidates should be accepted as a valid sectionElementId, given GetElementsByType("CutPlane") explicitly lists CutPlane as one of its supported enum values.

Environment
Archicad 29
Tapir add-on 1.5.5
Windows

body:
## Summary

Four small changes answering the issues filed since #631 merged.

Fixes #636. Fixes #632. Closes #637.

## Changes

**Add-On**
- `GetAttributesByType` reports `modificationTime` for every attribute (#637): `API_Attr_Head::modiTime`, a GSTime in seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC, the same stamp the Attribute Manager writes as `ModiTime` into its XML export. The three goldens that list attributes carry the field, masked to `<TIME>` by the existing time mask, and `get_attributes_by_type.py` checks that every stamp is positive.
- `GetDimensionData` reports each witness point's `line`, `inIndex`, `special`, `nodeType`, `nodeStatus` and `nodeId`, the values `CreateAssociativeDimensions` takes (#633), each described from the `API_Base` docs. A dimension placed by hand on a slab or zone can now be read back to learn the parameters that element type needs; the DevKit documents `node_id` as the polygon vertex id from the element memo, which the reporter's attempts never used.
- New example `get_dimension_data.py`: dimensions two walls, reads the witness parameters back and rebuilds the dimension from them. It has no golden yet; `test_examples.py` records one on its first run.

**Grasshopper**
- `GuidObject.CreateFromWrapper` accepts the wrapper types the components hand out (`ElementGuidWrapper`, `DesignOptionGuidWrapper`, ...) by reading their `Id` (#636). `MoveElementsToDesignOptions` and every other component that converts a guid this way now take the output of `SelectedElements` and the other element sources directly.
- A `RoofDetails` typed getter beside the slab one (#632): outline polygons and holes at the pivot level, roof class, structure type, thickness, the pivot line or pivot polygon, and one branch per roof of slopes and level heights. Icon and resource added.
- `GetDimensionData` gains one tree output per witness parameter (`WitnessLines`, `WitnessInIndices`, `WitnessSpecials`, `WitnessNodeTypes`, `WitnessNodeStatuses`, `WitnessNodeIds`), ready for the `AdditionalSettings` input of `CreateAssociativeDimensions`. They follow `ErrorMessages`, so canvases saved with 1.5.8 keep their wires.

title: Reliable way to check if furniture obstructs a door's swing area?
body:
We're checking a rule: furniture must not obstruct a door's swing arc (the space the leaf sweeps through when opening, plus clearance in front of it). Our current approach:

Compute a 2D circular-sector polygon for the door's swing (hinge point + leaf width + which side it opens to, derived from wall geometry + door GDL/details).
Approximate each furniture object's footprint via Get2DBoundingBoxes (axis-aligned).
Test polygon intersection between the two.

Problem: for rotated furniture, the axis-aligned bounding box is much larger than the real footprint, causing false positives. We improved this by reconstructing a true rotated rectangle from ObjectDetails.dimensions/angle, anchored at the center of the Get2DBoundingBoxes result (mathematically anchor-independent, since a rotated rectangle's AABB is always centered on the rectangle's own center) — with a self-consistency check that falls back to the AABB when the object's symbol isn't actually a plain A×B rectangle (composite/grouped library parts).

Even after that fix, real test models still show flagged "collisions" that don't visually exist, and we haven't yet isolated whether the remaining false positives come from the swept-area polygon itself or from the furniture footprint for non-rotated objects.

Is there a more reliable primitive for this kind of check — e.g. a way to get an Object element's true 2D symbol outline (not just its bounding box), or a way to query/construct the door's actual swept opening zone as real geometry (so GetCollisions could be used directly), rather than approximating both sides geometrically ourselves?

title: ChangeDrawingLink produces a Drawing showing the wrong model content (position wrong, orientation right)
body:
## `ChangeDrawingLink` produces a Drawing showing the wrong model content (position wrong, orientation right)

### Summary

`ChangeDrawingLink` copies `pos`/`angle`/`ratio`/`drawingScale`/`modelOffset`/`clipPolygon` from the old Drawing onto a newly-created one sourced from the new `navigatorItemId`, then deletes the old element. That part works and the new element's metadata (as read back via `GetDetailsOfElements`) looks correct. However, the actual model content rendered inside the relinked Drawing does not reliably match the new source view — even on the very first relink to a given view. Orientation/scale look right, but the framed content is off, as if the Drawing's real 2D transform wasn't resynced against the new source view.

### Suspected root cause

`ChangeDrawingLinkCommand::Execute` (`DocumentCreationCommands.cpp`) calls `ActivateLayoutDatabase` (switches to the **layout** window) and then `CreateOneDrawing` directly. It never makes the **source view** (`navigatorItemId`) the current view before creating the element.

`CreateDrawingsCommand` has the same underlying issue for a freshly-created (never-before-used) view: a Drawing created while its source view has never been made current inherits a stale 2D transform (`GetView2DTransformations` shows rotation 0 and an unrelated tiny zoom) instead of the one saved via `SetViewSettings`. The known workaround is to call `ChangeWindow` (`navigatorItemId` form, i.e. `ACAPI_View_GoToView`) on the source view immediately before `CreateDrawings` — after which the transform is correctly resynced. `ChangeDrawingLinkCommand` skips this step entirely for the new source view, which looks like the same bug reappearing through a different code path.

### Repro (JSON API)

1. Create view A (fresh, never used), `SetViewSettings` (rotation, zoom, scale).
2. `ChangeWindow` to view A, `CreateDrawings` on it → correct auto-fit (bounds match the saved zoom exactly).
3. Create view B (fresh, never used, different rotation/zoom), same setup, same correct result.
4. `ChangeDrawingLink` the Drawing from step 2 onto view B.
5. `GetDetailsOfElements` on the relinked Drawing reports the same `pos`/`bounds` as before the relink (as expected, since they're copied verbatim) — but visually in Archicad, the Drawing's content does not correspond to view B's real content. Same symptom happens when relinking onto an already-used-once shared view, or even a brand-new one.

### Suggested fix

In `ChangeDrawingLinkCommand::Execute` (`DocumentCreationCommands.cpp`), call `ACAPI_View_GoToView` on the new `navigatorItemId` before `CreateOneDrawing` — the same call `ChangeWindowCommand` already makes in `ApplicationCommands.cpp` for its `navigatorItemId` form. That should resync the source view's real 2D transform against its saved settings before the new Drawing is created from it, mirroring what's already necessary for `CreateDrawings` itself.

### Context

Found while trying to consolidate several auto-generated Drawings (each first correctly auto-fit on its own disposable/never-used view) onto a single shared view via `ChangeDrawingLink`, purely to avoid one extra clone view per item cluttering the Navigator. Metadata comparisons (`bounds`, `pos`) after the relink looked fine in every test, which is what made this hard to catch without visually checking the actual placed Drawing in Archicad.

Tapir 1.5.8, ArchiCAD 27 (Mac).
author: MathiasJon

title: GetNavigatorItemTree/GetNavigatorItemsType don't expose sourceGuid (or most of API_NavigatorItem)
body:
### What we're trying to do

Tell apart, among several Drawings already placed on the same layout, which one was created from a Schedule/List view versus a floor plan/section/etc. — without relying on custom names (not always set) or approximate position matching.

### What we tried and ruled out

- `GetDetailsOfElements` on a Drawing exposes `navigatorItemId`, which is a pass-through of the C++ `elem.drawing.drawingGuid` field. Per the SDK docs, that field's actual purpose is "Drawing GUID for autotext identification" — not a source-view reference. Confirmed live: once a Drawing is placed, that guid does not resolve through `GetNavigatorItemsType` (`"Navigator item not found"`), even for a Drawing created from a real, still-existing Story view. Dead end.
- The Drawing's *own* Navigator entry (its `DrawingItem` node, found by walking `LayoutBook`) *does* resolve correctly through `GetNavigatorItemsType`.

### The actual gap

Per the SDK docs, `API_NavigatorItem` — the struct behind every navigator item, including a placed Drawing's own `DrawingItem` entry — has a `sourceGuid` field: "GUID of source navigator item". That's exactly what would let us trace a placed Drawing back to the view/schedule it was created from, and from there read that source item's own `itemType` to know if it's a schedule, story, section, etc.

Neither `GetNavigatorItemTree` nor `GetNavigatorItemsType` returns it today — `GetNavigatorItemTree` items carry `type`/`name`/`navigatorItemId`/`prefix`/`uiId`/`customUiId`/`customName`/`isIndependent`, and `GetNavigatorItemsType` returns `navigatorItemType`/`navigatorItemId`. Neither of those already-exposed sets includes `sourceGuid`.

### Request

Please expose `sourceGuid` on `GetNavigatorItemTree` items and/or `GetNavigatorItemsType` results.

(Everything else in `API_NavigatorItem` looks either already covered — `uiId`, `guid`, `itemType`, `customName`, `customUiId`, `isIndependent` are already in your output under those or equivalent names, `db` is already reachable via `GetDatabaseIdFromNavigatorItemId` — or narrow enough not to be worth asking for on its own: `vType` is documented "for internal use", `owner` only matters in Teamwork, `floorNum`/`camId` only apply to specific item types, `mimeType` is Publisher-specific, `uAutoTextedName` is a narrow autotext-rendering variant of `name`. `sourceGuid` is the one genuine, broadly useful gap.)

title: "Drawing" favorite fails every time
body:
## `ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults` fails with "Failed to get favorite" — Drawing-specific

### What we found

`ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults` fails on every Drawing favorite we tried, but **works fine on other element types** — cleanly isolated with a same-session, apples-to-apples test:

**Wall favorite — succeeds:**
```
CreateFavoritesFromElements({elementId: <wall>, favorite: "TEST_WALL_FAVORI"})  → success: true
ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults({favorites: ["TEST_WALL_FAVORI"]})              → success: true
```

**Drawing favorite — fails, every time:**
```
CreateFavoritesFromElements({elementId: <drawing>, favorite: "TEST_ASCII_FAVORI"})  → success: true
GetFavoritesByType({elementType: "Drawing"})                                        → includes "TEST_ASCII_FAVORI"
ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults({favorites: ["TEST_ASCII_FAVORI"]})                 → {"error": {"code": -2130312312, "message": "Failed to get favorite"}}
```

Also fails the same way on a pre-existing, office-defined Drawing favorite (not one we created ourselves) — so it isn't about how the favorite was created either. `favorites: ["TEST_ASCII_FAVORI"]` is spelled and cased exactly as returned by `GetFavoritesByType` right before the failing call, ruling out a naming/encoding mismatch.

This also matches your own `test_favorites_commands.py` / its expected output: the exact same `CreateFavoritesFromElements` → `ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults` sequence, on a **Column**, is expected to (and does) succeed. So the sequence itself is fine — something about `API_DrawingType` specifically breaks `ACAPI_Favorite_Get` (or the surrounding handling) in `ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaultsCommand::Execute` (`FavoritesCommands.cpp`).

### Why it matters (context)

We were hoping to use this command as a workaround for a separate, already-reported limitation: `CreateDrawings` can't force `isCutWithFrame: false`, so a new Drawing silently inherits cropping from whatever the Drawing tool's current defaults happen to be. Applying a known-good Drawing Favorite (with cropping off) right before `CreateDrawings` would sidestep that — `ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults` calls `ACAPI_Element_ChangeDefaults`, which is exactly what `CreateOneDrawing`'s later `ACAPI_Element_GetDefaults` reads from. This bug blocks that workaround specifically for Drawings, while working for ordinary construction elements.

### Request

Since it reproduces with Walls but not Drawings in an otherwise identical test, this looks like a `Drawing`-specific code path issue inside `ACAPI_Favorite_Get`/its Tapir wrapper — worth a look with SDK-level access to `API_DrawingType`'s favorite handling.

title: # GetDimensionData crashes with Pydantic validation errors against Tapir 1.5.9 (embedded schema out of sync)
body:
# GetDimensionData crashes with Pydantic validation errors against Tapir 1.5.9 (embedded schema out of sync)

**tapir-archicad-mcp version:** latest available via `uvx` (PyPI 0.3.2 at time of writing)
**Tapir add-on version:** 1.5.9
**Archicad version:** 29

## Summary

Tapir 1.5.9 changed `GetDimensionData`'s response to include six new fields per witness point (`line`, `inIndex`, `special`, `nodeType`, `nodeStatus`, `nodeId`) — see [[ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation#638](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/pull/638)](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/pull/638), which references [[ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation#633](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/issues/633)](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/issues/633).

Calling `GetDimensionData` through this MCP server now fails outright, because the server's embedded Pydantic response model doesn't know about these new fields and is configured to reject unknown fields (`extra_forbidden`) rather than ignore them.

## Repro

1. Update the Tapir add-on to 1.5.9.
2. Create any associative dimension (e.g. on a Wall, using `elementId` + `inIndex`).
3. Call `GetDimensionData` on it through this MCP server.

## Actual result

The call throws a validation error instead of returning data, e.g.:

```
Received an invalid response from the Archicad API for GetDimensionData: 17 validation errors for GetDimensionDataResult
dimensionsData.0.DimensionData.witnessPoints.0.line
  Extra inputs are not permitted [type=extra_forbidden, input_value=False, input_type=bool]
dimensionsData.0.DimensionData.witnessPoints.0.inIndex
  Extra inputs are not permitted [type=extra_forbidden, input_value=0, input_type=int]
... (same for special, nodeType, nodeStatus, nodeId, and repeated for witnessPoints.1)
```

## Expected result

`GetDimensionData` should return successfully and surface the new `line`/`inIndex`/`special`/`nodeType`/`nodeStatus`/`nodeId` fields per witness point, matching Tapir 1.5.9's actual response shape.

## Likely cause

Per the README, this server embeds a schema snapshot synced from the Tapir repo via `archicad-mcp-sync`, rather than fetching schemas live from the running Tapir instance. That embedded snapshot appears to predate Tapir 1.5.9's `GetDimensionData` change. Re-running the sync (`archicad-mcp-sync deps/tapir`) against current Tapir and cutting a new release should resolve this.

This is currently blocking a real use case: reading back the witness-point parameters of a manually-placed dimension on a Zone/Slab, in order to learn what `CreateAssociativeDimensions` needs for those element types (see the discussion in ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation#633).

title: CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap/CreateViewsInViewMap with no parentNavigatorItemId create an undeletable orphan at the View Map root
body:
## API can create a View Map view outside the navigator hierarchy - impossible to delete

### Summary

Two connected problems, one root cause.

1. Creating a View Map view while leaving the destination parent unset does not fail and does not fall back to a sensible container - it attaches the new view directly to the View Map ROOT node, outside every folder and subset. The Navigator palette has no place to show such an item cleanly, and Archicad itself never creates views there.

2. A view in that position can then never be removed. `ACAPI_Navigator_DeleteNavigatorView` returns `NoError` but is a silent no-op - the item is still there on the next read. `ACAPI_Navigator_ChangeNavigatorItem` cannot move it into a real folder either (fails with error -2130313112, "Failed to move navigator item"). And it cannot be deleted by hand in the Navigator palette. The project is permanently stuck with the orphan view.

The same view, created inside a folder, deletes and moves without any problem.

### Suspected root cause (Tapir side)

`CloneProjectMapItemToViewMapCommand::Execute` and `CreateViewsInViewMapCommand::Execute` (both in `Sources/NavigatorCommands.cpp`) treat `parentNavigatorItemId` as optional. When it's omitted, both resolve it themselves via:

```cpp
if (parentGuid == APINULLGuid) {
    API_NavigatorSet viewMapSet = {};
    viewMapSet.mapId = API_PublicViewMap;
    Int32 idx = 0;
    if (ACAPI_Navigator_GetNavigatorSet (&viewMapSet, &idx) == NoError) {
        parentGuid = viewMapSet.rootGuid;
    }
}
```

... and then pass that `rootGuid` straight into `ACAPI_Navigator_CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap`. That is exactly the state described above: a clone attached to the View Map root that no subsequent API call (delete or move) can touch. So the two problems reduce to one: **Tapir's own fallback is what produces the broken item** - the command should never hand `viewMapSet.rootGuid` to `CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap` on the caller's behalf.

Read back via `ACAPI_Navigator_GetNavigatorItem`, the orphan item shows:
- `itemType`: story item (a clone of a Project Map story)
- `guid`: valid, resolvable (`GetNavigatorItem` succeeds, `GetDatabaseId` succeeds and returns the floor plan database)
- `parent`: the View Map root node
- `isIndependent`: false

### Steps to reproduce

1. Call `CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap` (or `CreateViewsInViewMap`) with a Project Map story `navigatorItemId` and **no `parentNavigatorItemId`**.
   -> succeeds, no error, no warning.
2. Read it back with `GetNavigatorItemTree` / `ACAPI_Navigator_GetNavigatorItem` - it is there, attached to the View Map root.
3. Call `ACAPI_Navigator_DeleteNavigatorView(&guid, &silentMode)` with `silentMode = true`.
   -> returns `NoError`.
4. Read the View Map tree again - the view is still present.
5. Try `ACAPI_Navigator_ChangeNavigatorItem` to move it into a real folder.
   -> fails with error -2130313112 ("Failed to move navigator item").
6. Try to delete it by hand in the Navigator palette.
   -> not possible.
7. For contrast: create a folder (`CreateViewMapFolder`), create a second view of the same story inside that folder (`parentNavigatorItemId` set), delete that one.
   -> succeeds, the folder view is gone.

### Suggested fix

Since Tapir's own root-fallback is what triggers the broken state, stop doing it:

- In both `CloneProjectMapItemToViewMapCommand` and `CreateViewsInViewMapCommand` (`Sources/NavigatorCommands.cpp`), make `parentNavigatorItemId` a **required** schema field (add it to each item's `"required"` array; update the `"description"` to say so) instead of silently defaulting to the View Map root when it's missing.
- In `Execute`, replace the `viewMapSet.rootGuid` fallback with an explicit `APIERR_BADPARS` error when `parentNavigatorItemId` is absent, with a message pointing the caller at `CreateViewMapFolder` to create a destination first.
- Update `Sources/AddOnMain.cpp`'s registered descriptions for both commands accordingly ("... into a specified View Map folder or subset" instead of "optionally into a specified folder" / "defaults to View Map root").
- `Examples/test_navigator_views.py` already always passes `parentNavigatorItemId`, so no example/test change should be needed - worth double-checking after the change.

This can't fix `ACAPI_Navigator_DeleteNavigatorView`/`ChangeNavigatorItem`'s behavior on items that already exist at the root (that's Archicad's API, out of Tapir's control, and worth reporting to Graphisoft separately) - but it stops Tapir from ever creating one, which is the only actionable part from this repo.

Both commands have shipped since Tapir 1.5.4 (July 2026) with `parentNavigatorItemId` optional, so this is a breaking schema tightening for anyone currently omitting it against these two commands specifically - worth a release-notes callout, but the alternative is leaving every such caller able to permanently corrupt a project's View Map.

title: GetDimensionData (and other read commands) reject valid Archicad 29 responses — Pydantic schema mismatch
body:
Archicad version: 29
Tapir Add-On: installed via the AC29 build from the releases page

Summary: Several read commands fail with Pydantic validation errors of the form Extra inputs are not permitted, because the live JSON response from Archicad 29 includes fields the connector's response models don't declare.

Reproduced on GetDimensionData:
Calling it on a dimension created via CreateAssociativeDimensions throws 17 validation errors, all extra_forbidden, on fields nested under witnessPoints: line, inIndex, special, nodeType, nodeStatus, nodeId. The underlying data is visible in the error payload before rejection and looks correct (e.g. direction, dimensionLinePosition, and witnessPoints[].coordinate all match what was sent/expected) — so this is a response-model gap, not a data problem.

Same class of bug also hit today on:

GetAttributesByType (attributeType: ZoneCategory / Layer) — fails on an extra modificationTime field.
GetAttributeFolderStructure (attributeType: Layer) — same pattern.

Suspected cause: Archicad 29's JSON API appears to return a richer field set (possibly IDs/metadata added in AC28/29) than the Tapir connector's Pydantic models currently declare, so additionalProperties-style strictness rejects otherwise-valid payloads.

Impact: Any read command touching these object types is unusable via the MCP/connector layer in AC29, even though writes to the same elements succeed.

title: ModifySlabs: floorFill.orientation.origin appears read-only via API (type and matrix write correctly, origin does not)
body:
## Environment
- Tapir Add-On: 1.5.8 (checked 1.5.9 changelog — no related fix found)
- Archicad: 29
- Connection: archicad-mcp (execute_script / ModifySlabs, official JSON API wrapper)

## Summary
`floorFill.orientation.type` and `floorFill.orientation.matrix00/01/10/11` write correctly via `ModifySlabs`, but `floorFill.orientation.origin` is silently ignored in every variation tested — including when overwriting an origin that was already correctly set via the UI. `ModifySlabs` returns `success: true` in all cases; the discrepancy only shows up on re-read via `GetDetailsOfElements`.

## Steps to reproduce

Starting state: a Slab with `floorFill.orientation.type: "Global"`, `origin: (0,0)`.

**Call 1** — set only `type: "Rotated"` (no origin/matrix):
- Result: `type` correctly becomes `"Rotated"`. `origin` stays `(0,0)` (expected, none was sent).

**Call 2** — set only `origin: (2.75, 0.15)` (no type repeated):
- Result: `type` reverts to `"Global"` (confirms the object is fully replaced, not merged — worth documenting separately). `origin` stays `(0,0)`, not applied.

**Call 3** — set `type: "Rotated"` + `origin: (2.75, 0.15)` + explicit identity matrix, all in one call:
- Result: `type` and `matrix` apply correctly. `origin` stays `(0,0)` — not applied.

**Call 4** (decisive) — with the Slab already manually set via the Archicad UI to `origin: (2.75, 0.15)` (confirmed correct via `GetDetailsOfElements`), attempt to overwrite it via API to a different value `(0.25, 0.15)`:
- Result: `success: true`, but re-read shows `origin` unchanged at `(2.75, 0.15)` — the API could not move it away from the manually-set value either, in any direction.

## Additional checks performed (ruling out user error)
- Compared the exact JSON structure sent in Call 3 against the structure read back after a manual UI edit — identical field names, nesting, and types. No schema mismatch.
- Checked for any local/element-relative coordinate system that `origin` might expect instead of global coordinates — none exists; the only orientation-related fields on the element are inside `floorFill.orientation`, and the manually-set value matches the same global coordinate system as `polygonOutline`.

## Expected behavior
`ModifySlabs` should be able to set `floorFill.orientation.origin` to an arbitrary point (as the Archicad UI itself allows when manually adjusting fill origin), both when moving away from the default `(0,0)` and when overwriting an already-set value.

## Question for maintainers
Is this a Tapir-side limitation (e.g. the field not being passed through to the underlying `ACAPI_Element_Change` call for Slab), or a limitation of the underlying Archicad API itself that Tapir cannot work around? Happy to test a patched build if useful.
author: leafaramil

title: GetPropertyValuesOfElements returns empty values for ColumnSegment subelement GUIDs
body:
## Environment
- Tapir Add-On: 1.5.9
- Archicad: 29
- Connection: official `archicad` Python package + `aclib`

## Summary

`GetPropertyValuesOfElements` (via `RunTapirCommand`) returns responses with `propertyValues` entries where every `propertyValue.status` is not `normal`/`hasValue` when called with `ColumnSegment` subelement GUIDs. No property — including user-defined writable ones like `General_ElementID` — returns a value. The documentation states the command *"works for subelements of hierarchical elements also"*, but this does not appear to hold for `ColumnSegment`.

## Steps to Reproduce

```python
import aclib

# 1. Get columns
col_elems = aclib.RunCommand('API.GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Column'})['elements']

# 2. Get ColumnSegment subelement GUIDs
sub_result = aclib.RunTapirCommand('GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements', {'elements': col_elems})
col_seg_guids = [
    seg
    for entry in sub_result.get('subelements', [])
    for seg in entry.get('columnSegments', [])
]
print(f'ColumnSegment GUIDs found: {len(col_seg_guids)}')  # → e.g. 11

# 3. Try to read ElementID on segment GUIDs (same pattern as set_properties_of_subelements.py example)
eid_prop_id = aclib.RunCommand('API.GetPropertyIds', {
    'properties': [{'type': 'BuiltIn', 'nonLocalizedName': 'General_ElementID'}]
})['properties'][0]['propertyId']

result = aclib.RunTapirCommand('GetPropertyValuesOfElements', {
    'elements': [{'elementId': seg['elementId']} for seg in col_seg_guids[:3]],
    'properties': [{'propertyId': eid_prop_id}],
})

for ev in result.get('propertyValuesForElements', []):
    for pv_entry in ev.get('propertyValues', []):
        print(pv_entry['propertyValue'])  # → status is never 'normal' or 'hasValue'
```

## Expected Behavior

`GetPropertyValuesOfElements` should return property values for `ColumnSegment` GUIDs, as the documentation states it works for subelements of hierarchical elements. At minimum, `General_ElementID` should be readable and writable (as demonstrated in `set_properties_of_subelements.py` for CurtainWall frames).

## Actual Behavior

All `propertyValue` entries come back with a non-normal status (no value). `col_seg_all_props_with_values` is empty even when iterating all properties in batches of 100 via `GetAllProperties`.

Additionally, `GetDetailsOfElements` called on `ColumnSegment` GUIDs returns:
```json
{"type": "ColumnSegment", "details": {"error": "Not yet supported element type"}}
```

## Impact

This blocks volume and building material data retrieval per individual column segment, which is critical for quantity takeoff tools. A column with multiple segments of different building materials (e.g. a reinforced concrete core with a steel casing) cannot be correctly evaluated — the only available workaround is reading the total volume from the parent Column element, which does not distinguish between segments.

`GetClassificationsOfElements` works correctly on `ColumnSegment` GUIDs — so the GUIDs themselves are valid and accepted by at least one Tapir command.

## Workaround

None for per-segment property reading. Reading properties from the parent `Column` element gives the total volume only.

author: betonrosa

title: `DeleteElements` reports `success: true` for an element on a locked layer without deleting it
body:
## Environment

- Archicad 27, macOS 14
- Tapir Additional JSON Commands add-on 1.5.10
- Command: `DeleteElements` (wraps `ACAPI_Element_Delete`)

## Summary

Calling `DeleteElements` on an element whose layer is locked returns `{"success": true}` — no error, no failed execution result — but the element is still present on the next read. The exact same call on the exact same element, after unlocking its layer, succeeds and actually deletes it.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a small element, e.g. a Mesh via `CreateMeshes`.
2. Note its layer: `GetDetailsOfElements` returns `layerIndex` (top-level, not inside `details`); resolve it to a name via `GetLayers`.
3. Lock that layer (native `API.GetAttributesByType` + `CreateLayers` with `isLocked: true`, or by hand in Layer Settings).
4. Call `DeleteElements`:
   ```json
   {"elements": [{"elementId": {"guid": "<the element's guid>"}}]}
   ```
   → response: `{"success": true}`
5. Call `GetElementsByType` for the same element type again — the element is still there.
6. Unlock the layer and repeat step 4 with the same guid.
   → response: `{"success": true}`, and this time the element is actually gone.

## Expected

Either:
- `DeleteElements` fails (`success: false`, with an error such as `APIERR_LOCKEDLAY`) when the target element's layer is locked, **or**
- it silently succeeds **and** actually deletes the element (auto-unlocking is not what we're asking for — just a return value that matches reality).

## Actual

The call reports success even though nothing happened. There is no way to distinguish "deleted" from "silently ignored because locked" from the response alone — a caller has to independently re-query for the element's existence afterward to find out.

## Impact

Any batch/automation tool that deletes elements after creating replacements (merge operations, cleanup passes, regenerating a set of elements, etc.) can silently leave stale elements behind while reporting full success, unless it adds its own after-the-fact existence check. We hit this in two of our own tools before adding that workaround:

- A terrain-generation tool that now unlocks and unhides every layer up front before generating, specifically because of this class of issue (creating/modifying elements on a locked or hidden layer produced similarly silent no-ops).
- A mesh-merging script (create a merged mesh, then delete the two originals) had exactly the symptom described here: the merged mesh was created correctly, `DeleteElements` on the two originals reported `{"success": true}`, and both originals were still in the project afterward.

We now defensively unlock every layer before any batch of creates/modifies/deletes, and re-verify deletions by re-querying `GetElementsByType` afterward — but this shouldn't be necessary for a command that already has a well-defined success/failure response shape.

## Request

Make `DeleteElements` — and possibly other element-modifying commands with the same underlying pattern (not separately verified here) — report failure when an element cannot actually be changed because its layer is locked, instead of reporting success unconditionally.
author: MathiasJon

title: CreateProjectInfoFields returns an id but the field is never created (AC29, Tapir 1.5.9)
body:
## What happens

`CreateProjectInfoFields` reports success and returns a new `projectInfoId`, but the field is never created: it does not appear in `GetProjectInfoFields`, and it is not available as an autotext key.

Tested on **Archicad 29 (build 5101, macOS, Apple Silicon) with Tapir 1.5.9**, on a solo project, in the same session, with no save in between.

```python
before = RunTapirCommand('GetProjectInfoFields')          # 84 fields, 7 of them custom
RunTapirCommand('CreateProjectInfoFields', {
    'projectInfoFields': [{'projectInfoName': 'DLA_PROBE', 'projectInfoValue': 'probe'}]})
# → {"fields": [{"projectInfoId": "autotext-87CCA2F3-52F3-2942-B609-AC83431F7104",
#                "projectInfoName": "DLA_PROBE", "projectInfoValue": "probe"}]}

after = RunTapirCommand('GetProjectInfoFields')           # still 84 fields, DLA_PROBE not among them
RunTapirCommand('GetAutoTextKeys')                        # 97 keys, none of them the new field
```

`GetProjectInfoFields` does list custom fields in general — this project has 7, with ids such as `autotext-CLIENT-1` and `autotext-BUILDING-1` — so the new one should be visible there and is not.

Creating the same field by hand (Options ▸ Project Preferences ▸ Project Info ▸ add a custom field) works, and the field then shows up in `GetProjectInfoFields` and as an autotext key.

## Second, smaller issue in the same area

`DeleteProjectInfoFields` returns `{"executionResults": [{"success": true}]}` for a `projectInfoId` that does not exist (the one returned by the failed create above). A delete that matched nothing probably shouldn't report success — that is what made this take a while to pin down on our side: both ends of the round trip claim to have worked.

## Why this matters

Custom project info fields are the natural anchor for a title block: the drawing sheet reads them as autotext, so the whole set (client, file number, planning reference, phase, revision…) fills itself in. For an office template that is generated and versioned as code, having to add ~37 of those fields by hand in the UI, once per project, is the last manual step in an otherwise scripted title block.

## Expected

Either the created field shows up in `GetProjectInfoFields` and as an autotext key, or the command reports the failure instead of returning an id.
author: xcastellnou

title: Wish: delete (and replace) embedded library items — ACAPI_LibraryManagement_DeleteEmbeddedLibItem(s)
body:
## What's missing

Tapir can add files to the embedded library (`AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary`), but there is no way to **delete** an embedded library part, and adding a file under a name that already exists does not replace the loaded part.

Observed while generating GDL objects from HSF and embedding them repeatedly (Archicad 29, macOS; behaviour seen on 1.5.8, not re-tested on 1.5.9): re-adding a recompiled `.gsm` with the same `outputPath` returns success, but the previously loaded version stays in use — so the object you then place is not the one you just compiled. The practical workaround is to embed every iteration under a new name, which leaves the project's embedded library full of dead parts that can only be removed one by one in the Library Manager.

## The API is already there

The Archicad 29 C++ API exposes the delete side of this in the Library Management group:

- `ACAPI_LibraryManagement_DeleteEmbeddedLibItem`
- `ACAPI_LibraryManagement_DeleteEmbeddedLibItems`

## Suggested commands

Mirroring existing Tapir naming:

- `DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItems` — take the same `outputPath`-style names (or library part names) that `AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary` writes.
- an `overwriteExisting` flag on `AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary` (defaulting to the current behaviour), so a recompiled part can replace the loaded one in place.

## Why this matters

Authoring library parts from source (HSF → `LP_XMLConverter` → `.gsm` → embed → reload) is a normal loop for anyone who keeps a template as code: title blocks, legends, symbol catalogues. Right now that loop can add but never tidy up, so the embedded library grows one dead part per iteration and the only cleanup is manual. With delete (and replace) it becomes a closed loop that can run unattended.

title: SetStories: keep non-ASCII characters in story names
body:
## Problem

`SetStories` writes the story name into `API_StoryCmdType::uName` (a UTF-16 field) with `GS::snuprintf`, passing the name's narrow C string as the format string. Two consequences:

- Every character outside ASCII is lost. A story named `1.EM FÉLSZINT` arrives in Archicad as `1.EM F`.
- A `%` in a story name is read as a format directive.

## Fix

Copy the name as UTF-16 with `GS::ucscpy`, clipped to `GS::ArraySize (storyCmd.uName) - 1` so the limit follows the field itself, the same way the other UTF-16 fields in this file are filled. Both call sites (new story creation in `FillNewStoryCmd` and the rename path in `Execute`) are changed.

## Testing

Built for AC26 and AC27 on macOS; the change is a plain string copy with no version-specific API.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
author: brncsk

title: GetStories: report the height of the top story
body:
## Problem

`GetStories` reports a `height` for every story except the top one. The Archicad API keeps a virtual story record past the last real story in `API_StoryInfo::data`, and its level is where the top story ends; the API reference notes it is there precisely so the height of the top story can be computed. Scripts that need every storey height (for example to write a building's storeys into another tool's configuration) currently have to guess the last one.

## Change

- `GetStoriesCommand::Execute` reads the next record for every story, the top one included, so `height` is always present. The record count is taken from `BMGetHandleSize` of the data handle, so a level is never read past the array.
- The `StoryParameters.height` description in `CommonSchemaDefinitions.json` no longer says the top story has no height. The field stays optional, so the guard above can omit it without violating the schema.
- The Grasshopper `GetStories` component uses the reported `height` and keeps its old difference-of-levels guess only for an add-on that does not report one.

Existing consumers are unaffected; the top story simply gains a value it lacked.

## Not in this PR

`docs/archicad-addon` is not regenerated here: `monthly_release.yml` requires a full `GenerateDocumentation` run in Archicad before a release and rejects hand edits to single docs files, and the two most recent schema-touching PRs (#650, #653) did not regenerate either.

## Testing

Built for AC27 on macOS; Grasshopper plugin built for net7.0. No golden output in `Test/ExpectedOutputs` prints `height`, so the example suite is unaffected.

title: Add SaveProjectAsArchive command
body:
## What

New `SaveProjectAsArchive` command (Project Commands) that saves the open project as a `.pla` archive through `ACAPI_ProjectOperation_Save` with `API_SavePars_Archive`.

Parameters:

| name | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `archiveFilePath` | required | Absolute path of the archive to write; overwritten if present. The archive becomes the open project, as Save As does. |
| `includeLibraryParts` | `true` | Put the library parts the project uses into the archive |
| `includeProperties` | `true` | Put the properties into the archive |
| `includeTextures` | `false` | Put the linked textures into the archive |
| `includeBackgroundPicture` | `false` | Put the background picture into the archive |

## Why

An archive holds the library parts the project uses from its linked libraries, and an archive can be linked as a library of another project. That is how a host that hotlinks a project gets the source's doors, windows and objects: a hotlink carries the source's elements but not its libraries. Producing that archive unattended was not possible through Tapir.

## Compatibility

Archicad 25 and 26 have no `ACAPI_ProjectOperation_Save (fileSavePars, formatPars)`; a shim in `MigrationHelper.hpp` routes the call through `ACAPI_Automate (APIDo_SaveID, ...)`. Registered as introduced in 1.5.10.

## Not in this PR

A Grasshopper `SaveProjectAsArchive` component (the sibling of `SaveAsModuleFileComponent`) is left for a follow-up, tracked in #673.

## Testing

Built for AC26 and AC27 on macOS (the AC25 DevKit's `ResConv` is x86_64 only, so AC25 relies on CI). Example: `Examples/save_project_as_archive.py`.

`Test/ExpectedOutputs/save_project_as_archive.py.output` is derived, not recorded: the example's output is the command, its one path-masked parameter and the fixed `ExecutionResult`, none of which depends on the test project. It was produced by running the example through `aclib` with the transport stubbed to the success result and applying `output_masks.Mask`, so the shape matches `save_as_module_file.py.output`. `TestProject.pla` is an Archicad 28 file and only Archicad 27 was available here, so a recorded run was not possible.

title: IFCFileOperation: save with a named export translator; add GetIFCExportTranslators
body:
## Problem

The `save` method of `IFCFileOperation` goes through the IFC add-on's `IO_SAVEAS` with `noDialog = true`, so the add-on saves with whatever translator Archicad remembers from its own Save dialog. A script can neither see nor set that translator, which makes an unattended IFC export nondeterministic: the same command produces different files depending on what a user last picked interactively.

## Change

**`IFCFileOperation`** gains two optional parameters for the `save` method:

- `translatorName`: name of an IFC export translator of the project. When given, the save goes through `ACAPI_ProjectOperation_Save` with `API_SavePars_Ifc` instead of the add-on path. The translator is looked up by name; a name the project does not have fails with the list of the names it does have. Given with any other method, it fails with `APIERR_BADPARS`.
- `elementsToExport`: `EntireProject`, `VisibleElementsOnAllStories` (default), `AllElementsOnCurrentStory`, `VisibleElementsOnCurrentStory` or `SelectedElementsOnly`. Only valid together with `translatorName`, since the add-on path has no such switch; given without one it fails with `APIERR_BADPARS` instead of being dropped silently.

Without `translatorName` the command behaves exactly as before.

**`GetIFCExportTranslators`** (new, IFC Commands) lists the project's export translators, the preview translator first, so a script can check for the one it needs (and fail early) before it exports.

## Compatibility

- The packed file type the Automate API accepts differs by version: `ifczip` from Archicad 27 on, `ifcxml` on 25 and 26. The command reports which one it needs when given the other.
- On Archicad 25 and 26 the save is routed through `ACAPI_Automate` by a shim in `MigrationHelper.hpp`; on 25 the translator list goes through `ACAPI_Goodies`.
- The existing Archicad 25 shim `ACAPI_IFC_GetIFCExportTranslatorsList` took its `GS::Array` by value, so a caller could never receive the list. It now takes the array by reference. This is a behaviour change on Archicad 25 beyond this feature: `IssueCommands.cpp` calls the same shim for the BCF export, so on 25 it now receives the translator list it was written to expect (before, the list was always empty).
- `GetIFCExportTranslators` is registered as introduced in 1.5.10.

## Not in this PR

The Grasshopper side (the two new inputs on `IFCFileOperationComponent` and a `GetIFCExportTranslators` component) is left for a follow-up, tracked in #673.

## Testing

Built for AC26 and AC27 on macOS (the AC25 DevKit's `ResConv` is x86_64 only, so AC25 relies on CI). Example: `Examples/ifc_export_with_translator.py`, which lists the translators and exports with the first one.

title: Grasshopper components for SaveProjectAsArchive, GetIFCExportTranslators and the IFCFileOperation translator inputs
body:
Follow-up to #671 and #672, which add commands on the Add-On side only. The Grasshopper plugin should expose them:

- **`SaveProjectAsArchive` component** (Project group), the sibling of `SaveAsModuleFileComponent`: `ArchiveFilePath` input, optional `IncludeLibraryParts`, `IncludeProperties`, `IncludeTextures`, `IncludeBackgroundPicture` booleans, `ExecutionResult` message output.
- **`GetIFCExportTranslators` component** (IFC group): outputs the translator names and which one is the preview translator, so a name can be wired into the save.
- **`IFCFileOperationComponent`**: two optional inputs, `TranslatorName` and `ElementsToExport` (a value list of `EntireProject`, `VisibleElementsOnAllStories`, `AllElementsOnCurrentStory`, `VisibleElementsOnCurrentStory`, `SelectedElementsOnly`), passed through `IFCFileOperationParameters` as `translatorName` / `elementsToExport`, both omitted when empty.

Each new component needs a 24x24 icon under `Resources/` and the matching `Resources.resx` / `Resources.Designer.cs` entries.

title: SaveProject fails unless the Floor Plan window is active
body:
### Summary

`SaveProject` fails with `Failed to save the project.` whenever the active window is **not** the Floor Plan. Switching to the Floor Plan first makes the very same call succeed, so the project data and file permissions are not involved.

### Reproduction

Archicad 29 build 3000 (CZE) on Windows, add-on 1.5.9, driven over the JSON API. Solo `.pln` on a local disk, writable, with unsaved changes.

| step | result |
|---|---|
| `GetCurrentWindowType` | `3DModel` |
| `SaveProject` | `{"code": -2130312308, "message": "Failed to save the project."}` |
| `ChangeWindow` → `FloorPlan` | `success` |
| `SaveProject` | **`success`** — file written to disk |
| `ChangeWindow` → `3DModel` | `success` |
| `SaveProject` | fails again |

Verified in both directions, so it reproduces on demand.

### Cause

`archicad-addon/Sources/ProjectCommands.cpp`:

```cpp
GSErrCode err = ACAPI_ProjectOperation_Save ();
if (err != NoError) {
    return CreateFailedExecutionResult (APIERR_COMMANDFAILED, "Failed to save the project.");
}
```

The parameterless overload of `ACAPI_ProjectOperation_Save()` saves *the content of the current window*, not the project. A 3D window has no file of its own, so the call fails — matching the documented `APIERR_READONLY` case "has never been saved to a file and the fileSavePars is nullptr".

`SaveProjectAsArchiveCommand` in the same file calls the same API function but passes an explicit `API_FileSavePars`, and it is covered by `Test/ExpectedOutputs/save_project_as_archive.py.output`. `SaveProject` has no example or test in the repo, which is probably why this went unnoticed.

This is not an Archicad API restriction: commands run through `ScheduleForExecutionOnMainThread`, so the call is on the main thread and outside an undo scope.

### Secondary issue — the real error code is discarded

The handler returns a hardcoded `APIERR_COMMANDFAILED` and throws away the `GSErrCode` that Archicad actually returned. The reported code is therefore always `-2130312308` regardless of what went wrong, which makes the failure considerably harder to diagnose than it needs to be. Returning `err` would have pointed straight at the cause.

### Suggested fix

1. Return the actual `err` instead of the hardcoded constant.
2. Either switch to the floor plan database for the duration of the save — `ChangeCurrentDatabase` already exists in `MigrationHelper.hpp` and is used by several other command groups — or pass an explicit `API_FileSavePars` describing the open project. Switching the database preserves the "save the project" semantics that the command name implies.

### Workaround for anyone hitting this

```
ChangeWindow { "windowType": "FloorPlan" }
SaveProject
ChangeWindow { ... restore previous window ... }
```

title: `CreateKeynoteFolders` terminates Archicad when `key` is an empty string
body:
**Environment**

| | |
|---|---|
| Archicad | 28, build 6003, language NZE |
| Tapir | 1.5.9 |
| OS | Windows 11 |

**Summary**

`CreateKeynoteFolders` ends the Archicad process when it is sent an empty `key`. The HTTP
connection is reset part way through the call, nothing is returned, no dialog appears, and
the process is gone. Unsaved work is lost.

`key` and `title` are the only two required properties in the command's own `inputScheme`,
and neither carries a `minLength`, so a payload that satisfies the published schema is
enough to end the session.

**Minimal reproducer**

Against any open project:

```json
{
  "command": "API.ExecuteAddOnCommand",
  "parameters": {
    "addOnCommandId": {
      "commandNamespace": "TapirCommand",
      "commandName": "CreateKeynoteFolders"
    },
    "addOnCommandParameters": {
      "foldersData": [{ "key": "", "title": "" }]
    }
  }
}
```

Result: `ConnectionResetError: [WinError 10054] An existing connection was forcibly closed
by the remote host`, and the Archicad process has exited.

**What was ruled out**

This was reached three times, and the first two were not conclusive, so the checks are
worth stating:

- The project was healthy immediately before the call. A snapshot taken in the same run
  read 3 storeys, 20 walls, 1 slab, 88 objects, 38 texts, 27 labels and 2 roofs.
- The call was reached. The run printed its "firing" line and died inside the function that
  posts the command, not in setup.
- It is not a connection that was already failing. Earlier runs in the same session sent
  over a hundred commands to the same seat and got structured answers, including many
  error responses.
- A second Archicad instance was open on another port throughout, holding a different
  project. It was unaffected, so this is the calling process only.

**Suggested fix**

Validate `key` before creating the folder and return an error, in the shape
`CreateKeynoteItems` already uses for an unusable key. A `minLength: 1` on `key` and
`title` in `inputScheme` would also stop the payload at schema validation, which is where
`CreateViewMapFolder` stops a comparable empty `folderName`, though that one enforces it in
the command rather than in the schema.

**How it was found**

Building a minimal schema-valid payload for every mutating command and firing it at a
scratch copy, to work out what each one does and refuses. Happy to run anything else you
want tested on 28/6003.

title: CreateLayoutSubset: success entries don't match the response schema, and includeToIDSequence is never applied
body:
Two problems in `DocumentCreationCommands.cpp` (at `1bde2f2`):

1. **Wrong success shape:** each created subset pushes `CreateSuccessfulExecutionResult()` (`{"success": true}`) into `navigatorItems`, but `GetRawResponseSchema` declares `navigatorItems` items as `#/NavigatorItemIdOrError`. Clients that validate responses raise *after* the subset was created (seen on 1.5.9: the subset is in the Layout Book, the call errors), and no caller ever gets the new subset's navigator item id. Returning the created subset's id would fix both.
2. **`includeToIDSequence` ignored:** it is declared in the input schema but `Execute` never reads it, so the flag has no effect. Every other boolean in that item (`continueNumbering`, `useUpperPrefix`, …) is read.

title: DeleteNavigatorItems fails on Project Map viewpoints (schedules): uses DeleteNavigatorView, which only handles View Map items
body:
What happens

DeleteNavigatorItems fails with -2130313115 / "Failed to delete navigator item." when the target is a schedule (ScheduleItem) in the Project Map. The same command succeeds on the corresponding view in the View Map.

Reproducible on Archicad 29, Tapir 1.5.9, on any schedule viewpoint in the Project Map.

Why, from the source

In DeleteNavigatorItemsCommand::Execute (NavigatorCommands.cpp), layouts get ACAPI_Database_DeleteDatabase, subsets get an explicit APIERR_NOTSUPPORTED, and everything else falls through to:


err = ACAPI_Navigator_DeleteNavigatorView (&guid, &silentMode);
Per Graphisoft's documentation, that function deletes View Map views only. A Project Map viewpoint is not a view, so the call fails. ACAPI_Database_DeleteDatabase is not an alternative either: it is documented as accepting only "independent detail, worksheet, layout, or master layout".

Suggested fix

Archicad exposes ACAPI_Navigator_DeleteNavigatorVPItem (const API_Guid* guid), documented as removing a viewpoint item (root, group or leaf) from the Project Map. Branching on navItem.mapId == API_ProjectMap (or on the viewpoint item types) to call it would cover this case.

One open question I could not verify without the DevKit: the documented APIERR_BADID return says "guid does not exist or is not an AddOn viewpoint", which may mean the function is limited to add-on-created viewpoints. Worth testing against a native schedule before committing to it. Note that the Archicad UI does delete these (Project Map context menu → Delete Schedule, and the Delete button in Scheme Settings), so some path exists.

Why it matters

Workflow: export Scheme Settings XML, edit, re-import (Archicad always creates a suffixed copy), then relink Drawings and clean up the old definition via the API. Everything else in that chain works through Tapir; only removing the superseded schedule from the Project Map has no API path, so the project accumulates a duplicate per edited schedule.
