title: ChangeSelectionOfElements reports success but selection is immediately cleared on Archicad 29
body:
## Summary

`ChangeSelectionOfElements` reports success for valid Wall elements, but the selection is sometimes immediately cleared. A following `GetSelectedElements` call returns an empty array.

## Environment

- OS: Windows
- Archicad: 29
- Tapir Add-On: 1.5.9
- JSON API endpoint: `http://127.0.0.1:19723`
- Active window: Floor Plan

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a project in Archicad 29.
2. Change the active Floor Plan story to story index `-2`.
3. Verify that two valid Wall elements are on the active story using `FilterElements` with `OnActualFloor`.
4. Call `TapirCommand.ChangeSelectionOfElements` with the two Wall GUIDs in `addElementsToSelection`.
5. The response contains `success: true` for both elements.
6. Wait approximately 500–800 ms and call `TapirCommand.GetSelectedElements`.

## Actual result

`GetSelectedElements` returns an empty list and Archicad shows no active selection, even though `ChangeSelectionOfElements` returned success for both walls.

Example response:

```json
{
  "executionResultsOfAddToSelection": [
    { "success": true },
    { "success": true }
  ],
  "executionResultsOfRemoveFromSelection": []
}
```

Immediate verification:

```json
{
  "activeStory": -2,
  "selectedCount": 0
}
```

## Expected result

The two walls remain selected and are returned by `GetSelectedElements`. If selection cannot be performed, `ChangeSelectionOfElements` should return an error instead of success.

## Additional observations

- Both GUIDs are valid and returned by `GetElementsByType` and `GetDetailsOfElements`.
- Both elements pass the `OnActualFloor` filter on story `-2`.
- `HighlightElements` works for the same two GUIDs.
- The problem is intermittent: during one test, with a different active story, the two GUIDs were returned by `GetSelectedElements`; after returning to story `-2`, the selection was again immediately cleared.
- No element deletion or modification is involved.

This may be related to changing the active Floor Plan story and then setting the selection, or to selection-state refresh in Archicad 29.

title: Issue bot: respond to follow-up comments on issues
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Before merging, set up these repository rulesets and confirm they are active.** `issue_comment` workflows run from `main` as soon as this lands. The rulesets are the only barrier that holds whatever a prompt-injected run does:
> - block direct pushes to `main`. `monthly_release.yml` ships HEAD of `main`, so this rule is load-bearing.
> - block force pushes and deletions on all branches
> - restrict tag creation
>
> Also accept the documented residuals (workflow header): a plain push onto another contributor's open PR branch stays possible, and the Claude OAuth token sits in the run's environment.

## Problem

`claude_issue_triage.yml` only triggered on `issues: [opened, labeled]`, and no workflow listens to `issue_comment`. A new comment or question on an issue never started a run.

## Change

- **Trigger.** Adds `issue_comment: [created]`. The `triage` and `fix` jobs gate on `opened`/`labeled`, so they are unaffected.
- **New `reply` job.** Runs for every human comment on an issue: not PR conversations, not bot comments, from **anyone**, with write access. It reads the whole thread and handles the newest comment. It also handles any earlier comment still unanswered, because a burst of comments collapses into one run. It then does one of four things:
  - **nothing**, for thanks or +1
  - **answer** in one short comment
  - **fix**
    - Reuses its own draft PR for the issue (a github-actions[bot] draft with `Fixes #<n>`, found in the live PR list, not search), or opens a new draft.
    - Every PR body carries `Fixes #<n>`.
    - While the `fix` job is working on the issue (the issue has `claude-fix` or was opened by a collaborator), it says so and does not fix. It treats that job as dead only after two hours with no outcome.
  - **close as already fixed**, only when it verifies this itself on `main`, with `gh issue close <n> --reason completed`
- **`fix` job.** Gets the same reuse check, so a later `claude-fix` label doesn't open a duplicate PR.
- **Concurrency.** Moves to job level:
  - `triage` and `fix` share `claude-issue-<n>`
  - `reply` uses `claude-issue-<n>-reply`
  - A comment, even a skipped bot comment, can't cancel a pending `claude-fix` run.
- **Hardening in both write jobs.**
  - `git push` is limited to `origin`.
  - `--disallowedTools` denies edits under `.git/`, `.github/`, `archicad-addon/Tools/` and `tools/`. The Claude Code harness enforces this, and it closes the `.git/hooks` / `.git/config` route to arbitrary code.

## Security trade-off (deliberate, maintainer's decision)

Comments bypass the `claude-fix` label gate. What bounds a run:
- `GITHUB_TOKEN` is scoped to this repository and has no `workflows` permission.
- Every push lands under this repository's rulesets.
- The bot's PRs are drafts authored by a bot, which `claude_auto_merge.yml` never merges.
- The edit denial above.

The workflow header says plainly that the tool allowlist on its own is not a security boundary. Cost is also open: any account can start 60-minute runs, one per issue at a time, in parallel across issues.

## Verification

- `actionlint` and a YAML parse pass on every commit.
- This can only be exercised after merge, because `issue_comment` runs from the default branch:
  - a question on a test issue gets one reply
  - "please fix" gets a draft PR with `Fixes #<n>` and a link comment
  - a comment on a PR skips the job
  - an attempted edit under `.git/` is denied

title: PR review: re-run on comments and pushes, resolve settled threads
body:
## Problem

`claude_pr_review.yml` re-ran on pushes (`synchronize`), but not on comments. Every run also started from scratch: it re-posted findings that were already open, and never resolved the threads it had opened once they were fixed.

## Change

**Triggers.** Besides `pull_request_target`, the review now also runs on:
- `issue_comment` (a PR conversation comment)
- `pull_request_review_comment` (a reply on a line)

Bot comments never trigger it, and neither do PRs opened by the automation itself. Drafts and closed PRs are skipped: a new first step reads the draft/open state and the base SHA from the API, because comment payloads don't carry them.

**Forks.** Line replies get no secrets on fork PRs, so that trigger only covers branches in this repo. On a fork, a conversation comment works. This is documented in the header.

**Concurrency.** A job-level group per PR: bursts of pushes and comments collapse into one review of the latest state, and a skipped bot event can't displace a pending one.

**Earlier review as input.** A shell step writes two files for the model:
- `.review-context/threads.json`: the threads this bot opened, with every reply
- `.review-context/trigger.json`: the push or comment that started the run

The model needs no GraphQL access of its own.

**Prompt.** A re-review:
- marks a thread settled when the diff fixes it, or when a reply shows against the code that it isn't a problem. A bare "fixed" is treated as a claim to check.
- doesn't re-post an open finding
- answers a question the triggering comment asked
- posts nothing when a comment brought nothing new
- ends its summary with `<!-- claude-review-resolve: PRRT_… -->`

**Resolving.** A final shell step parses that marker from this run's summary comment and resolves each listed thread via `resolveReviewThread`. It first checks that the thread is on this PR and that the bot started it, so no comment text can get anything else resolved.

**Permissions.** Adds `issues: read`, needed to read back the summary comment.

## Verification

- `actionlint` and a YAML parse pass.
- The thread `jq` filter and the marker parsing were checked locally against sample payloads, including the `none` case.
- `issue_comment` runs from the default branch, so the comment trigger and resolving can only be exercised after merge. Push-triggered re-reviews on this PR run the new file itself:

title: Edit property definitions and classifications in place (UpdatePropertyDefinitions extended, new Update/Import commands)
body:
Editing property definitions and classifications currently means exporting XML from Property Manager or Classification Manager, editing it, and importing it back. `UpdatePropertyDefinitions` (1.5.4) covers expressions and appending enum values. This PR covers the rest, **in place**: every edit reads the definition, patches only the fields sent, and calls `ACAPI_*_Change*`. GUIDs never change, so element values, classifications and availability links survive renames.

## Commands

**Extended**
- **`UpdatePropertyDefinitions`**: new optional fields `name`, `description`, `groupId` (move to another custom group), `defaultValue` (basic value or expressions; switching between the two is allowed), `availability` (`set`, or `add` / `remove`), `renameEnumValues` (by option guid, so stored values follow the new text), `removeEnumValues`, and `enumOrder` (every option's text, once). Applied in the order rename, remove, add, order, then the default, so a new default can name a renamed or added option. Existing requests (`expressions`, `possibleEnumValues`) behave as before.
- **`GetAllProperties`**: each property also reports `propertyGroupId` and `propertyDescription`. Custom properties also get `availability`, `defaultValueDisplay`, and `defaultEnumValueIds` (the option guids an enum default holds). A top-level `propertyGroups` lists every group, including empty ones.

**New** (registered as 1.5.10)
- **`UpdatePropertyGroups`**: name / description of custom groups.
- **`UpdateClassificationSystems`**: name, description, source, version, date.
- **`UpdateClassificationItems`**: id (code), name, description. There is no parent field in `API_ClassificationItem`, so moving an item is not offered.
- **`ImportPropertiesXml`** / **`ImportClassificationsXml`**: wrap `ACAPI_Property_Import` / `ACAPI_Classification_Import` with the conflict policies exposed. Those calls return only an error code, so the commands compare guids before and after, and return `created` and `removed`.

## Guard rails
- Built-in properties and groups are refused.
- Each batch runs in one `ACAPI_CallUndoableCommand`, so one undo reverts it.
- A failing item fails alone; the rest of the batch still runs.
- Removing the option that is (part of) the default is refused unless the same item sends a new `defaultValue`. Archicad would otherwise answer `APIERR_BADVALUE`.
- `DescribeDefinitionChangeError` (CommandBase) turns the documented `Change*` errors into plain text, for example `APIERR_NOACCESSRIGHT` for missing Teamwork rights.

## Refactor
- The default-value parsing of `CreatePropertyDefinitions` moved into `ParseDefaultValue`, shared with `UpdatePropertyDefinitions`.
- One behaviour change: the C++ now takes the collection type from the definition and ignores the basic default's `type` field. The input schema still requires `type`, so callers must keep sending it.

## Verified (AC29, macOS, live)
- Built for **AC29 only** (DevKit 29.3000). AC25 to AC28 have not been compiled here. The classification date code copies the existing `ServerMainVers_2900` split from `CreateClassificationSystems`.
- All four new examples ran against a live project and printed the expected results:
  - property and option guids are kept through rename, regroup, enum rename, remove and reorder
  - removing the default option alone is refused
  - system and item guids are kept through a rename and a code change
  - an import created one property
- Found along the way:
  - Removing an enum option leaves elements that held it at `<Undefined>`. They do not fall back to the default.
  - `ImportPropertiesXml` with `replace` keeps the property's guid and updates it in place.
- Docs: `docs/archicad-addon/*.js` were generated with `GenerateDocumentation`, then limited to this PR's commands and the `PropertyDetails` schema. The docs on `main` currently lag several merged commands (keynotes, IFC export translators, `SaveProjectAsArchive`, and others), and those are left for a full regeneration.

## For a maintainer with a live seat
1. Build AC25 to AC28.
2. Run `test_examples.py`. The new examples create and delete their own groups, properties and classification systems, so they pin their output on first run. The golden output of `get_all_properties.py` **will** change: the response gains the new fields, and the example prints three extra lines.
3. Teamwork: whether definition edits need anything beyond the user's rights has not been tried on a Teamwork project.

title: Issue bot: fix every new issue without the claude-fix label
body:
## Problem

#698 removed the `claude-fix` requirement for **comments**. A **newly opened** issue from someone without write access still went to the read-only `triage` job, which ends by asking a maintainer to apply `claude-fix` before any PR is written. The maintainer asked for no label to be needed for write access.

## Change

- **Removes the `triage` job.**
- **`fix` runs on every newly opened issue, from anyone.** It now sets `allowed_non_write_users: "*"`.
  - Its prompt answers questions and feature requests in one comment.
  - It closes an issue only when it has verified on `main` that it is already fixed. It uses `gh issue close <n> --reason …`, and that pinned command is added to its allowlist.
  - Otherwise it opens the fix as a draft PR on `claude/issue-<n>-…`, as before.
- **Applying `claude-fix` still re-runs `fix`** on an existing issue, as a manual trigger.
- **`reply`'s wait for an in-progress fix** now applies to every newly opened issue, not just labelled or collaborator-opened ones. It no longer needs the author-association input.
- **The header** now describes the label-free design. The existing hardening is unchanged: pushes only to `origin claude/…`, the edit denial under `.git/`, `.github/` and the tooling folders, and the rulesets requirement. The cost note now says that opening an issue also starts a run.

The fix prompt's existing rule is kept: if a fix is large, ambiguous in design, or touches the crash-sensitive element creation paths, the bot describes it in a comment instead of opening a PR.

## Verification

- `actionlint` and a YAML parse pass. The two jobs' `if` conditions don't overlap: `fix` runs only on `issues` events, `reply` only on `issue_comment` events.
- This can only be exercised after merge, because `issues` events run from the default branch:
  - an issue opened by a non-collaborator gets an answer or a draft PR with no label
  - `claude-fix` on an old issue re-runs `fix`

Fixes #701.

The `hotlinkId` field in `GetDetailsOfElements` is documented as `ElementId` (`{ "guid": ... }`). The implementation built it with `CreateElementIdObjectState`, so it actually returned `{ "elementId": { "guid": ... } }`, which is the `ElementIdArrayItem` shape.

title: Grasshopper: sync components with the add-on commands
body:
## Problem

The add-on gained commands and changed schemas that have no matching Grasshopper components yet, mostly through #702, plus the beam and drawing changes since 1.5.9.

## New components

| Component | Inputs → JSON | Outputs |
|---|---|---|
| **UpdatePropertyGroups** | `PropertyGroupGuids` → `propertyGroupId`, optional `Names`, `Descriptions` | `ErrorMessages` |
| **UpdateClassificationSystems** | `ClassificationSystemGuids`, optional `Names`, `Descriptions`, `Sources`, `Versions`, `Dates` | `ErrorMessages` |
| **UpdateClassificationItems** | `ClassificationItemGuids`, optional `Ids`, `Names`, `Descriptions` | `ErrorMessages` |
| **ImportPropertiesXml** | `Xml` (content), `ConflictPolicy` (default `append`) | `CreatedPropertyGuids`, `RemovedPropertyGuids`, `Message` |
| **ImportClassificationsXml** | `Xml`, `SystemConflictPolicy` (default `merge`), `ItemConflictPolicy` (default `skip`) | `CreatedGuids`, `RemovedGuids`, `Message` |

In the update components, each optional input takes 0, 1 or N items. A field that isn't given is left out of the request, so the add-on keeps its current value.

## Updated components

Existing inputs and outputs keep their order. New ones are only appended, so saved definitions keep their bindings.

- **UpdatePropertyDefinitions**
  - New optional inputs: `Names`, `Descriptions`, `GroupGuids`, `DefaultValues` (JSON), availability `Set`/`Add`/`Remove` trees, and enum trees to add, rename, remove and order options.
  - `Expressions` is now optional.
- **GetAllProperties**
  - New per-property outputs: `PropertyGroupIds`, `Descriptions`, `DefaultValues`.
  - New trees: availability guids, enum option guids and texts, default enum ids.
  - New list of every property group: ids, names, descriptions, custom flags.
- **CreateDrawings:** optional `NameTypes`, `Angles`, `DrawingScales`, `ModelOffsets`. `Names` is now optional.
- **CreateBeams:** optional `CircleBased`.
  - It comes after the metadata toggles, through a new `TrailingFields` hook on `CreateElementsComponentBase`, so their input indices don't move.
  - The switch that creates the inputs moved into `AddFieldInput`, with no change in behaviour.

## Checked and unchanged

- **CreateLayoutSubset:** already reads the corrected response shape.
- **`sourceGuid`:** the navigator-tree components use Archicad's official `GetNavigatorItemTree`, and already output `SourceIds`.
- **`isCutWithFrame`:** no component sends Drawing details.
- **`hotlinkId`:** nothing in the plugin reads it.
- **Deliberately out of scope:** the notification-client, script-UI and `GenerateDocumentation` developer commands, which never had components.

## Known limits

- An empty availability or enum branch can't be sent, so the "clear all availability" case isn't expressible.
- The five new icons are composites of existing icons.

## Verification

- `dotnet build … -f net7.0 -p:EnableWindowsTargeting=true` gives 0 warnings and 0 errors. It also compiles with `LangVersion=7.3`, the C# version the net48 target uses.
- The net48 and net7.0-windows targets need Windows. The Grasshopper build check on this PR covers them.

title: Generate the Add-On docs without Archicad and regenerate them in the monthly release

## Summary

- **New `tools/generate_addon_docs.py`.** It writes the same `docs/archicad-addon/command_definitions.js` and `common_schema_definitions.js` as the `GenerateDocumentation` developer command, without needing Archicad.
  - It reads the command groups and `RegisterCommand<>` calls from `AddOnMain.cpp`, then each command's name and schema functions, following the class hierarchy like the virtual calls do. The common schemas come from `CommonSchemaDefinitions.json`.
  - A small interpreter evaluates the schema code, which is mostly plain literals. It covers named constants, `GS::UniString::Printf`, `+`/`+=`, `if` on bool parameters, static helper calls (for example `BuildLibraryPartBasedSchema`) and `OtherCommand ().GetRawResponseSchema ()`.

- **Validation:** the output is byte-identical to the committed, Archicad-generated docs for every command whose sources haven't changed since the last regeneration. That includes the Object/Lamp schemas that are built at runtime.
- **`monthly_release.yml`:** the step that failed on stale docs now regenerates the docs, commits them and pushes to `main` before tagging.

title: Resync the Grasshopper components with the Tapir commands
body:
## Summary

This PR comes from an audit of every Grasshopper component against the input and response schemas of the Tapir command it calls. The audit compared the JSON the components actually serialize (the plugin's `Types` classes loaded by reflection from the built assembly) against `docs/archicad-addon`.

The built-in script windows that were briefly part of this PR moved to their own pull request, on branch `claude/builtin-scripts-windows`.

### Fixes
- **Unset optional inputs no longer break Tapir commands.** Archicad validates the parameters against the command's input schema, and no Tapir schema accepts `null`. The plugin serializes its parameter objects with `JObject.FromObject`, which writes every unset field as `null`, so the whole command failed. `ArchicadConnection.SendAddOnCommand` now removes null properties at every depth before sending. Confirmed broken cases this fixes:
  - `SetStories`: the `height` field added to `StoryData` on 2026-09-17 for GetStories was sent as `null`.
  - `SetProjectInfoField`: sent `projectInfoName: null`.
  - `SetClassificationsOfElements`: unclassifying sent `classificationItemId: null`. The schema says to omit the key instead.
  - The same applies to any other component with optional inputs left unset.
- **Add-On schema bug in `MoveDesignOptionsToAnotherSet`.** The item schema required `elementId`, but it defines and the command reads `designOptionId`, so every valid call failed validation. The docs are regenerated.

### New and extended components
- **`DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItems`** (Library group). It was the only user-facing Tapir command without a component. Its icon is a copy of the AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary image, used as a placeholder.
- **`AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary`:** new `OverwriteExisting` input. It is only sent when true, so older Add-Ons still accept the call.
- **`CreateIssue`:** new optional `ParentIssueGuid` and `TagText` inputs. A wired ParentIssueGuid that is not an issue identifier is reported as an error instead of silently creating a top-level issue.
- **`AddCommentToIssue`:** new optional `Status` input (Error / Warning / Info / Unknown).
- New inputs are added after the existing ones, so saved definitions keep their wiring.

### Not changed on purpose
- `CreateViewMapFolder`, `MoveNavigatorItem` and `RenameNavigatorItem` call Archicad's own `API.*` commands, not the Tapir commands of the same name, and their payloads match those commands.
- The remaining schema gaps are deep options the components never exposed. Examples: text and label styling, most of the new `Modify*` detail fields, the SetDetailsOfElements type-specific settings, and `circleBased`/`isSlanted` on Create/Modify Columns and Beams. Exposing them is a UI design decision for follow-ups, not drift in existing behaviour.
- `SetElementNotificationClient`, `RemoveElementNotificationClient`, `ShowScriptUI`, `GetScriptUIResult` and `GenerateDocumentation` are internal or developer commands with no component.
- Two response-only schemas require keys they don't define: `CurtainWallDetails` (`begCoordinate`) and `RevisionChangesArrayItem`. Response schemas are documentation only, not validated, so these are not touched here.

## Testing
- `dotnet build -f net7.0` succeeds on Linux. `net48` and `net7.0-windows` need the Windows Desktop SDK and are covered by the Grasshopper build check.
- I ran `RemoveNullProperties` on the real `StoryData` and `ProjectInfoField` payloads and on a nested anonymous object. The nulls are removed and the real values are kept.
- `python3 tools/generate_addon_docs.py --check` reports the docs as up to date.
- Nothing here has been tested against a running Archicad.

title: Give every built-in script a proper window
body:
## Summary

These changes were split out of #708.

- **Shared window and connection code.** All three built-in scripts now use one window layout, `utilities/ui.py`: a header explaining the script, the body, a status line, a "Keep on top" switch and the action buttons. It uses tkinter/ttk only, so no extra packages are needed.

  - Failures are shown in the window instead of killing it.
- **UnusedViewCleaner** had no UI and moved views as soon as it started.
  - It now analyzes first. It shows counts (views in the View Map, placed on layouts, in Publisher Sets, unused) and the unused views in their folder structure, with a check mark per view.
  - Clicking a line includes or excludes it. The target folder name can be edited. Only the checked views are moved, after a confirmation.
  - Clone folders that are only partly unused are shown but locked.
  - Folders that already exist under the same parent are reused at every level, so moving in several batches fills one folder tree instead of creating duplicates. The window re-analyzes after every move, and views already in the target folder are not listed again.
  - The `multiconn` dependency is gone.
- **AutomaticNumberingBasedOnPolyline** replaces its popups with a window.
  - It shows what was found in the selection and previews the new Element IDs, in order, next to the current ones.
  - New options: prefix, suffix, number of digits, and numbering from the other end of the polyline.
  - Elements without a 3D extent, and elements whose details cannot be read, are reported as skipped.
  - After a partial failure, only the elements that were actually renumbered show their new ID.
  - The `archicad` package dependency is gone.
- **OrthoWallFinder** gets the same look, plus:
  - a list of the faulty walls with story, angle and deviation, largest deviation first;
  - a choice of allowed angle step (90/45/30/15°; 45° is the default, as before);

- Each script ran under Xvfb (Python 3.12, Tk 8.6) against a mock Archicad JSON server. The main actions were driven and the windows screenshotted.

title: Compare Add-On versions numerically and bump to 1.6.0
body:
## Problem
`VersionChecker::IsUsingLatestVersion` compared the latest GitHub release tag with `ADDON_VERSION` as strings (`latestVersion <= ADDON_VERSION`). So `"1.5.10" <= "1.5.9"` is true, and anyone on 1.5.9 would never be told about 1.5.10 (or any later `x.y.10+` / `x.10+` version).

## Changes
- **`VersionChecker.cpp`**: parse both versions into numeric components (a leading `v` is ignored, missing parts count as 0) and compare the numbers. If the latest version can't be parsed, for example because the GitHub request failed and left it empty, it still counts as "up to date", as before.
- **Version bump to 1.6.0**: 1.5.10 was never released (the latest release is 1.5.9), so the next release is 1.6.0. The version files were updated with `tools/update_version.py`. The commands registered as introduced in `"1.5.10"` in `AddOnMain.cpp` now say `"1.6.0"`, and `docs/archicad-addon` was regenerated with `tools/generate_addon_docs.py`; the only change there is those 8 version strings.
- Because of the old bug, 1.5.9 installs only offer the update if `"1.6.0"` is also greater than `"1.5.9"` as a string. It is, so 1.5.9 users will be told about this release.

## Other places checked
There were no other version comparisons. The installer (`tapir_installer.py`) always installs the latest release's asset without comparing versions. `update_addon_and_restart_archicad.py` only calls `GetAddOnVersion` to check whether Archicad is still running. The workflow bump splits the version into integers.

## Testing
I compiled the comparison logic on its own and tested it: `1.5.9<=1.5.10` ✔, `1.5.10<=1.5.9` ✘, `1.6.0<=1.5.10` ✘, equal versions ✔, empty ✔, `v1.6.0<=1.6.0` ✔, `1.10.0<=1.9.9` ✘, `2.0<=1.9.9` ✘. The full Add-On build is left to CI.

title: SetGDLParametersOfElements: size objects in the unit Archicad stores
body:
## Problem

After every write, `SetGDLParametersOfElements` sets `element.object.xRatio = getParams.a` and `element.object.yRatio = getParams.b` for Objects and Lamps. What those two fields hold depends on the element's `useXYFixSize` (reported as `useFixSize` by `GetDetailsOfElements`):

- **on**: the placed size in metres.
- **off**: the placed size divided by the library part's own A and B, as `APIdefs_Elements.h` documents for `API_ObjectType::xRatio`.

Objects placed in Archicad carry it on (100 of 100 sampled in a production project). Objects placed through the API take it from the Object tool defaults, where it can be off; `CreateObjects` copies it unless the request sets `useFixSize`.

With `useXYFixSize` off the parameter interface mixes two units: `getParams.a/b` and a written A or B are in the stored unit, while the parameter list and whatever the Parameter Script sets are in metres. Two things go wrong:

1. **A written A or B lands multiplied by the library part's A or B.** `ChangeAParameter` reads the written value as a ratio.
2. **An A or B set by the Parameter Script is copied back in metres.** After the script changes A, `getParams.a` holds metres, and the command writes that into `xRatio`. An object whose script derives A (a path object setting A to its length) grows by the library A on every write, even a write that does not name A.

Writes that leave A and B alone are fine, and so is everything with `useXYFixSize` on.

Measured live on Archicad 29 build 5101 and Archicad 27 build 6080 (Tapir 1.5.10 fork build and 1.5.9; identical code for this command). Behaviour is the same in both versions:

| Library part (own A x B) | `useFixSize` | Action | Before this PR | After this PR (AC27) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Office Cabinet (0.8 x 0.6), placed with `dimensions` 0.8 x 0.6 | on | write `A = 0.9` | 0.9 | 0.9 |
| same | off (placed at 0.64 x 0.36) | write `A = 0.9` | **0.72** | 0.9 |
| same | off | write `B = 0.5` | not run | 0.5 |
| same | off | write A and B together (1.1, 0.45) | not run | 1.1 x 0.45 |
| Probe block, no Parameter Script (0.6 x 0.4) | off | write `A = 1.0` | **0.6** | 1.0 |
| Probe, Parameter Script `PARAMETERS A = len` (0.6 x 0.4) | off | write `len = 1.2`, then `1.5` | not run | A = 1.2, then 1.5 |
| Probe, Parameter Script `PARAMETERS B = A` (0.6 x 0.4) | off | write `A = 0.5` | not run | A = B = 0.5 |
| Path object deriving A from its nodes (library A = 3 m) | off | any write | **length x 3 per write** | not run (same path as the `len` probe) |
| Any of the above | either | write an unrelated parameter, twice | unchanged | unchanged |

In every row the 3D bounding box matches the A and B that read back.

Doors and windows are not affected: `openingBase.width/height` hold metres, and unrelated, A and B writes all landed exactly on the default Door and Window in both versions. Skylights share the struct but were not placed (no command creates them).

### How the units were pinned down

A probe part with `PARAMETERS B = A`, placed so that `xRatio`, `yRatio`, A / library A and B / library B all differed, showed that `getParams.b` right after `ACAPI_LibraryPart_OpenParameters` is B divided by the library part's B, not the stored `yRatio`. An unrelated write therefore brings a stale stored size back in line with A and B (which is what an edit in Archicad does too); that behaviour is kept. A first version of this fix that only converted the final A/B still failed direct A writes, which showed that `ChangeAParameter` reads a written A in the stored unit as well.

## Fix

When the parameters are opened, take the scale between the stored unit and metres from `getParams.a / A` and `getParams.b / B`, with A and B from the parameter list (Objects and Lamps only).

- A written A or B is multiplied by the scale before `ACAPI_LibraryPart_ChangeAParameter`.
- After the writes, `xRatio/yRatio` = the parameter list's A/B times the scale.
- `useXYFixSize` on: the scale is 1, so nothing changes.
- A or B missing or 0: `getParams.a/b` are used as before.
- Doors, windows, skylights: unchanged.

## Test

New example `Examples/set_gdl_parameters_object_size.py`. For `useFixSize` off and then on, it places `Chair 01` (as `create_elements.py` does), lets one write bring the size in line with A and B, writes an unrelated parameter twice, writes A and B, writes them again, then deletes the chair.

| | useFixSize | Unrelated writes keep the size | A and B read back as written | Second identical write keeps the size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before (AC29) | off | True | **False** | True |
| Before (AC29) | on | True | True | True |
| After (AC27) | off | True | True | True |
| After (AC27) | on | True | True | True |

The fixed build was run on Archicad 27 only. On Archicad 29 the same states give the same results with the old code, so the fix follows the same path there; I did not install it into Archicad 29.

No `ExpectedOutputs` file: I could not run the example against `TestProject.pla`, and `test_examples.py` writes it on the first run.

## Related, not changed here

- `CreateObjects` / `ModifyObjects` write `dimensions` straight into `xRatio/yRatio`, so with `useFixSize` off an object comes out at `dimensions` times the library part's A/B (Office Cabinet 0.8 x 0.6 placed at 0.8 x 0.6 gives 0.64 x 0.36). Passing `useFixSize: true` places the exact size.
- `GetDetailsOfElements` reports `xRatio/yRatio` as `dimensions`, so with `useFixSize` off they are ratios, not metres (a 0.3 x 0.02 m junction box reads 3 x 0.4).
- `CreateObjects` without `dimensions` places the Object tool's current default size, not the library part's own.

title: CreateObjects/ModifyObjects: place 'dimensions' in the unit Archicad stores
body:
## Problem

Follow-up to #718, for `CreateObjects`, `ModifyObjects`, `CreateLamps` and `ModifyLamps`. Two things go wrong when the placed element has `useXYFixSize` off. API-placed objects take that flag from the Object tool defaults unless the request sets `useFixSize`.

1. **`dimensions` go into `xRatio/yRatio` as they are.** With the flag off those hold the size divided by the library part's own A and B, so the object comes out at `dimensions` times the library part's A/B.
2. **The parameter memo keeps the Object tool default's A and B.** `CreateObjects` starts from `ACAPI_Element_GetDefaults`, so the new element's memo carries the tool's A and B (A = 3, B = 0.2 in the test file), not the size it was given. `ModifyObjects` passes that memo back on every change, and Archicad reconciles it with `xRatio/yRatio`. A `dimensions` change comes out squared: (requested x library A)² on the current code (table below). With the conversion of point 1 alone, it is the requested size squared, so asking a 0.8 x 0.6 cabinet for the size it already had gave 0.64 x 0.36. A change of only the angle snapped a 0.8 x 0.6 cabinet to 3 x 0.2.

With the flag on, both commands are already correct: Archicad brings the memo back in line with `xRatio/yRatio` by itself.

Measured on Office Cabinet (own A x B = 0.8 x 0.6), `useFixSize` off, Archicad 29 build 5101, current code:

| Request | Placed A x B |
|---|---|
| `CreateObjects` with `dimensions` 0.8 x 0.6 | 0.64 x 0.36 |
| then `ModifyObjects` to 1.0 x 0.5 | 0.64 x 0.09 |
| or `ModifyObjects` to 0.6 x 0.9 | 0.2304 x 0.2916 |

The 0.64 x 0.36 same-size result and the 3 x 0.2 snap were measured on Archicad 27 with only the first commit of this PR applied (converted `xRatio`, memo untouched). The example below shows the angle-only failure on the current code too.

## Fix

- `dimensions.x/y` are divided by the library part's own A and B (`ACAPI_LibraryPart_GetParams`) when the element ends up with `useXYFixSize` off. That is the request's `useFixSize` if it has one, otherwise the element's current flag, which for `CreateObjects` is the tool default's.
- A and B in metres are written into the parameter memo next to ZZYZX, so the memo and `xRatio/yRatio` agree after create and after modify.
- With the flag on, `xRatio/yRatio` are unchanged; the memo's A and B now hold the same size too.
- A library part A or B of 0 leaves that value undivided.

How the memo was found: an instrumented build reported `ACAPI_Element_GetMemo` returning A = 3, B = 0.2 on a freshly created 0.8 x 0.6 cabinet. All the other routes it tried landed exactly: writing the target A/B into the memo (with or without the `xRatio` mask), skipping the memo, or going through `ACAPI_LibraryPart_OpenParameters`. This PR writes the target A/B into the memo and keeps the `xRatio` mask, because it applies ZZYZX in the same change and keeps both channels in agreement.

## Test

New example `Examples/create_objects_dimensions.py`. For `useFixSize` off and then on, it places `Chair 01` with `dimensions` 0.55 x 0.55, changes only its angle, changes its `dimensions` to 0.65 x 0.65, and checks A and B each time. Then it deletes the chair. Chair 01 keeps A = B, hence the square sizes.

| | useFixSize | CreateObjects places A and B as given | Angle-only ModifyObjects keeps A and B | ModifyObjects sets A and B as given |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before (AC29) | off | **False** | **False** | **False** |
| Before (AC29) | on | True | True | True |
| After (AC27) | off | True | True | True |
| After (AC27) | on | True | True | True |

Also checked on Archicad 27 with the fix, on Office Cabinet 27 with the flag off and on: create 1.0 x 0.45 x 1.8, modify to 1.2 x 0.5 x 2.0, modify to the same size, modify only the angle, modify only the pen, then `SetGDLParametersOfElements` on an unrelated parameter and on `A = 0.9`. Every step read back exactly, and the 3D bounding box matched.

The fix was built and run on Archicad 27 only, together with #718. I did not install it into Archicad 29. Lamps share the code but were not placed. `test_object_lamp_full_support.py` places with `useFixSize: true`, where `xRatio` stays the given size, so its checks are unaffected. No `ExpectedOutputs` file, as in #718.

## Related, not changed here

- `CreateObjects` without `dimensions` still leaves the tool default's A and B in the memo. I did not check whether a later `ModifyObjects` resizes such an object.
- `GetDetailsOfElements` still reports `xRatio/yRatio` as `dimensions`, so with the flag off they are ratios, not metres.

title: GetDetailsOfElements: report object 'dimensions' in metres
body:
**Merge together with or after #719.** On its own this PR already makes `dimensions` match A and B, but the round trip into `CreateObjects`/`ModifyObjects` is only exact once #719 converts `dimensions` on the way in.

## Problem

`GetDetailsOfElements` reports an Object's or Lamp's `dimensions.x/y` as `xRatio/yRatio` exactly as stored. Those hold the placed size only when the element's `useXYFixSize` is on. With it off, they hold the size divided by the library part's own A and B (see #718), so the reported `dimensions` are ratios, not metres. For example, a 0.3 x 0.02 m junction box read 3 x 0.4.

This also breaks the round trip the schema promises (`ObjectDetails` is "the same shape CreateObjects/CreateLamps/ModifyObjects/ModifyLamps accept back"). #719 makes those commands take `dimensions` in metres for both flag settings, so feeding them the ratios read here would resize the object.

## Fix

With `useXYFixSize` off, `dimensions.x/y` are `xRatio/yRatio` multiplied by the library part's own A and B (`ACAPI_LibraryPart_GetParams`), so they match the object's GDL A and B. With it on, nothing changes. A failed lookup, or a library part A or B of 0, leaves the stored value, the same way the other library part reads in this function ignore a failed lookup. `z` (ZZYZX) is unchanged.

## Test

New example `Examples/get_details_object_dimensions.py`. For `useFixSize` off and then on, it places `Chair 01` with `dimensions` 0.55 x 0.55 and checks that `GetDetailsOfElements` reports the same x and y as the GDL parameters A and B. Then it deletes the chair.

| | useFixSize | dimensions x and y equal A and B |
|---|---|---|
| Before (Archicad 29 build 5101) | off | **False** |
| Before (Archicad 29) | on | True |
| After (Archicad 27 build 6080) | off | True |
| After (Archicad 27) | on | True |

Also checked on Archicad 27 in a build that carries #718, #719 and this PR, on Office Cabinet 27 (own A x B 0.8 x 0.6):

| useFixSize | Placed | `dimensions` reported | After `ModifyObjects` with those `dimensions` |
|---|---|---|---|
| off | 1.0 x 0.45 x 1.8 | 1.0 x 0.45 x 1.8 | 1.0 x 0.45 x 1.8 |
| on | 1.0 x 0.45 x 1.8 | 1.0 x 0.45 x 1.8 | 1.0 x 0.45 x 1.8 |
| off, placed without `dimensions` | A x B = 2.4 x 0.12 | 2.4 x 0.12 (the stored ratios are 3 x 0.2) | not run |

The examples of #718 and #719 also pass on that build. I did not install it into Archicad 29.

The golden `Test/ExpectedOutputs/get_and_set_details_of_elements.py.output` lists `dimensions` for curtain-wall frames and panels reported as Objects. That file predates the full object details (it has no `useFixSize`), so I can't tell whether those values change; whoever regenerates it should compare them with A and B.

## Related, not changed here

- `ModifyObjects` that sends only `useFixSize: true` for an object that has it off reinterprets the stored ratio as metres: a 1.0 x 0.45 cabinet became 1.25 x 0.75. Turning it off the same way left the size unchanged. The review of #719 predicted this.
- `z` still comes from the memo's `ZZYZX` (uppercase only). On an object placed without `dimensions` it read 0.2 while the GDL `ZZYZX` read 0.6, because the memo keeps the Object tool default's values (the case #719 lists as not changed).

title: MEP: expose pipe preference table, story visibility, system material and preference tables (AC29 C++ API)
body:
We drive Archicad 29 + MEP Designer 29 from Python via Tapir 1.6.0 to produce plumbing/heating drawing sets from a template.
Four gaps force manual GUI steps on every project; all four are available in the AC29 C++ MEP API:

1. `CreateMEPRoutingElements` / `ModifyMEPRoutingElements`: accept the preference table of segments, elbows and tees
   (`RoutingSegment::Modifier::SetPreferenceTableId`). Today `crossSectionReferenceId` is refused on Modify, so we delete and recreate routes.
2. Same commands: accept the "Show on Stories" setting (e.g. Home Story Only). Routes are created with All Relevant Stories,
   so pipes below level 0 disappear from floor plans when a basement exists.
3. `CreateMEPSystems` (and a Get/Set for existing systems): `materialId` / `insulationMaterialId` (`API_MEPSystemType.materialInd`),
   so 3D surfaces follow the system colour.
4. New command `SetMEPPreferenceTables` (and Get): create/modify route specification tables (pipe DN -> outer diameter/wall)
   so a template can carry local pipe series (PEX-AL, PPR PN20, PP-HT EN 1451) without the GUI.

Environment: Archicad 29 INT, MEP Designer 29, Tapir 1.6.0, Windows 11. Happy to test builds.

title: Installer: fix SSL certificate error on macOS, show Tapir logo
body:
## SSL fix
On macOS the installer failed with `Failed to get the latest Tapir release from GitHub: <urlopen error [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] ... unable to get local issuer certificate>`.

The PyInstaller-bundled Python has its own OpenSSL. That OpenSSL doesn't read the macOS Keychain and has no CA bundle, so every HTTPS request failed. All requests now go through one `UrlOpen` helper. It checks certificates using, in order:
1. **`truststore`**, which uses the OS trust store (macOS Keychain / Windows cert store). This also accepts corporate TLS-inspection root CAs.
2. **`certifi`**, the Mozilla CA bundle.
3. OpenSSL defaults, which is the old behaviour.

Both packages are now installed next to PyInstaller in `archicad_addon.yml` and `installer_build_check.yml`, so they are bundled into the executables. Running from source still needs only the standard library. README updated.

Tested in a TLS-inspecting proxy environment: plain stdlib fails with the same `CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED` error. With `truststore` installed, the `--console --dryRun` run finds release 1.6.0.

## Logo
The installer window now shows the Tapir logo next to the title. It is the black logo on a light disc, so it shows up on both light and dark (macOS dark mode) backgrounds. It is embedded as a base64 80×80 PNG, so no extra files or `--add-data` are needed. If Tk can't load PNGs, the window still opens without the logo. I checked it renders with Tk 8.6 under Xvfb.

author: tlorantfy

title: Monthly release: one-week guard and a Discord announcement
body:
Two additions to the monthly release workflow.

A release that went out less than a week ago now suppresses the scheduled one, so the 1st-of-the-month run cannot cut a second release days after a manual or hotfix release. The age comes from the published release's publish time via the API, falling back to the tagged commit's date for a tag with no release behind it. The guard is checked after the "nothing changed" test, so the more informative summary wins when both apply, and it does not apply when resuming an already tagged release. A new allow_early_release dispatch input overrides it.

After publishing, the run announces the release in the project's Discord channel with the DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN secret the Discord Issue Bot already uses, through urllib so the release path gains no pip step. The step is continue-on-error: the release is already published by then, so a Discord outage or a revoked token must not block the version bump that follows. A resumed run checks the channel's recent messages for the release URL before posting, so a release is announced once. Without the secret the step is a no-op with a warning.

The header, the dry-run summary and the dispatch inputs are updated to match. The YAML parses and both embedded Python blocks compile; the channel id is taken as given and has not been checked against Discord.
author: tlorantfy

title: Monthly release: fall back on a gh api error, and a real party popper
body:
Two findings from the review of #726.

On a 404, gh api copies the raw error body to stdout instead of applying the --jq filter, so the published-time lookup left LAST_RELEASE_AT holding '{"message":"Not Found",...}' rather than nothing: the commit-date fallback never ran, and date -d then failed the plan step under set -e for exactly the tag-without-a-release case the fallback exists for. The lookup now branches on gh api's exit status, and only an empty result falls through to the tagged commit's date.

Discord expands :tada: only in the client's input box, not in content posted through the API, so the announcement would have shown the literal shortcode. The message now carries the character itself.

title: `CreateMorphs` with `size`: every face gets the building material index as its surface override (wrong surface in 3D)
body:
First, thank you for this awesome project. It really helped a lot in planning with Archicad via Claude and ChatGPT. I am currently using it daily (will become less when the house's planning comes to a close). I stumbled upon this issue when trying to do electric planning in Archicad via Beams and Morphs for cables (which is probably not what a pro would do, but it works for me..). The issue took a while to work around for me and the following description is from Claude, so feel free to remove this issue if you don't accept robotic issues here:

When a Morph is created with `CreateMorphs` and `size` (the simple box), each of its faces gets a custom surface override. The index of that override is the Morph's **building material index**, but it is read as a **surface index**. In 3D, Archicad therefore shows whichever surface happens to have that index, not the Morph's `surfaceId`. The Morph Settings dialog warns under *Override Surface*: "One or more faces of the selected Morph have a custom parameter setting that differs from the Morph's overall parameters".

### Environment

- Archicad 29, Windows 11
- Tapir 1.5.9 (observed live). The code is unchanged in 1.6.0 and current `main` (`eee7c60`).

### Steps to reproduce

```json
{"morphsData": [{
  "basePoint": {"x": 0, "y": 0, "z": 0},
  "size": {"x": 0.02, "y": 0.02, "z": 1.0},
  "buildingMaterialId": {"guid": "<building material with index 61>"},
  "surfaceId": {"guid": "<any surface, e.g. Paint - Cadmium Orange (index 77)>"}
}]}
```

Then read the element back with `GetDetailsOfElements`.

### Expected

The Morph shows its `surfaceId` (Paint - Cadmium Orange) on all faces. Its faces have no override, or an override equal to the Morph surface, which is the state of a box Morph modelled in Archicad itself.

### Actual

- `details.surfaceId` is correct (Paint - Cadmium Orange).
- Every entry in `details.body.polygons[].surfaceId` is the surface with **index 61** (in our project: *Brick - Red HerringBone*), because the building material has index 61.
- In 3D the Morph renders as brick.
- Without `buildingMaterialId`, the building material from the Morph tool defaults is used the same way. In our project that gave *Siding - Dark* on every face.

We hit this on 874 Morphs. The only fix in the UI is, per Morph, to toggle *Override Surface* and tick "Apply changes to custom faces/edges too".

### Root cause

In `BuildCuboidMorphMemo` ([ExtendedElementCommands.cpp L2436–L2449](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/eee7c60481031884f9baa294bab8f280cf6777d1/archicad-addon/Sources/ExtendedElementCommands.cpp#L2436-L2449)):

```cpp
#ifdef ServerMainVers_2700
    API_OverriddenAttribute material;
    material = buildingMaterial;   // building material index used as a surface (API_MaterialID) index
#else
```

That `material` value is passed to every `ACAPI_Body_AddPolygon`. The per-polygon value is a surface override, so it receives an index from the wrong attribute type. `BuildMorphBodyFromGeometry` already has a comment warning against exactly this ("do NOT fall back to the building material's own index here …"), but the cuboid path still does it.

### Suggested fix

In `BuildCuboidMorphMemo`, either leave the per-face override unset (`API_OverriddenAttribute material = {};`) or set it to the requested `surfaceId` when one is given. The `buildingMaterial` parameter of `BuildCuboidMorphMemo` can then be dropped.

### Possibly related: bottom face missing

A box created this way reads back with only **5** polygons, `bodyType: "Surface"` and `isClosed: false`; the bottom face (z = 0) is missing. The bottom face is built from `edges[0..3]` in the same order as the top face, so its normal probably points into the box, and Archicad may drop it for that reason. That cause is a guess and is not verified. A box passed as an explicit `body` with all six faces wound counter-clockwise seen from outside reads back as `Solid` with 6 faces.

### Workaround

Pass an explicit `body` instead of `size`, with all six faces wound counter-clockwise seen from outside, and set `surfaceId` on each face to the Morph surface. Existing Morphs can be repaired the same way with `ModifyMorphs` and a replacement `body`. Origin, axes, layer and properties are kept.
author: Itja

title: Expose IFC map conversion X axis and scale in Get/SetGeoLocation; Discord bot files question-worded reports
body:
## Why
`GetGeoLocation`/`SetGeoLocation` couldn't read or write the X axis direction (`XAxisAbscissa`/`XAxisOrdinate`) or the `Scale` of an IFC map conversion. That meant IFC georeferencing couldn't be fully passed to Archicad's Location Settings.

The request came in on Discord, but the Discord issue bot didn't file it. Because it was worded as a question, the classifier's confidence was 0.55, below the 0.7 filing threshold, so it only reached the borderline issue (#721).

## What
- **Add-On:** three new number fields in `surveyPoint.geoReferencingParameters`: `xAxisAbscissa`, `xAxisOrdinate` and `scale`. They map 1:1 to `API_GeoReferenceData` and `IfcMapConversion`. Every supported DevKit (AC25–AC29) has these fields, which I checked in each `APIdefs_Environment.h`, so no version guards are needed. On Get they're required in the response; on Set they're optional, like the other fields. `xAxisAbscissa = cos θ` and `xAxisOrdinate = sin θ`, where θ is the rotation of the project x axis from grid east. This is separate from `projectLocation.north`.
- **Grasshopper:** `ProjectLocation` / `SetProjectLocation` get three outputs/inputs, appended after the existing ones so existing wires stay connected.
- **Example:** `set_geo_location.py` sets the values, reads them back, then restores the original geolocation. New expected output added.
- **Docs:** `docs/archicad-addon/command_definitions.js` regenerated with `tools/generate_addon_docs.py`.
- **Discord issue bot:** the classifier prompt now says to judge the substance, not the phrasing. A question that points at something concrete Tapir lacks or gets wrong ("command X does not support Y, how should I handle that?") counts as a feature request or bug report. Plain help requests are still ignored. README updated. The bot's unit tests pass (33/33).

## Needs checking with Archicad
I couldn't run Archicad here. `set_project_info.py.output` now expects `xAxisAbscissa: 1`, `xAxisOrdinate: 0`, `scale: 1` from `TestProject.pla`. These are assumed defaults, so please confirm them with `Test/test_examples.py`. The same applies to the new `set_geo_location.py.output`, which assumes 0.8/0.6/0.5 read back exactly.

`API_GeoLocation.surveyPointPosition` (the survey point's position in project coordinates) is still not exposed. That can be a follow-up if needed.

title: Release weekly, with a minor release each month and major releases on demand
body:
The scheduled release now runs every Monday instead of on the 1st of each month. It still does nothing when there were no changes since the last release.

**Which version it ships.** `main` keeps carrying the next patch version (1.6.1 after 1.6.0), as before:

| Release | When | 1.6.1 on main ships as | main afterwards |
|---|---|---|---|
| patch | every week | 1.6.1 | 1.6.2 |
| minor | the first release of a calendar month | 1.7.0 | 1.7.1 |
| major | a PR merged since the last release has the `major-release` label | 2.0.0 | 2.0.1 |

A manual run can force the type with the new `release_type` input (`auto` / `patch` / `minor` / `major`).

For a minor or major release, a new step sets the release version before tagging and pushes it to main:
- the version files (`tools/package_info.json` + `tools/update_version.py`)
- the "introduced in" version of the commands registered with the skipped version in `AddOnMain.cpp`

So new commands keep using the version main carries, and they're relabeled when that version is skipped. This is what happened by hand for the 1.6.0 commands.

**Other changes**
- The minimum gap between releases drops from 1 week to 3 days. A release is published hours after its run starts, so with a 1-week minimum, every Monday run would have found the previous release too recent and skipped.
- `monthly_release.yml` is renamed to `weekly_release.yml`. References in the other workflows, `tools/update_version.py` and `CLAUDE.md` are updated, and `CLAUDE.md` describes the versioning rules.

**Testing:** I tested the version calculation for every type, plus the step that sets the version against a copy of the repo with commands registered as 1.6.1. It set 1.7.0 in every version file and in the 8 command registrations. The workflow itself hasn't run yet; a manual run with `dry_run` will show what it would release.

title: Start the Claude issue triage for issues the Discord bot files
body:
Issues filed by the Discord issue bot (for example #722) never got an answer or a fix from the Claude issue bot.

**Why:** `discord_issue_bot.yml` creates the issues with the workflow's own `GITHUB_TOKEN`. GitHub never starts a workflow run from an event caused by that token, so `claude_issue_triage.yml` never received `issues: opened` for them. The only exceptions are `workflow_dispatch` and `repository_dispatch`.

**What changes**
- `discord_issue_bot.py` writes the numbers of the bug and feature issues it created to the step output `created_issues`.
  - It writes them before its failure checks, so a run that ends red still hands over the issues it did create.
  - The rolling "Borderline Discord reports" issue is not included.
  - Two unit tests cover this.
- `discord_issue_bot.yml` has a new `triage` job that runs `gh workflow run claude_issue_triage.yml -f issue_number=N` for each created issue.
  - It is a separate job and the only one with `actions: write`. The job that passes Discord text to the classifier never holds that permission.
  - A failed dispatch is only a warning. A comment or the `claude-fix` label still starts the triage.
  - A new manual-run input, `triage_issues`, adds issue numbers to the same dispatch. Use it to catch up on issues filed earlier, and as the end-to-end test below.
- `claude_issue_triage.yml` gets a `workflow_dispatch` trigger with an `issue_number` input that runs the `fix` job.
  - A new first step accepts only a plain number naming an open issue (not a PR). The number goes into the prompt and the tool allowlist.
  - The concurrency group, prompt and tool allowlist use `github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number`.
  - A dispatch sent with `GITHUB_TOKEN` runs as `github-actions[bot]`, so `allowed_bots: "github-actions"` is added.
    - Checked against claude-code-action's source: `src/github/validation/actor.ts` strips `[bot]` and compares names case-insensitively, and `src/github/validation/permissions.ts` accepts actors ending in `[bot]`.
    - Events caused by that token never start a run, so this lets only these dispatches through. Dispatching needs write access to the repo, so outsiders get no new way in.
  - The `reply` job is unchanged.
- The Discord bot README and `CLAUDE.md` describe the new behaviour.

**Cost:** each Discord-filed issue now starts one `fix` run on the subscription, capped by the bot's existing daily issue limit.

**Testing**
- `python -m unittest test_discord_issue_bot` passes (35 tests).
- Both workflow files load as valid YAML.
- Nothing here has run in GitHub Actions yet.
- A dispatch of *Claude Issue Triage* from the Actions page runs as you, so it tests only the validation step and the prompt. It does not test the `github-actions[bot]` path.
- After merge, the end-to-end check is a manual run of **Discord Issue Bot** with `dry_run` checked and `triage_issues: 722`.
  - The `triage` job dispatches with the workflow's token.
  - The resulting *Claude Issue Triage* run should show actor `github-actions[bot]`, pass the action's actor check, and comment on #722 or open a draft PR.

This PR changes `.github/workflows`, so `claude_auto_merge` skips it and it needs a manual merge.

title: Set charCode CC_UniCode on Text/Label content so AC25–AC27 get the whole string
body:
Fixes #722

## Root cause

The earlier fix for #712 (#714, normalizing CRLF to LF) is in release 1.6.0. I checked with `git merge-base --is-ancestor d974e33 1.6.0`. The reporter installed it and ran the unmodified `Examples/create_texts.py` on Archicad 27, and still got only the first character. That example sends plain `'\n'` text, so CRLF was never the cause.

The actual cause is specific to Archicad 25 to 27. Before AC28, `API_ElementMemo::textContent` is a `char**` handle. On those versions both content writers in `archicad-addon/Sources/ElementCreationCommands.cpp`, `TextLabelDetails::ApplyTextContent` and `SetTextContentAndParagraphs`, copy **UTF-16** into it with `GS::ucscpy`. Neither one sets `API_TextType::charCode`, and nothing else in `Sources/` sets it either.

The AC27 DevKit is explicit about this requirement. `APIdefs_Elements.h` (27.3001) says: *"you can pass the content as a UniCode string (set charCode field of API_TextType structure to CC_UniCode and cast textContent field of API_ElementMemo to (unsigned short*))"*. The DevKit's own `Element_Test` sample `CreateMultiTextElement` writes UTF-16 exactly the way Tapir does, and it then sets `element.text.charCode = CC_UniCode;`.

Without that setting, Archicad reads the buffer as an 8-bit string. In UTF-16LE, `"Hello"` is the byte sequence `H 00 e 00 …`, so the string ends after `H`, which is exactly the symptom reported. AC28+ uses `GS::UniString *textContent` instead, has no `charCode` field, and is not affected. That is why the command works for users on AC28/29.

## Change

All new code is guarded with `#ifndef ServerMainVers_2800`, so AC28/AC29 builds are unchanged.

- `ApplyTextContent` (used by CreateTexts, CreateLabels, ModifyTexts, ModifyLabels and the SetDetailsOfElements height rebuild) and `SetTextContentAndParagraphs` (used by SetDetailsOfElements text) now set `textData.charCode = CC_UniCode` after writing the UTF-16 content. This also makes Archicad read the paragraph, run and eolPos offsets as character offsets, which is how they are already computed.
- The modify paths in ModifyTexts, ModifyLabels and the three SetDetailsOfElements text/label cases now also mask `charCode` / `u.text.charCode`. `ACAPI_Element_Change` only applies masked fields, so without the mask the stored charCode would still be used.
- `AddTextContent`, the read-back used by GetDetailsOfElements and by style-only modifies, now uses `APIMemoMask_TextContentUni | APIMemoMask_ParagraphUni` on pre-28 versions. The existing code already interprets the handle as UTF-16 with character offsets, and the `*Uni` masks are the documented way to get the content in that form.
- The comment on `NormalizeLineBreaks` is corrected. It no longer attributes the first-character symptom to CRLF.

No command was added, so no registration or version change is needed, and no docs were regenerated.

## How to test (AC27, and ideally AC25/26)

This change was written on a runner that has no Archicad and is **unbuilt**. A maintainer needs to start the AC25–AC29 build checks by pushing a commit or by closing and reopening the PR. Then:

1. Load the built AC27 Add-On and run `archicad-addon/Examples/create_texts.py`. Every text should show its full content, including the multi-line ones.
2. Run `python archicad-addon/Test/test_examples.py` on AC27. The `create_texts.py` read-back, which goes through `AddTextContent`, should match `ExpectedOutputs/create_texts.py.output`.
3. Check that `ModifyTexts` with a new `text`, and `SetDetailsOfElements` with a Text's `text`, also persist the full string on AC27.
4. Run a quick regression on AC28/29. Nothing should change there.

## Uncertain

- I only checked the AC27 DevKit headers and sample. `charCode`, `CC_UniCode` and the `*Uni` masks are documented as existing since AC9, so AC25/26 should compile, but CI should confirm this.
- Whether the `charCode` mask bit is strictly needed on `ACAPI_Element_Change` was not verified live. It is included because Change only applies masked fields.

title: Build and release the Add-On for Archicad 30
body:
Adds Archicad 30 to the Add-On builds on Windows and macOS: the PR build check and the release pipeline. Fixes for Archicad 30 reports such as #731 can be tested with a CI-built add-on, and releases ship an AC30 version.

Both use the release-candidate DevKits, which are not on the GitHub DevKit releases yet:
- `https://dl.graphisoft.com/release-candidate/30/API.Development.Kit.WIN.30.2000.zip`
- `https://dl.graphisoft.com/release-candidate/30/API.Development.Kit.MAC.30.2000.zip`

Switch both workflows to the final DevKit when it is published; a comment next to each entry says so.

**What changes**
- `archicad_addon_build_check.yml`: new `acVersion: 30` entries in `build_win` and `build_mac`. Windows uses the existing `>=AC29` step (toolset v143). Both upload an artifact like the other versions.
- `archicad_addon.yml`: the same AC30 entries in the release matrices. Windows builds the `.apx`; macOS builds a signed, notarized `.zip`. Both are attached to the draft release.
- `weekly_release.yml`: `EXPECTED_ASSETS` goes from 12 to 14 (6 versions × 2 platforms + 2 installers). Without this the release would be published before the AC30 files were attached.
- `archicad-addon/Tools/build_all_win.bat` builds AC30 locally too.
- `CLAUDE.md` mentions the AC30 build and its toolset.

The installer already looks for Archicad 25–39, so it picks up AC30 with no change.

**Risks**
- Every release now also depends on `dl.graphisoft.com` being reachable.
- An add-on built against the release-candidate DevKit may need a rebuild if Graphisoft changes the API before the final release.

**Testing**
- All three workflow files load as valid YAML.
- `dl.graphisoft.com` is blocked by the network policy where I work, so I couldn't download either DevKit.
- This PR's own CI run is the first check that both DevKits download and that the sources compile against AC30. The code already has several `ServerMainVers_3000` guards.
- The release pipeline itself only runs at the next weekly release.

The same commits are merged into #736 (the UTF-8 crash fix for #731), so that PR's CI produces AC30 builds for testing.

This PR changes `.github/workflows`, so `claude_auto_merge` skips it and it needs a manual merge.

title: CreateLabels: Symbol labels are created without their GDL parameters
body:
# CreateLabels: Symbol labels are created without their GDL parameters

**Tapir:** 1.6.0 (also on `main`, 1.6.1) · **Archicad:** 29, macOS

## What happens

`CreateLabels` with `labelClass: "Symbol"` (or a `favoriteName` of a Symbol label, e.g. a zone label like
`Flexi_Zone_Label`) creates the label with the right library part, layer and style, but **without any GDL
parameters**:

- only the label's hotspot is drawn in the floor plan, no content
- `GetGDLParametersOfElements` on the new label fails: *"Failed to get parameters of element with guid …"*
- `SetGDLParametersOfElements` fails as well: *"Failed to change parameters of element …"*
- `ApplyFavoritesToElements` on the label does not repair it

Tried: `favoriteName`, `ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults` + `CreateLabels` without favorite, with and without
`parentElementId` (zone). Labels placed by hand in Archicad with the same favorite are fine (140 parameters).

## Cause

`CreateElementsCommandBase::Execute` builds each element from `ACAPI_Element_GetDefaults (&element, &memo)`.
For Symbol labels the tool defaults do not carry the library part parameters (`memo.params` stays empty), and
`CreateLabelsCommand::SetTypeSpecificParameters` does not load them, so `ACAPI_Element_Create` creates the
label without additional parameters.

A second, related surprise: unless `midCoordinate` **and** `endCoordinate` are given,
`createAtDefaultPosition` is set to `true`, and Archicad moves the label to its default position relative to
the parent after creation – `begCoordinate` is then not where the label ends up. Reading the label back in the
same call still shows the requested `begCoordinate`.

## Proposed change (patch attached)

In `CreateLabelsCommand::SetTypeSpecificParameters`, Symbol branch:

1. New optional input `parametersFromElementId`: an existing Symbol label to copy the library part (`libInd`)
   and its parameters from (`ACAPI_Element_GetMemo (…, APIMemoMask_AddPars)`). Typical use: label all zones
   like one zone label placed by hand.
2. Fallback when `memo.params` is still empty: `ACAPI_LibraryPart_GetParams (libInd, …)` so a Symbol label
   always gets at least the library part defaults.
3. Schema description of `begCoordinate`: note the default-position behaviour.

Plus an example `Examples/create_symbol_labels_for_zones.py`.

Not compiled or run yet (no DevKit build here) – please review the memo handle ownership
(`memo.params` taken over from the source memo).

[createlabels-symbol-parameters.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32959853/createlabels-symbol-parameters.patch)

# Expose the survey point's position in project coordinates (and lock/visibility) in Get/SetGeoLocation

## Summary

`GetGeoLocation` / `SetGeoLocation` currently expose the survey point's *map* coordinates
(`surveyPoint.position.eastings / northings / elevation`, plus the IFC georeferencing parameters).
They do not expose where the survey point sits **in the project**, which is the value shown in
*Options > Project Preferences > Location Settings > Survey Point > Position* (labelled
Easting / Northing / Elevation in the English UI, "Felmérési pont X / Y / Magasság" in Hungarian).

That value exists in the C++ API (`API_GeoLocation::surveyPointPosition`, an `API_Coord3D`), so this
looks like a small addition rather than a missing capability. PR #732 already notes it as a possible
follow-up ("`API_GeoLocation.surveyPointPosition` ... could be a follow-up if needed").

## Use case

A script that places a DWG site plan as an external drawing and aligns the project to it. The DWG's
world origin ends up at some point Q in Archicad coordinates, and the survey point should be moved to Q

# Command to place an external DXF/DWG file as a Drawing element (File > External Content > Place External Drawing)

## Summary

There is no way to place an external DXF/DWG drawing through the JSON API or Tapir. `CreateDrawings`
only places existing navigator items on layouts. A script that needs a site plan or survey DWG in the
project has to simulate the menu, a file dialog, a unit dialog and a placement click.

Request: a Tapir command that does what *File > External Content > Place External Drawing* does, and
returns the new Drawing element's id.

## Use case

Placing a surveyor's DWG site plan (or any other DWGs of other disciplines), then aligning it with the project: DWG world origin to the
Archicad origin, a named UCS to the origin, or origin and X axis from two clicked points; then setting
story, layer, rotation, unit scale, and optionally project north and survey point. Everything after the
placement step already works through Tapir (`GetSelectedElements` / `GetElementsByType` for the new
Drawing, `SetDetailsOfElements` for `pos`, `angle`, `ratio`, `floorIndex`, `layerIndex`). Only the
placement itself is missing.

title: SetStories: a story's level cannot be changed while a story above it is active (AC28, 1.6.0)
body:
Follow-up to #574. My post-merge AC28 report there sits on a merged PR, so I'm filing it as its
own issue.

On 1.6.0 the AC28 failure from #574 turns out to be deterministic once the active story is
controlled. The result depends only on which story is active.

**Setup:** untitled project, AC28 (Win, GER), two stories (S0 at 0.00, S1 at 3.00). The active
story is switched with `ChangeWindow {navigatorItemId}` (the StoryItem from
`GetNavigatorItemTree {navigatorMapId: "ProjectMap"}`) and confirmed via `GetStories.actStory`.
One `SetStories` call per row, both stories with indices 0 and 1.

| active story | change requested | result |
|---|---|---|
| S0 | S0 0.00 -> -1.00 | converges |
| S0 | S0 -1.00 -> 0.00 | converges |
| S0 | S1 3.00 -> 4.00 | converges |
| S1 | S1 3.00 -> 4.00 | converges |
| S1 | S0 0.00 -> -1.00 | fails: "Failed to set the level of story 0: requested -1.0000, got 0.0000." S0 stays at 0.00 and S1 moves to 4.00 instead |
| S1 | both shifted by -1.00 | fails with the same message |

So every change converges while the active story is at or below the lowest story whose level
changes. A level change on a story below the active story fails with the named error, and the
height between the two stories is applied on the other side: the active story moves.

The same probes on AC26 (1.6.0) all pass. But on AC26 the active story cannot be switched at all
(see #748), so the failing rows were never reached there.

This might be why your AC29 run was green: if story 0 was active, every row passes. I'm
reporting the measurements only.

Client-side workaround that converges on AC28: activate the lowest story whose level changes via
its navigator StoryItem before calling `SetStories`.
author: weltmaister

title: ChangeWindow {windowType: "FloorPlan", storyIndex} returns success but does not change the active story
body:
Verified on 1.6.0 with AC26 and AC28 (Win, GER), untitled project with two stories:

- `ChangeWindow {"windowType": "FloorPlan", "storyIndex": 1}` returns `{"success": true}`, but
  `GetStories.actStory` stays `0`.
- `ChangeWindow {"navigatorItemId": <StoryItem of story 1>}` does switch it (`actStory` becomes
  `1`) on AC28. That path is AC27+ only, so on AC25/AC26 there is currently no working way to
  activate a story through Tapir.

Where this matters in practice:
- automatic zones (`CreateZones` with `referencePosition`) on an upper story did not find their
  boundary, because the zone search runs on the story that is really active;
- `SetStories` level changes depend on the active story (#747).

The code path is in `ChangeWindowCommand::Execute`: `windowInfo.index = storyIndex`, then
`ACAPI_Window_GetDatabaseInfo` + `ACAPI_Database_ChangeCurrentDatabase` +
`ACAPI_Window_ChangeWindow`. Each call returns NoError, but the active story is unchanged.

title: DeleteElements (#679): a nonexistent guid is reported as deleted, and placed after a real element it stops that element's deletion
body:
#679 made the per-element results honest for elements on locked or hidden layers. I re-verified
that on 1.6.0: a wall on a hidden layer is now reported as "The element was not deleted, because
it is not editable." with `success: false`, and it really stays. Thank you, that closes the delete
half of #555. (I have not re-tested MoveElements.)

Two cases still report the wrong thing. Identical on AC26 and AC28 (1.6.0, Win, GER), untitled
project. `BOGUS` is a well-formed guid that never existed:

| call | executionResults | walls afterwards |
|---|---|---|
| A: [real] | [success] | deleted |
| B: [BOGUS] | [success] | — |
| C: [real, BOGUS] | [failed -2130313115 "Failed to delete the element.", success] | **real wall still there** |
| D: [BOGUS, real] | [success, success] | deleted |
| E: [real, real] | [success, success] | both deleted |

  says it should get a failed result with APIERR_BADID.

  element's result is honest (failed, element still present), but whether it gets deleted depends
  on the order of the list.

title: RenameNavigatorItem reports success without renaming Project Map exterior elevations (AC28, Tapir 1.6.0); View Map control works
body:
## Summary

On Archicad 28, Tapir 1.6.0, `RenameNavigatorItem` reports `{"success":true}` when renaming an exterior elevation in the **Project Map**, but immediate read-back of the **same navigator GUID** shows the original name unchanged. A separate **View Map** control succeeds and is independently verified.

Related: #466, especially its follow-up reporting success without a rename on Project Map interior elevations. This report adds an exterior-elevation reproduction on Windows with Tapir 1.6.0 and a verified View Map control.

## Environment

- Archicad 28, build 6300, Swedish edition
- Windows
- Tapir 1.6.0
- Project: Pungen 8.pln; diagnostic testing was requested on a disposable copy
- Tests performed through a companion calling Tapir commands and verifying results through fresh native reads

## Project Map reproduction

1. Read `GetNavigatorItemTree` with `{"navigatorMapId":"ProjectMap"}`.
2. Identify elevation **F1** and use its freshly read `navigatorItemId`.
3. Call `RenameNavigatorItem` with that ID and `newName: "TEST NORTH"`.
4. Tapir returns exactly `{"success":true}`.
5. Immediately read the Project Map again and locate the **same GUID**.
6. Its name remains **FASAD MOT NORR**, rather than **TEST NORTH**.

Earlier, the same pattern occurred when attempting to rename F1 from **Fasad A1** to **FASAD MOT NORR** through Tapir. It remained **Fasad A1**, including after reopening the project. Manual renaming in Archicad works. The later diagnostic started with the manually established name **FASAD MOT NORR**.

The Project Map GUID is not included here because it was not provided in the summarized diagnostic result; it should not be inferred from the View Map GUID below.

## Independent View Map control

The companion stopped further writes after the failed Project Map verification, so the control was performed as a separate request/session. The user configured View Map names to inherit from the Project Map beforehand.

| Map | Before | Requested | Exact native response | Immediate read-back |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Project Map elevation F1 | FASAD MOT NORR | TEST NORTH | `{"success":true}` | FASAD MOT NORR, same GUID |
| View Map view | FASAD MOT NORR, `customName:false` | TEST NORTH VIEW | `{"success":true}` | TEST NORTH VIEW, `customName:true`, same GUID |

View Map control GUID: `4EFE818F-0F99-C507-9CAE-EB8F059F8ABF`.

No geometry change, save, restoration or other item modification was performed during the control. Manual renaming works for both Project Map and View Map.

## Expected versus actual

Expected: the requested Project Map rename persists and is visible through fresh reads, or Tapir reports that the item type/map is unsupported or that verification failed.

Actual: the command reports success although the requested Project Map name is unchanged. A client trusting only the success response would incorrectly conclude the rename happened. Our companion detects the mismatch and stops dependent writes.

## Source inspection: confirmed findings

In [NavigatorCommands.cpp at the 1.6.0 release](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/e0d4cca231f15c99da0b91cb2e591ab3758ae97a/archicad-addon/Sources/NavigatorCommands.cpp#L1330), `RenameNavigatorItemCommand::Execute`:

- Reads the item through `ACAPI_Navigator_GetNavigatorItem`.
- Copies the requested name into `navItem.uName` and sets `customName = true`.
- Calls `ACAPI_Navigator_ChangeNavigatorItem` and **checks its return code**.
- Returns success without reading the name back or using an elevation-specific modification path.

Therefore, source inspection does not establish that an error from the rename call is ignored. It establishes that API success is not checked against persisted state. The separate `newId` layout branch contains unchecked layout-modification behavior, but these name-only tests do not exercise that branch.

The current published [Graphisoft navigator API documentation](https://graphisoft.github.io/archicad-api-devkit/group___navigator.html) describes `ACAPI_Navigator_ChangeNavigatorItem` as modifying only View Map items. [API_NavigatorItem](https://graphisoft.github.io/archicad-api-devkit/struct_a_p_i___navigator_item.html) documents `customName` as relevant to View Map/Layout Map. These documentation pages are currently labeled **Archicad 29**, so they are not a direct runtime confirmation for build 6300 of AC28.

At investigation time on 2 October 2026, 1.6.0 was the latest release. `NavigatorCommands.cpp` was identical between that release and inspected main commit `c994b35e356d58bbab07cb91800a3b1f034cdfe2`.

## Hypothesis and investigation request

The successful View Map control supports a Project Map-specific issue in this environment. It does **not** establish the exact internal cause or rule out every localization-dependent difference. The requested test names contain only ASCII characters; no comparison with another language edition has been performed.

Could Project Map elevation renaming require modifying the underlying elevation element's segment/name settings rather than its navigator representation? The SDK describes elevations using `API_CutPlaneType` / `API_SectionSegment`, including `cutPlName`, and database information exposes `linkedElement`. This is a candidate path to investigate, not a tested fix:

- [Elevation element representation](https://graphisoft.github.io/archicad-api-devkit/group___element.html)
- [API_SectionSegment name field](https://graphisoft.github.io/archicad-api-devkit/struct_a_p_i___section_segment.html)
- [Database linkage](https://graphisoft.github.io/archicad-api-devkit/struct_a_p_i___window_info.html)

Simply switching to `ACAPI_Database_ModifyDatabase` is not an established fix: [its documented supported types](https://graphisoft.github.io/archicad-api-devkit/group___database.html) are independent details, worksheets, layouts and master layouts, not elevations.

Suggested diagnostic: record `mapId`, `itemType`, database/linked-element identity, exact API return code and independent read-back on AC28. An explicit unsupported-item failure or post-write verification would prevent false success even before an elevation-specific implementation is available.
