body:
## Find the localized Add-Ons folder
The Add-Ons folder has a different name in some Archicad language versions (e.g. `Extensions` in FRA, `Dodatki` in POL). The installer used to look only for `Add-Ons`, so it missed those installations.

- New `FindAddOnsFolder (installPath)` looks at the installation's direct subfolders, skipping `.app` bundles and symlinks:
  1. It first takes a folder with one of the Add-Ons folder names Graphisoft lists for each language version (`LOCALIZED_ADDONS_FOLDER_NAMES`). The names are compared ignoring case (`ArchiCAD` vs `Archicad`) and after Unicode normalization, because macOS stores accented file names in decomposed form.
  2. If there is none, it takes the folder that contains `XReadCfg.txt`, directly or up to two levels below, as the Graphisoft multi-language add-on guide recommends. The shallowest match wins.
- `AddInstallationCandidate` uses that folder and skips the installation when none is found. An `.app` bundle is never treated as an installation folder; on macOS the Add-Ons folder sits next to the bundle.
- `ArchicadInstallation` now receives `addOnsFolderPath` explicitly. `--addOnsFolder` works the same as before.

The list of localized names comes from the Graphisoft community forum thread "Addon folder name in different languages". The build environment couldn't open Graphisoft's pages directly, so I collected the names via search; please check them against the official list.

## Modern GUI
Redesigned the Tk window in the Tapir colors (charcoal on white, green accent). It still uses only the standard library:
- White header with the logo, title and latest release.
- One card per Archicad installation, showing its Add-Ons folder path, a checkbox and a status badge: Installed / Not installed / Downloading NN% / Failed. The installed status is detected at startup, and a progress bar runs along the bottom of the card during the download.
- *Select all / Select none* link and an "N of M selected" count.
- Flat Install (primary), Uninstall and Close buttons. They are labels, because `tkinter.Button` ignores colors on macOS. Install and Uninstall are disabled while nothing is selected; Enter installs and Esc closes.
- Results and per-version errors appear in an inline banner instead of a modal message box.
- The window keeps a fixed size while statuses change, and on Windows it opens DPI-aware, so text isn't blurry on high-DPI displays.

## Testing
- Detection: `--console --dryRun --uninstall --mockRoot` on mocked folder trees:
  - `Add-Ons` with a stray `Documentation/Sub/Deep/XReadCfg.txt` → `Add-Ons`
  - `Extensões` with a decomposed accent → `Extensões`
  - `Расширения Archicad` → picked
  - unknown name containing `XReadCfg.txt` → picked by the marker search
  - neither → not detected
  - `.app` bundle → ignored
- GUI: rendered under Xvfb with Python 3.12 / Tk 8.6, and driven through the buttons against mock installs with a stubbed download:
  - it detected 28 = Installed and 29 = Not installed, and installed both; the stray `TapirAddOn_AC28_Win.apx` was moved into `Tapir/`
  - deselecting 28 and uninstalling removed only 29
  - the banner and button states were correct throughout
- `py_compile` passes. The GUI hasn't been tried on real Windows or macOS yet.

title: Run the Tapir Installer for the Add-On's auto-update
body:
The Add-On's auto-update downloaded `update_addon_and_restart_archicad.py` from `main` and ran it with `uv`. The script runs without administrator rights, so it fails when the Add-On is in a protected folder: `Program Files` (where the Tapir Installer puts it) or, for non-admin users, the Archicad folder in `Applications`. It quit Archicad first and then failed to replace the Add-On, so Archicad disappeared and wasn't started again. Every failure was silent: no window, no output.

The update now goes through the Tapir Installer, which already handles the Windows admin prompt, the macOS password fallback and bundle replacement.

## Installer (`archicad-addon/Installer/tapir_installer.py`)
- **New update mode:** `--addOnFile <loaded .apx/.bundle> --versions N [--archicadPort P [--archicadPid PID]] [--noRestart]`. It shows the GUI unless `--console` is given.
- **Order of steps:** download (size and file signature checked) → quit Archicad through Tapir's JSON API → replace exactly the loaded Add-On → start Archicad again.
  - Archicad is started again even when replacing failed.
  - Archicad is only quit after the download succeeded.
  - On Windows the restart goes through `explorer.exe`, so Archicad does not run as administrator.
  - On macOS it uses `open -n`.
- **macOS bundle swap:** the new bundle goes to `<bundle>.new`. The old one is renamed to `.old` and only deleted once the new one is in place. If that delete fails, the result is a warning, not an error.
- **Save prompt:** while Archicad asks whether to save changes, the window waits with no time limit. After about 5 s it tells the user to answer the prompt in Archicad and offers Cancel. On Windows, `AllowSetForegroundWindow` lets the prompt come to the front.
- **One update per Archicad:** `TapirUpdate_<port>.lock`, shared with the legacy script. A second update shows a message based on what the first one is doing.
- **Option parsing:** unknown options are ignored and no abbreviations are accepted, so a newer Add-On or script can pass new options to an older installer.
- **Tests:** new offline suite `test_update_mode.py` (65 tests), using a mock Archicad, a fake `ditto` for macOS paths, and Windows-locking emulation.

## Add-On (C++)
- **`VersionChecker`:** also records the `TapirInstaller_Win.exe` / `TapirInstaller_Mac.zip` asset of the same release. It offers no update when the release has no Add-On for this Archicad version.
- **`TapirPalette::UpdateAddOn`:**
  - Downloads the installer as binary, following redirects itself. It shows Archicad's progress window with Cancel (pre-AC27 mappings added in `MigrationHelper.hpp`), and a second update can't start meanwhile.
  - Starts the installer:
    - Windows: `ShellExecuteExW` with `runas`. If the admin prompt is declined but the Add-On's folder is writable, it starts the installer without admin rights; otherwise it explains the cancel.
    - macOS: `ditto` + `open -n`. On an Intel Mac it gives a clear message if the installer has no Intel code.
  - No `uv`, and no script from `main`. The installer process is not attached to the palette, which fixes the Run button that stayed stuck on Kill after an update.

## Legacy script (`archicad-addon/Tools/update_addon_and_restart_archicad.py`)
Already released Add-Ons keep downloading this script from `main` (same arguments).
- **Hand-off:** it hands off to the installer of the same release tag when that tag's installer source has update mode. This doesn't depend on when this PR is merged; for today's 1.6.0 release it updates in place.
- **Otherwise it updates in place, with fixes:**
  - checks the download and that the folder is writable *before* quitting Archicad;
  - replaces the bundle instead of merging into it;
  - always starts Archicad again;
  - shows native error dialogs;
  - takes the shared lock.

## CI
- **Universal2 macOS installer:** built from a pinned python.org 3.12.10 package with `--target-arch universal2`, then checked with `lipo`. Until now `TapirInstaller_Mac.zip` was arm64-only and didn't run on Intel Macs. The macOS zip will be larger.
- **PR check:** now also compiles the legacy script, runs `test_update_mode.py`, and does a dry-run update against a dummy Add-On.

## Testing
- **Installer:** `test_update_mode.py` passes on Python 3.11 and 3.12. It also passes with macOS paths faked; strict Windows-locking emulation passes the lock tests.
- **Legacy script:** an offline harness (137 tests) passes on 3.11 and 3.12. Earlier rounds also ran it on 3.8.
- **C++:** `clang -fsyntax-only` with the AC25–AC29 DevKit headers, on the macOS path (MAC29, AC25) and the Windows path (mingw-w64; AC25–AC29), with `-Wall -Wextra -Werror` on macOS and extra warning flags on Windows: no errors or warnings.
- **GUI:** every update window state was rendered under Xvfb. Install mode is pixel-identical to `main`.
- **Not run yet:** none of it on real Windows, a real Mac, or with a real Archicad. CI on this PR is the first real build (MSVC/Xcode for AC25–AC30, the universal2 installer, the Windows test run).

title: AC25-AC27, 1.7.0+: changing the content or size of a text with two or more characters fails with -2130312713
body:
On the official 1.7.0 binary for AC28 (Win, GER), every change to an existing Text element's
content or size fails. The same calls worked on 1.6.0 on the same instance (2026-10-02), and they
work on 1.7.0 for AC26. Untitled project, floor plan active, a fresh text created with
`CreateTexts {"textsData":[{"coordinate":{"x":800,"y":800,"z":0},"text":"Hello Tapir","height":3.0}]}`.

| call | AC28, 1.7.0 | AC26, 1.7.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `SetDetailsOfElements` `details.typeSpecificDetails.height: 7.5` | failed `-2130312713` "Failed to change element", height stays 3 | success, height 7.5 |
| `SetDetailsOfElements` `details.typeSpecificDetails.text: "Changed"` | failed `-2130312713`, text unchanged | success |
| `SetDetailsOfElements` `typeSpecificDetails.angle` / `.position` | success | success |
| `ModifyTexts` `text: "Changed text"` | failed `-2130312713` "Failed to modify the Text." | success |
| `ModifyTexts` `style: {height: 6.0}` | failed `-2130312713` | success |
| `ModifyTexts` `text` + `style.height` | failed `-2130312713` | success |
| `CreateTexts` (content + height) | works | works |

So on AC28 every write path that rebuilds the text content fails, while angle/position (no
content rewrite) still work. A build from `main` at c994b35 (2026-10-02, before #735 was merged)
passed the SetDetailsOfElements height change on AC28 as well.

Between that build and 1.7.0, the only commit touching the text code is 8c25c92 (#735). Its new
code is guarded with `#ifndef ServerMainVers_2800`, so I can't see from the source how it would
reach AC28. I'm reporting the measurement only and can run a probe build on AC28 (for example
1.7.0 with 8c25c92 reverted) within minutes.

Workaround on AC28 until then: delete the text and create it anew with the target content and
height.
author: weltmaister

title: Wish: CreateLayout – let the caller choose the position in the subset (new layouts are inserted first and renumber all existing sheets)
body:
Observed with Tapir 1.5.9, Archicad 29.

When CreateLayout is called with a parentNavigatorItemId (a subset), the new layout is inserted at the FIRST position of that subset. Because layouts are numbered by subset (PK-01, PK-02, ...), every existing sheet gets renumbered. In a project with an issued sheet list this silently changes the numbers of existing sheets (e.g. "PK-01 Title page" became "PK-02", an existing "PK-04 Visualization" became "PK-05").

There is no parameter to say where the new layout should go. MoveNavigatorItem has previousNavigatorItemId, CreateLayout does not.

Workaround today: call CreateLayout, read the layout book tree to get the new item's navigatorItemId, then call MoveNavigatorItem with previousNavigatorItemId = the last sheet. When creating several layouts in one call, each of them has to be moved separately, and the numbers should be re-checked afterwards.

Request: add an optional previousNavigatorItemId to LayoutData in CreateLayout (same meaning as in MoveNavigatorItem), and ideally append to the end of the subset when it is omitted, which is what most scripts expect. If changing the default is a compatibility concern, an explicit option (e.g. "position": "end") would also work.

Related use case: generating a series of sheets (one per rendered visualization) at the end of an existing subset without disturbing the numbering of the sheets that are already there.
author: cichym

title: Archicad crashes (ODB access violation) on element modification while an element notification client is registered
body:
## Summary

With an element notification client registered through `SetElementNotificationClient`,
Archicad 28 crashed while I stretched a door by hand. Archicad logged an
object-database assertion followed by an access violation. With no notification
client registered, the same kind of manual door edits no longer crash.

The same client worked without crashing on Tapir 1.5.8 in August 2026, including
manual moves and deletes of doors and zones, so this looks like a regression in a
later release.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Tapir | 1.7.0 |
| Last known good | 1.5.8 |
| Archicad | 28.0.0 v1 AUS (build 7006), Apple Silicon (arm64) |
| macOS | 26.7.1 (25G241) |
| Project | solo `.pln`, not Teamwork |

## How the client is registered

A Python script registers one client, served by a local HTTP server that answers
`POST /element_notification` with `200` immediately:

```json
{
  "host": "localhost",
  "port": 50153,
  "notifyOnNewElement": false,
  "notifyOnModificationOfAnElement": true,
  "notifyOnReservationChanges": false
}
```

The port is chosen by the OS. The client is removed with
`RemoveElementNotificationClient` using the same host and port.

## Steps that led to the crash

1. Open a project and register the client as above.
2. About 40 seconds later, stretch a door by hand on a floor plan (the `Stretch`
   command on a door, Level 02).
3. Archicad terminates.

## What the logs show

Archicad's own FastLogger log ends with:

```
User, Command
Stretch / 2-Level 02
ODB error assertion failed at /Volumes/P/Dev/28U40F/Sources/ObjectDatabase/ObjectDatabaseDll/Database/ODBDatabase.cpp 2182
Serious error encountered.
Application terminated (application error). Reason: ODB: access violation encountered
```

The notification server **received no POST** before the crash, so the failure
happens inside Archicad or the add-on before the notification is sent, not in the
client.

## Workaround

Do not register a notification client. Since we stopped registering one, manual
door edits have not crashed.
author: ImLovinIt

title: newId never sets a view's ID: RenameNavigatorItem writes it for layouts only, and still reports success
body:
Summary
On Archicad 29 with Tapir 1.7.0, calling RenameNavigatorItem with newId on a
View Map item returns {"success":true} and changes nothing. The ID shown
for the view (and its customUiId flag) is exactly as before the call. newName
on the same GUID works in the same request, so the GUID and the command itself
are fine — only the ID write is missing.
Related: #755 and #756 (same "reports success, does nothing" pattern, for Project
Map renames), #538 and #539 (which exposed uiId / customUiId for reading).
Environment
Archicad 29, Windows
Tapir 1.7.0
Two projects open, calls made through the JSON API on ports 19723/19724
Every call followed by an immediate fresh GetNavigatorItemTree read of the
same GUID (no manual editing, no save in between)
Reproduction
Pick a View Map view and read its item with GetNavigatorItemTree
(navigatorMapId: "ViewMap"). In my project the view came back as
"uiId": "1", "customUiId": true.
Call RenameNavigatorItem with that view's GUID and newId:
{
  "command": "API.ExecuteAddOnCommand",
  "parameters": {
    "addOnCommandId": {
      "commandNamespace": "TapirCommand",
      "commandName": "RenameNavigatorItem"
    },
    "addOnCommandParameters": {
      "navigatorItemId": { "guid": "<view guid>" },
      "newId": "A-101"
    }
  }
}
Response is exactly {"success": true}.
Read the same GUID back with GetNavigatorItemTree.
Steps 2-4 repeated with newName plus newId in the same call, and with
newId: "" first, then the value. All four variants return {"success": true}.
Actual result
before: uiId = "1", customUiId = true
after:  uiId = "1", customUiId = true
The ID is unchanged in every variant. (The commandName was also tried through
the standard namespace first — Command 'RenameNavigatorItem' not found, this is
Tapir-only command.)
Expected result
The view's ID becomes "A-101" (and customUiId is set to true, i.e. the View
Settings ID radio switches to "Custom"), or, if the write is not possible for
this item type, the command fails with an explicit error instead of reporting
success.
Root cause
RenameNavigatorItemCommand::Execute (Sources/NavigatorCommands.cpp) writes
newName to the navigator item and then handles newId like this:
    // For layouts: set custom layout number (ID) via ChangeLayoutSets
    GS::UniString newId;
    if (parameters.Get ("newId", newId)) {
        API_LayoutInfo layoutInfo = {};
        BNZeroMemory (&layoutInfo, sizeof (layoutInfo));
        if (ACAPI_Navigator_GetLayoutSets (&layoutInfo, &navItem.db.databaseUnId) == NoError) {
            CHTruncate (newId.ToCStr ().Get (), layoutInfo.customLayoutNumber,
                        GS::ArraySize (layoutInfo.customLayoutNumber));
            layoutInfo.customLayoutNumbering = true;
            ACAPI_Navigator_ChangeLayoutSets (&layoutInfo, &navItem.db.databaseUnId);
            ...
        }
 
For anything that is not a layout, ACAPI_Navigator_GetLayoutSets does not
succeed, so the whole block is skipped silently and the function returns a
successful execution result. The name write above it is unaffected, which is
exactly the behaviour observed.
This matches #538: customUiId and uiId "aren't referenced anywhere in
Sources/" — they are serialised by NavigatorItemToObjectState but never
written.
Suggested fix
API_NavigatorItem carries both fields with the same names in the AC25-AC29
DevKit headers (APIdefs_Navigator.h):
char uiId[128] — "The ID of the navigator item."
bool customUiId — "Custom ID of the item (relevant only in the View Map and
Layout Map)."
So for a View Map (or Layout Map, when the layout number is not the intent) item
the write could mirror the name path: set navItem.uiId and
navItem.customUiId = true, then call ACAPI_Navigator_ChangeNavigatorItem
again (the current code only calls it before the newId block, so the ID would
have to be set before that call or a second call added after it).
If ChangeNavigatorItem turns out not to persist uiId for views, please make
the command fail instead of reporting success — the same read-back verification
that PR #756 introduces for names would cover it, and a silent success is the
worst outcome for a caller.
Why it matters
I use Tapir to copy a View Map between two projects. Names, layer combinations,
pen sets, scale, zoom and rotation all transfer correctly; the ID is the one
thing that does not. In this project several views in the same folder share the
same name (four electrical plans, all named "1-й Этаж"), and the ID is what
distinguishes them in the View Map — without it the migrated views are
indistinguishable and have to be fixed by hand, one by one, in View Settings.
A command that can read uiId/customUiId but cannot write them leaves that
gap open.
author: SergeyLastukhin

title: CreateWalls with `favoriteName` errors when combined with `floorIndex`, and silently drops the favorite's composite/top link otherwise
body:
When creating a Wall via `CreateWalls`, the optional `favoriteName` parameter behaves inconsistently:

1. **`favoriteName` + `floorIndex`** → the call fails with a generic error (no detail returned).
2. **`favoriteName` alone** (no `floorIndex`, no explicit `height`/`thickness`) → the call "succeeds" but produces a **plain Basic** wall: the favorite's composite build-up and top-story link are silently ignored.
3. The documented **ApplyFavoritesToElements** path works correctly and is the only reliable way to get a wall that actually matches the favorite.

Because `height` and `thickness` are marked **required** on `CreateWalls`, the natural "just draw a reference line and let the favorite supply everything" flow cannot be expressed cleanly, so users are pushed toward either of the two broken paths above.

## Expected behaviour
A favorite is a complete recipe (this matches how Archicad itself behaves when you draw from a saved wall favorite). Passing `favoriteName` to `CreateWalls` should produce a wall whose **structure/composite, reference-line location, home story, top link and offsets** all come from the favorite. The user should only need to supply the reference-line endpoints (`begCoordinate`, `endCoordinate`).

## Observed behaviour (Archicad 29, Tapir 1.7.0)

| Call | Params (besides `begCoordinate`/`endCoordinate`) | Result |
|------|---------------------------------------------------|--------|
| A | `favoriteName: "EXTERIOR WALL 25CM"` + `floorIndex: 0` + `height: 3.3` | ❌ generic error, no element created |
| B | `favoriteName: "EXTERIOR WALL 25CM"` + `floorIndex: 0` + `height: 1.0` | ❌ same generic error (so it is not caused by a specific height value) |
| C | `favoriteName: "EXTERIOR WALL 25CM"` + `height: 3.3` + `thickness: 0.31` (no floorIndex) | ✅ element created, **but** `structureType: "Basic"`, single building material, `relativeTopStory: 0` — favorite settings **not applied** |
| D (control) | plain wall, no `favoriteName` (`height: 3.3`, `thickness: 0.25`) | ✅ created fine (Basic, as expected) |
| E (workaround) | plain create → then `ApplyFavoritesToElements` with the same favorite | ✅ wall matches the favorite exactly (composite, layer, CoreOutside reference line, top linked to next story) |

### Favorite in question
- Name: `EXTERIOR WALL 25CM` (a user-saved wall favorite in the test project)
- Its own **Wall Default Settings** dialog shows:
  - Top Link: `1. BİRİNCI KAT PLANI (Home + 1)`
  - Top offset: `0.00`, Bottom offset: `0.00`
  - Home Story: `0. ZEMIN KAT PLANI (Current)`
  - Structure: `DIŞ DUVAR (25CM)` → 31.00 cm overall composite
- So the favorite **does** carry a next-story top link and a home story; they are simply not transferred by path C.

### Read-back of the wall created via path C (path E result for comparison)
Path C output:
```json
{ "structureType": "Basic", "referenceLineLocation": "Center",
  "relativeTopStory": 0, "height": 3.3, "begThickness": 0.31 }
```
Path E (ApplyFavorites) output — the correct result:
```json
{ "structureType": "Composite", "referenceLineLocation": "CoreOutside",
  "relativeTopStory": 1, "height": 3.3, "begThickness": 0.31 }
```

## Environment
- Archicad **29** (macOS)
- Tapir Add-On **1.7.0** (latest release, 4 Oct 2026)
- The same `favoriteName` + `floorIndex` error was also observed earlier on **Tapir 1.5.9**, so this is not a regression introduced in 1.6/1.7 — the `favoriteName` path on CreateWalls appears simply not fully wired up for composite favorites.

## Suggested resolution
1. Make `CreateWalls` + `favoriteName` actually apply the favorite's structure/composite, reference-line location, home story and top link to the new wall (mirroring `ApplyFavoritesToElements`).
2. Make `favoriteName` + `floorIndex` a supported combination (currently it errors). If an explicit `floorIndex` should override the favorite's home story, that precedence should be documented and honoured rather than erroring.
3. Where a favorite supplies required values (height/thickness/top link), either relax the "required" fields when `favoriteName` is present, or document that explicit values must be passed *and* will override the favorite (matching the `favoriteName` field description: "Its settings are applied first, then the explicitly given fields override them").
4. Return a specific error (not a bare failure) when `favoriteName` is not found or cannot be resolved, so the cause (e.g. name mismatch / trailing spaces / non-ASCII) is diagnosable.

## Reproduction steps
1. In an Archicad 29 project, save a composite wall as a favorite (e.g. `EXTERIOR WALL 25CM`, with a next-story top link).
2. Call `CreateWalls` on port 19723 with a single wall:
   ```json
   { "wallsData": [ { "begCoordinate": {"x":0,"y":1}, "endCoordinate": {"x":3,"y":1},
       "favoriteName": "EXTERIOR WALL 25CM", "floorIndex": 0, "height": 3.3 } ] }
   ```
   → returns a generic error (no element).
3. Repeat without `floorIndex` (keep `height`/`thickness`) → element created but as a Basic wall.
4. Repeat via plain create + `ApplyFavoritesToElements` → correct composite wall (the workaround).

## Workaround
Create the wall with plain geometry, then apply the favorite with `ApplyFavoritesToElements`, and read back to verify structure/composite/reference line/top link. This works reliably, but it is a two-step operation instead of the intended one-call create-from-favorite.

title: BUG: ShowScriptUI with `navigationDisabled: true` never loads the page (palette stays blank)
body:
Calling `ShowScriptUI` with `"navigationDisabled": true` shows the palette, but the HTML in `htmlContent` never loads: the palette stays blank and the page's scripts never run. The same call without `navigationDisabled` loads normally. Other options (`title`, `width`/`height`, `contextMenuEnabled: false`) are fine. **Environment:** Archicad 29 build 3000 (INT), Windows 11, Tapir 1.6.0. **Reproduction:** each page reports back through `ACAPI.SubmitResult` once the bridge exists. Results, run one after another on the same palette: | `ShowScriptUI` options | Page reports within 3 s? | |---|---| | none | yes | | `contextMenuEnabled: false` | yes (twice) | | `navigationDisabled: true` | **no** (twice) | | none again | yes | ```python import json, time, urllib.request def tapir(cmd, params=None): body = json.dumps({"command": "API.ExecuteAddOnCommand", "parameters": { "addOnCommandId": {"commandNamespace": "TapirCommand", "commandName": cmd}, "addOnCommandParameters": params or {}}}).encode() req = urllib.request.Request("http://127.0.0.1:19723", body, {"Content-Type": "application/json"}) return json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req).read())["result"]["addOnCommandResponse"] PAGE = """

probe

""" for options in ({}, {"navigationDisabled": True}, {}): tapir("ShowScriptUI", {"htmlContent": PAGE, **options}) loaded = False for _ in range(30): r = tapir("GetScriptUIResult") if r.get("hasResult") and r["result"] == "loaded": loaded = True; break time.sleep(0.1) print(options, "->", "loaded" if loaded else "NOTHING (page did not load)") ``` **Likely cause:** in `ScriptUIPalette::ShowWithHTML`, `browser.DisableNavigation (options.navigationDisabled)` runs before `browser.LoadHTML (...)`, so loading the page counts as the navigation being blocked. Disabling navigation after the content has loaded (for example from the browser's load-finished event) would keep the option's purpose (no navigating *away*) without blocking the page itself. _Investigated and written up with Claude Code; the tests above were run on my own machine (Archicad 29, Tapir 1.6.0)._
author: AlexanderBurkeAB

title: BUG: Stop in the Tapir palette kills `uv` but leaves the script's Python process running
body:
While a script runs, the palette's Run button becomes Stop, which calls `process.Kill ()` on the process Tapir started, i.e. `uv`. On Windows the Python process(es) that `uv run --script` started are not killed with it: they keep running with no parent. A script that waits for something (for example polling `GetScriptUIResult` for a ShowScriptUI page) carries on in the background, and after Stop and Run there are two copies talking to the same ArchiCAD. In our case the new copy's page appeared frozen: its buttons greyed on Next but it never moved on, most likely because the orphan, waiting on the same page number, took the click.

**Environment:** Archicad 29 build 3000, Windows 11, Tapir 1.6.0, uv 0.12.22. Also present in the source of 1.7.0 and main (`TapirPalette.cpp`: `process.Kill ();`).

**Reproduction:**
1. Add and Run a script that loops forever, e.g. `while True: time.sleep(1)`.
2. Press Stop.
3. Task Manager (or `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process`) still shows the script's `python.exe` processes, whose parent `uv.exe` is gone.

Confirmed 07-10-2026 with the real Stop button on a plain `while True: time.sleep(1)` script: before Stop, `Archicad.exe → uv.exe (5660) → python.exe (6376)`; after Stop, `uv.exe` was gone and `python.exe` 6376 was still running, with no parent.

Observed process tree before Stop, for a script with dependencies: `Archicad.exe → uv.exe → python.exe (venv launcher) → python.exe`. After Stop: both `python.exe` remain.

**Since when:** up to 1.1.8 the palette started Python itself (`python -X utf8=1 <script> --port <N>`), so `process.Kill ()` killed the script. From 1.2.0 ("Using uv to execute scripts", July 2025) the started process is `uv`, and the same `Kill ()` no longer reaches Python. Short scripts hide it, since the orphan finishes and exits; it shows with scripts that wait, such as ShowScriptUI pages.

**Suggestion:** kill the whole process tree. On Windows, start the process inside a Job Object with `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` (also cleans up if Archicad itself exits), or `taskkill /PID <uv pid> /T /F`. On macOS, start it in its own process group and signal the group.

**Our workaround** (in case it helps others): the script finds its ancestor `uv` process with psutil and exits when it disappears.

_Investigated and written up with Claude Code; the tests above were run on my own machine (Archicad 29, Tapir 1.6.0)._

title: FEATURE: let a script know when the ShowScriptUI palette is closed by the user
body:
A script that drives a multi-page ShowScriptUI page polls `GetScriptUIResult` and waits for the user. When the user closes the palette with its close box, the script has no way to find out, so it keeps running (and keeps Tapir's Run button in its Stop state) until it gives up on its own or the user presses Stop.

We checked whether the page could tell the script instead: when the palette is hidden (`ACAPI.ClosePalette()` runs the same `Hide ()` as the close box), the page gets no `visibilitychange`, `pagehide`, `blur` or `resize` event, and `requestAnimationFrame` keeps firing at about 30 per second. So neither side can see the close today.

#485/#488 fixed the palette reappearing after it was closed; this request is the next piece: reporting the close.

**Environment:** Archicad 29 build 3000, Windows 11, Tapir 1.6.0.

**Possible shapes**, any of which would do:
- `GetScriptUIResult` also returns `"isVisible": true/false` (from `IsVisible ()`), or a one-shot `"closedByUser": true` set in `PanelCloseRequested`.
- `PanelCloseRequested` fires a page event (e.g. `window.dispatchEvent(new Event('acapiclose'))`) before hiding, so the page can `SubmitResult` a close message itself.
- A small `GetScriptUIState` command.

The first is the smallest change and fits the existing polling model.

_Investigated and written up with Claude Code; the tests above were run on my own machine (Archicad 29, Tapir 1.6.0)._
author: AlexanderBurkeAB

title: FEATURE: hide Morph edges with ACAPI_Element_ChangeMorphEdgeType (Archicad 29+)
body:
The schema notes for `edgeDefault` / `edgeOverrides` describe the SDK bug where `element.morph.edgeType` is discarded by `ACAPI_Element_Create/Change`, so a script cannot hide a Morph's edges. The Archicad 29 API added a dedicated function for this: `ACAPI_Element_ChangeMorphEdgeType (const API_Guid& elemID, API_MorphEdgeTypeID edgeType)`, listed under the AC29 "New API features" (https://graphisoft.github.io/archicad-api-devkit/newfeatures.html). Its documentation says it changes all edge types of a morph element, which `ACAPI_Element_Change` does not offer. It is not called anywhere in Tapir 1.7.0.

Could it be exposed, either as a command (e.g. `SetMorphEdgeType {elements, edgeType}`) or by having `CreateMorphs`/`ModifyMorphs` call it after creation when `edgeDefault` is given (Archicad 29 and later only)?

**Environment:** Archicad 29 build 3000, Windows 11, Tapir 1.6.0 (checked against the 1.7.0 source).

**Use case:** we place a generated, triangulated building envelope (a few thousand faces) as a closed Morph. With visible edges every triangle shows, and the architect currently has to hide them by hand.

(We do not need a layer field on `CreateMorphs`: `SetDetailsOfElements` with `layerIndex` moves a new Morph to another layer and leaves its body intact, tested on 1.6.0.)

_Investigated and written up with Claude Code; the tests above were run on my own machine (Archicad 29, Tapir 1.6.0)._

title: Require parentNavigatorItemId for CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap/CreateViewsInViewMap
body:
Fixes #658.

## Problem

Both `CloneProjectMapItemToViewMapCommand` and `CreateViewsInViewMapCommand`
(`Sources/NavigatorCommands.cpp`) treated `parentNavigatorItemId` as optional.
When omitted, both silently resolved it themselves to the View Map root
(`ACAPI_Navigator_GetNavigatorSet(...).rootGuid`) and passed that guid to
`ACAPI_Navigator_CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap`.

That is exactly the broken state described in #658: a view cloned directly
onto the View Map root becomes impossible to delete
(`ACAPI_Navigator_DeleteNavigatorView` returns `NoError` but is a silent
no-op) or move (`ACAPI_Navigator_ChangeNavigatorItem` fails with
-2130313112), and cannot be removed by hand in the Navigator palette either.
Tapir's own fallback is what produces the orphan - the API itself is never
asked to clone *without* a destination, it's always handed `rootGuid`
implicitly.

## Change

- `parentNavigatorItemId` is now a **required** schema field in both
  commands (`CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap` and `CreateViewsInViewMap`).
- `Execute` refuses with `APIERR_BADPARS` when it is missing, with a message
  pointing at `CreateViewMapFolder` to create a destination first, instead
  of silently falling back to the root.
- Updated the two commands' registered descriptions in `AddOnMain.cpp`
  accordingly.

## Compatibility

Both commands have shipped since 1.5.4 (July 2026) with
`parentNavigatorItemId` optional, so this is a breaking schema tightening
for any caller currently omitting it against these two specific commands.
Given the alternative is a permanently corrupted View Map with no recovery
path, the trade-off seems clearly worth it - but flagging it explicitly
since it's a behavior change, not just a bugfix in the narrow sense.

`Examples/test_navigator_views.py` already always passes
`parentNavigatorItemId` into a folder, so no example/test changes were
needed.

## What a maintainer should verify

Not built or tested against a live Archicad seat by me (same limitation
the auto-generated PRs on this repo flag) - compiles cleanly against the
current `main` (AC27, macOS/Xcode), but the actual `APIERR_BADPARS` error
path and the two commands' happy paths with an explicit parent should be
exercised against a running Archicad before merging.

title: Expose 17 previously-missing Wall fields (Get/Set/Create)
body:
## Problem

`API_WallType` carries several native fields Tapir never read or wrote at all:
`contPen`/`contPen3D` (contour pen, floor plan and 3D), `contLtype`/`belowViewLineType`/
`aboveViewLineType` (contour/overhead line types), `aboveViewLinePen`, `displayOption`,
`viewDepthLimitation`, `wallConnPriority`, `useCompositePriority`, `sequence`,
`linkToSettings`, `inheritEndSurface`, `alignTexture`, `offsetFromOutside`, `polyCanChange`,
`materialsChained`, `logHeight`, `hasWindow`, `hasDoor`. `WallDetails` only exposed
`cutFillPen`/`cutFillBackgroundPen` (the cut fill pattern's pens, inherited from the
building material) - nothing about the wall's own contour pen/line type, display options,
or junction behavior.

This surfaced while investigating a report that a Basic wall's "cut line pen" couldn't be
read or set through Tapir: `cutFillPen` is the fill pattern pen, not the contour pen -
`contPen` is the actual field for that, and it (along with the other 16) was simply never
wired up.

## What changed

Added as `contourPen`, `contourPen3D`, `contourLineTypeId`, `belowViewLineTypeId`,
`aboveViewLinePen`, `aboveViewLineTypeId`, `displayOption`, `viewDepthLimitation`,
`connectionPriority`, `useCompositePriority`, `junctionSequence`, `linkToSettings`,
`inheritEndSurface`, `alignTexture`, `offsetFromOutside` (read-only), `polyCanChange`,
`materialsChained`, `logHeight`, `hasWindow`/`hasDoor` (read-only) to:

- `GetDetailsOfElements` (`ElementCommands.cpp`)
- `ModifyWalls` (`ExtendedElementCommands.cpp`, via the existing `ApplyWallDetails`)
- `CreateWalls` (same `ApplyWallDetails`, reused from `SetTypeSpecificParameters`)

`displayOption`/`viewDepthLimitation` reuse Morph's `ElemDisplayOptionToString`/`FromString`
and `ViewDepthLimitationToString`/`FromString` - moved from `ExtendedElementCommands.cpp`'s
anonymous namespace to global scope (declared in `CommandBase.hpp`) so
`ElementCommands.cpp` can call them too. They were internal-linkage definitions shadowed by
the new external declaration, which made every call site ambiguous - fixed as part of this
change, visible fallout of wiring Wall's Get side into the same helpers Morph's Get side
already used privately.

## Verified live

Tested against a running Archicad 27 (a Teamwork/BIMcloud project) with a throwaway wall
created far from any real geometry, round-tripped through Create → Get → Modify → Get →
Delete, asserting every field both ways:

- **11 fields are fully reliable** through Get, Set and Create: `contourPen`/`contourPen3D`,
  the 3 line type ids, `aboveViewLinePen`, `displayOption`, `useCompositePriority`,
  `inheritEndSurface`, `alignTexture`, `materialsChained`, `logHeight`, `hasWindow`/`hasDoor`.
- **`connectionPriority` and `junctionSequence` never take effect**, through either Create
  or Modify - Archicad appears to manage wall junction priority/ordering entirely on its
  own, with no externally writable path despite the fields being readable. Documented as
  such in both fields' descriptions; no workaround exists.
- **`viewDepthLimitation`, `linkToSettings` and `polyCanChange` are silently ignored by
  Create**, and a separate `ModifyWalls` call applying them was inconsistent across
  repeated, otherwise-identical test runs against the same project - sometimes took
  effect, sometimes didn't. Documented as unreliable, with a recommendation to verify with
  `GetDetailsOfElements` after writing rather than trust a single call.

  A Create-then-automatic-Modify workaround was tried (re-applying just these three fields
  via a follow-up `ACAPI_Element_Change` in its own undoable command, right after
  `CreateElementsCommandBase::Execute` returns) and then deliberately removed: it did not
  fix the unreliability, it only added a second silent-failure code path on top of the
  first. Left as a documented caveat instead of a false sense of reliability.

## What a maintainer should verify

- The three unreliable-write fields were tested only against one Teamwork/BIMcloud project;
  worth re-testing against a local (non-Teamwork) file to rule out a reservation/sync
  timing issue specific to shared projects versus a plain Archicad API behavior.
- `connectionPriority`/`junctionSequence` being entirely unwritable might be specific to
  this Archicad version/build (tested: AC27, build 6080) - worth confirming across
  AC25-29 if there's reason to think it could differ.

title: claude_pr_review.yml's thread-resolution step fails on fork PRs, making every review check red
body:
## `claude_pr_review.yml`'s "Resolve settled threads" step always fails on fork PRs, turning a passing review into a red "review" check

### Summary

On a pull request from a fork, the `review` job's final step ("Resolve settled threads") consistently fails with `gh: Resource not accessible by integration`, even though:

- The review itself completes and posts its summary comment correctly (e.g. "Looks correct, nothing blocking").
- The job already declares `permissions: pull-requests: write` at the job level (claude_pr_review.yml:99-102).
- The workflow already uses `pull_request_target`, specifically to avoid the fork-PR read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN` restriction (see the comment at claude_pr_review.yml:16-20).

So the review's actual content is fine, but the `review` status check still shows red, which reads as "blocked" even when the review says the opposite.

### Where it fails exactly

The job has two GitHub-write steps:
1. "Review the pull request" - posts the summary comment and inline comments via the `claude-code-action`. **This succeeds.**
2. "Resolve settled threads" - calls the GraphQL mutation `resolveReviewThread` for each thread id in the summary's marker. **This fails.**

Log excerpt from a failing run (PR #777, run `37619621084`):

```
review  Resolve settled threads  gh: Resource not accessible by integration
review  Resolve settled threads  ##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

Same failure, same step, on PR #776 (run `37611078017`).

### Why `pull-requests: write` isn't enough here

`resolveReviewThread` is reported in multiple community threads as a mutation the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` (identity `github-actions[bot]`) cannot perform reliably, independent of the `permissions:` block requesting `pull-requests: write` - unlike posting a review or a comment, which that same token can do (and does, in this workflow, successfully). This looks like a GitHub platform-level gap rather than something fixable purely by adjusting the YAML's `permissions:` section, which claude_pr_review.yml already sets correctly per its own stated intent.

### Impact

Every fork-originated PR that gets a Claude review ends up with a permanently red `review` check, regardless of what the review actually concludes - e.g. #776 and #777, both currently showing a failing `review` check after a review that said "looks correct, nothing blocking" / "mergeable". This likely affects `claude_auto_merge.yml` too, since it gates on "every check green" (see claude_pr_review.yml:362-367) - a clean review from a fork contributor can never auto-merge as things stand.

### Possible directions (not prescribing one)

- Make "Resolve settled threads" best-effort: log the failure but don't fail the job (e.g. don't propagate `failed` as the step/job exit code). Thread resolution is a nice-to-have for readability, not the point of the review.
- Mint the mutation call with a token that can actually perform it (a PAT or GitHub App installation token stored as a secret, scoped narrowly to this one step) instead of the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- Split the job's status so the review's own outcome isn't entangled with the thread-resolution housekeeping step's success/failure.

### Repro

Open (or push to) any pull request from a fork - e.g. #776 or #777 - and check the `review` job's "Resolve settled threads" step.

title: RenameNavigatorItem: newId reports success but the ID of View Map items is not changed
body:
Environment

Tapir Add-On 1.5.9
Archicad 27 and Archicad 29 (both reproduced), macOS
Teamwork and solo projects (in Teamwork, the view was reserved)

Steps to reproduce

Open a project with a view in the View Map, e.g. ID NAW, name Innenwaende.
Call RenameNavigatorItem on that view:
json
   {
     "navigatorItemId": {"guid": "<view guid>"},
     "newId": "X-NAW"
   }
Read the View Map again with GetNavigatorItemTree (ViewMap), or check the view in the Navigator.

Expected The view's ID (prefix) is X-NAW. If the ID cannot be changed (for example because of the view's ID setting), the command should return an error.

Actual

The command returns success.
The ID stays NAW.
The same happens with the view's ID setting on "By Project Map" and on "Custom".
If newName and newId are sent in the same call, only the name is changed.
Changing only newName works as expected.

Additional notes

There seems to be no way through Tapir to switch a view's ID setting (By Project Map / Custom), which might be the underlying reason.
Reporting success on a change that is not applied makes it hard for scripts to detect the failure. A clear error or a working newId would both help.

title: Full Get/Set/Create access to Model View Option combinations, including custom GDL-contributed fields
body:
## Full Get/Set/Create access to Model View Option combinations, including custom GDL-contributed fields

### Summary

Tapir only exposes the **name** of a project's Model View Option (MVO) combinations (`GetModelViewOptions` - one command, no parameters, returns `[{"name": "..."}]`). There is no way to read or write a combination's actual settings: door/window/skylight display, beam/roof/slab/column drawing style, Curtain Wall/Stair/Railing detail levels, or - importantly - the custom entries that GDL library parts contribute to the "Model View Options" dialog (visible there as extra checkboxes/options next to Archicad's own, e.g. from office-specific library objects).

### What exists on the Archicad API side (AC27+, confirmed from the DevKit headers)

- `ACAPI_Navigator_ModelViewOptions_Search` / `_GetNum` / `_Get` - **read-only**, by index or by name/guid via `API_ModelViewOptions_Head`. Fills an `API_ModelViewOptionsType { head; modelViewOpt; }`.
- `API_ModelViewOptions` (the `modelViewOpt` payload), exact fields (all in `APIdefs_ViewSettings.hpp`, AC27 DevKit):
  - `char doorMode`, `char windowMode`, `char skylightMode` (hole display mode)
  - `char sectionMarker`, `char beamMethod`, `char roofShellMode`, `char showColumnSymbol`, `char slabMethod`
  - `bool coluHiddenlineUnderSlabs`, `bool beamHiddenlineUnderSlabs`, `bool zoneHideZoneStamp`
  - `API_CurtainWallModelViewOptions curtainWallModelViewOptions`: `char cwFrameDetailLevel`, `char cwPanelDetailLevel`, `char cwJunctionDetailLevel`, `char cwAccessoryDetailLevel`
  - `API_StairModelViewOptions stairModelViewOptions`: `char stair3DDetailLevel`, `char stairFloorPlanVisualization`, `bool showStairHeadroom`, `bool stairFloorPlanCompWalkingLine`, `bool stairFloorPlanCompNumbering`, `bool stairFloorPlanCompUPDOWNText`, `bool stairFloorPlanCompDescription`, `bool stairFloorPlanCompTreadAccessories`, `bool stairFloorPlanCompStructureBeamSupport`, `bool stairFloorPlanCompStructureStringers`, `bool stairFloorPlanCompStructureCantilevered`, `bool stairReflectedCompWalkingLine`, `bool stairReflectedCompDescription`, `bool stairReflectedCompStructureBeamSupport`, `bool stairReflectedCompStructureStringers`, `bool stairReflectedCompStructureCantilevered`, `API_AttributeIndex stairSchemeSurfaceIndex` (Surface/`API_MaterialID`), `API_AttributeIndex stairSchemeCutLineIndex` (`API_LinetypeID`), `short stairSchemeCutLinePenIndex`, `API_AttributeIndex stairSchemeUncutLineIndex` (`API_LinetypeID`), `short stairSchemeUncutLinePenIndex`
  - `API_RailingModelViewOptions railingModelViewOptions`: `char railing3DDetailLevel`, `bool railing2DDisplayCompPosts`, `bool railing2DDisplayCompTopRail`, `bool railing2DDisplayCompHandrails`, `bool railing2DDisplayCompRails`, `bool railing2DDisplayCompInnerPosts`, `bool railing2DDisplayCompBalusters`, `bool railing2DDisplayCompPanels`, plus the same 4 scheme-attribute fields as stair (`railingSchemeSurfaceIndex`/`railingSchemeCutLineIndex`/`railingSchemeCutLinePenIndex`/`railingSchemeUncutLineIndex`/`railingSchemeUncutLinePenIndex`)
- **The custom part**: `API_ModelViewOptions::gdlOptions` is a `API_GDLModelViewOptions*` (allocated array, each entry `{name, guid, params (API_AddParType**), checkSum, supersetGuid}`) - this is where GDL library parts' own contributed MVO entries live. Must be released with `ACAPI_FreeGDLModelViewOptionsPtr` after use. `params` is the same GDL add-on parameter shape Tapir's existing `GetGDLParametersOfElements`/library-part commands already serialize - that existing serializer should be reusable here instead of writing a new one.
- **Changing** the current window's options: `ACAPI_Navigator_GetViewOptions` / `ACAPI_Navigator_ChangeViewOptions` (`API_ViewOptions { modelViewOpt; onScreenViewOpt; }`). Two important caveats, both from the DevKit's own remarks:
  - `ACAPI_Navigator_ChangeViewOptions` is documented as **non-undoable**.
  - It operates on the **active plan window's current** settings, not a named combination in isolation. It takes an optional `modelViewOptionAttributeIndex` that *also switches the active window to that combination* as a side effect - there is no way to edit a stored combination's values without live-switching to it first.
- **No Create function exists at all** for MVOs in the AC27 DevKit - only `_Search`/`_GetNum`/`_Get`. The pre-27 fallback (generic `ACAPI_Attribute_Create` with the legacy `API_ModelViewOptionsID` constant) is also gone: that constant is no longer declared anywhere in the AC27 DevKit headers, so a build targeting AC27 can't even reference it. Creating a new combination from scratch may simply not be possible through this API - worth confirming, but don't assume it has a workaround.

### A real, confirmed gotcha worth knowing before starting

While prototyping this, `ACAPI_AddOnAddOnCommunication_InstallAddOnCommandHandler` **failed to register a command** (error -2130313112, logged, not thrown) whose *input* ("parameters") schema embedded the full `API_ModelViewOptions` shape with the `stair` and `railing` sub-objects both included (~50+ properties combined, several nested two levels deep). The **identical JSON text registered and worked fine as a *response* schema** on a sibling Get command - so this isn't a JSON-syntax problem, and it isn't tied to any single field (every subset tried individually registered fine, including the full `stair` object alone with ~20 fields). It looks like Archicad enforces some total-complexity or size ceiling specifically on *input* schemas that response schemas aren't held to. Not isolated to an exact cause or threshold. If you hit this: register a Set/Create command's input schema in pieces (e.g. one array item per section instead of one giant nested object), or flatten deeply nested sections, and verify registration succeeds (not just that `Execute` runs) before assuming a schema change is fine - "the add-on builds" is not enough, you need to confirm Archicad actually installs the command handler at runtime.

### The char-typed "mode" fields' values aren't in the DevKit

`doorMode`/`windowMode`/`skylightMode`/`sectionMarker`/`beamMethod`/`roofShellMode`/`showColumnSymbol`/`slabMethod` and the three sub-structs' detail-level fields are documented only by the *names* of their constants in DevKit comments (e.g. `API_Hole_ShowWithDim`...`API_Hole_HideHole`, `API_Beam_Drawing_Full`/`RefLine`/`Contour`) - those constants are not declared anywhere in this DevKit's headers, so their numeric values can't be verified from the headers alone. Expose them as raw integers rather than guessed string enums until a maintainer with access to the full Archicad SDK docs (or a live Archicad, trying each value and observing the dialog) can confirm the mapping.

### Suggested shape

- `GetModelViewOptionDetails` - `{"names": [...]}` optional (all combinations if omitted) → full `API_ModelViewOptions` per combination, **including a `gdlOptions` array** (name, guid, params - reuse the existing GDL parameter serialization).
- `SetModelViewOptionDetails` - `{"modelViewOptionsWithDetails": [{"name", "details"}]}`, built on `ACAPI_Navigator_ChangeViewOptions`. Document the non-undoable, active-window-switching behavior loudly in the schema description, not just a code comment - a caller needs to know this before using it on a real project.
- `CreateModelViewOptions` - investigate whether this is possible at all first; if not, a command that clearly reports "not supported by the Archicad API" is more useful than silence or a misleading schema.
- Grasshopper components for all three.

The **identical JSON text registered and worked fine as a *response* schema** on a sibling Get command - so this isn't a JSON-syntax problem, and it isn't tied to any single field (every subset tried individually registered fine, including the full `stair` object alone with ~20 fields). It looks like Archicad enforces some total-complexity or size ceiling specifically on *input* schemas that response schemas aren't held to. Not isolated to an exact cause or threshold. If you hit this: register a Set/Create command's input schema in pieces (e.g. one array item per section instead of one giant nested object), or flatten deeply nested sections, and verify registration succeeds (not just that `Execute` runs) before assuming a schema change is fine - "the add-on builds" is not enough, you need to confirm Archicad actually installs the command handler at runtime.

### The char-typed "mode" fields' values aren't in the DevKit

`doorMode`/`windowMode`/`skylightMode`/`sectionMarker`/`beamMethod`/`roofShellMode`/`showColumnSymbol`/`slabMethod` and the three sub-structs' detail-level fields are documented only by the *names* of their constants in DevKit comments (e.g. `API_Hole_ShowWithDim`...`API_Hole_HideHole`, `API_Beam_Drawing_Full`/`RefLine`/`Contour`) - those constants are not declared anywhere in this DevKit's headers, so their numeric values can't be verified from the headers alone. Expose them as raw integers rather than guessed string enums until a maintainer with access to the full Archicad SDK docs (or a live Archicad, trying each value and observing the dialog) can confirm the mapping.

### Suggested shape

- `GetModelViewOptionDetails` - `{"names": [...]}` optional (all combinations if omitted) → full `API_ModelViewOptions` per combination, **including a `gdlOptions` array** (name, guid, params - reuse the existing GDL parameter serialization).
- `SetModelViewOptionDetails` - `{"modelViewOptionsWithDetails": [{"name", "details"}]}`, built on `ACAPI_Navigator_ChangeViewOptions`. Document the non-undoable, active-window-switching behavior loudly in the schema description, not just a code comment - a caller needs to know this before using it on a real project.
- `CreateModelViewOptions` - investigate whether this is possible at all first; if not, a command that clearly reports "not supported by the Archicad API" is more useful than silence or a misleading schema.
- Grasshopper components for all three.
author: MathiasJon

title: **Title:** Attribute names with non-ASCII characters are garbled (built-in "Archicad Layer" shows as a box)
body:
**Description**

Attribute names returned by Tapir are wrong when they contain non-ASCII characters, for example Hungarian accented letters. The built-in Archicad layer (index 1) comes back as a single unprintable character, which shows up as a box (▮) in a client UI. The same names are correct in Archicad and in the official JSON API (`API.GetLayerAttributes`).

**Environment:** Archicad 28 HUN, Tapir 1.6.1, Windows.

**To reproduce**
1. Open a project that has a layer with an accented name, for example `Fal – Tartó`.
2. Run `GetAttributesByType` with `{"attributeType": "Layer"}`, or run `GetLayers`.
3. The accented names are garbled, and the name of index 1 (Archicad Layer) is an unprintable character.
4. Run `API.GetLayerAttributes` with the same attribute ids. It returns the correct Unicode names.

**Cause (probably)**

In `archicad-addon/Sources/AttributeCommands.cpp`, the name is built from the legacy 8-bit `char` field:

```cpp
attributeDetails.Add ("name", GS::UniString (attr.header.name));
```

There are about ten places like this. The same pattern is in `GetAttributesByType` (line ~160) and `GetLayers` (~2374), and in the line, fill, zone category, MEP system, pen table, profile, composite and surface getters.

**Suggested fix**

Before calling `ACAPI_Attribute_Get` / `ACAPI_Attribute_GetAttributesByType`, set `attr.header.uniStringNamePtr` to a `GS::UniString` and return that string instead of `header.name`. `CreateAttributes` already does this. Calling `GS::UniString (attr.header.name, CC_Default)` (system codepage) would at least fix the accents, but the `uniStringNamePtr` approach is the reliable one.

**Workaround we use:** we read the names from `API.GetLayerAttributes` by guid.

Thanks for Tapir, it is a great tool!

title: Add a way to open a Teamwork/BIMcloud project, not just local .pln/.pla files
body:
## OpenProject rejects Teamwork/BIMcloud project locations - only local .pln/.pla accepted

### Summary

`OpenProjectCommand` (`Sources/ProjectCommands.cpp`) is the only command that opens a project, and it hard-rejects anything whose last path component doesn't end in `.pln` or `.pla`:

```cpp
if (extension.Compare ("pln", CaseInsensitive) == GS::UniString::Equal) {
    openPars.fileTypeID = APIFType_PlanFile;
} else if (extension.Compare ("pla", CaseInsensitive) == GS::UniString::Equal) {
    openPars.fileTypeID = APIFType_A_PlanFile;
} else {
    return CreateFailedExecutionResult (APIERR_BADPARS, "projectFilePath parameter is invalid, the extension must be pln or pla");
}
```

There is no way through Tapir to open a Teamwork/BIMcloud project - only local files. A user asked for exactly this: automating opening a BIMcloud project without clicking through Archicad's UI.

### Why this is probably a small, not a new, feature

Archicad itself opens a Teamwork project via a `teamwork://` URL passed as a plain command-line argument - confirmed directly from a running process's own argv on this user's machine (user/token/server/project redacted here, but the shape was):

```
-openasplan teamwork://<user>:<token>@<serverUrlEncoded>/<ProjectName>
```

Two DevKit facts point at `ACAPI_ProjectOperation_Open` - the same function `OpenProjectCommand` already calls - already supporting this, given the right `IO::Location`, without needing a different Archicad API call:

1. There is no Teamwork/BIMcloud-specific `API_FTypeID` in the whole DevKit (`APIdefs_Automate.h`) - every plan, local or shared, uses the same `APIFType_PlanFile`. The Teamwork-ness is a property of the *location*, not the file type.
2. `ACAPI_Teamwork_GetTeamworkProjectDetails (const IO::Location& twProjectLocation, ...)` (`ACAPinc.h`) takes an `IO::Location` and parses a server URL, project name and username out of it, and is documented as working purely from the location ("does not try to reach the server") - i.e. `IO::Location` already has a notion of a `teamwork://`-shaped location distinct from a local path, elsewhere in this same API.

So the likely fix is: build the `IO::Location` from a `teamwork://...` string the same way `GetTeamworkProjectDetails` expects it, keep `fileTypeID = APIFType_PlanFile`, and call `ACAPI_ProjectOperation_Open` exactly as already done for local files - skipping (or branching around) the extension check for a `teamwork://` prefix instead of a `.pln`/`.pla` suffix. **This needs confirming against a live Archicad with a real BIMcloud server** - it has not been tried, only inferred from the two DevKit facts above.

### Suggested shape

- Either loosen `OpenProjectCommand` to accept a `teamwork://...` string in `projectFilePath` alongside local paths, or add a dedicated `OpenTeamworkProject` command (`{"teamworkUrl": "teamwork://user:token@server/project"}` or broken into `{"serverUrl", "projectName", "username", "password"}` fields assembled into the URL internally - whichever keeps credentials out of a single opaque string more cleanly for callers). Prefer not inventing a username/password exchange if the existing BIMcloud auth token shape (as in the example URL above) is what real callers already have on hand.
- Response: the existing `#/ExecutionResult` pattern `OpenProjectCommand` already uses is probably enough (success/fail + error), since connecting can fail for many server-side reasons (auth, network, project locked) that don't need individual schema fields - just a clear message.
- A Python example under `archicad-addon/Examples/` would need a real BIMcloud server to run against, which generate_documentation/CI don't have - document in the example's docstring that it must be run manually against a real server, as the project's other server-dependent examples already do, if any precedent exists in this codebase for that.

### What a maintainer/implementer should verify live (can't be confirmed without a DevKit + a running Archicad connected to a real BIMcloud server)

- That `ACAPI_ProjectOperation_Open` actually accepts a `teamwork://` `IO::Location` and connects, rather than failing or requiring a different call entirely for the connect step.
- What happens on auth failure, wrong/expired token, or the project already being open elsewhere - whether Archicad blocks synchronously with a clear `GSErrCode` or needs the caller to poll.
- Whether opening while Archicad already has a different project open needs `CloseProjectCommand` first, or `ACAPI_ProjectOperation_Open` handles that itself (as it presumably does for the existing local-file path already).

### Context

Tapir 1.7.1 (`main`), ArchiCAD 27 (macOS), BIMcloud/Teamwork server. Confirmed via the AC27 DevKit headers that no Teamwork-specific open function or file type exists, and that `OpenProjectCommand`'s current extension check is the only thing standing between it and (possibly) working today for Teamwork locations too - not verified end-to-end.
author: MathiasJon

title: Add a command to open a Teamwork/BIMcloud project by launching a new Archicad instance
body:
### Summary

Confirmed in #791: `ACAPI_ProjectOperation_Open` cannot join a Teamwork/BIMcloud project at all — fails with `APIERR_GENERAL` (`-2130313215`) whether the `IO::Location` is built from a `teamwork://...` string or copied directly from a live `API_ProjectInfo.location_team` object (no parsing issue, both paths return identical error). So there is no DevKit call, from inside the running Add-On's own process, that opens a Teamwork project in-place.

But Archicad itself *can* open one — via its own CLI argument, confirmed directly from a running process's argv:
```
-openasplan teamwork://<user>:<token>@<serverUrlEncoded>/<ProjectPathEncoded>
```
This is exactly the string already returned by the existing `location`/`sourceLocation` fields of `GetProjectInfo`, `GetHotlinks`, etc. (all via `IO::Location::ToDisplayText()`).

### Suggested feature

A new command, e.g. `OpenProjectInNewInstance`, that:
1. Takes a `teamworkUrl` (or reuses `projectFilePath` from `OpenProjectCommand` — see note below) string parameter: the `teamwork://...` location.
2. Finds the current Archicad executable's own location — already exposed by `GetArchicadLocationCommand` (`ApplicationCommands.cpp`), which uses `IO::fileSystem.GetSpecialLocation (IO::FileSystem::ApplicationFile, &applicationFileLocation)`.
3. Launches a **new** Archicad process pointed at that executable with `-openasplan <teamworkUrl>` as an argument — this spawns a second Archicad instance that joins the Teamwork project the normal way Archicad itself would.
4. Returns success/failure of the *launch* (not of the join itself, which happens asynchronously in the new process and can't be awaited here) — the existing `#/ExecutionResult` pattern is probably enough, with a clear description that this only confirms the process started, not that the project opened.

### How to launch the process — precedent already in this codebase

There are two different mechanisms already used elsewhere in the Add-On, either is fine:
- `GS::Process::Create (const GS::UniString& command, const GS::Array<GS::UniString>& argv)` — `Modules/GSRoot/Process.hpp` in the DevKit. Clean, takes argv as an array (no shell-escaping needed for the token/URL). No current usage in `Sources/` to copy from, but it's a standard DevKit class.
- Plain C `system (command.ToCStr ().Get ())` — used today in `Sources/UvManager.cpp` (`OpenWebpage`, `AttemptAutomaticInstallation`), with the `WINDOWS`-vs-not branch already written there (`"start"` vs `"open"`) as a pattern to copy for cross-platform handling. Simpler, but needs the URL properly quoted/escaped in the command string since it goes through a shell — `GS::Process::Create` avoids that entirely, so prefer it for this command given the URL contains an auth token.

Either way, this needs to work on both Windows and macOS (project requirement) — macOS executable launch is `open -a "<path to .app>" --args -openasplan <url>` (same shape already used in `archicad-addon/Installer/tapir_installer.py` / `Tools/update_addon_and_restart_archicad.py`, e.g. `subprocess.Popen (['open', '-n', archicadLocation])`, for restarting Archicad after an update — same idea, just add `--args -openasplan <url>`). On Windows, launching the `.exe` directly with `-openasplan <url>` as an argument should work the same way Archicad's own shortcut/URL-handler does it (not verified live on Windows, flag this as something to confirm).

### Context already established (don't re-investigate)

- `ACAPI_ProjectOperation_Open` + any `IO::Location` shape: dead end, see #791. Don't retry this path.
- `GetHotlinks` (existing command, `ProjectCommands.cpp`) already returns `location` as a plain string for hotlink module nodes, including a `teamwork://...` value when a module's source is a BIMcloud project — that's the main intended caller of this new command (open each BIMcloud-sourced hotlink module in its own instance), though the command itself should just take a plain URL/location string and not know about hotlinks at all.
- `GetArchicadLocationCommand` (`ApplicationCommands.cpp:117`) already resolves the current executable's own path — reuse it rather than re-deriving it.
- Token in any `teamwork://user:<token>@...` value is a live credential — never log it in a way a caller wouldn't already have provided themselves; the command's own error messages should avoid echoing the full URL back if avoidable, or at least this isn't a new exposure since the caller already has to pass it in.

### What needs live verification

- That a second Archicad instance, launched this way while a first instance is already running, is Archicad's normal supported "work on two Teamwork projects / two files at once" case and not something that conflicts with an existing per-port lock (Tapir's own JSON API port is per-instance, so this shouldn't be an issue, but worth confirming no single-instance assumption exists elsewhere, e.g. the `TapirUpdate_<port>.lock` per-instance locking described in CLAUDE.md — unrelated mechanism, just flagging the pattern of "per-instance" assumptions in this codebase to check against).
- Windows argument-passing behavior for `-openasplan` (only confirmed on macOS so far).
