title: Sign the Windows installer with SignPath
body:
TapirInstaller_Win.exe is now code signed through SignPath, with a certificate by SignPath Foundation, so Windows shows a verified publisher in the UAC prompt instead of "Unknown publisher".

archicad_addon.yml:
- build_installer_win writes a version resource first. SignPath's artifact configuration requires ProductName "Tapir" and ProductVersion equal to the release version on every signed file, and the PyInstaller build had none. write_version_file.py writes it from tools/package_info.json, and a step checks it before signing.
- "Decide Signing" picks the SignPath policy. A release tag (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH), pushed or dispatched by the weekly release, gets release-signing, which waits up to 3 h for a manual approval. The tag must equal the package_info version, so a signed file is never labelled with another version. A dispatch with the new signing_policy input set to test-signing, on a branch or a non-release tag, test-signs without approval and is never attached. Anything else - pull requests, forks, dispatches on main - builds without signing, as before.
- The SignPath action (v3, pinned by commit) signs the uploaded artifact, and "Verify Signature" fails the job unless a release signature is valid, by CN=SignPath Foundation, timestamped, and the version resource survived.
- The job is read-only. The action hands the job token to SignPath, which holds it for the whole approval wait, so the signed file is attached to the draft by a separate release_installer_win job with contents:write. In this repository only a release-signed installer is ever attached; if signing fails, the draft lacks it and the weekly release refuses to publish, so an unsigned installer is never released. Forks keep releasing the unsigned build.

weekly_release.yml waits up to 350 min (was 240) for the approval inside the 6 h hosted-runner cap, documents the approval and its recovery - a new run from main, never GitHub's Re-run, which reuses the old commit - and adds the "Code signing policy" footer the SignPath Foundation requires on release pages.

The installer build tools are pinned, including PyInstaller's own dependencies, in Installer/requirements-build.txt, used by both workflows and the README, so a new bootloader or hook reaches a signed release only through a reviewed change. installer_build_check.yml builds exactly like the release, without signing or secrets, and claude_auto_merge.yml now protects archicad-addon/Installer/: the signed, elevated code and its build scripts are never merged automatically.

README.md gains the Code signing policy section the Foundation requires: the attribution line, team roles, and a privacy statement describing what the installer really does on the network and on disk.

Verified locally: all workflows parse; Decide Signing gives the intended policy for ten kinds of run; a real build with the pinned PyInstaller 6.22.3 embeds ProductName Tapir and ProductVersion 1.7.1; the pinned set installs with no broken requirements; the release-notes footer renders. Not verified: the SignPath round trip itself, which needs a test-signing dispatch after merge.
author: tlorantfy

title: PR review: do not fail the check when GitHub refuses to resolve a thread on a fork PR
body:
GitHub does not let the workflow token run resolveReviewThread on a pull request from a fork - it answers "Resource not accessible by integration" even under pull_request_target with pull-requests: write. The mutation in "Resolve settled threads" was unguarded under set -e, so on every fork pull request with a thread to resolve the review check turned red although the review itself had been posted (#776, #777; issue #779).

The thread lookup now also reads isCrossRepository. A refused mutation on a fork pull request is a warning and the thread stays open; on this repository's own branches a refusal is unexpected and still fails the step, as the earlier change intended. gh's message is logged either way.

Checked by running the step's script against a stubbed gh in four scenarios: fork + refused passes with a warning, same-repo + refused fails with an error, and a successful resolve passes on both.

Fixes #779
author: tlorantfy

title: [Bug] Synchronous GitHub requests during add-on startup can hang Archicad 28
body:
## Summary

On Windows 11, Archicad 28 build 7006 INT with Tapir 1.7.0 can stop responding while opening a project. On **two separate occasions**, the Archicad process held an established HTTPS connection to an address resolving to `api.github.com`; terminating **only that TCP connection** restored responsiveness and project loading. The Archicad process was not terminated for this recovery.

No blocked-thread stack was captured, so this is strong functional evidence rather than definitive thread attribution.

## Startup paths in Tapir 1.7.0

1. In `archicad-addon/Sources/AddOnMain.cpp`, `CheckEnvironment()` calls `VersionChecker::CreateInstance(...)`.
2. The `VersionChecker` constructor calls `GetVersionFromGithub()`, which synchronously connects to `https://api.github.com`, requests `/repos/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/releases/latest`, and waits for the response.
3. Separately, `Initialize()` creates the Tapir palette, whose script-list setup can call `AddScriptsFromRepositories()`, performing additional synchronous GitHub network operations. Please review both paths.

The preference `askUpdatingAddOnBeforeEachExecution=false` does **not** suppress the request in `CheckEnvironment()`.

## Minimal mitigation tested at source level

From the exact 1.7.0 tag, I prepared an isolated patch that removes `VersionChecker::CreateInstance(...)` from `CheckEnvironment()` and changes the update menu action into an offline informational dialog pointing to the releases page. This deliberately disables automatic update detection, rather than using an async request.

Source-level checks and `git diff --check` passed. The changed `AddOnMain.cpp` compiled into Mac arm64 and x86_64 object files against AC28.3001 DevKit headers. **No Windows APX has been built, installed, or runtime-tested**, and the separate repository script loading path remains to be addressed.

A robust upstream fix would prevent **all network I/O in synchronous startup/add-on validation paths**: defer nonessential fetches until after startup, use bounded timeouts/cancellation, and/or allow an offline startup mode. Preferably there should be a tested official AC28 Windows release, avoiding an independently rebuilt add-on using the maintainer's registered MDID.

## Expected / actual

**Expected:** Archicad should launch and open projects promptly even if GitHub cannot respond.

**Actual:** On the affected setup, project opening stalls; disconnecting the specific established GitHub TCP session allows it to resume.

This issue intentionally omits project names, private filesystem paths, IP addresses, customer details, and any other private site data.

Happy to provide the minimal diff or carry out additional isolated tests if useful.
author: Keles75

title: Name and reuse inline schema enums
body:
Inline enums require downstream naming patches and can produce inconsistent generated type names. Move them into named definitions in `CommonSchemaDefinitions.json` and reuse equivalent definitions across commands.

- Name attribute field-selection and detail enums.
- Share element and geometry enums across matching read, create, and modify schemas.
- Name drawing, import/export, text/label, and MEP enums.

Preserve enum values, ordering, and requiredness. Update descriptions to separate shared enum meanings from caller-specific defaults and applicability, removing repeated wording. Distinct wall modification types and MEP filter domains remain separate.

For example, `systemConflictPolicy` now references `#/ClassificationSystemConflictPolicy` instead of repeating `{"type": "string", "enum": ["merge", "replace", "skip"]}` inline.
author: SzamosiMate

title: Reuse common identifiers and name shared geometry schemas
body:
Repeated inline identifiers and geometry objects require downstream extraction and replacement patches. Reuse equivalent existing definitions and give the remaining shared objects stable names.

- Reuse GUID identifiers, rotation coordinates, line/fill fragments, and story visibility.
- Name shared story-link, Morph, Mesh, and response-side beam-hole objects, including the Morph orientation enum.
- Name nested line, pen, and profile creation objects.

Preserve existing constraints. Update descriptions so shared geometry definitions explain the type, while references explain coordinate roles and override behavior without repeating that explanation. Beam modification holes retain their separate schema.

For example, rotation `beginPoint`, `endPoint`, and `origin` now reference `#/Coordinate2D`.
author: SzamosiMate

title: Name command payloads and classification/property update schemas
body:
Inline command objects can generate conflicting type names, particularly when creation, updates, and responses have different shapes. Give these objects explicit common definitions while preserving each role.

- Name favorites, libraries, hotlinks, IFC translators, project-info/autotext, dimension, solid-link, and interior-elevation objects.
- Name classification and property update objects, including nested availability and enum mutations; reuse GUID references inside those updates.
- Keep enum-value reads and additions separately named.

Update descriptions to distinguish shared types from creation/update behavior. For example, `HotlinkOrigin` describes the coordinate, while its uses explain that omitted `z` defaults to zero on creation and keeps the current value on modification.

For example, `HotlinkInstanceCreation` requires `hotlinkNodeId` and `origin`, while `HotlinkInstanceChange` requires only `elementId`.
author: SzamosiMate

title: Name project settings and separate geolocation read/update schemas
body:
Inline project settings and location objects require downstream naming patches. Move them into explicit definitions while retaining distinct read, creation, and partial-update shapes.

- Name drawing bounds, zoom, layout custom data, roof geometry, and design-option objects.
- Reuse `DesignOptionIdArrayItem` for the equivalent design-option input items.
- Name complete geolocation read models and their four separate update counterparts.

Update shared descriptions and remove duplication at references, keeping meaningful context such as current versus stored zoom, save prerequisites, and drawing/roof applicability at the relevant fields.

For example, a location update can still send `{"projectLocation": {"altitude": 0}}` without supplying latitude, longitude, and north. Complete read responses remain required.
author: SzamosiMate

title: Name MEP response objects and schema union variants
body:
Inline response objects and union branches force generated clients to invent type names. Move them into `CommonSchemaDefinitions.json` with explicit, reusable names.

- Name MEP elements, distribution systems, preference tables, and preference rows.
- Name the navigator window target and six element-relation variants.
- Preserve existing fields, optional fields, unconstrained strings, and union branch order.

For example, the wall-relation branch now references `#/WallRelations` instead of defining its `wallConnections` object inline.
author: SzamosiMate

title: Render field-specific description in documentation
body:
As the GitHub review bot pointed out, the documentation renderer silently discards descriptions beside `$ref`, hiding field-specific defaults and restrictions. JSON Schema 2019-09 allows these sibling descriptions, but the old renderer replaces the entire reference object with the shared definition. The codebase already uses field-specific descriptions, and I find it useful, so I opted to use that format for the last 5 PRs.

Changes:

- Display the shared description followed by the field-specific description, showing identical text only once.
- Remove redundant wording from existing description pairs that would now appear together, while keeping meaningful defaults, restrictions, and field roles.

Example:

 CreateDrawings → drawingsData[].modelOffset
   - Shared: "2D coordinate."
   - Field: "Offset of the model origin within the drawing. Defaults to the Drawing tool's current default."
   
  Note - I don't know javascript, so relied on AI. Checked in browser, seams to work fine there.
author: SzamosiMate

title: CreateHatches: support RGB foreground/background colors
body:
### Use case
I use a Tapir custom script to draw a zone area schedule next to the floor plan: one row per zone with a small solid-fill swatch, the zone name and its area. The swatch should show the **exact color of the zone's category** (`GetZoneCategories` already returns it as RGB).

Today `CreateHatches` only accepts pen indices (`fillPenIndex`, `fillBackgroundPenIndex`), so the script has to pick the closest pen of the active pen set, which is often visibly different from the zone color.

### Proposal
Add optional fields to the items of `hatchesData` in `CreateHatches`:

```json
"foregroundColor": { "red": 0.98, "green": 0.85, "blue": 0.55 },
"backgroundColor": { "red": 0.98, "green": 0.85, "blue": 0.55 }
```

Implementation hint (Archicad API, AC25+): set `hatch.foregroundRGB` / `hatch.backgroundRGB` and add `APIHatch_HasFgRGBColor` / `APIHatch_HasBkgRGBColor` to `hatch.hatchFlags`. It would also be great if `GetDetailsOfElements` returned these colors for Hatches, and `SetDetailsOfElements` could change them.

The `{red, green, blue}` (0–1) format would match `GetZoneCategories` / `GetPenTables`, so values could be passed straight through.

Thanks for Tapir, it's a great tool!
author: allatanohc-debug

title: Get/Set door & window marker settings, and Curtain Wall frame/panel class assignment
body:
## Summary
Two areas are reachable through the C++ API but not through any JSON command, official or Tapir. Today we have to edit them by hand in the settings dialogs, element by element. I'm asking for commands for both.

## 1. Door/window marker settings (read + write)
Marker parameters are not part of the opening's own GDL parameters (`GetGDLParametersOfElements` doesn't return them), and `ModifyWindows`/`ModifyDoors` only cover geometry. Examples from the Austrian library marker "F Marker AUT": dimension prefix, sill height reference, floor build-up thickness, display options.

Proposed:
- `GetMarkerParametersOfElements`: for given door/window GUIDs, return the marker library part and its parameters.
- `SetMarkerParametersOfElements`: set marker parameters (simple types: number, string, boolean, integer; no arrays needed) on existing doors/windows. The opening's own settings stay as they are.

C++ side, as far as I can tell: the main marker subelement (`API_SubElement`, `APISubElement_MainMarker`) together with `ACAPI_Element_ChangeExt` / `ACAPI_Element_GetMemo`.

Favorites are no workaround today: favorites created through the API don't contain the marker, and applying a favorite to a window fails. Bug report follows separately.

Related: #551 (marker settings replaced on CreateWindows/CreateDoors).

## 2. Curtain Wall frame and panel class assignment
`GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements` and `GetDetailsOfElements` can read CW frames and panels (#266). I found no command to change them.

Proposed:
- `ModifyCurtainWallSubelements` (or an extension of `SetDetailsOfElements`): assign a frame to an existing frame class (or a panel to a panel class) of its curtain wall, and if possible set frame class properties (type, profile attribute, width/depth).

Use case: frames with their own profile that must stay part of the CW. Today this takes a multi-step UI workflow per frame.

## Environment
Archicad 29 AUT (build 3200), Tapir 1.7.0, Windows 11. Used from scripts through `API.ExecuteAddOnCommand`.

Thanks for the great work on Tapir!
author: thespatialist

title: Bugs: flat 2D-array write silently breaks object; ApplyFavoritesToElements fails on windows; favorites don't store opening markers
body:
Environment: Archicad 29 AUT (build 3200), Tapir 1.7.0, Windows 11. Called through `API.ExecuteAddOnCommand`. All tests were run in a project copy.

## 1. Writing a 2D-array GDL parameter as a flat list breaks the object, but the command reports success
Object: "Konzeptküche" (DACH library), parameter `refLinePoints_1` (4×2 array).

- `GetGDLParametersOfElements` returns the 2D array **flat**, without dimensions: `[0.6,0,3.6,0,3,2.4,0,2.4]`.
- Writing that same flat list back with `SetGDLParametersOfElements` returns `{"success":true}`. Afterwards:
  - `GetGDLParametersOfElements` fails with -2130313215 ("Failed to get parameters of element")
  - the 2D bounding box collapses to a single point
  - every further `SetGDLParametersOfElements` call fails with the same code
- Works fine: a list of lists `[[0.6,0],[3.6,0],[3,2.4],[0,2.4]]`, or a single item via `index1`/`index2`.
- Recovery: `ApplyFavoritesToElements` with the part's favorite restores the object.

Expected: either reject a flat list for a 2D array, or report the dimensions in the Get output, so that a Get → Set round trip is safe.

## 2. ApplyFavoritesToElements fails on windows
- Target: a window ("1-Flügelfenster", DACH) placed in a wall.
- Every attempt returns -2130312311 "Failed to apply favorite to element". This includes a favorite just created from the **same window** with `CreateFavoritesFromElements`, with or without classifications/categories/properties. The window stays unchanged.
- On objects the same command works (see 1).

## 3. CreateFavoritesFromElements doesn't store the opening's marker
- Source window has a configured marker ("F Marker AUT").
- Favorite created with `CreateFavoritesFromElements`, then exported with `ExportFavorites`: the marker section is empty. `<LibPartId>` has zero GUIDs, `<UserGDLParamList/>` is empty, and AddPars holds only the window's own parameters.
- Favorite created in the Archicad UI from a window with the same marker, exported the same way: `<LibPartId>` names `W Marker AUT.gsm` / "F Marker AUT", and a second AddPars file holds all 267 marker parameters.
- So the API path drops the marker subelement, which the UI keeps.

Related: #811 (feature request for marker parameters), #551.
author: thespatialist

title: Get/Set marker parameters of existing doors and windows
body:
Split from #811 (part 1). #811 now tracks only the curtain wall frame/panel class part.

## Request
Commands to read and write the marker settings of existing Window/Door elements:

- `GetMarkerParametersOfElements`: for given door/window GUIDs, return the marker library part and its parameters.
- `SetMarkerParametersOfElements`: set marker parameters on existing doors/windows. The opening's own settings stay as they are.

Implementation, as outlined in #811: `ACAPI_Element_GetExt` / `ACAPI_Element_ChangeExt` with an `APISubElement_MainMarker` sub-element.

Parameter types: number / string / boolean / integer, matching `SetGDLParametersOfElements`. No arrays needed.

## Why
Marker parameters are not part of the opening's own GDL parameters, and `ModifyWindows`/`ModifyDoors` only cover geometry. Example: Austrian library marker "F Marker AUT" (dimension prefix, sill height reference, floor build-up thickness, display options). Today these can only be changed by hand in the settings dialog.

Related: #811, #812 / #813 (favorites don't capture or apply the marker), #551.

## Environment
Archicad 29 AUT (build 3200), Tapir 1.7.0, Windows 11. Used from scripts through `API.ExecuteAddOnCommand`.
author: thespatialist

title: Describe MEP enums and fix the design-option schema reference
body:
Unlike the previous PRs these are schema modifications/fixes that do somewhat alter behaviour. 
There is a typo fix, and 3 cases that used string as return type, but listed enum options in the description. Extractin these does tighten the contract, whitch might result in a modified error response, but no change on the happy paths. Response domains are kept separate, as they use the sentinel "Unknown" to signal error while retrieving domain.

- Use `MEPDomainOrUnknown` for routing-element, port and distribution-system response domains: `Ventilation`, `Piping`, `CableCarrier`, `Unknown`.
- Use the three-value `MEPDomain` for the optional `CreateMEPSystems` domain input and reuse it for existing domain filters and system-attribute domain items.
- Use `MEPElementType` for the eleven element types returned by `GetMEPElements` and reuse it for the existing element-type filter.
- Correct `#ref` to `$ref` in `GetElementsOfDesignOptions` response items so they resolve to `ElementsOfDesignOptionOrError`.

MEPDomain is reimplemented here, so merging might have a conflict, but wanted to separate clean and behavior altering changes.
author: SzamosiMate

title: Drawing details: read/write the "include scale in Autotext and index" flag
body:
Drawing Settings › Size and Appearance has a checkbox to include the drawing scale in Autotext and indexes. We uncheck it on a 1:1 schedule drawing placed next to a 1:200 plan, so the title block shows only 1:200. `GetDetailsOfElements` / `SetDetailsOfElements` (Drawing) cover name, numbering, scale and clipping, but not this flag, so today it needs the dialog.

Proposed: add this flag (read + write) to the Drawing details of `GetDetailsOfElements` / `SetDetailsOfElements`.

title: SetLayoutSettings: change the master layout of an existing layout
body:
`SetLayoutSettings` can set size, margins and numbering, but not the master layout. `CreateLayout` takes a master only at creation. Today a layout's master can only be changed in the Navigator.

Proposed: an optional `masterNavigatorItemId` (or master database id) in `SetLayoutSettings`, and the current master in `GetLayoutSettings`.

title: Copy 2D elements from one database to another (e.g. worksheet to worksheet)
body:
Example: copy the content of a title block worksheet into a new worksheet created with `CreateWorksheets`, keeping the coordinates. Today: open the source, select all, copy, open the target, paste. `MoveElements` / `RotateElements` work only inside the same database.

Proposed: `CopyElementsToDatabase` with source element GUIDs, a target database id and an optional offset; returns the new GUIDs. Scope: 2D elements (lines, polylines, arcs, texts, hatches, labels; drawings on layouts if possible).

title: Interactive schedules: list schedules, export/import a schedule scheme (XML)
body:
Interactive schedules have no API today. The scheme can be exported/imported as XML only through Document › Schedules › Scheme Settings › Export/Import, so every schedule change needs manual UI steps, even when the XML itself is edited by script.

Proposed:
- `GetSchedules`: list the interactive schedules of the project (name, id, navigator item id).
- `ExportScheduleScheme`: write a schedule's scheme to an XML file (same format as the UI export).
- `ImportScheduleScheme`: import a scheme XML file, as a new schedule or replacing an existing one.

Use case: per project we build the same area and green-area schedules (criteria + fields + totals). With export/import the scheme could be versioned and applied by script.

title: Interactive schedules: read the computed table values
body:
After a schedule is set up, its result (rows, columns, totals) can only be read on screen or exported by hand. Reading element properties instead is not an option for us: `GetPropertyValuesOfElements` crashes Archicad on our real project.

Proposed: `GetScheduleValues` for a given schedule: column headers, then the rows as displayed (including merged "same items" rows and totals), as strings and, where available, as numbers.

Related: the schedule export/import request (separate issue).

title: CreateZones over an existing zone opens a modal warning that blocks the API
body:
Creating a zone with `CreateZones` where an existing zone overlaps opens the modal warning about overlapping zone areas ("Warnung! … überlagernde Raumflächen" in the German UI). The command doesn't return until someone clicks the dialog, so a script hangs and every other API call is blocked.

Expected: no modal dialog during an API call. Either fail the item with an error ("overlaps existing zone"), or add an option like `allowOverlap: true/false`.

Seen first on Tapir 1.5.9, AC29 AUT. Workaround today: delete the old zone first.

Environment: Archicad 29 AUT (build 3200), Windows 11. Used from scripts through `API.ExecuteAddOnCommand`.

title: GetDetailsOfElements: support Stair elements (read stair settings)
body:
`GetDetailsOfElements`, `Get3DBoundingBoxes` and `GetGDLParametersOfElements` return errors for Stair and its subelements (Tread, Riser, StairStructure). Only `GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements` and the 2D bounding box work.

Proposed: Stair details in `GetDetailsOfElements`: baseline/walkline, number of risers, riser height, tread depth, flight width, total height, top/bottom links, structure type (e.g. monolithic/stringer), structure thickness and underside shape, tread/riser finish settings.

Use case: check a precast stair against the slab opening and the building code by script.

Related: #425, #578 (CreateStairs).

title: ModifyStairs: change settings of existing stairs
body:
There is no command to change an existing stair. `ApplyFavoritesToElements` used to move stairs (#576, fixed), but it doesn't change single settings.

Proposed: `ModifyStairs` for simple settings without new geometry: riser/tread values within the existing baseline, structure type (e.g. monolithic), structure thickness, underside shape, tread/riser finish on/off and thickness.

Depends on reading them first (separate issue: Stair support in `GetDetailsOfElements`).

title: Export the current view (or a given view) as an image for visual checks
body:
API readback confirms values and geometry, but not the final drawing: text collisions, hatch appearance, symbol orientation, graphic overrides. Today the only way to check these from a script is a screenshot of the Archicad window.

Existing commands cover other scopes: `GetElementPreviewImage` (one element), `GetRoomImage` (one zone), `GetFavoritePreviewImage`. `PublishPublisherSet` can publish saved views to PNG/PDF, but only through a pre-configured publisher set and not for the current zoom.

Proposed: `ExportViewImage`
- source: the current window, or a navigator item id
- extent: the current zoom, or an explicit model-coordinate box
- output: PNG path (or base64), resolution/DPI
- keeps the view's pens, layers, scale, graphic overrides
- returns the path plus the extent and scale actually used

Environment: Archicad 29 AUT (build 3200), Tapir 1.7.0, Windows 11. Used from scripts through `API.ExecuteAddOnCommand`.

title: SaveCurrentWindowAsImage: save the current window as PNG/JPEG
body:
Split from #829 (step 1 of the scoped design proposed there).

Proposed: `SaveCurrentWindowAsImage` with `path` and `format` (`png` / `jpeg`; optional colour depth), using `ACAPI_ProjectOperation_Save` with `API_SavePars_Picture`, following the `SaveProjectAsArchive` pattern. It renders what the current window shows (pens, layers, scale, graphic overrides). Return the path and, if available, the zoom/extent of the captured view (same data as `GetView2DTransformations`).

Out of scope for this first version: DPI, base64 output, rendering a navigator item without opening it.

title: ZoomToBox: zoom the current 2D window to a model-coordinate box
body:
Split from #829 (step 2 of the scoped design proposed there).

`FitInWindow` zooms to elements or to everything, but there is no command to zoom to a given area. Proposed: `ZoomToBox` with `xMin`, `yMin`, `xMax`, `yMax` in model coordinates for the current 2D window (floor plan, section/elevation, worksheet, layout). Together with `SaveCurrentWindowAsImage` (separate issue) this lets a script capture a chosen area for visual checks.

title: SetGDLParametersOfElements: reject mirrored size parameters on curtain wall frames instead of reporting success
body:
Split from #811 (request 2, option (a) in the bot's analysis there).

On curtain wall frames, `A`, `B`, `ac_frameWidth` and `ac_frameDepth` mirror the frame's native contour. `SetGDLParametersOfElements` returns `success: true` for them, but Archicad re-derives them from the native contour, so nothing changes (tested on Tapir 1.7.0, details in #811).

Proposed: for curtain wall frame owners, reject these parameters up front with an error that points to the native frame contour. Other frame parameters (e.g. pens) keep working as today. For invisible Boundary frames, the -2130313112 error could say that the frame has no library part.

title: Feature request: Drawing Manager data for Drawing elements
body:
# Feature request: Drawing Manager data for Drawing elements

**Title:** Drawing Manager data for Drawing elements (status, update type, stored in project, source link, renovation filter name)

## Summary

Archicad's **Drawing Manager** lists data for every drawing that Tapir does not expose yet:

- the drawing **status** (OK / Modified),
- the **update type** (manual / automatic),
- whether the drawing is **stored in the project**,
- the **source link** (internal view, external view, DWG/DXF, PDF, image …) and the **path** of an external source,
- the **renovation filter** of the source view, by name.

We are building a Python "Drawing Manager+" on top of Tapir: it lists all drawings with search, grouping and highlighting. The drawing list is complete except for these columns. Tapir already returns other drawing data through `GetDetailsOfElements` and `GetViewSettings` (scale, clipping, name/numbering type, model view options, layer combination, pen set …). The C++ API provides the remaining data too.

## Proposed additions

| Command | New field | Type | Archicad API |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GetDetailsOfElements` (Drawing details) | `status` | `"UpToDate"` \| `"Modified"` \| `"Unknown"` | `ACAPI_Drawing_CheckDrawingStatus` |
| | `manualUpdate` | boolean | `API_DrawingType::manualUpdate` |
| | `storedInProject` | boolean | `API_DrawingType::storedInProject` |
| | `linkType` | `"InternalView"` \| `"ExternalView"` \| `"Drawing"` \| `"DXF_DWG"` \| `"PDF"` \| `"Image"` \| `"PlotMaker"` \| `"AddOn"` \| `"Broken"` \| `"Other"` | `ACAPI_Drawing_GetDrawingLink` (`linkTypeID`) |
| | `linkPath` (only when there is a source file) | string | `ACAPI_Drawing_GetDrawingLink` (`linkPath->ToDisplayText ()`) |
| `GetViewSettings` | `renovationFilterName` (next to the existing `renovationFilterGuid`) | string | `ACAPI_Renovation_GetRenovationFilterName` |

All fields are optional and additive, so existing clients are not affected.

## Proposed patch

The attached `drawing-manager-details.patch` is based on commit `06a5e6e`. It changes:

- `ElementCommands.cpp`: the new Drawing fields. It also adds a `DrawingLinkTypeToString` helper. The `linkPath` / `viewPath` memory is released the same way as in Graphisoft's `Database_Control` example.
- `NavigatorCommands.cpp`: `renovationFilterName` in `GetViewSettings`.
- `MigrationHelper.hpp`: macros for the Archicad 25–26 API names:
  - `APIDb_CheckDrawingStatusID`
  - `APIDb_GetDrawingLinkID`
  - `APIAny_GetRenovationFilterNameID`
- `CommonSchemaDefinitions.json`: the new fields are added to the Drawing details and view settings schemas.

**Note:** the patch has not been compiled or tested, because we have no Windows build environment with the API DevKit. Please review it and adapt it as needed.

## Related observation

`customName` and `customNumber` in the Drawing details, and the attribute `name` fields in `GetAttributesByType`, `GetLayers` etc., are built with `GS::UniString (char*)`. This garbles accented characters, for example Hungarian ő/ű, and the built-in "Archicad Layer". Reading them through the Unicode name pointer would fix this. We reported this separately as well.

Thank you for Tapir, it is a great tool!

[drawing-manager-details.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33367844/drawing-manager-details.patch)
author: ferencz-tamas

title: CreateZoneCategories: "Failed to create." for every input, including name-only
body:
## Summary

`CreateZoneCategories` always answers `-2130313112 "Failed to create."` and creates nothing, even for the most minimal valid input.

## Steps to reproduce

```json
{ "zoneCategoryDataArray": [ { "name": "ZZ test" } ] }
```

→ `{"code": -2130313112, "message": "Failed to create."}`

I then added the optional fields one at a time; every variant fails identically:

| input | result |
|---|---|
| `{"name": "ZZ test 1"}` | Failed to create. |
| `+ "categoryCode": "10"` | Failed to create. |
| `+ "color": {"red":0.9,"green":0.9,"blue":0.9}` | Failed to create. |
| `+ "stampName"/"stampMainGuid"/"stampRevGuid"` copied verbatim from an existing Zone Category via `GetZoneCategories` | Failed to create. |

Also tried with the Floor Plan as the active window and with a Layout active — no difference.

## Why this is not a malformed request

`CreateLayers` succeeded in the same session, seconds apart, with the same minimal shape:

```json
{ "layerDataArray": [ { "name": "ZZ test kiht" } ] }
→ {"attributeIds": [{"attributeId": {"guid": "..."}}]}
```

so attribute creation in general works; the schema validator also passes (a genuinely malformed body returns `4002` with a schema path, which this does not).

`GetZoneCategories` reads the existing 9 categories correctly, including `stampName`, `stampMainGuid`, `stampRevGuid` and `color`.

## Environment

- Tapir **1.7.0** (also reproduced on 1.5.9)
- Archicad 29 INT, build 5101, macOS
- Reproduced in both a solo `.pln` and a BIMcloud SaaS Teamwork project

## Context

We are building an office template and need two measurement zone categories (gross floor area and built-up area) added programmatically; this is currently the only part of our zone setup that cannot be scripted.
author: LuisaRaadius

title: SetGDLParametersOfElements: "Failed to change parameters" for every parameter on Label and Object
body:
## Summary

`SetGDLParametersOfElements` answers `-2130312912 "Failed to change parameters of element with guid ..."` for **every** parameter I try, on **two different element types**, while reading the same parameters works.

## Steps to reproduce

Create a wall, attach an associative label, then try to set any parameter:

```json
{ "elementsWithGDLParameters": [
    { "elementId": {"guid": "<label guid>"},
      "gdlParameters": [ { "name": "AC_TextFont_1", "value": "Inter" } ] } ] }
```

→ `{"code": -2130312912, "message": "Failed to change parameters of element with guid ..."}`

Tried three different parameters on the same Label (libPart `Property Label`):

| parameter | type | value sent | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AC_TextSize_1` | RealNumber | `2.5` | Failed to change parameters |
| `AC_TextFont_1` | String | `"Inter"` | Failed to change parameters |
| `AC_bLabelFrame` | Boolean | `false` | Failed to change parameters |

And on a plain Object (our own library part), parameter `A` (Length) → same error.

## Why this is not a malformed request or a bad value

- `GetGDLParametersOfElements` on the same elements returns all 65 parameters with `isLocked: false`.
- The values I sent are inside the reported `possibleValues`: `AC_TextFont_1` lists `"Inter"` explicitly (the machine has Inter installed), and `AC_TextSize_1` is a plain RealNumber.
- Input validation passes: a genuinely wrong body returns a specific message such as `Invalid input: %s is not a GDL parameter of element %T`, which this does not.

## Environment

- Tapir **1.7.0** (also reproduced on 1.5.9)
- Archicad 29 INT, build 5101, macOS
- Reproduced in a solo `.pln` **and** in a BIMcloud SaaS Teamwork project (element freshly created in the same session, so it is ours)

## Context

We have five office Label favorites that still carry `Arial` and need to be switched to our brand font. Setting the parameter and calling `UpdateFavoritesFromElements` would do it in one script; right now the only route is doing it by hand in the UI.
author: LuisaRaadius

title: DeleteNavigatorItems reports success:true but does not delete a View Map view (Teamwork)
body:
## Summary

`DeleteNavigatorItems` returns `{"executionResults": [{"success": true}]}` for a **View Map** view that is still there afterwards. The command reports success while deleting nothing.

This is not the same as #690 / #700, which are about **Project Map** viewpoints. This is a View Map view, in a Teamwork project, and the difference is that it claims to have worked.

## Steps to reproduce

In a BIMcloud SaaS Teamwork project:

1. `CreateViewsInViewMap` → a new view in the View Map (this works)
2. `DeleteNavigatorItems` with that view's `navigatorItemId`

```json
{ "navigatorItemIds": [ { "navigatorItemId": { "guid": "D0560697-..." } } ] }
→ { "executionResults": [ { "success": true } ] }
```

3. Re-read the View Map with `GetNavigatorItemTree` → the view is still present.

Repeated six times, same guid each time, `success: true` every time, view never removed.

## What the UI says

Deleting the same view by hand in Archicad shows:

> **Cannot delete item. You must reserve the item before deleting it.**

The user reserved the item (Teamwork Status showed `Editable`) and the UI still refused, so the underlying cause may be a Teamwork access right rather than reservation. Either way, the API returned success for an operation that did not happen.

## Why this matters more than the delete itself

A silent `success: true` is worse than an error: a cleanup script believes it has tidied up and moves on. In our case several scripts reported a successful cleanup across a working session while the items were still in the project, and we only noticed much later.

Suggestion: surface the Archicad-side refusal (reservation / access right) as an error in `executionResults`, the way the UI does.

## Environment

- Tapir **1.7.0**
- Archicad 29 INT, build 5101, macOS
- BIMcloud SaaS Teamwork project
- `RenameNavigatorItem` on the same items works, so the items are addressable and the guid is right
- `DeleteNavigatorItems` **does** really delete Layouts in the same project, so the command is not broken everywhere
author: LuisaRaadius

title: CreateTexts / ModifyTexts silently ignore style.font (name); only style.fontIndex works
body:
## Summary

`CreateTexts` and `ModifyTexts` accept `style.font` as a **font name**, report success, and silently ignore it. The element keeps the current default font. `style.fontIndex` does work, so the field that is documented in the schema is the one that does nothing.

## Steps to reproduce

Create three texts, each asking for a different font:

```json
{ "textsData": [ { "coordinate": {"x":200,"y":200,"z":0},
                   "text": "x", "height": 2.5,
                   "style": { "font": "Arial" } } ] }
```

Then read each back with `GetDetailsOfElements`:

| `style.font` sent | `style.fontIndex` returned |
|---|---|
| `"Arial"` | 18 |
| `"Inter"` | 18 |
| `"Helvetica Neue"` | 18 |

All three are the current default (18 = Arial on this machine), so none of the three requests had any effect. No error, no warning.

`ModifyTexts` behaves the same:

```json
{ "textsWithDetails": [ { "elementId": {...}, "style": { "font": "Inter" } } ] }
→ executionResults success, fontIndex unchanged at 18
```

while

```json
{ "textsWithDetails": [ { "elementId": {...}, "style": { "fontIndex": 174 } } ] }
→ fontIndex 174   ✅
```

## The names are valid

They come from the font list Tapir itself reports. `GetGDLParametersOfElements` on a Label returns `AC_TextFont_1` with 684 `possibleValues`, and that list is 1-based alphabetical:

```
17  Apple Symbols
18  Arial          ← the default these texts fall back to
19  Arial Italic
...
173 Impact
174 Inter
175 Inter Italic
```

So `"Arial"`, `"Inter"` and `"Helvetica Neue"` are all names Archicad knows, and the index they map to is exactly what `fontIndex` wants.

## Why this is worth fixing

A silent ignore is worse than an error. We generated seven office text favorites with `"font": "Inter"`, the command reported success for every one, and we only discovered weeks later — by reading `fontIndex` back — that all seven had been created in the default font instead. Nothing in the response suggested anything had gone wrong.

Either resolving the name to an index, or rejecting `style.font` with a message pointing at `style.fontIndex`, would have caught it immediately.

## Side note on `fontIndex`

`ModifyTexts` with `fontIndex` is documented to rebuild the content as one paragraph, and it does: `paragraphCount` went 3 → 1 on a three-line text. It also failed outright on one multi-line text with `-2130312696 "Failed to modify the Text."` while succeeding on a two-line one in the same session, which may be worth a look on its own.

## Environment

- Tapir **1.7.0**
- Archicad 29 INT, build 5101, macOS
- BIMcloud SaaS Teamwork project
author: LuisaRaadius

title: Wish: delete/rename design options, sets and combinations; get/set a view's combination
body:
## What's missing

Tapir's design option commands (1.7.0) can create, get, move elements and set a combination's active options, but nothing can **delete or rename** an option, set or combination, or **read or set which combination a view uses**. So any script that manages alternatives has to finish in the Design Option Manager and the Quick Options bar by hand:

- deleting the options and combinations of rejected alternatives;
- renaming a combination or option when its alternative changes;
- setting a saved view's combination (Quick Options, then Redefine with Current Window Settings). `SetViewSettings` and `GetViewSettings` have no field for it, so a script can't even check what a view shows.

Seen on Archicad 29 (macOS), Tapir 1.7.0, tapir-archicad-mcp 0.6.4.

## The API is already there

The Archicad 29 C++ API (devkit 29.3100, unchanged in 30.3000) has all of it in `ACAPI::DesignOptions`:

- `DesignOptionManager`: `DeleteDesignOption`, `DeleteDesignOptionSet`, `DeleteDesignOptionCombination`, `DuplicateDesignOptionCombination`, `SetDesignOptionAsDefault`, `GetDesignOptionCombinationSettingsOf` (a view's settings)
- `DesignOption`, `DesignOptionSet`, `DesignOptionCombination`: `SetName` (and `SetId` on an option)
- `DesignOptionCombinationViewSettings`: `GetStatus` (MainModelOnly / Standard / Custom / Missing), `SetStandardCombination`, `SetMainModelOnly`

## Suggested commands

Mirroring the existing names:

- `DeleteDesignOptions`, `DeleteDesignOptionSets`, `DeleteDesignOptionCombinations` (by GUID)
- `RenameDesignOptions`, `RenameDesignOptionSets`, `RenameDesignOptionCombinations` (GUID plus new name, and id for options)
- `DuplicateDesignOptionCombinations`
- `GetDesignOptionCombinationOfViews` / `SetDesignOptionCombinationOfViews`: by navigator item id, returning or taking the status and the combination's GUID (or Main Model Only)

## Why this matters

With these, a set of alternatives (bath candidates, layout options, service routes) can be made, shown in saved views, cut down and accepted entirely by script. Today the last steps are always manual or screen-driven, and a view silently switching combination (for example after OK in the Design Option Manager) can only be caught by a screenshot.
author: BenTristem

title: Release the unsigned Windows installer when signing fails
body:
The 1.7.1 weekly release failed because the SignPath `release-signing` policy is invalid: its certificate is still a pending CSR, and the production SignPath Foundation certificate has not been issued yet. A release should not get stuck on signing, so with this change it falls back to the unsigned Windows installer.

## `archicad_addon.yml`
- `Sign Installer` and `Verify Signature` are `continue-on-error`. A new `Decide Release File` step sets the `signed` output to `true` only when SignPath signed the file and the existing signature check (valid, `CN=SignPath Foundation`, timestamped, version resource intact) passed.
- If release-signing fails for any reason (policy or certificate not usable, request denied, not approved within 3 h, or the check fails), the job still succeeds. It posts a warning, and `release_installer_win` attaches the unsigned build as `TapirInstaller_Win.exe`. A file that failed the check is never published as signed.
- If test-signing fails, the job still fails, since test-signing never releases anything.
- `release_installer_win` now runs on every tag except test-signing, and picks the signed or unsigned artifact from `signed`.

## `weekly_release.yml`

title: ModifyWalls with isAutoOnStoryVisibility hangs the Add-On (no response, no dialog) – regression in 1.7.0
body:
Archicad 29 AUT (build 3200), Tapir 1.7.0, Windows.

ModifyWalls never returns when the item contains isAutoOnStoryVisibility. After that call every TapirCommand on that Archicad instance hangs as well (API.IsAlive still answers), no dialog is open, and only restarting Archicad helps.

Reproduced 4 times on a fresh test wall (single wall, far from the building, no zone around it):
1. CreateWalls {begCoordinate {300,300}, endCoordinate {306,300}, floorIndex 1, height 2.5, thickness 0.2, referenceLineLocation Center} -> ok
2. ModifyWalls {elementId, zoneRel: "None"} -> {"success":true} immediately (control)
3. ModifyWalls {elementId, isAutoOnStoryVisibility: true} -> no response (waited > 2 min)

The same happens with isAutoOnStoryVisibility:false + visibility {...}. The wall is left unchanged.

The same call (isAutoOnStoryVisibility:true via ModifyWalls) worked for us on Tapir 1.5.9 (2026-10-01), so this looks like a regression.
Expected: the visibility change is applied, or an error is returned, but the command must not block the Add-On.

title: CreateZones with referencePosition fails on a story that is not active ("Failed to create new Zone")

Archicad 29 AUT (build 3200), Tapir 1.7.0.

An automatic zone (geometry.referencePosition) can only be created on the story that is active in the floor plan window. On any other story CreateZones returns only:
{"elements":[{"error":{"code":-2130313215,"message":"Failed to create new Zone"}}]}

title: Feature request: CreateLevelDimensions – associative level dimensions on meshes, slabs, roofs
body:
[tapir-CreateLevelDimensions.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33490827/tapir-CreateLevelDimensions.patch)

## Use case

When a terrain mesh is generated from spot heights (e.g. a DXF site survey) with `CreateMeshes`, the spot heights should be annotated the way a site plan does it: with Archicad's **Level Dimension** tool, placed as *associative* dimensions on the mesh. An associative level dimension shows the mesh height at its position, follows the mesh when it is edited, uses the project's dimension formats and can be driven by a Level Dimension favorite.

Today Tapir 1.7.x has no way to create level dimensions:

- `CreateAssociativeDimensions` / `CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection` create linear dimensions only.
- `CreateLabels` with `parentElementId` of the mesh works, but a text label carries a fixed string; the value does not follow the mesh and the label style differs from the project's level dimension favorites.
- `CreateTexts` is not associative at all.

So the workaround is to place hundreds of text labels per terrain, which become stale as soon as the mesh is edited.

## Proposal

A new command in the Elements group, following the pattern of `CreateLabels` / `CreateTexts` (`CreateElementsCommandBase`):

```jsonc
"CreateLevelDimensions": {
  "levelDimensionsData": [
    {
      "favoriteName": "Level Dimension 1.8 mm",   // optional, applied first
      "position": { "x": 12.5, "y": 7.25 },          // Coordinate2D, required
      "parentElementId": { "guid": "…" },            // optional: Mesh, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Beam, Column, Wall, Object …
      "level": 73.5,                                 // optional, static value when no parent is given
      "floorIndex": 0,                               // optional, default: floor of the parent / current floor
      "layerIndex": 12,                              // optional
      "pen": 3, "textPen": 3, "textHeight": 1.8,     // optional
      "dimForm": 0, "needPlus": false,               // optional, marker type 0–9 of the tool settings
      "markerSize": 3.0, "angle": 0.0,               // optional, mm / rad
      "origin": "ProjectZero"                        // optional: ProjectZero | ReferenceLevel1 | ReferenceLevel2 | StoredOrigin | Altitude
    }
  ]
}
```

Response: `elements` (`ElementIdsOrErrors`), like the other `Create*` commands.

Mapping to the API: `API_LevelDimensionType` with `parentType`/`parentGuid` set from the parent element's header (`API_ZombieElemID` without a parent, which measures the floor), `loc` = position, `staticLevel` = false with a parent, `dimForm`, `needPlus`, `markerSize`, `angle`, `origin`, `note1.noteSize`/`notePen` for the text, then `ACAPI_Element_Create`. Favorites work through the existing `ApplyFavoriteToElementDefaults` path of the base class.

Additionally `GetDetailsOfElements` could return a `LevelDimensionDetails` object for `LevelDimension` elements (`position`, `level`, `staticLevel`, `ownerElementId`, `ownerElementType`, `dimForm`, `needPlus`, `pen`, `textHeight`, `textPen`, `markerSize`, `angle`, `origin`), so a script can read back the value Archicad computed.

## Draft implementation

A draft is attached as a patch against `main` (commit 55b618a, 2026-10-15): `tapir-CreateLevelDimensions.patch`. It adds

- `CreateLevelDimensionsCommand` in `ElementCreationCommands.{hpp,cpp}` (schema + `SetTypeSpecificParameters`),
- the registration in `AddOnMain.cpp` (Elements group),
- a `LevelDimension` case in `GetDetailsOfElements` plus `LevelDimensionDetails` / `DimensionOrigin` in `CommonSchemaDefinitions.json`,
- `Examples/create_level_dimensions.py` (one associative level dimension at the centre of every mesh).

It compiles for Archicad 29 on macOS (arm64, API DevKit 29.3000) and `tools/generate_addon_docs.py` runs clean. **It has not yet been run in Archicad**: in particular it still has to be confirmed that `ACAPI_Element_Create` computes `level` from the parent at `loc` (as the tool does when clicking on a mesh) and that the dimension updates when the mesh changes. This can become a PR once the behaviour is confirmed, or be reshaped if you prefer a different form for the command.

## Environment

- Archicad 29 (macOS, Apple Silicon), Tapir 1.7.0; the command list of 1.7.1 (released 2026-10-15) and of `main` has no level dimension command either
- Typical data set: several hundred spot heights per terrain mesh, created with `CreateMeshes` with sublines

title: Add GetQuantitiesOfElements command
body:
## Summary

Adds a new Element command, `GetQuantitiesOfElements`, that returns the quantities Archicad itself calculates for elements (volumes, surfaces, lengths, heights, perimeters, opening areas…) via `ACAPI_Element_GetQuantities`, so scripts no longer need property expressions to read them.

- Supported types: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Zone, ColumnSegment, BeamSegment. Each type gets its own response schema (`WallQuantities`, `SlabQuantities`, …) in `CommonSchemaDefinitions.json`.
- For composite and complex-profile elements, `composites` lists every skin with its building material, volume, projected area, core/finish flags and, when Archicad attaches one, the sub-element (column/beam segment).
- Optional `minOpeningSize` input controls the conditional values (Archicad uses it for walls).
- Unsupported types, unknown GUIDs and missing `elementId` give a per-item error; the rest of the batch still succeeds.
- Example: `archicad-addon/Examples/get_quantities_of_elements.py` prints a small bill of quantities of walls and slabs per building material.
- Registered with version 1.7.2.

Note: the mask is always passed explicitly (`ACAPI_ELEMENT_QUANTITIES_MASK_SETFULL`). The API documentation says a `nullptr` mask is allowed when both `elements` and `composites` are set, but in Archicad 30 it crashed with an access violation inside `ACAPI_Element_GetQuantities`.

## Testing

Built locally on Windows for AC25, AC29 and AC30 (AC26–AC28 not built locally: v142 toolset missing; relying on the build check).

Tested in Archicad 30 (30.0.0 R1 3001) with `TestProject.pla` plus a Roof, a Shell and a Morph:

- The example script runs and prints totals per element type and building material.
- All 10 supported types return their quantities; the field sets match the schemas.
- A composite Shell returns its 6 skins, and the skin volumes sum to the element volume.
- An Object returns "Quantities are not supported for this element type", an unknown GUID returns "Failed to find element in Archicad", and a missing `elementId` returns an error. Archicad stays up.

Not done: no `Test/ExpectedOutputs/get_quantities_of_elements.py.output` is committed yet, so `test_examples.py` will record it on its first run instead of comparing. Not tested on macOS.

title: Add MEP electrical commands (Archicad 30 electrical API) and MEP system/fitting-table reads
body:
Archicad 30's DevKit adds a full electrical API under ACAPI::MEP: ElectricalPanel, ElectricalCircuit, ElectricalDevice, ElectricalProjectSettings, and the ElectricalPanelDefault / ElectricalDeviceDefault placers. None of it is wrapped by Tapir yet. The current MEP commands (CreateMEPElements etc.) only accept MEPComponentType = Terminal, Accessory, Equipment, Fitting.
This issue asks for JSON commands covering the electrical API, plus a few read-only piping/system additions. Everything new must sit behind #ifdef ServerMainVers_3000 (electrical) or the matching guard for the AC29 classes, and should follow the existing patterns in MEPCommands.cpp and registration in AddOnMain.cpp.
Part A — Electrical reads (priority, read-only)
[ ] GetElectricalPanels: for each panel, return element id, panel name, circuit name prefix, circuit id style, circuit ids, parent circuit id, anchor point, orientation, connected load and demand load (total and per phase A/B/C).
DevKit: ElectricalPanel::Get, GetPanelName, GetCircuitNamePrefix, GetCircuitIdStyle, GetCircuitIds, GetParentCircuitId, GetAnchorPoint, GetOrientation, GetConnectedLoad[PhaseA/B/C], GetDemandLoad[PhaseA/B/C]
[ ] GetElectricalCircuits: by circuit ids or panel ids. Return name with prefix, description, owner panel id, child device ids, child panel ids, voltage, phase string, wiring type name, connected/demand load (total and per phase), voltage drop and estimated cable length.
DevKit: ElectricalCircuit::Get… (GetCircuitNameWithPrefix, GetCircuitDescription, GetOwnerPanelId, GetChildDeviceIds, GetChildPanelIds, GetVoltage, GetPhaseString, GetWiringTypeName, GetConnectedLoad*, GetDemandLoad*, GetVoltageDrop, GetEstimatedCableLength)
[ ] GetElectricalDevices: return element id, parent circuit id, anchor point, orientation, rotation, reflected, size, object id, apparent power (+ enabled flag), load classification name, demand load, directly connected MEP element ids.
DevKit: ElectricalDevice::Get…
[ ] GetElectricalProjectSettings: default voltage, wiring type names with cross-sectional area, load classification names with demand factor.
DevKit: GetElectricalProjectSettings, GetVoltage, GetWiringTypeNames, GetWiringTypeCrossSectionalArea, GetLoadClassificationNames, GetLoadClassificationDemandFactor
[ ] Make GetMEPElements / GetElementsByType recognise electrical panels and devices so they can be discovered without knowing ids.
Part B — Electrical writes
All writes go inside ACAPI_CallUndoableCommand and use the Modify (…Modifier&) pattern already used for routing elements. Return per-item ExecutionResult / error, like other batch commands.
[ ] CreateElectricalPanels: place from CreateElectricalPanelDefault → Place; inputs: position, orientation, optional library part / object id, size, panel name, circuit prefix.
[ ] CreateElectricalDevices: place from CreateElectricalDeviceDefault → Place; inputs: position, orientation, optional object id, size, apparent power, load classification, optional circuit id to connect to.
[ ] ModifyElectricalPanels: SetPanelName, SetCircuitNamePrefix, SetCircuitIdStyle, AddCircuit, RemoveCircuit, SetAnchorPoint, SetOrientation, SetBaseRotation, SetReflected, size, object id.
[ ] ModifyElectricalCircuits: SetCircuitDescription, SetVoltage, SetWiringTypeName, SetIsPhaseAUsed / B / C.
[ ] ModifyElectricalDevices: SetApparentPower, SetApparentPowerEnabled, SetLoadClassificationName, SetAnchorPoint, SetOrientation, SetBaseRotation, SetReflected, size, object id.
[ ] ConnectToElectricalCircuits: array of {elementId, circuitId}; works for devices (ElectricalDevice::Modifier::ConnectToCircuit) and sub-panels (ElectricalPanel::Modifier::ConnectToCircuit).
[ ] ModifyElectricalProjectSettings: SetVoltage, AddWiringType / RemoveWiringType, AddLoadClassification / RemoveLoadClassification.
Part C — Piping / systems (read-mostly)
[ ] GetMEPPreferenceTables: extend (or add GetMEPFittingPreferenceTables) to also return pipe and duct elbow, branch and transition tables, plus GetPipeReferenceSet / GetDuctReferenceSet and GetPipeAngleSet / GetDuctAngleSet. Today only segment tables are returned.
[ ] GetPhysicalSystems / GetSystemGroups: names, domain/category, root element, member systems (GetSystemGroupIDs, GetSystemIDs, GetName, GetRootElementId, GetSystemCategory).
[ ] CreatePhysicalSystems / CreateSystemGroups: PhysicalSystem::Create, CreateSystemGroup, SetRootElement, SetSystemCategory; optional CreateLabelOnElement.
Out of scope
UI managers, SystemBrowserCalculationCallbackInterface, modifying fitting/duct/cable-carrier preference tables.
Acceptance
New commands registered in AddOnMain.cpp with version and description, schemas in the shared schema definitions, and entries in the command docs / Python examples where other MEP commands have them.
Builds for all supported AC versions; electrical commands compile only for AC30 and are absent from older builds.
If the whole scope doesn't fit one PR, ship Part A first as its own PR.
Reference
AC30 DevKit (30.3000) docs: class_a_c_a_p_i_1_1_m_e_p_1_1_electrical_*, group___m_e_p.html in https://graphisoft.github.io/archicad-api-devkit/

title: Add read-only electrical commands for Archicad 30 (#862, part A)
body:
Part A of #862: read-only access to the Archicad 30 electrical API.

## New commands (MEP group, available from Archicad 30)

- **GetElectricalPanels**: panel name, circuit name prefix and ID style, circuits, parent circuit, placement (anchor point, orientation, rotation, mirroring, library part, size), and connected and demand loads (total and per phase). Takes an optional `elements` list; without it, it returns every panel.
- **GetElectricalCircuits**: name, description, owner panel, child devices and panels, voltage, phases, wiring type, connected and demand loads, voltage drop and estimated cable length. Takes circuits (`elements`), panels (`electricalPanels`), or nothing for all circuits.
- **GetElectricalDevices**: parent circuit, placement, apparent power, load classification, demand load and directly connected MEP elements. Takes an optional `elements` list.
- **GetElectricalProjectSettings**: project voltage, wiring types (with cross-sectional area) and load classifications (with demand factor).

`GetMEPElements` also lists electrical panels and devices now (types `ElectricalPanel` and `ElectricalDevice`). Their domain is empty, as for Equipment, because the MEP domain enum has no electrical value.

On Archicad 25–29 the commands compile and return "This command requires Archicad 30 or newer."

## Note

`ACAPI_Element_GetElemList (API_ExternalElemID)` returns no electrical elements. In a project with 5 electrical elements it returned 0. They are therefore collected by class ID (`API_ElemType (ElectricalPanelID)` / `ElectricalDeviceID`).

## Testing

Tested in Archicad 30 on a project with two panels, two circuits and three outlets:
- Loads add up as expected. A 200 VA outlet with the Sockets classification (demand factor 0.5) plus an unclassified 200 VA outlet gives 400 VA connected and 300 VA demand on the circuit.
- The wiring type, phases, parent circuit and child devices match what Archicad shows.
- Bad GUIDs, and GUIDs of the wrong element type, return an error item for that element.
- All responses validate against the new schema definitions.
- Builds without errors or warnings for AC30, AC29 and AC25. AC26–28 are left to CI.

Example: `Examples/get_electrical_data.py`. It has no expected output, because TestProject has no electrical elements.

One thing I couldn't confirm is the unit of `voltageDrop`. It is passed through exactly as the API returns it.

Parts B and C of #862 (write commands) are not included.

Refs #862

title: Add CreateCurtainWalls command
body:
# Add CreateCurtainWalls command

## Motivation

Tapir can create most construction elements (walls, columns, beams, slabs, roofs, stairs, meshes, openings), but not Curtain Walls. Reading them works (`GetDetailsOfElements` and `GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements` report segments, frames and panels), creating them has to be done by hand. The Archicad API supports it: `ACAPI_Element_Create` with `API_CurtainWallID`, the reference polyline in the memo, the column and row pattern in `cWSegPrimaryPattern` / `cWSegSecondaryPattern` and the cell assignment in `cWSegPatternCells` (see `Element_Test ‚Ä∫ Do_CreateCurtainWall_UsingPattern` in the DevKit examples).

This PR adds `CreateCurtainWalls`, following the pattern of the other `Create*` commands (`CreateElementsCommandBase`, so `favoriteName`, undo and the `elements` response come from the base class). Scripts can then generate a mullion-transom facade as a real Curtain Wall element instead of imitating it with columns and beams.

## What the command does

Input: `curtainWallsData`, an array of curtain walls. Per item:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `coordinates` (required) | 2D reference polyline on the floor plan; every pair of consecutive coordinates is one segment. |
| `favoriteName` | Curtain Wall favorite applied to the tool defaults first (frame and panel classes, surfaces, boundary and corner frames, pattern, base level). |
| `zCoordinate` | Absolute elevation of the bottom. When omitted, the base level of the favorite or the tool defaults is kept. |
| `floorIndex` | Optional; derived from `zCoordinate` when that is given (`ResolveFloorIndexAndOffset`, as in `CreateStairs` and `CreateColumns`), otherwise the current story. |
| `height` | Optional; the favorite's or tool default's height is kept when omitted. |
| `primaryPattern` | Column pattern: `sizes[]` (m), `logic` (`FixedSizes` or `BestDivision`), `origin` (`StartWithPattern`, `StartFromCenter`, `AlignToCenter`, `EndWithPattern`), `flexibleIndices[]` (columns `BestDivision` may stretch; default all). |
| `secondaryPattern` | Row pattern, same shape. |
| `cells[]` | Panel and frame classes per cell of the pattern unit: `columnIndex`, `rowIndex`, `panelClassIndex`, `rightPanelClassIndex`, `leftFrameClassIndex`, `bottomFrameClassIndex`, `crossingFrameType`, `crossingFrameClassIndex`. The unit repeats along and up the segment, so an assignment applies to every repetition of that cell. |

Everything except `coordinates` is optional, so the simplest call places a curtain wall with the tool defaults along a line.

The frame and panel classes are not created by the command; they come from the favorite or the tool defaults, and the cells reference them by Archicad's class numbering (panels: 0 = no panel, 1 = first panel class; frames: 0 = merged, 1 = Division, 2 = Corner, 3 = Boundary, 4 = first custom frame class). The class indices in `cells` are validated against the number of classes of the curtain wall, pattern sizes must be positive, and consecutive identical coordinates are rejected.

New common schema definitions: `CurtainWallPattern`, `CurtainWallPatternCell`, `CurtainWallPatternLogic`, `CurtainWallPatternOrigin`, `CurtainWallCrossingFrameType`.

## Example

```python
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateCurtainWalls', {
    'curtainWallsData': [{
        'coordinates': [{ 'x': 0.0, 'y': 0.0 }, { 'x': 8.0, 'y': 0.0 }, { 'x': 8.0, 'y': 6.0 }],
        'height': 7.0,
        'primaryPattern': { 'logic': 'BestDivision', 'sizes': [1.5, 1.5] },
        'secondaryPattern': { 'logic': 'FixedSizes', 'sizes': [1.0, 2.5] },
        'cells': [
            { 'columnIndex': 0, 'rowIndex': 0, 'panelClassIndex': 2 },
            { 'columnIndex': 1, 'rowIndex': 0, 'panelClassIndex': 0, 'bottomFrameClassIndex': 0 }
        ]
    }]
})
```

`archicad-addon/Examples/create_curtain_walls.py` has three calls (defaults only, fixed-size grid, two segments with best division and assigned cells) and reads the panels back with `GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements`.

## Tested

Built for AC29 on macOS (arm64) without warnings; `tools/generate_addon_docs.py` evaluates the new schemas. Run against Archicad 29 (German) on a local project with a test script that creates curtain walls and reads them back through `GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements`, `GetDetailsOfElements` and `Get3DBoundingBoxes`:

- Defaults only: a curtain wall with the tool default's pattern, classes (two panel classes, two custom frame classes plus boundary frames) and height.
- Fixed sizes: `[1.25]` columns and `[0.9, 2.1]` rows at height 6 on a 5 m line give 4 √ó 4 panels with column starts at 0 / 1.25 / 2.5 / 3.75 and row starts at 0 / 0.9 / 3.0 / 3.9.
- Cell assignment: a 2 √ó 2 unit with sizes `[1, 2]` √ó `[1, 2]`; `panelClassIndex: 0` on cell (1, 0) produces Archicad's hidden "deleted panel" at x 1‚Äì3 / z 0‚Äì1, `panelClassIndex: 1` on cell (0, 1) puts the first panel class (glass) at x 0‚Äì1 / z 1‚Äì3. So the memo's `cWSegPatternCells` are ordered row by row from the bottom row, column index running fastest - that is the mapping the command uses.
- Two segments around a corner with `BestDivision` `[1.5, 1.5]` on a 7 m segment: 4 equal columns (two whole units), the corner is mitred by Archicad.
- Base level: `zCoordinate: 4.0` lands on floor 1 (story level 4.0) with the bounding box at z 4.0‚Äì7.5; `zCoordinate: -1.0` on floor ‚àí1 (story level ‚àí3.4) with the bottom at ‚àí1.0; `floorIndex` without `zCoordinate` keeps the default base level on that floor. On creation Archicad places the base surface by `planeOffset`, not by `storyRelLevel` (that one is read back correctly but ignored by `ACAPI_Element_Create`), so the command sets both.
- `favoriteName` with the project's Curtain Wall favorites: pattern, classes and height come from the favorite, an explicit `height` / `zCoordinate` override it, an unknown name is reported per item.
- A crossing frame on a cell of a 1-column unit splits that cell in every repetition of the unit (2 columns √ó 3 rows + 2 diagonals = 8 panels), with the left and right panel classes as given.
- Errors: identical coordinates, non-positive sizes, unknown logic, flexible index, column/row index or class index out of range are all reported per item, nothing is created for that item.
- All created elements could be deleted with `DeleteElements`; the example script runs as is.

## Not covered (deliberately left for later)

- Creating or editing frame and panel classes (profiles, materials, GDL panels such as windows or doors in the facade); use a favorite for that.
- Curved segments (`arcs`), inclined curtain walls (`angle`), boundary frame position, the panel offset from the reference line, and the "infill" panel of an incomplete `FixedSizes` pattern.
- Junctions and accessories.
- The `NumberOfDivisions` pattern logic (a given `sizes` list with that logic is switched to `FixedSizes`).
- A `ModifyCurtainWalls` counterpart.
- Unrelated, noticed while testing: `CreateFavoritesFromElements` fails for a Curtain Wall ("Failed to create the favorite"), so a favorite for this command has to be saved in Archicad.

## Notes for reviewers

- The pattern's `flexibleIDs` are always rewritten (all columns/rows flexible unless `flexibleIndices` is given), because the defaults' flexible indices belong to the default pattern.
- The pattern cells of the defaults are reused when the pattern is unchanged; with a new pattern every cell starts from the first default cell.
- Only AC29 was built and run locally; the Curtain Wall memo API used here is the AC22+ one, so AC25‚ÄìAC30 should compile unchanged, which CI will show.

title: Add electrical write commands for Archicad 30 (#862, part B)
body:
Part B of #862: electrical write commands for Archicad 30.

**This builds on #863 (Part A).** Until #863 is merged, this PR also shows its commits. The Part B changes are the commits after the merge of `feature/862-electrical-reads`, plus the first "WIP" commit.

## New commands (MEP group, available from Archicad 30)

- **CreateElectricalPanels**: places panels from the defaults of the Electrical Panel tool. Optional inputs: orientation, rotation, mirroring, library part, size, panel name, circuit name prefix and circuit ID style.
- **CreateElectricalDevices**: places devices from the defaults of the Electrical Device tool. Optional inputs: orientation, rotation, mirroring, library part, size, apparent power, load classification, and a circuit to connect to.
- **ModifyElectricalPanels**: panel name, circuit naming and placement (anchor point, orientation, rotation, mirroring, library part, size).
- **ModifyElectricalDevices**: apparent power, load classification and placement.
- **CreateElectricalCircuits / DeleteElectricalCircuits**: `AddCircuit` and `RemoveCircuit` of the owning panel. They are separate commands rather than part of ModifyElectricalPanels, so that the IDs of new circuits can be returned. A new circuit can be given a description, voltage, wiring type and phases straight away.
- **ModifyElectricalCircuits**: description, voltage, wiring type and the used phases.
- **ConnectToElectricalCircuits**: connects devices, and panels as sub-panels, to circuits.
- **ModifyElectricalProjectSettings**: sets the voltage and adds or removes wiring types and load classifications. Removals are applied first, so one call can replace an entry.

Creation runs in one undoable command. Modifications use the `Modify` pattern of the routing element commands. Results are reported per item.

## Archicad behaviours handled

Archicad gives no error in these cases, so the commands check for them:
- An unknown library part, load classification or wiring type is ignored, and the old value is kept. These are reported as errors.
- Duplicate names in the electrical project settings are accepted. Adding an existing name is refused.
- Some library parts, for example the outlet, calculate their own size and ignore `xSize` / `ySize`. A create command removes the element it just placed and reports the error. A modify command keeps the other changes and reports that the size was not applied.

## Testing (Archicad 30)

- Every field was checked against the values read back with Part A.
- Placement was checked against the element's 3D geometry (`Get3DGeometryOfElements`):
  - anchor height, rotation (0°, 45°, 90°, 180°) and mirroring of panels and devices;
  - panel sizes.
- Loads add up through sub-panels. A main panel feeding a kitchen panel with a 2000 VA socket on "Kitchen" (0.7), plus 40 VA and 60 VA lights, gives 2100 VA connected and 1500 VA demand.
- Deleting a circuit disconnects its devices and sub-panels. Undo in Archicad restores them.
- Invalid IDs and wrong element types return per-item errors.
- `Examples/create_electrical_system.py` runs repeatedly without errors.
- Builds without errors or warnings for AC30, AC29 and AC25 on Windows. AC26–28 and macOS are left to CI.

Grasshopper components for the electrical commands are not included.

Refs #862

title: Add MEP fitting preference tables and physical systems (#862, part C)
body:
Part C of #862: MEP fitting preference tables and physical systems. It is independent of Parts A (#863) and B and is based on `main`.

## GetMEPPreferenceTables (extended, still from Archicad 28)

The existing `tables` output (the circular segment tables) is unchanged. New outputs:
- `referenceSet`: the reference IDs (nominal sizes) of the domain, from `GetPipeReferenceSet` / `GetDuctReferenceSet`.
- `angleSet`: the angles of the domain, from `GetPipeAngleSet` / `GetDuctAngleSet`. Archicad 29 and newer.
- With the new optional input `includeFittingTables: true`, also:
  - `elbowTables`: reference ID, angle, diameter, radius, description;
  - `branchTables`: main and branch reference IDs and diameters, branch angle, length, branch offset, connection length, description;
  - `transitionTables`: begin and end reference IDs and diameters, plus length (piping) or angle (ventilation), description. Archicad 29 and newer.

Angles are in degrees and sizes in metres. On Archicad 28 the elbow and branch rows have no angle, because the AC28 API doesn't have one.

## Physical systems (Archicad 29 and newer)

- **GetMEPSystemGroups**: the system groups with their physical systems. Each system has its name, root element and MEP system attribute, which is the system category.
- **CreateMEPSystemGroups**: creates system groups by name.
- **CreateMEPPhysicalSystems**: creates physical systems in a group, optionally with a root element and an MEP system. If either can't be set, the new system is removed again and an error is reported.

Notes:
- `CreateLabelOnElement`, mentioned in the issue, does not exist in the AC29 or AC30 DevKit, so it isn't included.
- Archicad keeps a root element only while it is part of an MEP network. The root of a stand-alone element, for example equipment with nothing connected, is cleared the next time the MEP networks are recalculated. A duct root is kept. This is documented in the schema, and the example uses a duct.

## Testing (Archicad 30)

- **Preference tables:** the default project has 6 piping and 1 ventilation table of each kind. The reference sets have 41 pipe and 23 duct sizes, and the angle sets match what Archicad shows. Every response validates against the new schemas.
- **Groups and systems:** created systems are read back with their root element and MEP system. Bad group IDs, bad MEP system IDs and bad root elements return per-item errors, and nothing is left behind.
- **Examples:** `Examples/mep_systems.py` is new and `Examples/get_mep_preference_tables.py` is extended. Both run without errors.
- **Builds:** no errors or warnings for AC30, AC29 and AC25 on Windows. AC28 (which needs the v142 toolset, not installed here), AC26–27 and macOS are left to CI.

## Found while testing, not changed here

The existing commands that return `mepSystemId`, such as GetMEPRoutingElements and GetMEPPorts, return `{"attributeId": {"guid": …}}`, but the schema says `#/AttributeId`, which is `{"guid": …}`. The new commands follow the schema. Fixing the existing commands changes their output, so it should be a separate change.

Refs #862
