title: Grasshopper components for the new Tapir commands, and sync with changed commands
body:
Adds Grasshopper components for the Tapir commands that had none, and brings existing components in line with commands whose schema changed since 1.5.0.

## New components (45)

Every user-facing Tapir command now has a component. Not covered on purpose: `GenerateDocumentation` (developer tool), `SetElementNotificationClient` / `RemoveElementNotificationClient` (add-on notification plumbing) and `ShowScriptUI` / `GetScriptUIResult` (Archicad dialogs).

- **Electrical (Archicad 30), MEP group (13):** GetElectricalPanels, GetElectricalCircuits, GetElectricalDevices, GetElectricalProjectSettings, CreateElectricalPanels, CreateElectricalDevices, CreateElectricalCircuits, ModifyElectricalPanels, ModifyElectricalCircuits, ModifyElectricalDevices, DeleteElectricalCircuits, ConnectToElectricalCircuits, ModifyElectricalProjectSettings. Shared code is in `ElectricalComponentHelp.cs`. Batch inputs take 0, 1 or one value per item.
- **Design options (Archicad 29) (6):** Rename and Delete for design options, option sets and option combinations.
- **Navigator (2):** Get3DProjectionSettings, Set3DProjectionSettings (perspective).
- **Project (1):** SaveCurrentWindowAsImage.
- **Teamwork (5):** ReserveLockableObjectSet, ReleaseLockableObjectSet, LockableObjectSetStatus, ReserveHotlinkCacheManagement, ReleaseHotlinkCacheManagement.
- **Elements (4):**
  - MarkerParameters / SetMarkerParameters
  - ElementQuantities (GetQuantitiesOfElements)
  - CreateCurtainWalls, on `CreateElementsComponentBase`, with patterns as trees and cells as parallel trees.
- **IFC (1):** SetIFCPropertiesOfElements. It only works on Archicad 25–27, and the component now reports the add-on's error on newer versions.

Each component has a new GUID and a 24x24 icon. The icons are derived from the closest existing icon with a corner badge.

## Components synced with changed commands

The flattened input/output schemas of 1.5.0, 1.6.0 and current `main` were diffed and compared with the component code.

- **Broken, fixed:** CreateFavoritesFromElements sent `{"elementId":{"elementId":{...}}}`, which the command always rejected. It now sends the plain element id and has a new optional `Folders` input.
- **New inputs/outputs.** All are appended at the end; no existing parameter was renamed, reordered or given a new GUID, so saved definitions keep their wiring.
  - **Walls:**
    - CreateWalls: Heights and Thicknesses are now optional, plus AdditionalSettings for the new wall fields.
    - ModifyWalls: ReferenceLineLocations.
  - **Beams and columns:**
    - CreateBeams and CreateColumns: building material, profile, circle-based and AdditionalSettings.
    - ModifyBeams and ModifyColumns: sizes, anchors, circle-based, material and profile.
  - **ModifySlabs:** ReferencePlaneLocations.
  - **Texts and labels:**
    - CreateTexts, LabelElements, ModifyTexts and ModifyLabels: font names.
    - LabelElements also gets LabelClasses.
    - TextDetails and LabelDetails: a FontNames output.
  - **CreateHatches:** foreground and background colours.
  - **MEP:**
    - Create, Modify and Get MEP routing elements: cross-section reference id and preference table.
    - GetMEPSystems: material and insulation material.
  - **Stories:** GetStories outputs index and IFC id. SetStories takes a first-story index.
  - **Properties:** CreatePropertyDefinitions takes enum values. GetAllProperties outputs expression-based flags and expressions.
  - **Design options:** GetElementsOfDesignOptions now outputs error messages instead of dropping failed items.
  - **RenameNavigatorItem:** a `CustomName` switch; off resets the item to "By Project Map".
  - **SetViewSettings:** structure display, renovation filter, 3D style, rendering scene and photo rendering.
- **Shared bases:**
  - `CreateElementsComponentBase` gains Color, NumbersTree and IntegersTree field kinds, dotted JSON keys, trailing AdditionalSettings and a `CompleteItem` hook.
  - `ModifyElementsComponentBase` gains trailing fields.
  - Existing derived components behave as before.

## Other fixes

- **Whole-command errors:** `TryGetCadResponse` now turns a Tapir result holding nothing but `{"error":…}` into a component error. Before, a command failing as a whole, for example on an older Archicad, produced empty outputs with no message. Per-item execution results are unaffected.
- **Add-on schema:** `ViewSettings.renovationFilterGuid` is now `{"guid": …}`, which is what GetViewSettings writes and SetViewSettings reads. The plain-string schema made every SetViewSettings call that used it fail validation. This is the only change outside the plugin.

## Testing

- **Build:** the plugin builds for `net7.0` with 0 errors and 0 warnings using the .NET 8 SDK on Linux. The Windows targets (`net48`, `net7.0-windows`) are left to the Grasshopper build check.
- **Review:** an independent pass compared every key, nesting, required field, enum and response field each new or changed component sends or reads against the add-on schemas and C++. Its findings are fixed in the last commit.
- **Not run in Rhino/Grasshopper or against Archicad.**

## For the maintainer to confirm

- Units of the 3D projection angles (azimuth, view cone, roll). The DevKit doesn't state them; the components pass the values through unchanged.
- The new Teamwork Reserve/Release components need the Execute button. The existing ReserveElements / ReleaseElements and Teamwork Send / Receive components run on recompute.
- New Modify inputs that take enum values (anchor points, reference line/plane locations) have no auto-attached value list. An attached list always sends its value, which would silently change elements.

title: Add graphic override rule and combination commands
body:
Adds commands for graphic override rules and combinations (Document > Graphic Overrides), from Archicad 27, where the `ACAPI_GraphicalOverride_*` functions first appear. On Archicad 25 and 26 they return a "requires Archicad 27" error.

## Commands (new `GraphicOverrideCommands.cpp`, in Attribute Commands)

- **GetGraphicOverrideRules**: every rule with its id, name, rule group name, criterion XML and style.
- **CreateGraphicOverrideRules**: creates rules by name in a rule group, given by name. The group is created if it doesn't exist yet. Criterion and style are optional. Returns an id or an error per rule.
- **ModifyGraphicOverrideRules**: changes the name, criterion or style of rules. A given style replaces the whole style.
- **DeleteGraphicOverrideRules**
- **GetGraphicOverrideCombinations**: every combination with its rules, in priority order.
- **CreateGraphicOverrideCombinations**: creates combinations from existing rules. Returns an id or an error per combination.

## Style

The new common `GraphicOverrideStyle` maps `API_OverrideRuleStyle`. A field that is left out is not overridden.
- Line type, fill type and surface are `#AttributeId`s. An unknown guid, or one of the wrong attribute type, gives a per-item error.
- Pens are pen indices.
- The background pen and the surface can each be a pen or attribute, or an RGB color (`fillBackgroundPen` / `fillBackgroundColor`, `surface` / `surfaceColor`). Giving both is an error.
- `…AppliesTo` and `hiddenContours` choose the cut, cover and drafting fills, or the cut and uncut surfaces.

Rule and combination ids follow the attribute pattern: `GraphicOverrideRuleId` = `{guid}`, plus `…ArrayItem` and `…OrError` definitions in `CommonSchemaDefinitions.json`.

Criteria are passed through as the XML Archicad saves override rules in. There is no structured criterion editor; the API only offers the XML. A rule created without `criterionXML` gets Archicad's default criterion for new rules.

Deleting a rule also removes it from the combinations that contain it (that's Archicad's behaviour; the description says so).

## Testing (Archicad 30)

A test script ran every command against a new project and validated every input and output against the command schemas, including the common definitions:
- **Built-in data:** the built-in rules and their criterion XML and styles are read correctly, every rule has its group name, and all 9 built-in combinations are listed.
- **Create rules:** a rule with every style field set reads back the same. Colours come back at Archicad's 16-bit precision (0.25 becomes 0.24999). A pen background with a surface colour also round-trips. New rule groups are created and assigned. A duplicate name, an empty name, a fill guid given as a line type, and both `surface` and `surfaceColor` each give a per-item error and leave nothing behind.
- **Modify:** rename, criterion and style replacement work. A duplicate name, an unknown id and a bad attribute each give a failed result and leave the rule unchanged.
- **Combinations:** created with their rules in order. A duplicate name and an unknown rule give errors, and an empty rule list is allowed.
- **Delete:** works, and an unknown id gives a failed result.
- **Examples:** all six run without errors on a project with no leftovers from earlier runs, which is what the test runner gives them.
- **Builds:** no errors or warnings (`/W4 /WX`) for AC30 and AC29 on Windows. AC25–AC28 need the v142 toolset, which isn't installed here, so they and macOS are left to CI.
- **Docs:** `tools/generate_addon_docs.py` parses all the new schemas. The docs aren't committed; the release regenerates them.

The command skeletons (schemas, registration, parameter parsing, examples) were generated with the scaffolder proposed in the separate tools PR. Only the API calls in `Execute` and the style mapping were written by hand.

title: tools: add new_command.py scaffolder
body:
Proposes `tools/new_command.py`, a standard-library script that writes the repetitive part of new JSON commands from a short spec. This is a workflow change, so it's the maintainers' call. If it isn't wanted here, it works fine as a local tool, because what it writes is plain house-style C++.

## Why

Each command is about 140 lines. In #870 (13 electrical commands), the schemas, constructor and `GetName` were about half of the code, and `Execute` was the other half. The script writes everything except the Archicad API calls inside `Execute`.

## What it writes

- **Header:** the class declaration in `Sources/<file>.hpp`.
- **Source:** constructor, `GetName`, `GetInputParametersSchema`, `GetRawResponseSchema` and an `Execute` skeleton in `Sources/<file>.cpp`. The skeleton has parameter parsing, the per-item loop with one result per input item (for `executionResults`, `elements`, or an array of `#…OrError` ids) and `continue` on a missing field, `API_Guid` conversion of `{guid}` id fields, the `ACAPI_CallUndoableCommand` scope and the `ServerMainVers_XX00` guard.
- **Registration:** the `RegisterCommand` call in `AddOnMain.cpp`, with the version from `tools/package_info.json`.
- **Example:** a starter script in `archicad-addon/Examples/`.
- **New file:** when `file` names a group file that doesn't exist yet, it creates the `.hpp`/`.cpp` pair and the `#include`. CMake already globs the sources.

The spec uses a compact schema notation (`"#Coordinate3D | description"`, `"field?"` for optional fields, `enum(A,B)`, `[item, "description"]`). Output shortcuts are `executionResults` and `elements`. The full format is in the docstring. Use `--schemas` to print the expanded schemas and `--dry-run` to print the code.

It only appends: a command whose class already exists is skipped, so running it twice changes nothing. It keeps each file's line endings.

## Checked

- **Schemas:** specs for 5 merged electrical commands (`ConnectToElectricalCircuits`, `ModifyElectricalCircuits`, `CreateElectricalPanels`, `GetElectricalCircuits`, `DeleteElectricalCircuits`) expand to the same input and response schemas as the merged code.
- **Build:** the same 5, generated under new names, compile with no warnings (`/W4 /WX`) for AC30 and AC29 before any TODO is filled. So does the new-file path.
- **Docs:** `tools/generate_addon_docs.py` parses the generated schemas.
- **Real use:** #873 (graphic override commands, tested in Archicad 30) was scaffolded with it. The loops it then needed by hand (create with id-or-error results, delete with `#…ArrayItem` items) are now generated too, and the 6 commands regenerated under new names also compile with no warnings.

`CLAUDE.md` gets a two-line pointer under "Adding or changing a command".

title: Add CreateLevelDimensions command
body:
Closes #859

## Motivation

Tapir has no way to create Level Dimensions (the Level Dimension tool of the floor plan). `CreateAssociativeDimensions` and `CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection` create linear dimensions only, and a text label created with `CreateLabels` on a mesh carries a fixed string that does not follow the mesh. A typical case is a terrain mesh generated from spot heights with `CreateMeshes`: the spot heights should be annotated with associative level dimensions that show the mesh height at their position and update when the mesh is edited.

This PR adds `CreateLevelDimensions`, following the pattern of the other `Create*` commands (`CreateElementsCommandBase`, so `favoriteName`, undo and the `elements` response come from the base class).

## What the command does

Input: `levelDimensionsData`, an array of level dimensions. Per item:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `position` (required) | Location of the marker on the floor plan. With a parent it has to lie on that element; outside the parent's outline Archicad still creates the dimension, but without a height (level reads -110000000). |
| `parentElementId` | Element the dimension is associated with (Mesh, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph ‚Ä¶). Sets `parentType` / `parentGuid` from the element header and the floor of the parent. Without it the dimension refers to the floor (`API_ZombieElemID`). |
| `level` | Fixed level value in meters (absolute), only used without a parent. The value is kept, although Archicad reads `staticLevel` back as false. |
| `favoriteName` | Level Dimension favorite applied to the tool defaults first. |
| `floorIndex`, `layerIndex` | Optional overrides. |
| `pen`, `textPen`, `textHeight` | Marker pen, text pen and text height in mm (`note1` / `note2`). |
| `dimForm` | Marker type 0‚Äì19 as Archicad stores it. The API docs say 0‚Äì9, but Archicad 29 favorites use 11 and 16‚Äì19; values above 19 are silently replaced by 0, so they are rejected. |
| `needPlus`, `markerSize`, `angle` | Plus sign, marker size in mm, rotation in radians. |
| `origin` | `ProjectZero`, `ReferenceLevel1`, `ReferenceLevel2`, `StoredOrigin` or `Altitude` (`API_DimOriginID`). |

`GetDetailsOfElements` now also returns `typeSpecificDetails` for `LevelDimension` elements (`LevelDimensionDetails`): `position`, `level` (the value the dimension shows), `staticLevel`, `ownerElementId` / `ownerElementType` for an associative one, `dimForm`, `needPlus`, `pen`, `textHeight`, `textPen`, `markerSize`, `angle`, `origin`.

New common schema definitions: `LevelDimensionDetails`, `DimensionOrigin`.

## Example

```python
aclib.RunTapirCommand ('CreateLevelDimensions', {
    'levelDimensionsData': [{
        'parentElementId': meshId,
        'position': { 'x': 12.5, 'y': 7.25 },
        'dimForm': 0,
        'textHeight': 1.8
    }]
})
```

`archicad-addon/Examples/create_level_dimensions.py` places one associative level dimension at the centre of every mesh and reads the details back.

## Tested

Built for AC29 on macOS (arm64); `tools/generate_addon_docs.py` evaluates the new schemas (docs not committed, they are regenerated with the release). Run against Archicad 29 (German) on a local project:

- A tilted test mesh with a known plane: associative level dimensions at four points read back exactly the plane height (3.00 / 4.40 / 4.50 / 3.05), with `ownerElementId` / `ownerElementType: Mesh`. A picture of the floor plan window shows the same values.
- Moving the mesh up by 1 m: all four dimensions show the new height, the markers stay in place. Moving it sideways: the markers move with the mesh. Deleting the mesh deletes its level dimensions.
- `favoriteName` with the project's Level Dimension favorites: marker type, marker size, text and layer come from the favorite; an item without `favoriteName` after one with it gets the tool defaults again; explicit `textHeight` / `layerIndex` override the favorite; an unknown name is reported per item.
- All optional fields read back as given (`dimForm`, `needPlus`, `markerSize`, `angle`, `pen`, `textPen`, `textHeight`, `origin`); a larger `textHeight` is visibly larger on the plan.
- Without a parent: the dimension shows the floor level (floor 1 ‚Üí 4.00), with `level` the fixed value, also on an upper floor.
- `dimForm` 0‚Äì19 are kept, higher values are replaced by 0 by Archicad (hence the schema maximum).
- Errors: unknown parent, unknown origin, negative or too large `dimForm` are reported, nothing is created for that item.
- Volume: a terrain mesh from a real site survey (497 spot heights, 486 single-point sublines) and one associative level dimension with a favorite at every spot height: created in 0.4 s, all 497 show their spot height with no deviation, and again after moving the mesh up by 0.5 m.
- Everything created could be deleted with `DeleteElements`.

## Notes for reviewers

- Only AC29 was built locally. `API_LevelDimensionType` with `parentType` as `API_ElemType` exists since AC26; the `ServerMainVers_2600` guard follows `CreateLabels`, so AC25 should compile as well, which CI will show.
- A `ModifyLevelDimensions` counterpart is not included.

title: Feature request: Get/Set view commands
body:
# Feature request: expose the complete set of view settings (incl. 3D cut planes, 3D Document and 3D window settings) through Get/Set view commands

## Summary

`GetViewSettings` / `SetViewSettings` currently expose only a small subset of what Archicad stores in a saved view.
I would like Tapir to make **everything that is available through the Archicad API** about a view readable and writable,
with special attention to the settings that are stored with 3D views and 3D Documents:
**3D cutting planes, filter-and-cut settings, 3D projection/camera, 3D window settings and the custom (per-view) attribute sets.**

In addition, `Set3DCutPlanes` should be able to **clear** the cut planes, and there should be a way to **store the current 3D window settings into a view**
(the equivalent of the *"Redefine image settings based on current"* checkbox in the *View Settings* dialog).

## Motivation / use case

I am building an automated "exploded axonometry" workflow: the model is sliced storey by storey with 3D cut planes,
every slice is saved as a separate view in the View Map and placed as a Drawing on a layout (`CreateViewsInViewMap`, `CreateDrawings`, `UpdateDrawings`).

The workflow cannot be completed with the current commands:

1. `Set3DCutPlanes` changes the cut planes of the **currently open 3D window** only.
2. `CreateViewsInViewMap` clones the **Project Map item** (`ACAPI_Navigator_CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap`), so the new view carries the cut planes stored in the Project Map item, not the ones just set in the 3D window.
3. The *View Settings* dialog shows that a saved 3D view stores *"3D projection/camera settings (incl. zoom), custom sun position, 3D cutting and cut planes"*, but `GetViewSettings` / `SetViewSettings` do not return or accept any of them, so there is no way to read or assign the cut planes of a saved view or 3D Document from a script.
4. There is no Tapir way to tell Archicad "redefine the stored image settings of this view from the current window", which in the UI is a single checkbox.
5. The cut planes cannot be removed again: `Set3DCutPlanes` rejects `null`, `{}` and an empty array (`Invalid parameter: cutPlanes.`), so a script cannot restore the window to "no cut". The workaround I used was setting two far-away planes (±5000 m).

The same gaps affect any automation that needs to produce view variants (section-like 3D views, phasing images, per-storey axonometries, reproducible presentation sets).

## Current behaviour (verified in the Tapir source)

| Item | Where | Observation |
|---|---|---|
| `GetViewSettings` | `NavigatorCommands.cpp`, `GetViewSettingsCommand::Execute` | Returns only: `modelViewOptions`, `layerCombination`, `dimensionStyle`, `penSetName`, `graphicOverrideCombination`, `drawingScale`, `saveZoom`, `ignoreSavedZoom`, `zoom` (if `saveZoom`), `rotation`, `structureDisplay`, `renovationFilterGuid`, `d3styleName`, `renderingSceneName`, `usePhotoRendering`. |
| `SetViewSettings` | `NavigatorCommands.cpp` | Uses the same `#/ViewSettings` schema, so the same limited set. |
| `Set3DCutPlanes` | `3DCutPlaneCommands.cpp` | Calls `ACAPI_View_Get3DCuttingPlanes` + `ACAPI_View_Change3DCuttingPlanes` on the current 3D window. Schema requires `minItems: 1`; an empty list returns `APIERR_BADPARS`. `isCutPlanes` is always set to `true`, never `false`. Only `pa/pb/pc/pd` are written (`cutStatus`, `cutPen`, `cutMater`, `useCustom`, `customPen`, `customMater` are ignored). |
| `CreateViewsInViewMap` | `NavigatorCommands.cpp` | Clones a Project Map item via `ACAPI_Navigator_CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap`, then sets `isIndependent` and the name. |
| `Get/Set3DProjectionSettings` | `3DProjectionCommands.cpp` | `ACAPI_View_Get3DProjectionSets` / `Change3DProjectionSets` on the current 3D window only (perspective + axonometric parameters). |
| 3D Document | — | No command reads or writes `API_DocumentFrom3DType`. |

Note: `Get3DProjectionSettings` / `Set3DProjectionSettings` (perspective and axonometric parameters of the current 3D window) already exist on `main` (`3DProjectionCommands.cpp`). They act on the **current 3D window** only, not on a stored view or 3D Document, so the gaps below remain.

## Proposed change

### 1. Extend `GetViewSettings` / `SetViewSettings` (`#/ViewSettings`)

Return and accept **all** fields of `API_NavigatorView`, including the *"stored in this view"* flags, which are essential to interpret the other values:

| New / extended field | `API_NavigatorView` member | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `saveFlags` object: `zoom`, `displayOptions`, `layers`, `drawingScale`, `dimensions`, `penSet`, `structureDisplay` | `saveZoom`, `saveDispOpt`, `saveLaySet`, `saveDScale`, `saveDim`, `savePenSet`, `saveStructureDisplay` | Today only `saveZoom` is returned. |
| `customModelViewOptions` | `modelViewOpt` (`API_ModelViewOptions*`) | Used when the view stores custom (unnamed) model view options. |
| `customLayerStatus` | `layerStats` | Layer states stored in the view when no layer combination name is used. |
| `customDimensionPreferences` | `dimPrefs` (`API_DimensionPrefs*`) | Stored dimensioning settings when custom. |
| `customPens` | `pens` | Stored pen colours when custom. |
| `transformation` (full 2D matrix) | `tr` | Today only the derived `rotation` angle is returned. |

### 2. New: read/write the 3D data stored with 3D views and 3D Documents

Add `GetView3DSettings` / `SetView3DSettings` (or put the data in a `view3D` object inside `ViewSettings` for 3D view items and 3D Document items).
The Archicad API already provides this for 3D Documents (since Archicad 26):

```
ACAPI_View_GetDocumentFrom3DSettings    (API_DatabaseUnId*, API_DocumentFrom3DType*)
ACAPI_View_ChangeDocumentFrom3DSettings (API_DatabaseUnId*, API_DocumentFrom3DType*)
```

`API_DocumentFrom3DType` contains exactly what is needed:

| JSON property (proposal) | API member |
|---|---|
| `cutPlanes[]` with `pa, pb, pc, pd`, `pen`, `material`, plus `enabled`, `useCustomAttributes`, `customPen`, `customMaterial` | `cutSetting` (`API_3DCutPlanesInfo`, `API_3DCutShapeType`) |
| `cutaway3D` | `cutaway3D` |
| `filterAndCut`: `firstStory`, `lastStory`, `allStories`, `trimToStoryRange`, `filterMode`, `marqueeFilter`, `elementTypeFilter` | `filterAndCutSettings` (`API_3DFilterAndCutSettings`) |
| `projection`: `isPerspective`, `cameraGuid`, `cameraSet`, perspective parameters or axonometric parameters | `projectionSetting` (`API_3DProjectionInfo`, `API_PerspPars` / `API_AxonoPars`) |
| `window`: `setWindowSize`, `width`, `height`, `setZoom`, zoom scale and displacement | `window3DInfo` (`API_3DWindowInfo`) |
| `uniformCutAttributes`, `planConnectivity` (current / intended), `effects3D`, `drawRect` | `attributeOptions`, `currPlanConn`, `intPlanConn`, `effects3D`, `drawRect` |

Notes on the API (checked in the AC28 DevKit headers):

- `ACAPI_View_GetDocumentFrom3DSettings` / `ACAPI_View_ChangeDocumentFrom3DSettings` take a database unique ID and return `APIERR_BADDATABASE` if the database is not a 3D Document. The database ID can be obtained from the navigator item (as `GetDatabaseIdFromNavigatorItemId` already does). `ChangeDocumentFrom3DSettings` is documented as a **non-undoable data structure modifier**, so it should not be wrapped in `ACAPI_CallUndoableCommand` the way `Set3DCutPlanes` currently is.
- For **stored 3D views** (not 3D Documents) I found **no** API that reads or writes the stored cut planes directly:
  - `ACAPI_View_Get3DCuttingPlanes` / `ACAPI_View_Change3DCuttingPlanes`, `ACAPI_View_Get3DProjectionSets` / `ACAPI_View_Change3DProjectionSets` and `ACAPI_View_Get3DImageSets` / `ACAPI_View_Change3DImageSets` have **no view or database parameter**; they act on the current 3D window.
  - `API_NavigatorView` (used by `ACAPI_Navigator_GetNavigatorView` / `ChangeNavigatorView`) and the `API_NavigatorViewSettingsFlags` enum contain no cut plane, projection or filter-and-cut member.
  - Yet the *View Settings* dialog of Archicad says the saved view stores "3D vetítés/kamerabeállítások, egyéni nappozíció, 3D vágás és vágósík" (3D projection/camera, custom sun, 3D cut planes), so the data exists but is not reachable through the documented API.
- Possible workaround to investigate: open the stored view in the 3D window (`ChangeWindow`), then use the current-window functions above. This is **untested**, and storing the changed window settings back into the view still has no API equivalent of the *"Redefine image settings based on current"* checkbox. If no such API exists, this request needs a corresponding addition from Graphisoft (ACAPI); Tapir can then expose it. Part 4 below should be read in that light.
- 3D Documents are not affected by this gap: their cut planes are available through `API_DocumentFrom3DType::cutSetting`.

### 3. `Set3DCutPlanes` improvements

- Allow **clearing**: accept `"cutPlanes": null` or `[]` and set `isCutPlanes = false` (keeping the shapes handle empty).
- Add `Get3DCutPlanes` (read the current window's cut planes, including `isCutPlanes`, `useCustom`, `customPen`, `customMater`).
- Allow the optional `cutPen`, `cutMater`, `useCustom`, `customPen`, `customMater` properties.
- Document the sign convention (which side of the plane is kept) in the command description.

### 4. Store the current window settings into a view

Add a command (e.g. `RedefineViewImageSettings` or a flag on `SetViewSettings`, such as `"redefineImageSettingsFromCurrentWindow": true`) that does what the checkbox
*"Redefine image settings based on current"* does in the View Settings dialog: store the 3D projection/camera, sun position and 3D cut planes of the current 3D window in the selected view.

Alternatively, let `CreateViewsInViewMap` take an optional `"copyImageSettingsFromCurrentWindow": true` so a new view can be created directly from the current 3D window.

## Acceptance criteria

1. For a saved 3D view and for a 3D Document, `GetViewSettings` (or the new 3D command) returns the stored cut planes, projection and filter-and-cut settings, and `SetViewSettings` writes them back; a round trip (`Get` → `Set` → `Get`) returns identical data.
2. The `save*` flags are returned for every view and respected on write.
3. `Set3DCutPlanes` can switch cut planes off again, and `Get3DCutPlanes` reports the current state.
4. A Python example script is added (`archicad-addon/Examples/`) that: sets two horizontal cut planes, stores them in a new View Map view, creates a Drawing from it on a layout, and clears the cut planes of the window afterwards.
5. The new and extended response schemas validate against the MCP wrapper.
6. Commands carry the version `main` currently carries; version-dependent API calls are guarded (`ACAPI_View_GetDocumentFrom3DSettings` requires Archicad 26 or later).

## Notes and open questions

- The JSON names above are proposals; please align them with existing Tapir conventions (`pa/pb/pc/pd` for cut planes are already used by `Set3DCutPlanes`).
- Teamwork projects: changing view settings modifies the navigator item, so the usual reserve/ownership rules apply to the View Map.
- Unit conventions: cut-plane `pd` is in meters in the Tapir command today. Please keep that and state it in the schema description.
- I verified the structures and function signatures against the AC28 DevKit headers (`APIdefs_Navigator.h`: `API_NavigatorView`; `APIdefs_Environment.h`: `API_3DCutPlanesInfo`, `API_3DCutShapeType`, `API_3DProjectionInfo`, `API_3DFilterAndCutSettings`, `API_3DWindowInfo`, `API_DocumentFrom3DType`; `ACAPI_Environment.h`, `ACAPI_Navigator.h`). I did not compile or run any C++ for this request. Not yet tested on a real project: clearing the cut planes with `isCutPlanes = false`, writing `API_DocumentFrom3DType` back, and the window-switch workaround.

## Environment

- Archicad 28 (teamwork project), Tapir Add-On (current `main`), used through the JSON interface and through the Archicad MCP wrapper.
author: ferencz-tamas

title: Fix the palette reading its preferences past the buffer and crashing on non-UTF-8 script output
body:
## Problem

1. `SaveScriptsToPreferences` stores the script list without its terminating null (`strlen` bytes), and `AddScriptsFromPreferences` builds a `GS::UniString` from the raw pointer, so it reads past the end of its buffer. On my machine (Archicad 29, Japanese Windows) the heap garbage made GSRoot's UTF-8 assert (`Unicode.cpp` line 343) fire at startup in every session from July. The bug reports (`BugReporting-29\*.RPT`) show the stored selection index followed by garbage as the assert data. The assert's report path converts the same string again and can recurse into a stack overflow, which crashed Archicad once (`0xc00000fd` in GSRoot.dll).
2. The script output reader converts the pipe bytes with `CC_UTF8`. Python writes to a pipe in the system code page unless told otherwise (cp932 tracebacks on Japanese Windows), and a multi-byte character can be split at a read-chunk boundary, so the same assert can fire there.

## Fix

- Store the terminator, read into an `nBytes + 1` buffer and take the length from `nBytes`, so blobs written by older builds still load. The code page is unchanged.
- New `SafeUTF8String` replaces every byte that does not start a well-formed UTF-8 sequence (Table 3-7 of the Unicode Standard, so overlong forms and surrogates are rejected too) with `?` before the script output becomes a `UniString`.
- `std::unique_ptr<char[]>` for the two `new char[]` buffers (they were `std::unique_ptr<char>`, which calls `delete` instead of `delete[]`).

## Testing

- A slightly different version of this fix (it also switched the stored text to UTF-8) has been in my own build since 2026-08-16, on Archicad 29 and 30 (Windows, Japanese). Since then the bug reports no longer show this assert coming from the palette.
- This branch builds for Archicad 30 on Windows (Visual Studio 2022, toolset v143) without errors or warnings. I have not built the other versions or macOS locally.
- `SafeUTF8String`, compiled on its own, was run against 24,581 inputs (random bytes, every lead byte with boundary second bytes, cp932 and UTF-8 text): every output is valid UTF-8, and valid UTF-8 input comes back unchanged.

author: ooki-atsufumi

title: Add creation parameters and fix curved beams and box morphs
body:
These come from my own build, where I have used them in daily work on Archicad 29 and 30. This is the second of a few PRs that bring those additions upstream (the first one is #877).

## New parameters

| Command | Parameter | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| CreateColumns | `slantAngle`, `isSlanted`, `slantDirectionAngle` | Slanted columns. Same rule as CreateBeams and SetDetailsOfElements: a non-zero `slantAngle` makes the column slanted, unless `isSlanted` is given explicitly. |
| CreateMeshes | `buildingMaterialId` | Building material of the mesh. Its top, side and bottom surface overrides are cleared, also one left in the Mesh tool defaults, so the mesh shows the building material's own surface and follows it. |
| CreateTexts | `layerIndex` | Layer of the text. Like the other create commands, only a positive index takes effect. |
| CreateWindows, CreateDoors | `libraryPartName` | Places a library part by its localized name (docu_UName), also one that has no favorite, such as a shutter or a grille. It is applied to the tool defaults before they are cloned, the same way as `favoriteName`. |
| SaveProject | `projectPath` | Saves the project to a .pln path, as File > Save As does. This saves an untitled project, or one opened from an older Archicad version, which cannot be saved in place (`APIERR_READONLY`). A path to the project's own file takes the plain save, which keeps the refusal of a project opened read-only. SaveProject had no input schema; it now has one. |
| CreateLayout | `paperWidth`, `paperHeight` | Paper size in mm of the new layout, and of the master layout when the command creates it from `masterLayoutName`: a new master starts with the template's default size (A1 in the Japanese template), and `layoutParameters` only sizes the new layout, not its master. An existing master keeps its size. |
| CreateMorphs | `topExpansion` | For `size` (box) morphs: grows the top rectangle by this amount on all four sides, which makes a frustum, for example an excavation with sloped sides. |

## Fixes in the same code

- **CreateMorphs with `size`, surface:** on AC27 and later the faces' surface override got the building material index (`material = buildingMaterial`), so an unrelated surface was shown and `surfaceId` had no visible effect. The faces now get the surface of `surfaceId`, or no override when it is not given.
- **CreateMorphs with `size`, solid:** the bottom face ran in the same direction as the side faces, so the morph was not a closed solid and solid element operations (subtraction) failed on it. The bottom face is now reversed, so every edge runs in opposite directions in its two faces.
- **CreateBeams:** `arcAngle` and `verticalCurveHeight` had no effect, because `beamShape` stayed straight. A non-zero value now sets the matching curved shape. Both fields also got a description.

## Left out

My build also had `materialIndex` on CreateMEPSystems. It is not in this PR, because the existing `materialId` does the same.

## Testing

- This branch builds for Archicad 30 and 29 on Windows (Visual Studio 2022, toolset v143) without errors or warnings. The other versions and macOS are left to CI.
- I have not run it against TestProject.pla. The same code has been in my own build since mid-2026, where I use it on Archicad 29 and 30 (Windows, Japanese): box morphs subtracted from site meshes for excavations (98 of 98 subtractions worked after the bottom-face fix), meshes colored by building material, shutters placed by name, layouts with a given paper size on masters that start as A1, and Save As of Archicad 29 files on Archicad 30.
- Compared with my build, I renamed `slantDirection` to `slantDirectionAngle` and added `isSlanted` to match SetDetailsOfElements, made the slant and curve switches depend on a non-zero value, and left the master layout's margins as they are (my build also set them to 10 mm).

## Changes after the review (689c020b)

- CreateMorphs: `surfaceId` is resolved once. The box faces take the surface that `ApplyMorphCosmeticDetails` already put into `element.morph.material`, so the unreachable error branch is gone.
- CreateWindows / CreateDoors: `libraryPartName` has to name a window or a door library part (`APILib_WindowID` / `APILib_DoorID`); another part type is refused with `APIERR_BADPARS` before the tool defaults change.
- CreateLayout: `paperWidth` / `paperHeight` only size a master layout that the command creates. An existing master keeps its size, since the layouts already on it depend on it.
- The comment of `ApplyWindowOrDoorFavoriteToDefaults` no longer says that placing a library part by name is not possible.
- New example `Examples/creation_parameters.py`: a slanted column, a curved beam, a frustum morph and a text on a chosen layer, read back with GetDetailsOfElements.
- `API_FileSavePars` and the one-argument `ACAPI_ProjectOperation_Save` are unchanged: the CI built the first commit of this PR for Archicad 25 to 30 on Windows and macOS, and `MigrationHelper.hpp` adds the overload before Archicad 27.

## Second review round (2add2acd)

- SaveProject: when `projectPath` is the open project's own file (compared with `API_ProjectInfo::location`), the plain save runs instead of a Save As, so a project opened read-only is still refused.
- CreateMeshes: `buildingMaterialId` clears the three surface overrides instead of overriding them with the building material's surface, so the mesh stays tied to its building material.
- CreateLayout: when the paper size of a master the command just created cannot be set, the item now reports an error instead of creating a layout whose size its master does not have.
- The mesh fields (`buildingMaterial`, `topMat`, `sideMat`, `botMat`) compiled for Archicad 25 to 30 on Windows and macOS in the CI run of 689c020b. A cleared override is a value-initialized `API_OverriddenAttribute`: an empty `APIOptional` from Archicad 27, `overridden = false` before.
- The new SaveProject helper leaves the pointers of `API_ProjectInfo` to its destructor, as GetProjectInfo does.
- Grasshopper inputs for the new parameters are not part of this PR; they can follow.

## Third review round and a run on Archicad 30 (59dd6412, a9ea79ce)

- CreateMeshes resolves `buildingMaterialId` with `ResolveAttributeIndex` from the same file.
- SaveProject compares `projectPath` with the project's location as text without case, like the hotlink source lookup in the same file.
- CreateWindows / CreateDoors: the `typeID` check of the first round refused real windows on Archicad 30, where every library part reports `APILib_ObjectID` (GetAvailableLibraryParts lists no window or door among about 10,000 parts). The DevKit describes the typeID-based distinction as obsolete next to the subtype hierarchy and lets the typeID select a subtype in a search, so the search now gets the window or door `typeID` together with the name, and only a part of that subtype is found.

Run on Archicad 30.0.0.3001 (Windows, Japanese) with a local build that merges the open PRs (#878 to #883):

- `Examples/creation_parameters.py`: a slanted column (`isSlanted` true, `slantAngle` 1.30), a horizontally curved beam (`arcAngle` 0.50) and a text on the requested layer.
- SaveProject: the own path, given in upper case with forward slashes, took the plain save (the project path stayed as it was). A new path saved the project there, and the project then referred to the new file.
- CreateWindows with `libraryPartName` placed the simple window opening and a wall window, and CreateDoors a shutter with a side door; GetDetailsOfElements shows the requested library parts. A shutter panel object, a window part given to CreateDoors and an unknown name were refused.

title: Add GetGridElementDefaults, GetGridElements and CreateGridElements
body:
Third of the PRs that bring the additions of my own build upstream (after #877 and #878).

## New commands (Element Commands, 1.7.2)

- `GetGridElementDefaults`: the Grid Tool defaults, that is the library part, size and GDL parameters a new grid element gets.
- `GetGridElements`: every grid element of the project with its position, angle, length, size, library part and, on request, its GDL parameters.
- `CreateGridElements`: grid elements from begin and end coordinates. The line length goes where the Grid Tool's grid marker takes it, the GDL parameter `AC_Length`; for a library part without it, to the A size, converted to `xRatio` as in CreateObjects. `lengthMode: none` leaves the length to `parameters`. Story, layer and GDL parameters are optional; parameters that could not be set are reported in `warnings`.

Grid elements are the elements the Grid Tool places: `API_ObjectID` elements with the `APIVarId_GridElement` ('GREL') variation, driven by a library part. Unlike gridlines drawn as lines, circles and texts, they show their bubbles in sections automatically, keep associative dimensions and are exported to IFC as grids. Neither the JSON API nor Tapir could list or create them so far.

## Notes

- `ACAPI_Element_GetElemList` with the grid element type ignores the variation and returns every object (elevation and story level markers came back too), so GetGridElements scans `API_ObjectID` and keeps the 'GREL' variation.
- The Grid Tool defaults can look different from a grid drawn with the tool (a short line with a leader to the bubble). The description of `parameters` says how to get the same look: copy the parameters of a drawn grid (GetGridElements with `includeParameters`).
- The commands need Archicad 26 or later; on Archicad 25 they return `APIERR_NOTSUPPORTED`.
- Example: `Examples/grid_elements.py`. It has no expected output yet; the first test run records it.

## Testing

- Builds for Archicad 30 and 29 on Windows (Visual Studio 2022, toolset v143) without errors or warnings. The other versions and macOS are left to CI. `tools/generate_addon_docs.py` evaluates the new schemas.
- I have not run it against TestProject.pla. The same code has been in my own build since 2026-10-12. On Archicad 29 I used it for the grids of a building model: the bubbles showed in sections, associative dimensions to the grid ends followed when a grid was moved, and an IFC 2x3 export contained them as grids.
- Compared with my build, the two Get commands got full response schemas (they had plain objects), a debug field was removed from the GetGridElements response, and `layerIndex` only takes effect when positive, like in the other create commands.

## Changes after the review (851c9ec8)

- The Grid Tool's grid marker draws the length given in its GDL parameter `AC_Length`; its A size does not change the line. `lengthMode: length` (the new default, it was `xRatio`) writes the line length there, and only for a library part without `AC_Length` to the A size.
- When A or B change (that fallback, or `parameters`), `xRatio` and `yRatio` are converted as in CreateObjects: the size itself with `useXYFixSize` on, otherwise the size divided by the library part's own A/B, so they agree with A and B in the memo. The raw `xRatio` / `yRatio` inputs are gone.
- GetGridElements and GetGridElementDefaults return `length` (from `AC_Length`, or the A size computed from `xRatio`) and `useXYFixSize`; `xRatio` and `yRatio` are described as stored. The parameters are read for every grid, since the length comes from them.
- Still open: whether the Grid Tool default has `useXYFixSize` on needs a running Archicad. The scripts I use on Archicad 29 always set `AC_Length`, with the other parameters copied from a grid drawn with the tool, which matches the new default.

## Run on Archicad 30

Run on Archicad 30.0.0.3001 (Windows, Japanese) with a local build that merges the open PRs (#878 to #883):

- `Examples/grid_elements.py` created the two grids with a 20 m line each and read them back with GetGridElements (`length` 20, from `AC_Length`).
- The open point above is settled for this template: GetGridElementDefaults returns `useXYFixSize` true for the Grid Tool default (library part 標準通り芯マーカー, `length` 14.15).

## Maintainer's fixes (ab94b877)

This branch now includes the maintainer's `claude/resolved-pr-879` (ab94b877, a fast-forward): the `parameters[].value` input is untyped with a description, and GetGridElementDefaults and GetGridElements return top-level errors with `CreateErrorResponse`.

title: Add graphic override rule and combination commands
body:
Fourth of the PRs that bring the additions of my own build upstream (after #877, #878 and #879).

## New commands (new group Graphic Override Commands, 1.7.2)

- `CreateGraphicalOverrideRule`: creates a graphic override rule in a rule group, which is created when it does not exist (default name `Tapir`), or overwrites the rule of the same name wherever it is (rule names are unique in the project). It sets the criterion XML, a color for the cut and uncut surfaces, a pen for lines, markers and texts, and whether the contours follow.
- `GetGraphicalOverrideRules`: every rule with its rule group and criterion XML.
- `CreateGraphicalOverrideCombination`: a combination of rules given by name, or the rules of the combination of the same name replaced.

The JSON API and Tapir had no way to create override rules or combinations. The official Archicad 30 MCP can create a combination from existing rules, but not the rules themselves.

## The criterion XML

Archicad keeps a criterion only in its own XML format. GetGraphicalOverrideRules returns that XML for a rule made in the GUI; with its values changed, it can be passed to CreateGraphicalOverrideRule to make similar rules. XML written from scratch is dropped without an error, and the rule then applies to all elements. Because the command still reports success in that case, the descriptions say so.

## Notes

- IDs are returned as `{guid}` objects (`ruleId`, `combinationId`), like the other Tapir IDs.
- There is no command to delete a rule; it can be overwritten by creating a rule with the same name.
- The commands need Archicad 27 or later (rule groups); on older versions they return `APIERR_NOTSUPPORTED`.
- Example: `Examples/graphic_override_rules.py`. It has no expected output yet; the first test run records it.

## Testing

- Builds for Archicad 30 and 29 on Windows (Visual Studio 2022, toolset v143) without errors or warnings. The other versions and macOS are left to CI. `tools/generate_addon_docs.py` evaluates the new schemas.
- I have not run it against TestProject.pla. The commands have been in my own build since mid-2026, where I use them on Archicad 29 (Japanese) to make rule sets and combinations for 3D views per story, with rules colored by RGB and criteria copied from a rule made in the GUI.
- Compared with my build, the IDs are `{guid}` objects instead of strings, and the descriptions now explain the criterion XML.

## Changes after the review (44c7f191)

- Rule names are unique in the whole project (`API_OverrideRule::name`), so the rule to overwrite is now found by name among all rules; a same-named rule in another group no longer makes the overwrite fail. The overwritten rule keeps its group. CreateGraphicalOverrideCombination uses the same lookup.
- `API_OverrideRule`, `API_OverrideRuleGroup` and `API_OverrideCombination` are filled member by member instead of by aggregate order (the AC29 `API_OverrideRule` already has a member after `criterionXML`).
- GetGraphicalOverrideRules returns the `ruleGroupName` of each rule, taken from the rule lists of the groups.

## Changes after the second and third review (760398ac, d527801e)

- The rule is looked up by name before anything is created. An existing rule is overwritten where it is, and only a new rule finds or creates its group, so overwriting a rule no longer leaves an empty group behind.
- The existing combination is found by comparing names over `ACAPI_GraphicalOverride_GetOverrideCombinationList`, in the same way as the rules, and then changed; otherwise it is created. Neither path relies on Create returning `APIERR_NAMEALREADYUSED`.
- `ruleGroupName` in GetGraphicalOverrideRules comes from the `ruleList` output of `ACAPI_GraphicalOverride_GetOverrideRuleGroup`, which the Archicad 29 DevKit documents as the rules that belong to the group.

## Fourth review round and a run on Archicad 30 (ff07b760)

- The example prints a version message and stops on Archicad 25/26, like `mep_systems.py`, instead of raising a `KeyError`.
- The `ruleId` and `combinationId` response objects use the common `#/GuidId` definition.

Run on Archicad 30.0.0.3001 (Windows, Japanese) with a local build that merges the open PRs (#878 to #883):

- `Examples/graphic_override_rules.py` ran. GetGraphicalOverrideRules listed the nine rules of the template's own rule group, each with that group's name, and the new rule in `Tapir examples`: `GetOverrideRuleList` returns the rules of every group, and `GetOverrideRuleGroup (group, &ruleList)` lists the rules of a group.
- CreateGraphicalOverrideCombination with the same name and another rule list returned the same combination, so it was changed in place.
- Overwriting a rule with another `ruleGroupName` kept it in its group.
- An unknown rule name is refused with `Override rule not found`.

title: CreateMEPRoutingElements: add layerIndex for the route and its parts
body:
Fifth of the PRs that bring the additions of my own build upstream (after #877 to #880).

## New parameter

`CreateMEPRoutingElements`: `layerIndex` sets the layer of the routing element and of all its parts: routing segments, rigid segments, elbows (Archicad 29 and later) and transitions. Only a positive index takes effect; without it the routing tool default layer is used, as before.

## Why

The MEP API has no layer setter, so new routes always got the routing tool default layer. In my build, changing only the layer of the routing element (classic `ACAPI_Element_Change` on its header) did not always move the parts that carry the geometry, so the layer is set on each part as well, inside the same undoable command. Every part is tried; if one cannot be changed, the route stays placed and the item reports an error that names its guid.

## Where this comes from

My build has a separate `CreateMEPRoutes` command (route from 3D nodes, system by name, diameter to the closest preference table row, layer by name). `CreateMEPRoutingElements` covers almost all of that now, so instead of a second command this PR adds the missing piece, the layer, to the existing one. The `SetElementsLayer` command of my build is not proposed either, since `SetDetailsOfElements` sets `layerIndex` for ordinary elements. If it helps, the same parameter could go to `ModifyMEPRoutingElements` for existing routes.

## Testing

- Builds for Archicad 30 and 29 on Windows (Visual Studio 2022, toolset v143) without errors or warnings. The other versions and macOS are left to CI. `tools/generate_addon_docs.py` evaluates the schema.
- Before the run on Archicad 30 below, I had not run this branch in Archicad. The helper that sets the layers is the one my build has used since mid-2026 for automatic piping on Archicad 29 (Japanese), called there after `CreateMEPRoutes` placed a route; here it is called after `Place` in `CreateMEPRoutingElements`.
- Example: `Examples/mep_routing_element_layer.py`. It has no expected output yet; the first test run records it.

## Second review round and a run on Archicad 30 (a215b60c)

- `layerIndex` is checked before anything is placed: a layer that does not exist (`APIERR_BADINDEX`) or is locked (`APIERR_LOCKEDLAY`) gives a per-item error, and no route is placed.
- `SetLayerOfRoutingElement` tries every part and returns the first error; the item then reports that the route was placed but its layer, or that of some parts, could not be set.
- The example creates its own unlocked and locked layers, so its output does not depend on the layers of TestProject.pla, and prints a version message on Archicad 25 to 27.
- Grasshopper: CreateMEPRoutingElements gets an optional `LayerIndices` input (1 or one per route), named like the layer inputs of the other components. I could not build the plugin here (no .NET SDK on this machine), so it is left to the Grasshopper build check.
- `RoutingNode::GetTransitionIds` and `RoutingSegment::GetRigidSegmentIds`: the `build_win (28)` and `build_mac (28)` checks passed on 633511dd, so both exist on Archicad 28.

Run on Archicad 30.0.0.3001 (Windows, Japanese) with a local build that merges the open PRs (#878 to #883):

- `Examples/mep_routing_element_layer.py`: the route on the unlocked layer was placed there, and the one on the locked layer was refused with the new message.
- A four-point pipe route with `layerIndex`: its three routing segments and its four nodes were on the requested layer, as was the routing element in the example, and no part reported an error.
- A layer index that does not exist was refused.

## Third review round (2b22e480, replaced by the maintainer's e9b5a9f)

2b22e480 handled the last two review points by removing the route and by leaving the Archicad 28 bends out. The maintainer's `claude/resolved-pr-881` (e9b5a9f) fixed the same points better, and this branch now carries its version (merge 74159118, the same content as e9b5a9f):

- The Archicad 28 bends are set through `RoutingNode::GetBendIds ()` (in the 28.3001 DevKit).
- When the layer cannot be set after `Place`, the route stays placed and the error message gives its guid.

title: Report a command that fails to register in the report window
body:
Last of the PRs that bring the additions of my own build upstream (after #877 to #881).

## Problem

`Initialize` ORs the results of all `RegisterCommand` calls together. When `ACAPI_AddOnAddOnCommunication_InstallAddOnCommandHandler` fails, nothing tells which command failed, and the combined value is not a real error code either. In my build a failed registration (two commands with the same name) went unnoticed until Archicad crashed at the first command called through the JSON interface; finding it took a startup log written around every registration.

## Change

`RegisterCommand` writes one line to the report window when a command cannot be registered:

`Tapir: the <name> command could not be registered (error <code>).`

Nothing changes when all commands register. The startup log of my build is not proposed: it wrote a line for every registration on every start, which was useful once for the hunt, not for everyone.

## Testing

- Builds for Archicad 30 and 29 on Windows (Visual Studio 2022, toolset v143) without errors or warnings. The other versions and macOS are left to CI.
- The failure path was not triggered in this branch: all commands register.

title: Palette: let Python write UTF-8 to the output pipe on Windows
body:
Follow-up to #877, from the review there: Python writes to a pipe in the system code page unless told otherwise (cp932 on Japanese Windows), while the palette reads the script output as UTF-8. Since #877 that no longer crashes, but non-ASCII output such as Japanese messages or tracebacks turns into `?`.

## Change

On Windows, `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` is set in Archicad's environment while the script process is started, so Python writes UTF-8 to the pipe and the output stays readable. It is set only when the user has not set it, and removed again right after `GS::Process::Create` (a `GS::OnExit` takes care of it, also if `Create` throws), so the rest of Archicad does not see it. `SafeUTF8String` from #877 still covers a character split at a read-chunk boundary. macOS is not changed: Python already writes UTF-8 there.

## Testing

- Builds for Archicad 30 and 29 on Windows (Visual Studio 2022, toolset v143) without errors or warnings. The other versions and macOS are left to CI.

title: Renaming / re-IDing Project Map items, Schedules and Layout Book folders via RenameNavigatorItem
body:
Summary

TapirCommand.RenameNavigatorItem (and the stock API.RenameNavigatorItem) cannot rename several kinds of Navigator items that a user can rename by hand in Archicad. I would like to ask whether Tapir could support these, or, if the Archicad API really cannot do it, document the limitation.

I read archicad-addon/Sources/NavigatorCommands.cpp on main. RenameNavigatorItemCommand already has a read-back check that returns APIERR_REFUSEDPAR ("Archicad did not apply the new name"), so the old false "success" seems handled. The remaining problem is that the rename itself does not happen.

What does not work (Archicad 29, Tapir 1.7.0)

Item | Result -- | -- Project Map items (views, sections, elevations, details, schedules) | Name and ID are not changed. Archicad returns error 7403 / the read-back check fails. Schedules (Project Map > Schedules) | ACAPI_Navigator_ChangeNavigatorItem returns NoError but leaves the name untouched. The source comment says these are "named by their scheme". View Map items: newId | Has no effect on the item ID. Layout Book folders (subsets) | The ID/prefix can be changed only through the layout path (customLayoutNumber), and the name change locks the item (customName = true). I found no clean way to set a folder's own ID. Publisher Sets | No rename command at all. The code only reads names and GUIDs.

What works

  • View Map folders and views: name via newName.
  • Layouts: newId (sets customLayoutNumber), which is safe.

Why it matters

We keep a strict naming standard (document ID prefixes on every view, layout and schedule). Renaming a whole project by script is possible for most items. The items above must be renamed by hand, which defeats the automation. Schedule IDs and Project Map IDs are the most important for us.

Questions / possible directions

  1. Is there an Archicad API function that can rename Project Map items and schedules (for example through the schedule scheme settings, or ACAPI_Navigator_ChangeNavigatorItem with a different navigatorItem configuration)? If yes, could Tapir use it?
  2. Layout Book folders: could the command set the subset's ID (LayoutBookSubset / ACAPI_Navigator_ChangeLayoutSets with the folder's database id)?
  3. A Publisher Set rename command would be a useful addition (ACAPI_Navigator_ChangeNavigatorSet?).
  4. In RenameNavigatorItemCommand, the return value of ACAPI_Navigator_ChangeLayoutSets is ignored, and a failed ACAPI_Navigator_GetLayoutSets silently skips the ID change while the command still reports success. A read-back check like the one for names would make this reliable.
  5. If the Archicad API cannot do this, the command documentation could list the item types that are not renameable, so users do not lose time on them.

I can test any build on Archicad 29 and provide exact request/response JSON.

Environment: Archicad 29, Tapir 1.7.0, Windows 11, JSON API (Python client).

title: Add a community test runner that tests pull requests on real Archicad
body:
Following the Discord discussion about testing bot PRs on real Archicad without a maintainer in
the loop: a tester-side runner, standard library only, no Claude needed.

**What it does:** for every open PR labelled `needs-test`, for each Archicad version the tester
has: skip forks, fetch the PR's JSON checks (`archicad-addon/Test/checks/*.json`) and the build
check's artifact for the head commit; install it only while that Archicad is closed, start it
with a blank template, run the checks, quit Archicad, restore the previous add-on, and post a
comment whose first line a workflow can read: `tapir-test: AC26 PASS 61/61 build 1a2b3c4 tapir 1.7.2`.

**Checks are data, not code:** commands, saved values and expectations (`eq`, `approx`, `len`,
… and arithmetic over saved values). A PR can only make the runner send Tapir commands to an
empty untitled project. Seven example checks come from the verification of #747-#753 and #759.

**Verified on Windows:** `check` on AC26/AC28; `trial` (the full install-run-quit-restore cycle
with a local build) on AC26, which is how #886 was verified; the GitHub side (PR lookup, check
files, artifact download). 10 unit tests against an in-memory Archicad that models the measured
fixed and unfixed behaviour, so each check is shown to catch its bug.

**Not in this PR (needs maintainer decisions):** dispatching the build check for bot PRs (they
get no build today), the workflow that turns result comments into labels, Discord pings, and the
auto-merge rule. macOS is not written yet.

Happy to adjust structure or naming to the repo's conventions.

title: Automate the issue bot's pull requests end to end, and split large issues
body:
With this change, an issue goes from being opened to a merged fix with no maintainer step: the bot opens a PR, the PR is built, reviewed and fixed by the bot, the issue's author is asked to verify it in Archicad, and it is merged automatically three days after a clean review. Large issues are split into parts, with one PR per part.

## Changes

**Issue bot (`claude_issue_triage.yml`)**
- Opens its PRs ready for review, not as drafts. The PR body explains what happens next.
- Tags the issue's author in its issue comment and asks them to verify the fix in Archicad. It skips the tag when the issue was filed by a bot, such as the Discord bot.
- Splits an issue that is too large for one PR:
  - It posts a plan of at most six parts, ending with `<!-- claude-split-plan: parts=N -->`.
  - It builds one part per run on `claude/issue-<n>-part<k>-…`, titled `[k/N]`, with the line `Part k of N of #n` in the body. It does not use `Fixes`, so the issue stays open until every part is in.
  - The new `next-part` job starts the next run only if the current run opened a part, so the chain cannot loop.
- The new `start-steward` job starts the steward right away.

**Bot PR steward (`claude_bot_pr_steward.yml`, new)**
- Bot pushes made with `GITHUB_TOKEN` start no runs, so the steward dispatches the build checks and the review on every new head.
- Once the builds are green, it posts a comment that tags the issue's author, links the downloadable add-on (each AC version, Win and Mac) and the Grasshopper plugin, explains how to load them through *Options > Add-On Manager*, and asks the author to report on the PR.
  - When the head changes, it updates the links in place.
  - If someone has commented since the last links comment, it posts a new comment instead, so they get a notification.
- On a failed build or a blocking review, it runs a `fix` job (Claude, with the same tool restrictions as the issue bot).
  - This happens at most `BOT_PR_MAX_FIX_ROUNDS` times (default 3). After that it labels the PR `needs-maintainer` and stops.
  - `BOT_PR_STEWARD=false` turns the steward off.

**Review (`claude_pr_review.yml`)**
- It can now be dispatched for a given PR.
- On bot PRs it records its verdict as the `claude-review` commit status.
  - The status is set by a job that runs no model, from a marker in the review tagged with a per-run nonce.
  - A reported problem from someone who tried the change in Archicad counts as blocking.

**Auto merge (`claude_auto_merge.yml`)**
- Bot PRs on `claude/` branches are merged when all of these hold:
  - every build check ran on the head and passed;
  - `claude-review` has been a success for `BOT_AUTO_MERGE_DELAY_HOURS` (default 72);
  - no review thread opened by a person is unresolved, and no reviewer's latest review requests changes;
  - the PR has neither the `do-not-merge` nor the `needs-maintainer` label, and is not a draft.
- The release-critical paths gate still applies.
- `BOT_AUTO_MERGE=false` turns this off.

**Other**
- The build checks also accept `workflow_dispatch`.
- CLAUDE.md is updated.

## Accepted risk
This was the maintainer's explicit choice. Anyone can write an issue, and only the model review and the 3-day wait stand between that text and `main`. The release-critical paths and `.github/` are still never auto-merged.

## Testing
- `actionlint` (with shellcheck) passes on every changed workflow. The only remaining notes are intended single-quoted `jq` strings (SC2016) and the existing PowerShell steps of the installer check.
- I ran the steward's new test-build comment logic against a mocked `gh` in four cases: first post, update in place, re-post after a person commented, and no change on the current head. All four behaved as intended.
- None of this has run on GitHub yet. The first bot PR after merging is the real test.

title: Grasshopper: add GetGridElementDefaults, GetGridElements and CreateGridElements components
body:
Follow-up to #879, as suggested there: Grasshopper components for its three grid element commands. The components only send JSON, so this PR builds on its own, but the commands need the add-on with #879.

## Components

- **CreateGridElements** (Element Creation), on `CreateElementsComponentBase`: `StartPoints` and `EndPoints` of each grid line (X and Y), `FloorIndices`, `LayerIndices`, and `AdditionalSettings` for `lengthMode` and the GDL `parameters`. The parameters the add-on could not set (unknown name, wrong value type) come back in the `warnings` of the response, and the component shows them as runtime warnings.
- **GetGridElements** (Elements): the line (from the insertion point in its direction, as long as the grid line, at Z = 0), angle, length, story, layer and library part of each grid element. With `IncludeParameters` also its GDL parameters as JSON, and `ParameterSettings`: the settable parameters (numbers, booleans and strings, without arrays, titles and `AC_Length`) as an AdditionalSettings object for CreateGridElements, so a new grid looks like an existing one and keeps its own length. `AC_Length` is left out because CreateGridElements sets the length from the points before it applies the parameters.
- **GetGridElementDefaults** (Element Details): library part, length, story, layer, `useXYFixSize`, parameters and ParameterSettings of the Grid Tool default.

## Change to the base class

`CreateElementsComponentBase` gets an `OnResponse (JObject)` hook, called after a command succeeded and before the created elements are stamped and the outputs are set. CreateGridElements uses it for the warnings; the other components do not change.

## Icons

SVGs in `IconSource` and 24 px PNGs in `Resources`, drawn like the existing ones (#28292C, 1 px strokes, the plus badge for Create). The PNGs were rendered with headless Chrome; rendered the same way, three existing icons match their PNGs in the repository closely.

## Testing

- I could not build the plugin here (no .NET SDK or Rhino on this machine), so the build is left to the Grasshopper build check. A compiler pass over the new and changed files without the Rhino, Grasshopper and Newtonsoft references gave no syntax errors, only the expected unknown-type errors.
- Not run in Grasshopper yet. The commands themselves ran on Archicad 30 (Windows, Japanese) in the run described in #879.

## Changes after the review (88a56e53)

- GetGridElements: with `IncludeParameters` off, the `Parameters` and `ParameterSettings` outputs stay empty lists instead of holding one null per grid element.
- #879 is merged now, so the commands these components call are in main. The Grasshopper build check passed on 4ce8123e.

title: Build checks: build branches once, and drop superseded runs
body:
After the bot PR backlog was brought up to date, more than 120 Actions runs sat queued. Two causes, both fixed here in the three build checks (Archicad Add-On, Grasshopper Plugin, Tapir Installer):

- **Every in-repo branch with a pull request was built twice**, once by its `push` run and once by its `pull_request` run. `push` now runs only on `main`, which the README badges need. Pull requests are still built by their `pull_request` run, and the issue bot's branches by the steward's `workflow_dispatch`.
- **Runs for superseded commits kept building.** A new `concurrency` group per pull request (or per ref) has `cancel-in-progress` set, so a newer push cancels that PR's queued and running builds. Runs on `main` are never cancelled.

The cancelled runs belong to commits that are no longer any PR's head. The steward and the auto-merge only read the check runs on the current head, so these cancellations never count as a failed build.

CLAUDE.md's CI section is updated to match. `actionlint` passes on all three files.

title: Stop the cancelled runs on main, and judge the latest run of each check
body:
`main` showed red marks that were cancelled runs, not failures. On the latest commit, 14 "Bot PR sweep" runs and several "Auto Merge" runs were cancelled. The cause: every review verdict, fix run and finished build starts a sweep or an auto-merge pass. Their concurrency groups keep only one waiting run and cancel it whenever a newer one arrives, so each replaced run showed as cancelled on `main`. (The cancelled `build`/`deploy`/`report-build-status` jobs are GitHub Pages deploys superseded by the next merge, which is harmless.)

**Fewer cancelled runs**
- The steward's `restart` job, the review's `verdict` job and the issue bot's `start-steward` job now start a sweep only when none is already waiting.
- `claude_auto_merge.yml` no longer has a concurrency group. A pass now steps aside, successfully, when a newer run is waiting or running. Two passes that still overlap cannot double-merge: the merge is pinned to the head commit with `--match-head-commit`, and a refused merge only skips that pull request. The job gets `actions: read` to list the runs.

**A side effect of #890, fixed here**
- With `cancel-in-progress` on the build checks, starting the same build twice for one bot PR leaves a cancelled run on that PR's head commit, and it read as a failed build.
- Both gates now judge only the latest run of each check.
  - The steward starts a build again when its latest run was cancelled.
  - The auto-merge "all green" gate groups `gh pr checks` by workflow and name and keeps the latest. Its output is now read so that a nonzero exit while checks are pending doesn't empty the list.

`actionlint` with shellcheck passes; the only notices left are the intended single-quoted `jq` strings. I tested the dedupe expressions on sample data.

title: Bot PR steward: only work a sweep starts counts against its batch
body:
The sweep's batch limit (`BOT_PR_SWEEP_BATCH`, default 5) also counted pull requests whose builds, review or fix were merely **still running**. With the backlog's builds queued behind the macOS runners, the five oldest bot pull requests filled the batch on every sweep. In the 19:56 scheduled sweep:
- #648, #649, #674, #676 and #751 showed "builds still running";
- every newer pull request was "left for a later sweep";
- #761 and #813, both with a blocking review, and #885, which fails to compile, never got a fix run.

Now only the work a sweep **starts** counts against the batch: builds, a review or a fix it dispatches. Work already running holds nothing back. The limit still bounds what one sweep adds to the queue.

Everything else in the pipeline behaves as intended in that run. Test-build links were posted on #675, #743 and #750, which are now "green and reviewed - waiting for claude_auto_merge.yml". `claude-review` verdicts are recorded on all 26 bot pull requests: 17 clean and 9 blocking.

**Also: skip a fix run whose pull request moved on.** A fix run started by a sweep can sit in the queue until the pull request's head changes, because of a person's push or an earlier fix. It then worked on the new head with the old failures and findings. On #761, a fix dispatched for a blocking review ran after the review of the new head had come back clean. The sweep now passes the head it saw (`head_sha`), and the fix job does nothing when the head has moved; the next sweep looks at the new head.

`actionlint` with shellcheck passes; only the intended `jq` single-quote notices remain.
