title: Palette: stop a running script when Archicad quits (crash on quit)
body:
## Symptom

If a script started from the Tapir palette is still running when Archicad is closed, Archicad crashes while quitting and the Bug Reporter opens. Any long-running script does it, for example one that keeps a Script UI page and a relay loop alive until the user closes the page.

Reproduced on Archicad 29 every time with this script in the custom scripts folder:

```python
import sys, time
sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", line_buffering=True)
for i in range(600):
    print(f"test {i}")
    time.sleep(1)
```

Run it from the palette, wait a few seconds, close Archicad.

## Cause

Two things outlive the add-on:

1. `TapirPalette::ExecuteScript` runs `UIUpdaterThread` on the palette's `GS::ThreadedExecutor`. The thread loops on `process.WaitFor (10 ms)` / `ReadFromChannels ()` until the script exits. `FreeData` does not stop the script or the thread, so after the add-on is unloaded the thread keeps running on the destroyed palette. In the crash dump the faulting call is `GS::Process::GetStandardErrorChannel`, called from the address range the add-on had occupied.
2. For each piece of output the thread posts an `OutputUpdateTask` (and `IconUpdateTask` at start and end) to `GS::MessageLoopExecutor`. Tasks posted while Archicad is already closing are no longer run. Archicad destroys them after the add-on is unloaded, and the main thread crashes in `GS::CountedPtrImpl<GS::Runnable,...>::~CountedPtrImpl`, because the tasks' destructors are in the add-on. This one shows up once (1) is fixed.

## Fix

- New `TapirPalette::StopRunningScriptOnQuit ()`, called first in `FreeData`. It:
  - sets a `quitting` flag,
  - kills the running script with `process.Kill ()`, as the palette's Stop button does,
  - waits up to 2 seconds for the output reader to return.
- The output reader returns as soon as `quitting` is set, without touching the process, and posts nothing to the message loop after that.
- The palette keeps a reference to each task the reader posts until the task has run. In normal use, the reference is dropped after the task has run (on the next post, not inside the task's own `Run`). Tasks still queued at quit are kept alive on purpose and never freed, so that Archicad discarding them later does not call into the unloaded add-on.

## How to test

1. Put the script above in the custom scripts folder and reload the scripts.
2. Run it from the palette, wait a few seconds, then close Archicad.
3. Before: Archicad crashes while quitting and the Bug Reporter opens. After: Archicad quits normally, no crash report is written, and the script's process is gone.
4. Normal use: run a short script. The Run button switches to Stop and back, and the output and `ExitCode: 0` appear in the Session Report as before. Closing Archicad afterwards does not crash.

## Tested

- Builds: Archicad 29 and Archicad 30, Windows, Release, VS 2022, on `main`. No warnings.
- Archicad 29.0 JPN (5101), Windows, with the same change on my fork:
  - Before: crash on quit with the script running. The crash was in `GS::Process::GetStandardErrorChannel`, in the same place as a crash a user hit while closing Archicad with a long-running palette script open.
  - With only part (1) of the fix: crash on quit in `~CountedPtrImpl<GS::Runnable>` on the main thread.
  - After: no crash with the script running. No crash when quitting after a short script had finished. In both cases there was no new crash report.
- Archicad 30.3001 JPN, Windows, with the same change on my fork: no crash with the script running, and no new crash report. I did not run the "before" case on Archicad 30.
- Not run on macOS. The change itself is platform-independent: `std::atomic`, `std::mutex` and the existing `GS::Process` / `GS::ThreadedExecutor` calls.

title: Add MoveGraphicOverrideRules
body:
## Summary

Adds **`MoveGraphicOverrideRules`** (1.7.3, Archicad 27+), which exposes `ACAPI_GraphicalOverride_MoveOverrideRule`. It is the one rule group operation of the Graphic Overrides dialog that no command or open PR covers yet: moving a rule to another group, or to another place in its own group.

- Input: `graphicOverrideRules: [{ graphicOverrideRuleId, ruleGroupName, beforeGraphicOverrideRuleId? }]`, processed in the given order.
- The target group is found by name and created when no group has that name, like `CreateGraphicOverrideRules` does. A group created for an item whose move fails is deleted again.
- `beforeGraphicOverrideRuleId` puts the rule in front of a rule of the target group. If it is left out, the rule becomes the last rule of the group. If the given rule is not in the target group, the item is refused.
- Response: `executionResults`, one per item. All moves run in one undoable command. The error message names the reason when the target group already holds a rule with the same name, and for built-in rules (the renovation rules), which Archicad refuses to move (`APIERR_NOACCESSRIGHT`).

## Implementation note

Archicad refuses to move a rule into the group it is already in: `MoveOverrideRule` returns `APIERR_NAMEALREADYUSED`, because the rule's own name is taken in the target group. When the target group is the rule's own group, the command therefore builds the new order of that group and calls `ACAPI_GraphicalOverride_SetOverrideRuleOrder` instead.

## Testing

Tested live on Archicad 29 (macOS, arm64 build of this branch), 13/13 checks passing:

- Moving into a group that does not exist yet creates the group.
- Moving in front of a rule of the target group.
- Inside the own group: moving to the end and to the front; moving in front of itself changes nothing.
- Two moves in one call are applied in input order.
- Refused, with nothing changed:
  - a rule whose name is already used in the target group;
  - a `beforeGraphicOverrideRuleId` from another group;
  - an unknown rule;
  - a rule of the built-in renovation group (message names it; the target group created for it is removed again).
- Error messages for a taken name and a built-in rule.
- Cleanup leaves the project's groups as before.

The example `archicad-addon/Examples/move_graphic_override_rules.py` was run against the same build. The branch also builds for Archicad 30.

title: Auto Merge: ignore the API Coverage check, ask again when mergeability is UNKNOWN
body:
Two bugs in `claude_auto_merge.yml` hold back bot PRs that clear every other gate.

**1. The cancelled API Coverage check.** `api_coverage.yml` runs on `pull_request_target` for every PR event, with one global `cancel-in-progress` group. With 250+ open PRs, its `update` check on most PR heads ends up cancelled, and gate 2 treats that as not green. In the 23 Oct 21:13 UTC sweep, 16 of the bot PRs for parikshit99's issues were skipped only for `cancel update`, among them #1018, #1019, #1016, #952 and #967–970. API Coverage never tests the PR's code, so gate 2 now leaves that workflow out.

**2. Mergeability read only once.** GitHub recomputes mergeability in the background after every push to `main`, and the first read is often `UNKNOWN`. The sweep read it once and skipped the PR: 25 of those PRs showed `mergeable=UNKNOWN`. The REST API reports `mergeable: true` for #1204, #1157, #1167, #1289 and #1304. The sweep now asks again up to 3 times, 5 seconds apart, before skipping.

No other gate changes: who the author is, the review delay, protected paths and labels are all as before. The file is under `.github/`, so a maintainer has to merge this by hand.

title: Steward: merge main with an App token, act on why a fix pushed nothing
body:
Of the 129 open bot PRs labelled `needs-maintainer`, 125 were handed over by "Hand over if nothing was pushed". There were two causes:
1. About 100: the fix run's `git merge origin/main` could not be pushed, because `GITHUB_TOKEN` may not push main's `.github/workflows` changes.
2. About 25: the run pushed nothing on purpose. The finding was wrong, the CI failure was transient, or the PR waits for an unmerged earlier part.

This PR changes **release-critical paths** (`.github/`), so it needs maintainer review. It will not auto-merge.

## Changes
**`claude_bot_pr_steward.yml`**
- **Merging main (fix job).** A new step, "Merge main", runs without a model before the model step. It runs when the PR conflicts with main, or when the sweep asks for a merge (new input `merge_main`).
  - A clean merge is pushed at once with a GitHub App installation token (Contents and Workflows write). The model does not run.
  - On conflicts, the model only resolves them in the working tree. It gets a narrower tool set: `git add`/`git rm`, no commit, merge or push.
  - The push happens in a separate job, `push-merge`, on a fresh runner that never ran the model. The model's allowed `git show/diff/log --output=` can write any file on its own runner, so the token never goes there. `push-merge`:
    - merges the same two commits again in a new clone;
    - takes only the conflicted files from the model's working tree (uploaded as an artifact, treated as data);
    - refuses leftover conflict markers, symlinks and missing resolutions;
    - commits and pushes with `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` and `core.fsmonitor=false`. The token appears only on the command line of the fetch and the push, never in a config file. The push is never forced.
  - A conflict under `.github/`, `tools/`, `archicad-addon/Tools/` or `archicad-addon/Installer/` is never given to the model, so those folders are always exactly what git's merge produced.
  - **Without the App secrets:** if main brings workflow changes, the PR is handed over straight away, without a model run: "merge main into it with Update branch (or set up the steward's GitHub App …)". Otherwise the model merges main as before.
- **No double runs.** A push with the App token starts the build checks' `pull_request` runs by itself (a `GITHUB_TOKEN` push does not).
  - The sweep now looks at `actions/runs?head_sha=` and treats any queued or running build on the head as started or still running. This also covers the moment before its check runs exist, and a re-run of failed jobs.
  - The sweep's "build checks refuse a dispatch" handover now starts a merge-only fix when the App is set up.
- **Outcome markers.** The fix prompt now ends the comment with `<!-- steward-fix-outcome: OUTCOME NONCE -->`. A step without a model reads it; only this run's comment with this run's nonce counts. The decision moved from the fix job to `restart`, which runs no model:
  - `transient-ci`: re-runs the failed jobs of the failed build checks (`gh run rerun --failed`), at most twice per PR.
  - `review-disputed`: dispatches a fresh review, at most twice per PR, then hands over. While that review is queued or running, the sweep starts no fix.
  - `waits-for:#N`: sets the commit status `steward-fix` to pending ("waits for #N"). That also holds auto-merge back. The sweep skips the PR, with no label, until #N is merged, then sets the status to success and carries on. If #N was closed unmerged, the PR is handed over.
  - `merge-blocked`, `stuck` or no marker: handed over at once, as before.
  - Every such run still counts as a fix round, so `BOT_PR_MAX_FIX_ROUNDS` still bounds everything.
- `mergeable` is now read again while it is `UNKNOWN`.

**`claude_pr_review.yml`**
- Skips the `pull_request_target` run when a bot pushes to an issue-bot PR (that is the App's merge push). The steward dispatches the review once the builds are green. A person's push is still reviewed.
- On a re-review, the steward fix run's comment counts as a reply to each finding it answers, so a disputed finding gets judged again.

**`claude_auto_merge.yml`**: comment only. It said only the verdict job holds `statuses: write`; now it says only jobs without a model do.

**`CLAUDE.md`**: CI section updated.

## Setup the maintainer has to do
1. Create a GitHub App owned by the ENZYME-APD organization:
   - repository permissions **Contents: Read and write** and **Workflows: Read and write** (Metadata read is implied);
   - no webhook.
2. Install it on this repository only.
3. Add these repository secrets:
   - `TAPIR_BOT_APP_ID`: the App ID;
   - `TAPIR_BOT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`: a generated private key, the whole `.pem`.
4. If a ruleset restricts pushes to `claude/**` branches, allow the App.

Until the secrets exist, the steward behaves as it does today, except that the handover message is clearer and comes without a wasted model run.

## Not done here
- **The 129 PRs already labelled:** the steward doesn't touch them until the label is removed. Once the App is set up, removing `needs-maintainer` hands each one back with its counts reset.
- **Testing:** the YAML parses and every `run:` script passes `bash -n`, checked locally. actionlint wasn't available. I ran the `push-merge` script against a throwaway local repo: it refused a leftover marker and a missing resolution, and pushed a correct merge commit with main's workflow change and a resolved deletion. Nothing here has run on GitHub yet.

title: Do not open an empty Script UI palette when Archicad starts
body:
## What changed

`ScriptUIPalette::PaletteControlCallBack` now ignores `APIPalMsg_OpenPalette` until a script has shown a page with `ShowScriptUI` in the current session, which is when the palette instance gets created.

## Why

The Script UI palette is registered with `ACAPI_RegisterModelessWindow`, so Archicad saves whether it was open in the work environment. If it was open at the last quit, the next start sends `APIPalMsg_OpenPalette`. The old handler then created the palette and showed it. The HTML a script loaded is never saved, and that script isn't running any more, so Archicad started with an empty "Tapir Script UI" window.

When the request is ignored, `APIPalMsg_IsPaletteVisible` reports the palette as hidden, so Archicad should save it as closed at the next quit. Restoring a window layout after a script has shown a page still brings the palette back with that page.

## For reviewers

- The only other code that creates the instance is `ShowScriptUI`. Every other caller checks `HasInstance ()` first, so `HasInstance ()` is enough to tell whether a page was shown.
- Only the AC29 build was compiled locally; the other versions are covered by CI.

## Tested in Archicad 29

Each run quit Archicad with the Script UI palette open, then started Archicad again with a new project.

| Step | Released Tapir | This build |
|---|---|---|
| Start after quitting with the palette open | Empty palette appeared, `GetScriptUIResult` reported `isOpen: true` (bug reproduced) | No palette, `isOpen: false` |
| `ShowScriptUI` with a page | — | The page is displayed |
| Page calls `ACAPI.SubmitResult` and `ACAPI.ClosePalette` | — | `GetScriptUIResult` returned the result, then `isOpen: false` |

body:
Follow-up to #1287. Its six parts (#1288–#1294) cover about 175 of the MEP functions. The bot left the other 453 out, either because it couldn't check enum values or signatures without the DevKit, or because they needed a design decision. This issue has both: every remaining function below comes with its declaration, copied from the DevKits the build checks use (27.3001, 28.3001, 29.3000, 30.3000). Each line ends with the Archicad versions that have it. The design questions are answered by me as the requester. The `*UIManager` classes are already `notApplicable` and aren't listed. ### API functions All 453 functions are listed by their full names, with their declarations, under **Declarations from the DevKit** below. The six groups there are the suggested split. ### What should Tapir let you do? The same as #1287: read and write everything about MEP elements, preference tables and defaults that the Archicad dialogs allow, through the existing MEP command group. The six groups: 1. **Port and routing settings.** Add them to the existing commands: `GetMEPPorts`, `GetMEPRoutingElements`, `ModifyMEPRoutingElements` and `GetMEPElementDetails` (#1290). This means: - connection style, flow direction and nominal size (a string); - the AC29+ display options: cut plane position, floor plan display option, on-story visibility and show projection; - the preferred transition placement; - the insulation and radius modifiers. Enum values go over JSON as their names (table below). 2. **Reading the preference tables.** Extend `GetMEPPreferenceTables` with the getters #1293 left out. 3. **Editing the preference tables.** A new `ModifyMEPPreferenceTables`, which takes the same shape `GetMEPPreferenceTables` returns, and adds, deletes or changes rows, names and descriptions through each table's `Modifier`. 4. **Reading the tool defaults.** A read-only `GetMEPToolDefaults`. Per domain and element type, it returns what the `Create*Default` copy holds. The DevKit says it "returns a copy of Archicad's current Default … from the RoutingElement tool". Changing the tool defaults themselves is **not** wanted, so `Modify` on a default copy only feeds parts 5's commands. 5. **Pick up, inject and place**, all as undoable commands: - `TransferMEPSettings`: `PickUpDefault` from a source element, then `Modifier::Inject` into the target elements, like Archicad's pick up / inject parameters. - `PlaceMEPFlexibleSegments`: starts from `CreateFlexibleSegmentDefault`, optionally changed with part 4's keys, then calls `Place`/`PlacePolyline`. - `PlaceMEPTakeOffs`: the same, using `TakeOffDefault::Place` (segment id, distance from beginning, rotation). The DevKit says `Place` "creates an Undoable Command Scope before executing the placement". 6. **Systems and the rest:** - the distribution systems graph as a tree (`TraverseTree` and the tree node getters); - `PhysicalSystem::Create` and `FindSystemIdsFromElementIds`; - the electrical project settings; - `IsElectricalCircuit`, `GetLocalizedElemTypeName` and `CollectAllMEPElements`. **Enum values** (`MEPEnums.hpp`, and `MEPTypes.hpp` from AC29): | Enum | AC27 | AC28–AC30 | | --- | --- | --- | | `Domain` | Ventilation, Piping, CableCarrier | same | | `ConnectorShape` | Rectangular, Circular, UShape | Rectangular, Circular, Oval, UShape | | `ConnectionStyle` | NoConnector, Flanged, Overlap | SimpleBody, Flanged, Welded | | `FlowDirection` | FlowNotDefined, FlowIn, FlowOut | same | | `ConnectionSex` | Unisex, Male, Female | same | | `PreferredTransitionPlacement` | SmallToLarge, LargeToSmall | same | | `PreferenceTableShape` | Rectangular, Circular | (removed) | | `FloorPlanDisplayOption` | – | AC29–30: Projected, ProjectedWithOverhead, Symbolic, ByMVO | | `CutPlanePosition` | – | AC29–30: AtUpperDisplayLimit, ByViewSettings | | `ShowProjection` | – | AC29–30: ToFloorPlanRange, ToAbsoluteDisplayLimit, EntireElement | | `OnStoryVisibility` | – | AC29–30: AllRelevantStories, HomeStoryOnly | All are `enum class` in `ACAPI::MEP`. `PipingPort::GetNominalSize ()` returns `GS::UniString`, and `SetNominalSize (GS::UniString)` takes one. As in #1287, the commands cover Archicad 28–30, because the MEP commands already require AC28. Gate the AC29/AC30-only functions with `ServerMainVers_2900` and `ServerMainVers_3000`, using the versions on each line. ### Declarations from the DevKit

title: Expose the ACAPI:: functions left out of #1298 (Opening enums, Favorites, library part writes)
body:
This continues #1298. Five of its six parts (#1299, #1300, #1301, #1304, #1305) are merged; part 4 (#1302) is still open. Each part left items out, saying they needed a DevKit check or a design decision. Below are the 95 functions of #1298 that no merged or open pull request uses yet. Each comes with its declaration from the AC28–AC30 DevKits, and the enum values and design decisions the parts asked for. As the requester, I've made those decisions. Everything here is Archicad 28+ or 29+, as marked, and must be gated with `ServerMainVers_2800` / `ServerMainVers_2900` like the existing commands.

## 1. The Opening enums, and small additions

`GetOpeningDetails`, `SetOpeningDetails`, `GetOpeningFloorPlanParameters` and `SetOpeningFloorPlanParameters` (AC29+) get the settings parts 2 and 3 left out. Enum values go over JSON as their DevKit names:
- `constraint`: `ForcedVertical`, `ForcedHorizontal`, `Aligned`, `Free` (the DevKit says `Free` is not usable for `OpeningDefault`);
- `limitType`: `Infinite`, `Finite`, `HalfInfinite`;
- `linkedStatus`: `Linked`, `NotLinked` (the getter returns `std::optional`, so leave it out when it is empty);
- `shapeType`: `Rectangular`, `Circular`, `Polygonal`;
- `dividedOpeningMode`: `Disconnected`, `Connected`;
- `floorPlanDisplayMode`: `Symbolic`, `SymbolicCut`, `SymbolicOverhead`, `Projected`;
- `openEdgeStyle`: `Hide`, `ShowUncut`, `ShowOverhead`.

These are in `ACAPI/Element/Opening/OpeningExtrusionParameters.hpp` and `OpeningFloorPlanParameters.hpp`, in namespace `ACAPI::Element`.

- `ACAPI::Element::ModifiableOpeningExtrusionParameters::SetConstraint` (AC29–30): `Result<void> SetConstraint (const Constraint constraint)`
- `ACAPI::Element::ModifiableOpeningExtrusionParameters::SetLimitType` (AC29–30): `void SetLimitType (const LimitType limitType)`
- `ACAPI::Element::ModifiableOpeningExtrusionParameters::SetLinkedStatus` (AC29–30): `Result<void> SetLinkedStatus (const LinkedStatus linkedStatus)`
- `ACAPI::Element::ModifiableOpeningExtrusionParameters::SetShapeType` (AC29–30): `void SetShapeType (const ShapeType polygonType)`
- `ACAPI::Element::ModifiableOpeningFloorPlanParameters::SetDividedOpeningMode` (AC29–30): `void SetDividedOpeningMode (DividedOpeningMode value)`
- `ACAPI::Element::ModifiableOpeningFloorPlanParameters::SetFloorPlanDisplayMode` (AC29–30): `void SetFloorPlanDisplayMode (OpeningFloorPlanDisplayMode value)`
- `ACAPI::Element::ModifiableOpeningFloorPlanParameters::SetOpenEdgeStyle` (AC29–30): `void SetOpenEdgeStyle (OpeningOpenEdgeStyle value)`
- `ACAPI::Element::OpeningExtrusionParameters::GetConstraint` (AC29–30): `Constraint GetConstraint () const`
- `ACAPI::Element::OpeningExtrusionParameters::GetLimitType` (AC29–30): `LimitType GetLimitType () const`
- `ACAPI::Element::OpeningExtrusionParameters::GetLinkedStatus` (AC29–30): `std::optional<LinkedStatus> GetLinkedStatus () const`
- `ACAPI::Element::OpeningExtrusionParameters::GetShapeType` (AC29–30): `ShapeType GetShapeType () const`
- `ACAPI::Element::OpeningFloorPlanParameters::GetDividedOpeningMode` (AC29–30): `DividedOpeningMode GetDividedOpeningMode () const`
- `ACAPI::Element::OpeningFloorPlanParameters::GetFloorPlanDisplayMode` (AC29–30): `OpeningFloorPlanDisplayMode GetFloorPlanDisplayMode () const`
- `ACAPI::Element::OpeningFloorPlanParameters::GetOpenEdgeStyle` (AC29–30): `OpeningOpenEdgeStyle GetOpenEdgeStyle () const`

Also in this part:
- `GetOpeningDetails` reports `exists` (`Opening::Exists`) and the opening's `elementId` from `ElementBase::GetElemId`.
- `GetProductVersionInfo` reports `availableDomains`: `Architecture` and `MEP`, from `ACAPI::IsDomainAvailable (ACAPI::Domain)` in `ACAPI/DomainAvailability.hpp` (AC29+).
- `GetProductVersionInfo` reports `ceipProjectId` for the open project (AC29+), from `ACAPI::GetCEIPProjectID (projectLocation)` in `ACAPI/ProjectID.hpp`. Leave it out for an untitled project.

- `ACAPI::Element::Opening::Exists` (AC29–30): `bool Exists () const`
- `ACAPI::ElementBase::GetElemId` (AC27–30): `UniqueID GetElemId () const`
- `ACAPI::IsDomainAvailable` (AC29–30): `ARCHICADAPI_EXPORT bool IsDomainAvailable (Domain domain)`
- `ACAPI::GetCEIPProjectID` (AC29–30): `ARCHICADAPI_EXPORT GS::UniString GetCEIPProjectID (const IO::Location& projectLocation)`

**Coverage fix:** `GetProductVersionInfoCommand::Execute` already calls all the getters below, but through `const auto versionInfo` and with only `LicenseInfoManager.hpp` included. `tools/generate_api_coverage.py` only counts a member call in a file that names its class or includes its header, so the coverage page still lists them as open. Name the type, `const ACAPI::LicenseInfo::ProductVersionInfo versionInfo`, and include `ACAPI/LicenseInfo/ProductVersionInfo.hpp` with the same `__has_include` guard. Nothing else changes.

- `ACAPI::LicenseInfo::ProductVersionInfo::GetAppVersionString` (AC29–30): `GS::UniString GetAppVersionString () const`
- `ACAPI::LicenseInfo::ProductVersionInfo::GetBuildNum` (AC28–30): `Int32 GetBuildNum () const`
- `ACAPI::LicenseInfo::ProductVersionInfo::GetGSLanguageCode` (AC28–30): `GS::UniString GetGSLanguageCode () const`
- `ACAPI::LicenseInfo::ProductVersionInfo::GetGSProductType` (AC29–30): `GS::UniString GetGSProductType () const`
- `ACAPI::LicenseInfo::ProductVersionInfo::GetHotfixVersionString` (AC29–30): `GS::UniString GetHotfixVersionString () const`
- `ACAPI::LicenseInfo::ProductVersionInfo::GetMainVersionString` (AC29–30): `GS::UniString GetMainVersionString () const`
- `ACAPI::LicenseInfo::ProductVersionInfo::GetProductFamilyId` (AC28–30): `GS::UniString GetProductFamilyId () const`
- `ACAPI::LicenseInfo::ProductVersionInfo::GetProductName` (AC29–30): `GS::UniString GetProductName () const`
- `ACAPI::LicenseInfo::ProductVersionInfo::GetUpdateVersionString` (AC29–30): `GS::UniString GetUpdateVersionString () const`
- `ACAPI::LicenseInfo::ProductVersionInfo::GetVersionNum1` (AC28): `Int32 GetVersionNum1 () const`
- `ACAPI::LicenseInfo::ProductVersionInfo::GetVersionNum2` (AC28): `Int32 GetVersionNum2 () const`
- `ACAPI::LicenseInfo::ProductVersionInfo::GetVersionNum3` (AC28): `Int32 GetVersionNum3 () const`
- `ACAPI::LicenseInfo::ProductVersionInfo::GetVersionString` (AC28): `GS::UniString GetVersionString () const`

## 2. Opening symbol parameters and the Opening tool defaults

- `GetOpeningFloorPlanParameters` returns `cutSymbolParameters` and `unCutSymbolParameters`, and `SetOpeningFloorPlanParameters` sets them. Each is a list of `{name, type, value}`. They are `GDL::Parameters` (`GDL/GDLParamInterface.hpp`):
  - read with `GetVarNumber`, `GetVarNameRef`, `GetVarType`, then `GetBoolVar` / `GetIntVar` / `GetNumVar` / `GetUStrVar`;
  - write by name with `GetIndexOfName` and `ModifyBoolVar` / `ModifyIntVar` / `ModifyNumVar` / `ModifyUStrVar`;
  - skip arrays and dictionaries.
- New `SetOpeningDefault` (AC29+) takes the same extrusion and floor plan fields `GetOpeningDefault` returns. `OpeningDefault::Modify` only changes the in-memory copy from `CreateOpeningDefault ()`; the DevKit says it runs in a not-undoable command. So call `ElementDefault::SetAsArchicadDefault ()` after it to make it the Opening tool's settings. The response gives `elementType` from `ElementDefault::GetElemType`.
- New `PlaceOpenings` (AC29+): `[{parentElementId, point: {x, y, z}}]` → the new openings' ids, one execution result each. It uses the current Opening tool default (`CreateOpeningDefault ()`), or one set up as in `SetOpeningDefault` when the input gives settings. The DevKit says `Place` opens its own undoable command scope and closes it afterwards, so do **not** call it inside `ACAPI_CallUndoableCommand`. It also says a point off the parent's surface is projected onto the closest point of the surface.

- `ACAPI::Element::ModifiableOpeningFloorPlanParameters::SetCutSymbolParameters` (AC29–30): `Result<void> SetCutSymbolParameters (const GDL::Parameters& gdlParams)`
- `ACAPI::Element::ModifiableOpeningFloorPlanParameters::SetUnCutSymbolParameters` (AC29–30): `Result<void> SetUnCutSymbolParameters (const GDL::Parameters& gdlParams)`
- `ACAPI::Element::OpeningFloorPlanParameters::GetCutSymbolParameters` (AC29–30): `std::optional<GDL::Parameters> GetCutSymbolParameters () const`
- `ACAPI::Element::OpeningFloorPlanParameters::GetUnCutSymbolParameters` (AC29–30): `std::optional<GDL::Parameters> GetUnCutSymbolParameters () const`
- `ACAPI::Element::OpeningDefault::Place` (AC29–30): `Result<UniqueID> Place (const UniqueID& parentElemId, const API_Coord3D& inputPoint) const`
- `ACAPI::ElementDefault::GetElemType` (AC29–30): `API_ElemType GetElemType () const`
- `ACAPI::ElementDefault::SetAsArchicadDefault` (AC27–30): `Result<void> SetAsArchicadDefault () const`

## 3. Favorites

These are all AC29+, in `ACAPI/Favorite.hpp`. An `ACAPI::ElementDefault` comes from `Favorite::GetElementDefault ()` or from `CreateOpeningDefault ()`, which derives from `ElementDefault`.
- `CreateFavorite`: `{name, folder?, source: {favoriteName} | {toolDefault: "Opening"}, conflictPolicy?}`.
- `ChangeFavorite`: `{favoriteName, source}`, with the same `source` as `CreateFavorite`.
- New `ApplyFavoriteToToolDefault`: `SetAsArchicadDefault` on the favorite's `ElementDefault`; it returns `elementType`.
- `ImportFavorites`: from XML files, a folder (`ImportAllFavorites`) or a legacy `.prf` file (`ImportFavoritesFromLegacyPRF`), as the counterpart of `ExportFavorites`' `format`. `conflictPolicy` is `Error`, `Skip`, `OverwriteExisting` or `RenameNew` (`FavoriteManager::ConflictPolicy`), default `Error`.
- `MoveFavoriteFolder`: `{folder, targetFolder}`, with folders given as their path from the root as a list of names, and `FavoriteFolder::GetParentFolder` / `IsRoot` used to walk and report them. This doesn't need the open folder PRs of #1231.
- `RenameFavorites` and `GetFavoritePreviewImage` already exist. On AC29+ they should call `FavoriteManager::RenameFavorite` and `Favorite::GetPreviewImage`, keeping the current C API path for AC25–28. Their input and output don't change.

- `ACAPI::Favorite::Favorite::GetPreviewImage` (AC29–30): `Result<void> GetPreviewImage (API_ImageViewID viewType, NewDisplay::NativeImage& img) const`
- `ACAPI::Favorite::FavoriteFolder::GetParentFolder` (AC29–30): `Result<FavoriteFolder> GetParentFolder () const`
- `ACAPI::Favorite::FavoriteFolder::IsRoot` (AC29–30): `Result<bool> IsRoot () const`
- `ACAPI::Favorite::FavoriteManager::ChangeFavorite` (AC29–30): `Result<void> ChangeFavorite (const ACAPI::Favorite::Favorite& favorite, const ACAPI::ElementDefault& defaultElem) const`
- `ACAPI::Favorite::FavoriteManager::CreateFavorite` (AC29–30): `Result<ACAPI::Favorite::Favorite> CreateFavorite (const GS::UniString& name, const ACAPI::Favorite::FavoriteFolder& folder, const ACAPI::ElementDefault& defaultElem) const`
- `ACAPI::Favorite::FavoriteManager::ImportAllFavorites` (AC29–30): `Result<void> ImportAllFavorites (const IO::Location& sourceFolder, ACAPI::Favorite::FavoriteManager::ConflictPolicy conflictPolicy, const std::optional<ACAPI::Favorite::FavoriteFolder>& targetOrKeep) const`
- `ACAPI::Favorite::FavoriteManager::ImportFavorites` (AC29–30): `Result<void> ImportFavorites (const std::vector<IO::Location>& favoriteXMLs, ACAPI::Favorite::FavoriteManager::ConflictPolicy conflictPolicy, const std::optional<ACAPI::Favorite::FavoriteFolder>& targetOrKeep) const`
- `ACAPI::Favorite::FavoriteManager::ImportFavoritesFromLegacyPRF` (AC29–30): `Result<void> ImportFavoritesFromLegacyPRF (const IO::Location& prfFile, ACAPI::Favorite::FavoriteManager::ConflictPolicy conflictPolicy, const std::optional<ACAPI::Favorite::FavoriteFolder>& targetOrKeep) const`
- `ACAPI::Favorite::FavoriteManager::MoveFolder` (AC29–30): `Result<void> MoveFolder (const ACAPI::Favorite::FavoriteFolder& folder, const ACAPI::Favorite::FavoriteFolder& targetFolder) const`
- `ACAPI::Favorite::FavoriteManager::RenameFavorite` (AC29–30): `Result<void> RenameFavorite (const ACAPI::Favorite::Favorite& favorite, const GS::UniString& newName) const`

## 4. Zone labeling and library parts

- New `GetZoneLabelingSettings` (AC28+): `isAutomaticLabelingOn` and `selectedFavoriteName`, from `ACAPI::CreateZoneLabelingSettings ()` in `ACAPI/ZoneLabelingSettings.hpp`.
- The existing `SetZoneLabelingSettings` takes an optional `favoriteName` (`Modifier::SetSelectedFavorite`). The DevKit lists its errors: `APIERR_GENERAL` when there are no favorites, `APIERR_BADNAME` when there is no such favorite, `APIERR_BADELEMENTTYPE` when it isn't a label favorite.
- `GetAvailableLibraryParts` reports each part's `type` on AC28+, from `LibPart::GetType`: `Object`, `Image`, `Text`, `BinaryListCrit` or `Other` (`ACAPI::Library::LibPartType` in `ACAPI/Library/LibPart.hpp`).
- `LibraryManager::GetLibPartByGSMObject` reports the library part that part 6's `CreateLibraryPart` makes.

- New `SetLibraryPartMetadata`: `author`, `keywords`, `license`, `licenseVersion`, `placeable`, `uiDefault`, `isSubtype`, `hierarchicalPagesUsed` and `password`, only the given ones. It's the write side of #1272's `GetLibraryPartMetadata`, but it's a separate command, so it doesn't need #1272 merged.

title: Leave sub-element objects out of GetAllElements, as GetElementsByType does
body:
## Problem

`GetAllElements` also returns the objects that belong to another element: zone stamps and the parts of stairs and railings. `GetElementsByType` has left these out since the `IncludeSubElemObjects` filter was added (1ce6d1d3).

The built-in scripts that look at "all elements" therefore saw them as elements of their own. On a small office model, Project Health Check listed every stair part under *Elements without an Element ID* and *Unclassified elements*. On TestProject.pla, 141 of the 272 elements `GetAllElements` returns are such objects.

## Change

- **Add-on:** `GetAllElements` and `GetElementsInDrawOrder` follow the same rule as `GetElementsByType`. Sub-element objects are returned only when the `IncludeSubElemObjects` filter is given. One helper, `IsSubElemObject`, is used by both listing paths. The three command descriptions say so.
- **builtin-scripts:** `utilities.archicad.get_elements` drops sub-element objects itself, so the scripts behave the same with released Add-Ons (1.7.2 and older).
- **New check:** `archicad-addon/Test/checks/get_all_elements_skips_subelement_objects.json` creates a zone on story 1 and verifies that:
  - `GetAllElements` returns the zone without its stamp;
  - with `IncludeSubElemObjects` it returns both;
  - `GetElementsByType` Object behaves the same way.

  The check first deletes the template's elevation markers, because they are listed on every story.
- **Expected outputs re-recorded** for the four examples that list all elements: `filter_elements`, `get_and_set_details_of_elements`, `get_connected_elements` and `save_as_module_file`. Each was compared with a run that adds `IncludeSubElemObjects` to every `GetAllElements` call (the old behaviour). Their differences come from this change only, except that `get_and_set_details_of_elements` also picks up the wall detail fields added on `main` since it was last recorded.

## Behaviour change

Scripts and the Grasshopper *Get All Elements* component now get fewer elements: only the ones the user placed. To get the old list, pass `"filters": ["IncludeSubElemObjects"]`.

## Tested

On Archicad 29 with a local RelWithDebInfo build:
- the new check passes, 6/6 (`tapir_test_runner.py check ... --brief`);
- the 8 examples whose stored outputs use `GetAllElements` were run against TestProject.pla. After re-recording, the four above match. `get_classifications_of_mainelements_and_subelements`, `get_design_options` and `highlight_elements` pass unchanged. `test_ifc_commands` differs only in IFC property fields that are out of date on `main` and unrelated to this change.

title: CreateHatches: buildingMaterialId is lost and the tool default fill is used
body:
Archicad 29 AUT build 3200, Tapir 1.7.2, Windows. Reproduced in a disposable copy, using native API.ExecuteAddOnCommand (TapirCommand), without a geometry wrapper.

In an active worksheet, create a hatch with a valid building material and no fill/pens overrides:
```json
{"hatchesData":[{"coordinates":[{"x":0,"y":0},{"x":1,"y":0},{"x":1,"y":1},{"x":0,"y":1}],"buildingMaterialId":{"guid":"56403B22-CF68-924A-B1FF-F47DE89A6AEB"},"layerIndex":1}]}
```

CreateHatches succeeds and returns an elementId. GetDetailsOfElements on it returns:
```json
{"fillPenIndex":179,"fillBackgroundPenIndex":0,"fillId":{"guid":"E1913637-3D9D-D740-BF63-7791B52C344A"},"buildingMaterialId":{"guid":"00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"}}
```
Expected: the explicitly supplied building material is retained and used. Actual: it reads back as the null GUID, with the default fill/pens. The input GUID is the project building material Erdreich (cut fill 42, pens 35/55).

The current main schema accepts buildingMaterialId. CreateHatchesCommand::SetTypeSpecificParameters assigns hatch.buildingMaterial but does not switch the hatch into a building-material mode; please check whether a hatch flag/type also needs setting. This is a source observation, not a tested fix.

Workaround: read the material cut fill/pens and create an ordinary fill; this loses the material association. Test hatch deleted.

title: MoveElements: silent success for a worksheet element when another database is active
body:
Archicad 29 AUT build 3200, Tapir 1.7.2, Windows. Native TapirCommand requests, reproduced in a disposable project copy.

1. ChangeWindow to worksheet A. CreateTexts at (0,0,0), layerIndex 1 (Archicad layer), text "CODEX ROUND9 TEMP".

```json
{"executionResults":[{"success":true}]}
```
GetDetailsOfElements still reports position {"x":0,"y":0}.
4. ChangeWindow back to A and send the identical MoveElements request. It again returns success, and the position now reads {"x":1,"y":0}.

Expected: either move the referenced element or return a clear active-database error. Actual: success without a change when its worksheet is inactive. The layer is visible and unlocked; the same element and vector work as soon as its owning worksheet is active.

Related control: DeleteElements while B was active returned success:false, error -2130313215 "Failed to delete the element." Deleting in A succeeded. This report concerns the misleading MoveElements success; it is distinct from the hidden-layer case #555 / #861. Main still calls MoveElement after the editability check without an owning-database check.

Workaround: activate the owning worksheet before edits. Test text deleted.

body:

CreateDrawings from a worksheet view, position {"x":1,"y":1}. Readback: pos={"x":0.572,"y":0.485}, modelOffset={"x":0,"y":0}, bounds={"xMin":1,"yMin":1,"xMax":1.06,"yMax":1.12}.

title: MEP: the 237 functions left out of #1456 (preference table rows by key, AC27 tables, tool defaults, routing parameters, ports), with the DevKit declarations
body:
This continues #1456, whose six parts are open as #1457–#1462 and which hit the six-part limit. Below are the 237 MEP functions none of those parts uses. Each comes with its declaration (from the AC27–AC30 DevKits the build checks use: 27.3001, 28.3001, 29.3000, 30.3000) and the design decisions, which I've made as the requester. Everything is in namespace `ACAPI::MEP`, in `Support/Modules/MEPAPI/ACAPI/MEP<Class>.hpp` (for example `MEPPipeBranchPreferenceTable.hpp`). `MEPCommands.cpp` on `main` shows the includes and the `#ifdef ServerMainVers_2800` gating to follow.

**Building now, without waiting for #1457–#1462 to merge.** These parts must not wait for #1456's pull requests and must not be built on their branches: a part can only build on earlier parts of its own issue. So:
- Each part puts its commands in a **new source file** (named per part below) instead of `MEPCommands.cpp`. All six of #1456's parts edit that file heavily, so this part then only overlaps them in the `AddOnMain.cpp` registration, which the steward merges.
- Where a part needs a helper that exists only on one of #1456's branches (the table-type lookup from #1459/#1460, the JSON of a tool default from #1461), copy that code into the new file. #1459 did the same with #1293's changes. Keep it `static` with a different name, so the copies don't collide once both are merged.
- Never change a command that #1457–#1462 add.
- Register the new commands in a new `CommandGroup` "MEP Commands (extended)" block right after the existing MEP block in `AddOnMain.cpp`, with the version `main` carries.
- Ids as `{guid}` (`UniqueID` from GUID as on `main`), enums by enumerator name, lengths in metres, one execution result per item, writes in one undo step per call.


## 1. Preference table rows by key: branch and elbow tables

New file `MEPPreferenceTableRowCommands.cpp/.hpp` (see "Building now" above), AC28+:
- `GetMEPPreferenceTableRows {tableId, keys: [key]}`: for each key, `{key, valid, values}`. `valid` comes from `IsRowValid…`. `values` holds the table type's fields by name (`mainAxisDiameter`, `branchAxisDiameter`, `length`, `branchOffset`, `connectionLength`, `description` for branches; the elbow fields for elbows), each from its `Get…By…` getter.
- `SetMEPPreferenceTableRows {tableId, rows: [{key, values}]}`: partial. Only the given fields are set, each with its `Set…By…` setter, inside the table's `Modify`. Each row gets its own result.
- `AddMEPPreferenceTableRows {tableId, rows: [{key, values?}]}`: `AddNewRow (key)`, then the given values. Returns the new row index.
- `DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRows {tableId, keys}`: `DeleteRowBy…`.
- **The key:** AC29+ uses the table's `Key` struct (below) with the `…ByKey` functions. AC28 takes the same JSON key and calls the `…ByReferenceIds` functions with its reference ids; it rejects an angle it can't use, with a clear error. Find the table type from `tableId` the same way `GetMEPPreferenceTables` does on #1459's branch: copy that lookup into the new file rather than depending on it.
- Branch tables (pipe and duct) and elbow tables (pipe and duct) in this part.

The `Key` structs (AC29/AC30, `ACAPI/MEP<Table>.hpp`):
```cpp
// DuctBranchPreferenceTable
struct Key { uint32_t mainAxisReferenceId; double branchAxisAngle; uint32_t branchAxisReferenceId; };
// DuctElbowPreferenceTable
struct Key { uint32_t referenceId; double angle; };
// DuctTransitionPreferenceTable
struct Key { uint32_t beginReferenceId; uint32_t endReferenceId; };
// PipeBranchPreferenceTable
struct Key { uint32_t mainAxisReferenceId; double branchAxisAngle; uint32_t branchAxisReferenceId; };
// PipeElbowPreferenceTable
struct Key { uint32_t referenceId; double angle; };
// PipeTransitionPreferenceTable
struct Key { uint32_t beginReferenceId; uint32_t endReferenceId; };
```

## 3. Preference tables on Archicad 27

AC27 has a single `PreferenceTableBase` for every table: `ACAPI/MEPPreferenceTableBase.hpp`, namespace `ACAPI::MEP` with `inline namespace v1`. The tables come from `GetPipePreferenceTableContainer ()`, `GetDuctPreferenceTableContainer ()` and `GetCableCarrierPreferenceTableContainer ()` (`ACAPI/MEP…PreferenceTableContainer.hpp`). Their values are addressed by `PreferenceTableShape` (`Rectangular`, `Circular`, in `MEPEnums.hpp`) and an index, not by a key.
- On AC27 the part 1 commands take `{shape, index}` rows instead of a key. Get returns `{shape, index, value, description}` (`GetValue`, `GetDescription`) and `size` per shape (`GetSize`). Set works through `PreferenceTableBase::Modify`.
- `GetMEPPreferenceTables` also gets an AC27 path that lists `GetPreferenceTables ()` of each container, with `name` (`GetName`) and `exists`.
- `PreferenceTableContainerBase::Modify` is used to add a table where the AC27 modifier allows it; otherwise it is left out with a note.
- Main's MEP code is `#ifdef ServerMainVers_2800`. Add an `#elif defined (ServerMainVers_2700)` branch for this part only. Needs part 1.

## 4. MEP tool defaults: create, read and modify

New file `MEPDefaultCommands.cpp/.hpp`:
- `GetMEPToolDefaults` already comes in #1461. Don't depend on it. This part adds `ModifyMEPToolDefaults {defaults: [{tool, domain, settings}]}`. `tool` is one of `RoutingSegment`, `RoutingNode`, `RigidSegment`, `Elbow`, `Bend`, `Branch`, `Transition`, `FlexibleSegment` or `ElectricalPanel`. `domain` is `Ventilation`, `Piping` or `CableCarrier`.
- Each default is created with `Create<Tool>Default (domain)`. Then `Modify` sets the given keys:
  - insulation thickness, or `insulation: null` to remove it;
  - factor radius (elbow and bend);
  - preference table (elbow AC28+, transition AC29+);
  - the routing node's bend, elbow or transition default (bend AC27–28, elbow AC29+);
  - the routing segment's rigid segment default.

  Then the default is set as the Archicad tool default, as #1463's `SetOpeningDefault` does (`Modify`, then `SetAsArchicadDefault`).
- Reads, for `GetMEPToolDefaults` parity on older versions: `RigidSegmentDefault::GetWidth`, `GetHeight` and `GetShape` (AC27–28), `ElementDefault::GetShapeOfPort` (AC27), and the port defaults on AC30 (`GetPortDefaults`, `GetPipingPortDefaults`, `GetVentilationPortDefaults`, `GetCableCarrierPortDefaults`) as `ports`. Return them from a new `GetMEPToolDefaultDetails {tool, domain}` so #1461 stays untouched.
- `PlaceMEPFlexibleSegmentPolylines {segments: [{polyline, startDirection?, endDirection?}]}` (AC28+): `FlexibleSegmentDefault::PlacePolyline`.
- `ClearElectricalProjectSettings {loadClassifications?, wiringTypes?}` (AC30) and `circuitDefaultCount` in the details of `ElectricalPanel` (AC30).

title: Commands that miss a patch release keep the previous version (44 commands of 1.7.3 registered as 1.7.2)
body:
44 of the 112 commands that `AddOnMain.cpp` registers for the first time in release **1.7.3** carry the version **1.7.2** in their `RegisterCommand<…>(group, "1.7.2", …)` call — for example `Change3DStyles`, `Create3DStyles`, `CreateAttributeFolders`, `DeleteAttributeFolders`, `Get3DCutPlanes`, `Get3DStyleDetails`, `GetCategoryValuesOfElements`, `GetContainingDatabases`. Release 1.7.2 does not have them (compared by tag: the 1.7.2 source does not register them, the 1.7.3 source does). The command reference shows the same version, so it says these commands exist since 1.7.2.

**Why it happens:** a command gets the version `main` carries when its pull request is written (as the README says to do). Since the weekly releases, many pull requests stay open across a release: written while `main` carried 1.7.2, merged after 1.7.2 was tagged, released in 1.7.3. For minor and major releases the release workflow already rewrites the commands registered with the skipped version; for a patch release nothing rewrites the ones that missed the previous release.

**Effect:** a script or agent that checks the version before calling a command (for example "available since 1.7.2", and the add-on reports 1.7.2) calls a command that is not there and gets `4010`. Documentation generated from the registrations shows the wrong release.

**Possible fixes** (either would do):
- In the weekly release, before tagging version X: every command registered with a version lower than X that the previous release tag does not register gets X. That is the same rewrite the workflow already does for minor/major releases, extended to commands that missed the previous release.
- Or at merge time: the build check (or the steward when it merges `main` into a bot branch) flags or updates a newly registered command whose version is lower than `tools/package_info.json`.

Found while regenerating a command catalog from the release tags; it now takes the first tag that registers a command as its version instead of the registered string.

title: GetElementAtCoordinate: no hit is an error instead of found:false, and AC28 misses a slab at the default z
body:
`GetElementAtCoordinate` (new in 1.7.3) has two problems. Tapir 1.7.3 (release), Archicad 26 (GER, 7004) and Archicad 28 (GER, 7006), Windows 11, untitled projects from the stock templates, floor plan active.

**1. Nothing found is reported as an error.** Searching where there is no element returns `{"error": {"code": -2130313112, "message": "Failed to search for an element at the coordinate."}}` on both versions, although the output schema has `found`. A caller cannot tell "no element here" from a real failure. Expected: `{"found": false}`.

**2. Archicad 28 misses a slab at the default `z`.** A slab created with `{"level": 0, "thickness": 0.2, "polygonCoordinates": [(1000,1000), (1005,1000), (1005,1004), (1000,1004)]}`, searched with `{"elementType": "Slab", "coordinate": {"x": 1002, "y": 1002}}`:

| | AC26 | AC28 |
|---|---|---|
| `z` omitted (0) | `found: true` | error above |
| `"z": 0.1` | — | `found: true` |

The slab's top is at 0. Reproduced twice on AC28 in freshly started Archicads. Perhaps AC28 needs the point strictly inside the slab's height range, or a tolerance; either way the default `z` should find a slab whose top is at the story level, as on AC26.

title: MeasureTexts: fontIndex/fontName are optional in the schema but one of them is required
body:
`MeasureTexts` (new in 1.7.3, #1129): the schema marks both `fontIndex` and `fontName` as optional, but a text without either is refused. Tapir 1.7.3 (release), Archicad 26 (GER, 7004) and Archicad 28 (GER, 7006), Windows 11, untitled projects from the stock templates, floor plan active.

```json
{"texts": [{"text": "Hello", "height": 2.5}]}
```
→ `{"measurements": [{"error": {"code": -2130313112, "message": "Each text requires 'fontName' or 'fontIndex'."}}]}` on both versions (reproduced twice). With `"fontIndex": 1` it measures correctly (15.9 mm on paper, 1.59 m with `inModelUnits` at 1:100).

A caller that builds the call from the schema, as an MCP client or a generated wrapper does, gets an error for a schema-valid call. Either the schema should require one of them (`anyOf: [{required: [fontIndex]}, {required: [fontName]}]`), or the command should fall back to a default font (the text tool's default, for example).

Side note: `fontName` is matched against Archicad's font list, not Windows font names (`"Arial"` gives "No loaded font is named 'Arial'"). The description could point to `GetFontsByName`.

title: Discord bot: log every skipped message and move the 👀 past them
body:
## Problem

[Run 40358025580](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/actions/runs/40358025580) found one new message each in `#user-support-channel` and `#announcements`. It printed nothing for either message, filed no issue and left the 👀 where it was. The 12:01 run saw 0 messages in both channels, so these messages were new.

Some messages never reached the classifier: messages shorter than `MIN_MESSAGE_LENGTH` (25), attachments without text, bot or system messages, and the newest message while it is under 10 minutes old (its author "may still be typing"). The bot dropped them without a log line, and only classified messages moved the 👀.

## Change

- The channel line now also says how many messages come after the 👀 (`N message(s) in the last 1440 minutes, K after the 👀 checkpoint`). Before, it only gave the 24-hour window count, which read as "new messages".
- Every message after the 👀 that is not classified now gets a log line with the reason: bot or system message, wrong message type, too short, attachment without text, or left for the next run because its author may still be typing (with its age).
- Human messages that are skipped (too short, attachment without text) count as checked, so the 👀 moves past them. It still never moves past a message the classifier gave no answer for. Bot messages still never get the 👀.
- `is_candidate` became `skip_reason`, which returns why a message is skipped. README updated.

## Testing

`python -m unittest test_discord_issue_bot`: 56 tests pass, 3 of them new (a short message moves the checkpoint without classification, a short message does not move it past an unclassified one, every skip is logged).

title: SolveStairBaseline crashes Archicad 29 with one straight stair, including an input accepted by CreateStairs
body:
Tested on 2026-10-26 with released Tapir 1.7.3, Archicad 29 AUT build 3200, Windows, in a disposable PLN. Related command introduction: #1210 / #1214. This is a runtime crash report, not a request for the command. I have not established whether it is a regression.

## Single input already accepted by CreateStairs
The project has story index 2 at elevation 6.4 m. This input successfully created a temporary straight Stair (with id T173-Treppe-01 added only for CreateStairs):
```json
{"stairsData":[{"baseLinePoints":[{"x":110,"y":0},{"x":114.2,"y":0}],"zCoordinate":6.4,"floorIndex":2,"totalHeight":2.8,"flightWidth":1.2,"stepNum":16,"riserHeight":0.175,"treadDepth":0.28}]}
```
The created stair had a 3D box approximately x=110..114.2, y=0..1.2, z=6.4..9.2. All temporary elements were removed, absence read back, and the PLN saved before the solver call.

Calling **SolveStairBaseline** with exactly the JSON above (one item, not a mixed batch) closed the HTTP connection without a JSON response. The test-project window disappeared and it was absent from subsequent live instance discovery; a separate MAIN instance stayed available.

## Separate too-short case
After reopening and saving the test PLN, this independent call also crashed it:
```json
{"stairsData":[{"baseLinePoints":[{"x":110,"y":5},{"x":111,"y":5}],"zCoordinate":6.4,"floorIndex":2,"totalHeight":2.8,"flightWidth":1.2,"stepNum":16,"riserHeight":0.175,"treadDepth":0.28}]}
```
Expected: a Correct/Solved/NotSolved result or a structured error; the Archicad process/window should survive either input.

No empty-object schema probes were used. Schemas were read offline, both risky calls followed separate saves, and no solver element was created. The single straight valid input shows that neither multiple stairs in one call nor only an impossible baseline is required. No crash stack/minidump is available. Exact logical inputs and post-disconnect instance observations were retained locally.

title: GetDetailsOfElements: Stair elevation is doubled, baseline is local, and treadDepth is inconsistent
body:
Live readback in released Tapir 1.7.3, Archicad 29 AUT 3200 / Windows (2026-10-26). Related reader feature #823/#826; this concerns the returned data, not a request for Stair support. Regression status unknown.

A fresh temporary stair was created successfully with:
```json
{"stairsData":[{"id":"T173-Treppe-01","baseLinePoints":[{"x":110,"y":0},{"x":114.2,"y":0}],"zCoordinate":6.4,"floorIndex":2,"totalHeight":2.8,"flightWidth":1.2,"stepNum":16,"riserHeight":0.175,"treadDepth":0.28}]}
```
Story 2 is at 6.4 m. GetDetailsOfElements for the returned GUID reported:
```json
{"type":"Stair","floorIndex":2,"id":"T173-Treppe-01","details":{"stepNum":16,"riserHeight":0.175,"treadDepth":0,"flightWidth":1.2,"totalHeight":2.8,"level":6.4,"zCoordinate":12.8,"finishVisible":true,"baseLinePoints":[{"x":0,"y":0},{"x":4.2,"y":0}]}}
```

- zCoordinate is 12.8 although the actual stair base is 6.4; level also reads 6.4. Existing stairs on stories +6.4 and -3.05 similarly read zCoordinate=12.8 and -6.1 respectively.
- The returned baseline starts at (0,0), while the input/model is at (110,0). If local coordinates are intentional, a placement transform or explicit coordinate-space contract is needed for a round trip.
- Fresh readback treadDepth=0 for input 0.28. An existing straight stair read treadDepth=1 while two successive riser positions in its parent Get3DGeometryOfElements model are horizontally 0.2799999997 m apart. This reader discrepancy should be distinguished from the older CreateStairs input issue #425.

title: GetOpeningDetails returns translated points instead of direction vectors for opening axes
body:
Observed in released Tapir 1.7.3, Archicad 29 AUT 3200 / Windows, 2026-10-26. Regression status unknown. Related API coverage #1463.

A simple disposable fixture makes the translation evident. Story index 2 is at 6.4 m.

1. Relevant wall item from the original two-wall CreateWalls call (unrelated second wall omitted):
```json
{"wallsData":[{"id":"T173-Wand-01","begCoordinate":{"x":100,"y":0},"endCoordinate":{"x":104,"y":0},"floorIndex":2,"zCoordinate":0,"height":2.8,"structureType":"Basic","thickness":0.2}]}
```
2. CreateOpenings in the returned wall (HOST_GUID is that returned GUID):
```json
{"openingsData":[{"ownerElementId":{"guid":"HOST_GUID"},"basePoint":{"x":102,"y":0.1,"z":7.4},"width":1,"height":1}]}
```
3. GetOpeningDetails with the created Opening GUID, in the normal elements array, returned this geometry:
```json
{"anchorPoint":{"x":102,"y":0,"z":8.4},"extrusionDirection":{"x":100,"y":1,"z":6.4},"xAxis":{"x":101,"y":0,"z":6.4},"yAxis":{"x":100,"y":0,"z":7.4},"polygon":[{"x":-0.5,"y":-0.5},{"x":0.5,"y":-0.5},{"x":0.5,"y":0.5},{"x":-0.5,"y":0.5}]}
```
The three vectors contain the host origin (100,0,6.4). Subtracting that origin gives extrusion=(0,1,0), xAxis=(1,0,0), yAxis=(0,0,1). As returned, they are not unit direction vectors. A translation appears to have been applied to vectors as though they were points; this is an inference from the output, not a source-code diagnosis.

Two additional existing Opening elements also showed translated axes, so this was not limited to this fresh fixture. The schema describes xAxis/yAxis as the opening plane axes and extrusionDirection as its direction.

Expected: transform directions with the linear part only (or document a different representation and provide enough data to use it). Anchor points should remain world-coordinate points. All temporary fixtures were removed and verified absent. HOST_GUID above is an explicit placeholder; no project file is attached.

body:

A temporary Slab D74B4639-549D-407F-B938-CCB27F02ECE4 was the target and a temporary Stair A7032D72-2956-402E-9EC1-DA1B1C8DABC5 the operator. Both were on editable layer1.

```json
{"solidLinks":[{"targetId":{"guid":"D74B4639-549D-407F-B938-CCB27F02ECE4"},"operatorId":{"guid":"A7032D72-2956-402E-9EC1-DA1B1C8DABC5"}}]}
```
Response:
```json
{"executionResults":[{"error":{"code":-2130313110,"message":"Failed to remove solid element link."},"success":false}]}
```

5. Immediate GetSolidElementLinks for BOTH elements then returned:

```json
{"solidLinks":[{"solidLinksWithTheGivenTarget":[],"solidLinksWithTheGivenOperator":[]},{"solidLinksWithTheGivenTarget":[],"solidLinksWithTheGivenOperator":[]}]}
```

title: Get3DBoundingBoxes returns inverted sentinel bounds (+/-1e35) for Stair treads
body:
Observed in released Tapir 1.7.3, Archicad 29 AUT 3200 / Windows, on 2026-10-26. Related parent-Stair bbox fix #563/#564, but this report concerns tread subelements rather than the parent Stair. Regression status unknown.

GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements on a real Stair returned these two entries in stairTreads:
```json
[{"elementId":{"guid":"06510AF3-F482-41D7-B612-04C5DF8DD949"}},{"elementId":{"guid":"0D4BE99C-EA44-431B-B73E-8576F07A6C05"}}]
```
Passing them to Get3DBoundingBoxes as normal elements returned, for EACH tread:
```json
{"boundingBox3D":{"xMin":1e35,"xMax":-1e35,"yMin":1e35,"yMax":-1e35,"zMin":6.4,"zMax":6.4}}
```
The parent Stair in the same bbox call returned finite, ordered bounds. Its Get3DGeometryOfElements model was also successfully available.

Additional diagnostic: direct Get3DGeometryOfElements on the two tread GUIDs returned per-item -2130313215, "Failed to get the 3D model of the element", even after activating the 3DModel window. I am not claiming direct tread geometry must be supported if the underlying API cannot provide it; returning a clear unsupported/error result is acceptable.

The bounding-box problem is that success-shaped output contains xMin>xMax and yMin>yMax sentinel values. This is neither a usable bbox nor an error item, and can silently contaminate geometric calculations.

Expected: a valid ordered box, or a per-element error/unsupported indication when the tread has no directly accessible geometry. No existing Stair/tread was modified for these reads.

title: Fix the GetElementsInDrawOrder crash: walk between DrawOrderInit and DrawOrderTerm
body:
`GetElementsInDrawOrder` called `ACAPI_DrawOrder_DrawOrderGetNext` without `DrawOrderInit`, which the DevKit requires before the walk, and Archicad crashed.

- A small RAII helper (`DrawOrderWalk`) calls `DrawOrderInit` before the walk and `DrawOrderTerm` on every way out of `GetElementsInDrawOrderFromCurrentDatabase`, including the early error returns.
- `MigrationHelper.hpp` (AC25/26): new `DrawOrderInit`/`DrawOrderTerm` shims over `APIDb_DrawOrderInitID`/`TermID`. The `GetNext` shim now passes the filter value itself as `par1`, as the DevKit's `Element_Test` example does (`(GSPtr)(Int32)(APIFilt_…)`), using the file's existing `(void*) (GS::IntPtr)` idiom.
- New check `Test/checks/get_elements_in_draw_order.json`: every element, walls only, and walls only a second time (a second walk must start from the beginning, which only works when Init/Term pair up).

Tested with local builds, hidden Archicad, community test runner `trial`:

title: Test runner: skip checks that need a newer Archicad (minArchicad)
body:
A check file can now name the oldest Archicad version it runs on with `minArchicad`, next to `minTapir`. Older versions report the file as skipped instead of running it.

Why: `graphic_override_structured_criterion.json` exercises commands that answer `APIERR_NOTSUPPORTED` before Archicad 27 (`#ifdef ServerMainVers_2700` in `GraphicOverrideCommands.cpp`). On AC26, every `test --every-check` therefore reported a FAIL that had nothing to do with the pull request under test. That check now carries `"minArchicad": "27"`.

- `run_checks` reads the version once via `API.GetProductInfo` (the existing `archicad_version`) and skips with `needs Archicad 27, running 26`.
- README documents the field.
- Unit test: skipped on 26, run on 27. All 29 runner tests pass.

title: ModifyMEPRoutingElements: set the insulation of a route
body:
## Summary

`ModifyMEPRoutingElements` gets an optional `insulationThickness` (metres; `0` removes the insulation), and `GetMEPRoutingElements` reports it on each segment. Until now a route's insulation could only be set in its Selection Settings dialog. It applies to the whole route, the way the dialog's Insulation setting does:

```text
ModifyMEPRoutingElements { elementId, insulationThickness }
  route defaults           rigid segment, elbow (bend on AC28) and transition defaults
  each segment             its rigid segment default
  each node                its elbow / bend and transition defaults
```

Setting only the route's defaults insulates the segments but not the existing elbows and transitions, so every segment and node is updated too. The CableCarrier domain is not covered (cable carriers have no insulation). Archicad 28 and newer, like the rest of the MEP commands.

Also included: `Examples/mep_route_insulation.py` and the community check `Test/checks/mep_route_insulation.json`.

## Evidence

Archicad 29 (macOS), this branch merged into current `main`, on a duct route with one bend (two segments, three nodes) in a small test project made from the default template:

- **Before:** `GetMEPRoutingElements` → segments `insulationThickness`: `[0.02, 0.02]`
- `insulationThickness: 0` → `[none, none]`
- `insulationThickness: 0.035` → `[0.035, 0.035]`
- After `0.02`, the route's Info Box showed Insulation ticked and 20 (uniform), and the 3D window drew the bend insulated too.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

It adds one optional input field and one output field. Nothing that worked before changes.

**Blast Radius:** small

Only routes given `insulationThickness` are touched. A route that was already insulated by hand gets the new thickness on every segment, elbow and transition, including any part someone had customized.

title: Set3DProjectionSettings: set an axonometry as well as a perspective
body:
## Summary

`Set3DProjectionSettings` took only a perspective, so an isometric or a side view of the 3D window meant typing into the 3D Projection Settings dialog. It now also takes an axonometry. Only the given values change:

```diff
 Set3DProjectionSettings
-  { perspective }                       required
+  { perspective } | { axonometry }      exactly one
+  axonometry: { projectionType?, azimuth?, transformationMatrix? }
+    from a perspective: switch back to the last axonometry first (switchOnlyAxonoOrPersp)
+    read the current API_AxonoPars, change the given fields, Change3DProjectionSets
+    transformationMatrix: its inverse is computed for invtranmat, a singular one is refused

 Get3DProjectionSettings
   axonometric: { transformationMatrix
+                , projectionType, azimuth }
```

`projectionType` is the API's `projMod` (`#/AxonometryProjectionType`). Archicad works out the matrix itself from the type and the azimuth, so an agent never writes a matrix for the predefined views:

| Wanted | `axonometry` |
|---|---|
| Isometric from the south-east (X −30°, Y 30°, Z 90°) | `{"projectionType": "Isometric", "azimuth": 270}` |
| Isometric from the north-east | `{"projectionType": "Isometric", "azimuth": 0}` |
| Side view from the south | `{"projectionType": "YZ", "azimuth": 270}` |
| An exact saved view | `{"projectionType": "Custom", "transformationMatrix": [...]}` |

Also:
- The perspective schema now gives units and behaviour. `azimuth` is in degrees and recomputed by Archicad from the camera and target. `viewCone` is in degrees.
- The descriptions note that the 3D window shows the change only after `RebuildView`.
- `InvertTranmat` was in `ProjectCommands.cpp` and `ExtendedElementCommands.cpp`, and this would have been the third copy, so it moves to `CommandBase`.

## Evidence

Archicad 29, macOS, a test project. The new check `Test/checks/set_3d_axonometry.json` was run step by step:

```text
PASS isometric from the south-east        success == true
PASS read the isometric                   projectionType == "Isometric", azimuth ~= 270
PASS                                      matrix row 1 (0.866, 0.866, 0), row 2 (-0.5, 0.5, 1)
PASS side view from the east              projectionType == "YZ", screen X = model Y, screen Y = model Z
PASS custom matrix                        read back unchanged
PASS singular matrix                      success == false
failures: 0
```

Every type was also set at several azimuths and read back:
- YZ and XZ give the same side view, looking from the azimuth.
- XY is the top view, rotated by the azimuth.
- The predefined axonometries look from 45° past the azimuth.
- `Parallel` reads back as `Custom` with the matrix unchanged.

- **Before:** `{"axonometry": {...}}` was refused by the schema; only a perspective could be set.
- **After:** the calls above set the projection, and the 3D window shows it after `RebuildView`.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Additive. A call with only `perspective` behaves as before. Get adds two fields to `axonometric`.

**Blast Radius:** small

- The new `oneOf` refuses a call that gives both `perspective` and `axonometry`; no such call could exist before.
- `GetOpeningTransformations` and `GetSurveyPointTransformation` now use the shared `InvertTranmat`. Its maths and threshold (1e-12) are the same as both old copies.

title: Built-in scripts using tkinter crash on macOS: Tcl version conflict (launcher leaks TCL_LIBRARY into script environment)
body:
## Built-in scripts using tkinter crash on macOS: Tcl version conflict (launcher leaks TCL_LIBRARY into script environment)

### Summary
Running the built-in script **AutomaticNumberingBasedOnPolyline** (and presumably any built-in script that opens a `ScriptWindow` via `utilities/ui.py`) fails immediately on macOS when `tk.Tk()` is created. The script's Python (uv-managed CPython 3.14.5, Tcl/Tk 9.0.3) picks up the Tcl library folder bundled inside `TapirInstaller.app` (Tcl 8.6.16), which causes a version conflict.

### Environment
- macOS: 26.5.2, Apple Silicon (aarch64)
- Archicad: 28 / 7006
- Tapir add-on: 1.7.3
- Script Python: uv-managed `cpython-3.14.5-macos-aarch64-none` (Tcl/Tk 9.0.3)
- Script environment: `~/.cache/uv/environments-v2/automaticnumberingbasedonpolyline-501d63ab864a25b3`

### Steps to reproduce
1. In Archicad, open the Tapir palette.
2. Run the built-in script **AutomaticNumberingBasedOnPolyline**.
3. The script fails before the window appears.

### Expected behavior
The script window opens.

### Actual behavior
`tk.Tk()` raises `_tkinter.TclError`:
File “.../builtin-scripts/utilities/ui.py”, line 72, in init
self.root = tk.Tk()
File “.../cpython-3.14.5-macos-aarch64-none/lib/python3.14/tkinter/init.py”, line 2484, in init
self.tk = _tkinter.create(screenName, baseName, className, interactive, wantobjects, useTk, sync, use)
_tkinter.TclError: Cannot find a usable init.tcl in the following directories:
/tools/deps/lib/tcl9.0 /Users/<user>/.cache/uv/environments-v2/automaticnumberingbasedonpolyline-501d63ab864a25b3/lib/tcl9.0 ...

/private/var/folders/.../T/TapirInstaller/1793026743_3155/TapirInstaller.app/Contents/Frameworks/_tcl_data/init.tcl: version conflict for package “Tcl”: have 9.0.3, need exactly 8.6.16
version conflict for package “Tcl”: have 9.0.3, need exactly 8.6.16
while executing
“package require -exact Tcl 8.6.16”


Full traceback attached below.

### Analysis
- The error message shows Tcl 9.0.3 loading `init.tcl` from `TapirInstaller.app/Contents/Frameworks/_tcl_data/`. That folder layout matches a PyInstaller-frozen app, which sets `TCL_LIBRARY` / `TK_LIBRARY` to its bundled Tcl/Tk 8.6 data at startup.
- These environment variables appear to be inherited by the child process that runs the script under the uv-managed Python. That Python's tkinter is built against Tcl 9.0.3, so it loads the wrong `init.tcl` and fails on `package require -exact Tcl 8.6.16`.
- A secondary issue: without `TCL_LIBRARY`, Tcl only searches paths relative to the uv *environment* (`~/.cache/uv/environments-v2/...`), not the base interpreter (`~/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.14.5-macos-aarch64-none/lib/tcl9.0`), so simply unsetting the variables may not be enough on its own.

### Suggested fix
1. When launching script subprocesses, remove `TCL_LIBRARY` and `TK_LIBRARY` (and any other PyInstaller-injected variables) from the child environment.
2. Optionally, make `utilities/ui.py` robust by pointing Tcl/Tk at the libraries matching the running interpreter before creating the root window.

### Proposed Workaround
Add this to `builtin-scripts/utilities/ui.py` after `import tkinter as tk`:

```python
import os
import sys

def _fix_tcl_tk_env():
    for var in ("TCL_LIBRARY", "TK_LIBRARY"):
        os.environ.pop(var, None)
    lib = os.path.join(sys.base_prefix, "lib")
    tcl_dir = os.path.join(lib, f"tcl{tk.TclVersion}")
    tk_dir = os.path.join(lib, f"tk{tk.TkVersion}")
    if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(tcl_dir, "init.tcl")):
        os.environ["TCL_LIBRARY"] = tcl_dir
    if os.path.isdir(tk_dir):
        os.environ["TK_LIBRARY"] = tk_dir

_fix_tcl_tk_env()
```

Note: the built-in scripts live in a temp folder (`/private/var/folders/.../T/Tapir/`), so local patches may be overwritten on update.
