title: Proposal: let community Archicad test results gate the bot's auto-merge (commit status instead of comment)
body:
## Current state

The steward asks the issue's author to test each bot PR in Archicad, and the community test runner (`tools/community-test-runner/`) answers such requests with a comment whose first line is machine-readable (`tapir-test: AC28 GER PASS 17/17 build <sha> tapir <version>`). I run it on AC26 and AC28 for bot PRs.

These results are not used anywhere, though:

- `claude_auto_merge.yml` gates on the build checks, the `claude-review` status and open human threads. A failed Archicad test does not hold a bot PR back; only a person reading the comment can.
- Every result comment counts as a human comment, so `claude_pr_review.yml` starts a re-review. For a PASS it answers "Looks correct, nothing blocking" and changes nothing, but it costs a model run, which is scarce (#977). Today I tested ten bot PRs, and each PASS comment started a re-review. I have stopped posting PASS results for PRs that bring no checks of their own for that reason.

## Proposal

1. **Turn a result comment into a commit status.** A small workflow on `issue_comment` reads a comment whose first line matches `^tapir-test: AC(\d+)\S* \S+ (PASS|FAIL) \d+/\d+ build ([0-9a-f]{7,40})`. It acts only for authors listed in a repository variable (e.g. `ARCHICAD_TESTERS`), and only when the sha is the PR's current head. Then it sets the commit status `archicad-test/AC<v>` to success or failure on that head. Testers need no extra token, and the workflow runs no model and no PR code.
2. **Let auto-merge respect it.** A `failure` of any `archicad-test/*` status on the head blocks the bot's auto-merge, the same way `do-not-merge` does. A missing status does not block, so nothing changes for PRs nobody tested.
3. **Skip the re-review for result comments.** `claude_pr_review.yml` ignores comments whose first line starts with `tapir-test:`. The status from 1. carries the information, and the review already reruns on every new head.

A status is tied to a commit, so a new push (e.g. the steward merging `main`) leaves the old result behind by itself, and the test has to be repeated for the new head.

## What a result means

Without checks in the PR, the runner runs the general catalog (`archicad-addon/Test/checks/`). A PASS then means "the build loads and nothing known broke", not "the fix works". A FAIL that is not a known catalog gap is the useful signal, and that is what 2. makes count. For PASS results to say more, bot PRs could add a check file for their change. That could be a later step for the issue bot.

Happy to open a PR for 1.–3. if you agree with the approach. Since all three touch `.github/workflows/`, I'd rather ask first.
author: weltmaister

title: CreateMorphs, ModifyMorphs: say when the morph's layer is hidden
body:
## Summary

On a hidden layer, `CreateMorphs` with `body.edgeDefault` created the Morph, then failed to set its edge type and replied with only an error, so the caller never got the new Morph's guid. `ModifyMorphs` said only "Failed to modify morph.". Both now check the layer first and say why:

```diff
 CreateMorphs (per morph, AC29+)
   ACAPI_Element_GetDefaults
+  if edgeDefault given and the default layer is hidden or locked
+    error "The morph was not created, because its layer is hidden, so its edge type cannot be set."
   ACAPI_Element_Create
   ACAPI_Element_ChangeMorphEdgeType   // returned APIERR_BADID on a hidden layer

 ModifyMorphs (per morph)
   ACAPI_Element_Get
+  if its layer is hidden or locked
+    error "The morph was not modified, because its layer is hidden."
   ACAPI_Element_Change                // returned APIERR_HIDDENLAY
```

The layer check was inline in `GetFailedExecutionResultIfNotEditable` (`MoveElements`, `RotateElements`, `MirrorElements`). It moves to `CommandBase` as `GetLayerChangeError`, now shared by those and both Morph commands. The `edgeDefault` description says the layer must be shown and unlocked.

## Evidence

Archicad 29, macOS, a test project. Each call ran with the Morph tool's default layer shown, hidden and locked:

| Call | Shown | Hidden | Locked |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CreateMorphs` + `edgeDefault: "SoftHidden"` | created, reads back `SoftHidden` | `APIERR_HIDDENLAY` "…not created, because its layer is hidden…", no Morph made | `APIERR_LOCKEDLAY` "…its layer is locked…", no Morph made |
| `CreateMorphs` without `edgeDefault` | created | created (unchanged) | created (unchanged) |
| `ModifyMorphs` + `edgeDefault: "HardHidden"` | success, reads back `HardHidden` | "The morph was not modified, because its layer is hidden." | "…because its layer is locked." |
| `MoveElements` (refactored check) | success | "The element was not moved, because its layer is hidden." | "…because its layer is locked." |

- **Before** (same project, layer hidden): `CreateMorphs` + `edgeDefault` → `-2130313115` "Morph created, but failed to set its edge type." plus a Morph that no reply names. `ModifyMorphs` → `-2130312912` "Failed to modify morph."
- **After:** as in the table.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** small

Only calls that already failed change. A `CreateMorphs` with `edgeDefault` on a hidden or locked layer now creates nothing, where it used to leave an unreported Morph. `ModifyMorphs` on a locked layer is refused before `ACAPI_Element_Change` instead of by it. Messages of `MoveElements`/`RotateElements`/`MirrorElements` are unchanged.
author: BenTristem

title: Jacamar HUD: SetToolMode, GoToView, common menu operations and GetFullActionIndex
body:
I want to build **Jacamar HUD** as a Tapir script. It's a keyboard-driven command palette for Archicad: you type a few letters, it fuzzy-matches against everything you can switch to (tools, views, layouts, layer combinations, common operations), and Enter runs the match. For that the script needs four things from the add-on, listed below. I checked each against the AC25–AC30 DevKits the build checks use, and against `main`. As the requester I've made the design decisions.

Two requests had to change to fit the DevKits:
- **There is no `APIEnv_SetToolModeID`.** The call is `APIEnv_SetToolBoxModeID` on AC25–26 and `ACAPI_Toolbox_SetToolBoxMode` on AC27+.
- **There is no `ACAPI_Menu_ExecuteMenuCommand`.** The API has no way to run an arbitrary Archicad menu command; `ACAPI_MenuItem_*` only handles an add-on's own menus. Section 3 instead exposes the common menu operations, each through the API call that does the same thing.

`ACAPI_View_GoToView` is already on `main`, inside `ChangeWindow {navigatorItemId}`. Section 2 adds a `GoToView` command that reuses that code.

**For every part:**
- Match the surrounding code and reuse the `CommandBase` helpers (`GetElementTypeNonLocalizedName` / `GetElementTypeFromNonLocalizedName` for type names, the navigator helpers `GetNavigatorItemTree` uses).
- Register each command in `AddOnMain.cpp` with the version `main` carries, add a Python example under `archicad-addon/Examples/`, and gate version-specific calls with `ServerMainVers_*`.
- These can be one PR, or one per section if that's easier to review.

## 1. `GetToolbox` and `SetToolMode`

- `GetToolbox {includeHidden?}`: from `ACAPI_Toolbox_GetToolBoxInfo (&info, includeHidden)`, returns `{tools: [{type, variationId?, name}], activeTool: {type, variationId?}}`.
  - `type` is the non-localized element type name (`Wall`, `Door`, …), as elsewhere in Tapir.
  - `variationId` is set only for library part tools (doors, windows, objects, lamps; `API_ElemVariationID`, a four-character code as text).
  - `name` is the localized tool name, from `ACAPI_Element_GetElemTypeName`.
  - Dispose `info.data` with `BMKillHandle` on every path.
- `SetToolMode {type, variationId?}`: `ACAPI_Toolbox_SetToolBoxMode`. `type: "Arrow"` (or an empty type) selects the Arrow tool, which the DevKit does for `API_ZombieElemID`. Return `APIERR_BADPARS` / `APIERR_BADID` as the error.
  - The DevKit remark matters for the HUD: the switch is posted as an event and happens only once Archicad processes its event queue, after the command returns. Say so in the description, so a script doesn't read the mode back right away and expect the new tool.
- **AC25–26:** `ACAPI_Environment (APIEnv_GetToolBoxInfoID, &info, &includeHidden)` and `ACAPI_Environment (APIEnv_SetToolBoxModeID, &item)`. On AC25 `API_ToolBoxItem` has `typeID` + `variationID`; on AC26+ it has `type` (`API_ElemType`). Map these in `MigrationHelper.hpp` as `main` maps other renames.
- The coverage checklist marks the whole `Toolbox` group not applicable ("user interface"). Once this merges, a maintainer should take `Toolbox` out of that list in `tools/api_coverage_rules.json` (the bot can't edit `tools/`).

```cpp
// AC27–AC30, ACAPI_Environment.h
GSErrCode ACAPI_Toolbox_GetToolBoxInfo (API_ToolBoxInfo* toolBoxInfo, bool enableHidden = false);
GSErrCode ACAPI_Toolbox_GetToolBoxMode (API_ToolBoxItem* toolBoxItem);
GSErrCode ACAPI_Toolbox_SetToolBoxMode (API_ToolBoxItem* toolBoxItem);
// AC25–AC26, APIdefs_Environment.h (through ACAPI_Environment)
APIEnv_GetToolBoxModeID = 'GTBX', // par1: API_ToolBoxItem* par2: ---
APIEnv_SetToolBoxModeID = 'STBX', // par1: API_ToolBoxItem* par2: ---
APIEnv_GetToolBoxInfoID = 'GTBI', // par1: API_ToolBoxInfo* par2: bool (enable hidden)

// AC25, APIdefs_Environment.h
typedef struct {
  API_ElemTypeID typeID; // element type
  API_ElemVariationID variationID; // type subcategory (0 for generic types)
  Int32 filler_1[2];
} API_ToolBoxItem;
// AC26–AC30, APIdefs_Environment.h
typedef struct {
  API_ElemType type; // element type
  Int32 filler_1[2];
} API_ToolBoxItem;
// AC25–AC30, APIdefs_Environment.h
typedef struct {
  Int32 nTools; // number of tools installed (internal, subtypes)
  API_ToolBoxItem** data;
  API_ToolBoxItem activeTool;
  Int32 filler_1[6];
} API_ToolBoxInfo;
```

From the DevKit comment of `ACAPI_Toolbox_SetToolBoxMode`:
> For those types which can have more toolbox modes (ID_Wind, ID_Door, ID_Symb, ID_Light), the variationID of the tool should also be supplied. For `API_ZombieElemID` or an invalid element type ID specification the arrow mode will be set. Note that the function does not switch the toolbox immediately, but posts an event into the application queue. The command will be executed only when the application events are processed.

## 2. `GoToView`

`GoToView {navigatorItemId}`: opens a View Map view with its saved settings (layer combination, scale, model view options, zoom), through `ACAPI_View_GoToView (viewGuidStr)`. Move the view branch of `ChangeWindow` (`ApplicationCommands.cpp`, the `navigatorItemId` case, including its check that the item is a view or viewpoint and not a folder) into one helper that both commands call, so they can't drift apart. `ChangeWindow` keeps its schema and behavior. AC25–26: `ACAPI_Automate (APIDo_GoToViewID, …)`, as `main` already does.

```cpp
// AC27–AC30, ACAPI_Automate.h
GSErrCode ACAPI_View_GoToView (const char* viewGuidStr);
// AC25–AC26, APIdefs_Automate.h
APIDo_GoToViewID = 'GOVW', // par1: const char* par2: ---
```

## 3. `RunMenuOperation`: the common menu operations

`RunMenuOperation {operation}` runs one operation from a fixed list. Each maps to the API call behind the menu command, reusing the code of the Tapir command that already does it:

| `operation` | Menu command | Call |
|---|---|---|
| `FitInWindow` | View > Zoom > Fit in Window | as `FitInWindow` |
| `ZoomIn` / `ZoomOut` | View > Zoom > Zoom In / Out | `ACAPI_View_Zoom` with the current box (`ACAPI_View_GetZoom`) scaled by 0.5 / 2 around its center |
| `PreviousZoom` | View > Zoom > Previous Zoom | as `ResetZoom` |
| `ZoomToSelection` | View > Zoom > Zoom to Selection | `ACAPI_View_ZoomToSelected` (AC25–26 `APIDo_ZoomToSelectedID`) |
| `Rebuild` | View > Refresh > Rebuild | as `RebuildView` (`ACAPI_View_Rebuild`) |
| `Redraw` | View > Refresh > Redraw | `ACAPI_View_Redraw` |
| `Save` | File > Save | as `SaveProject` |
| `DeselectAll` | deselect everything | `ACAPI_Selection_DeselectAll` (AC25–26 `ACAPI_Element_DeselectAll`) |
| `ArrowTool` | the Arrow tool | section 1's `SetToolMode` with `Arrow` |

- An unknown `operation` is an `APIERR_BADPARS` error that lists the valid names. The input schema has the names as an `enum`, so the HUD can read the list from the schema.
- Not included: Undo / Redo, because the API has no call for them, and other add-ons' menu items.

## 4. `GetFullActionIndex`: everything the HUD can switch to, in one flat array

`GetFullActionIndex {kinds?}` returns `{actions: [...]}`, one entry per action. `kinds` filters by kind, all by default. Each entry:

```json
{
  "id": "view:4F0E…",            // stable across calls: kind + guid, or kind + name for tools and operations
  "kind": "view",                // tool | view | layout | layerCombination | operation
  "name": "3D / All",            // what Archicad shows (localized)
  "path": "Views/Interior",      // the navigator folders above it, "" for tools, layer combinations and operations
  "command": "GoToView",         // the Tapir command that runs it
  "parameters": { "navigatorItemId": { "guid": "4F0E…" } }
}
```

`command` and `parameters` are exactly what to send to run the action, so the script can pass them on as they are.

| `kind` | Source | `command` / `parameters` |
|---|---|---|
| `tool` | section 1's toolbox list (hidden tools left out) | `SetToolMode {type, variationId?}` |
| `view` | every view in the View Map (`API_PublicViewMap`) as `GetNavigatorItemTree` walks it; folders only go into `path` | `GoToView {navigatorItemId}` |
| `layout` | every layout in the Layout Book (`API_LayoutMap`); master layouts left out | `ChangeWindow {navigatorItemId}` (on `main`) |
| `layerCombination` | the layer combination attributes, as `GetLayerCombinations` lists them | `ActivateLayerCombination {attributeId}` (#916) |
| `operation` | section 3's list | `RunMenuOperation {operation}` |

- **Order:** by kind in the order above, then as the navigator shows them (views and layouts) or alphabetically (the rest), so the result is stable between calls.
- **Speed:** it is read-only and called often, so read each source once per call and do no per-item `ACAPI_Navigator_GetNavigatorItem` round trips beyond what the tree walk needs. Tested on a project with a few hundred views it should return well under a second.
- **#916 dependency:** the layer combination entries point at `ActivateLayerCombination`, which #916 adds (`ACAPI_Navigator_ChangeCurrLayerComb`; AC25–26 `APIEnv_ChangeCurrLayerCombID`). Wait for #916 to merge before building this part; don't add a second activate command.

Not tested in Archicad: I'll test each part's build when the bot links it.

title: GetAttributesFromProject returns empty lists for Layer, BuildingMaterial and Surface
body:
Tested on 2026-10-27 with released Tapir 1.7.3, Archicad 29 AUT build 3200, Windows, from a disposable test project. Related: #1216 / #1221.

`GetAttributesFromProject` on a closed `.pln` returns an empty `attributes` array for **Layer**, **BuildingMaterial** and **Surface**. The other requested types from the same call are filled. Reproduced with two different source files (both earlier copies of the open project), so the source files do contain these attributes.

```json
{"projectFilePath":"D:\\...\\WKL519_08.pln","attributeTypes":["Layer","LayerCombination","BuildingMaterial","Composite","Fill","Line","Surface","PenTable","ZoneCategory","Profile"]}
```

Result (5.5 s, no error items), compared with `GetAttributesByType` in the open project, which is a later copy of the same file:

|---|---|---|
| Layer | **0** | 192 |
| LayerCombination | 19 | 21 |
| BuildingMaterial | **0** | 90 |
| Composite | 49 | 49 |
| Fill | 214 | 216 |
| Line | 38 | 38 |
| Surface | **0** | 242 |
| PenTable | 12 | 13 |
| ZoneCategory | 18 | 18 |
| Profile | 29 | 30 |

The source's 49 Composites use building materials, and its 19 layer combinations refer to layers, so the empty lists can't be right. A second source file gives the same pattern: `["Layer","Fill","BuildingMaterial","Composite"]` → 0 / 214 / 0 / 49. A call with `["Layer"]` only also returns `[]`.

title: Label widthFactor / charSpaceFactor: ignored by CreateLabels, reset to 1 by a text-only ModifyLabels
body:
Tested on 2026-10-27 with released Tapir 1.7.3, Archicad 29 AUT build 3200, Windows, in a disposable project copy, on a visible and unlocked layer.

**1. CreateLabels ignores the factors.**
```json
{"labelsData":[{"labelClass":"Text","favoriteName":"Text/Autotext","text":"T173 Etikett","floorInd":0,"begCoordinate":{"x":400,"y":50},"midCoordinate":{"x":401,"y":51},"endCoordinate":{"x":403,"y":51},"style":{"widthFactor":1.2,"charSpaceFactor":1.1}}]}
```
The label is created, but GetDetailsOfElements reads `style.widthFactor` 1 and `style.charSpaceFactor` 1.

**2. A text-only ModifyLabels resets them.**

| step | call | widthFactor / charSpaceFactor read back |
|---|---|---|
| a | `ModifyLabels` with `style: {widthFactor: 1.2, charSpaceFactor: 1.1}` only → success | 1.2 / 1.1 |
| b | `ModifyLabels` with `text: "T173 Etikett neu"` only → success | **1 / 1** |

The schema says "Only provided fields are changed; omitted fields are left as-is". The text change rebuilds the content (as documented), but the factors aren't kept. In my run the leader-line coordinates stayed the same.

Expected: CreateLabels applies the given factors, and a text-only ModifyLabels keeps them. Workaround today: send `style` again in the same or a following ModifyLabels.

title: CreateLayout with position "last" at the Layout Book root creates the layout but returns only an error (no databaseId)

title: Fix revision response schemas and element GUID extraction
body:
ChatGPT found the following while updating the MCP:

- `GetCurrentRevisionChangesOfLayouts`
- `GetRevisionChangesOfElements`

These findings come from schema and C++ source inspection; I have not reproduced them in a running Archicad instance.

### 1. Incorrect required-property name

`RevisionChangesArrayItem` declares `revisionChanges`, but requires `revisionChange`.

Because `additionalProperties` is false, the successful object cannot satisfy the schema: the required singular property is undeclared.

The required property should be `revisionChanges`.

[Schema definition](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/1.7.3/docs/archicad-addon/common_schema_definitions.js#L10002)

### 2. Response schemas declare an object where implementations return an array

Both command response schemas reference `RevisionChangesOfEntities`, which describes one success/error object. However, both implementations return a list containing one success/error object per requested layout or element.

For example, the element command builds:

{
  "revisionChangesOfElements": [
    {"revisionChanges": []}
  ]
}

The contract currently expects an object at `revisionChangesOfElements`, so generated typed clients reject this list-shaped response.

The response contract should describe an array whose items are either a revision-change wrapper or an error. Fixing the required-property spelling alone will not resolve this mismatch.

[Layout command](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/1.7.3/archicad-addon/Sources/RevisionCommands.cpp#L340) · [Element command](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/1.7.3/archicad-addon/Sources/RevisionCommands.cpp#L414)

### 3. Element revision lookup uses the database-ID extractor

`GetRevisionChangesOfElementsCommand::Execute` transforms its `elements` input using `GetGuidFromDatabaseArrayItem`.

Valid element items contain `elementId`, while that helper reads `databaseId`. The shared extractor returns `APINULLGuid` when the requested field is absent, so the command passes null GUIDs instead of the supplied element GUIDs.

This should use `GetGuidFromElementsArrayItem`. The layout command's use of the database extractor is appropriate.

[Element lookup](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/1.7.3/archicad-addon/Sources/RevisionCommands.cpp#L430) · [Extractor definitions](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/1.7.3/archicad-addon/Sources/CommandBase.hpp#L67) · [Missing-field handling](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/1.7.3/archicad-addon/Sources/CommandBase.cpp#L115)

Suggested verification: query multiple layouts/elements, check success and error entries, validate the returned arrays against the corrected schemas, and confirm that element lookups receive the supplied element GUIDs.

title: Zones: let us read and set the contour pen and line type
body:
Hi Tapir team 👋

We use Tapir to create zones in bulk (`CreateZones`), and one thing we keep running into: there's no way to control the zone's contour line, meaning the pen and line type of the boundary on the floor plan.

Right now `GetDetailsOfElements` gives us the name, number, category, stamp position, outline and holes for a zone (tested on Tapir 1.7.2 / Archicad 28), but nothing about how the contour is drawn. The only workaround we've found is `ApplyFavoritesToElements`, but that's a pretty big hammer. It also swaps the category and resets the stamp, when all we wanted was a different line.

What would really help:

- **Read it:** return the contour pen and line type in ZoneDetails.
- **Change it:** accept those fields in `SetDetailsOfElements` (or in the new `ModifyZones` from #896 / #899, which seems like a natural fit), leaving everything else untouched.
- **Set it on creation:** optional fields in `CreateZones`, so new zones come out right the first time.

If it's not much extra work, the zone's cover fill (fill type, foreground and background pen) would be a nice bonus in the same spot.

Thanks a lot for all the work on Tapir. It's become the backbone of our in-house Archicad tools!

title: GetAttributesFromProject: report Layer, Surface, BuildingMaterial and MEPSystem as not read instead of an empty list
body:
Fixes #1582

I reproduced the issue on macOS with Archicad 29 and a build of `main` (1.7.4). It is not limited to Windows, and it affects one more type: **MEPSystem**.

| attributeType | closed .pln | Archicad 29 INT template (.tpl) | open project (`GetAttributesByType`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Layer | 0 | 0 | 174 |
| BuildingMaterial | 0 | 0 | 123 |
| Surface | 0 | 0 | 226 |
| MEPSystem | – | 0 | 6 |
| LayerCombination, Composite, Fill, Line, PenTable, ZoneCategory, Profile, OperationProfile | filled | filled | |

`ACAPI_Attribute_GetAttributesFromProject` returns `NoError` and an empty array for these four types. The calls are the same for every type and nothing filters the result. The AC29 DevKit documents no other way to read attributes from a file, and no flag for it (it is the only attribute function that takes an `IO::Location`). So Archicad itself doesn't return these types here. Tapir can't read them, but it can stop reporting "no attributes".

## What changes

- If one of Layer, Surface, BuildingMaterial or MEPSystem comes back empty, that type now gets an error item (`APIERR_NOTSUPPORTED`) instead of `{"attributes": []}`. The message says to open the file and use `GetAttributesByType`.
- A non-empty list is still passed through unchanged, so the command picks these types up again by itself if an Archicad version starts returning them.
- The registered description and the `attributeTypes` schema description name the four types. The example now reads only types that work.

## Tested

Archicad 29 (macOS), build of this branch:
- A closed .pln and the Archicad 29 INT template: Layer, BuildingMaterial, Surface and MEPSystem → error item. All other types are unchanged (same counts as before the change).
- An invalid attributeType and a missing file give the same errors as before.
- `Examples/get_attributes_from_project.py` runs without errors.

Not tested: Archicad 27/28/30 and Windows (the reporter's numbers show the same pattern on Windows AC29).

title: Zones: read and set the contour line and the cover fill
body:
Fixes #1594

Reads and sets the contour line and the cover fill of a zone on the floor plan.

## Field names (checked in the AC29 DevKit, `APIdefs_Elements.h`, `API_ZoneType`)

| JSON | API_ZoneType | type |
|---|---|---|
| `contourLine.use` | `useContourLine` | bool |
| `contourLine.pen` | `floorContLPen` | short |
| `contourLine.lineTypeId` | `floorContLType` | API_AttributeIndex |
| `coverFill.use` | `useFloorFill` | bool |
| `coverFill.fillId` | `floorFillInd` | API_AttributeIndex |
| `coverFill.foregroundPen` | `floorFillPen` | short |
| `coverFill.backgroundPen` | `floorFillBGPen` | short |

The names the bot recalled in the issue are right. I only have the AC29 (and AC30) DevKit here, so the build checks will show whether AC25–AC28 differ.

## What changes

- **`GetDetailsOfElements`**: `ZoneDetails` gets `contourLine` and `coverFill`. `coverFill` uses the key names of the existing `CoverFill` of columns and beams (`use`, `fillId`, `foregroundPen`, `backgroundPen`), and `contourLine` uses `lineTypeId` as lines do.
- **`SetDetailsOfElements`** (zone case, next to `stampPosition`, so it works on `main` today): the same keys. Only the given fields are masked, so the category, the stamp and the rest of the zone stay as they are.
- **`CreateZones`**: the same optional keys. Fields that are left out keep the favorite's or the Zone tool defaults' value.
- Unknown attribute ids and pens out of range (contour and foreground pen 1–255, background pen 0–255) fail the item **before anything is changed**. The range check is also in the code, because `SetDetailsOfElements` doesn't hold `typeSpecificDetails` to the schema's `minimum`/`maximum`: pen 0 was written before the check was added.
- One shared pair of helpers, `AddZoneContourAndCoverFill` / `ApplyZoneContourAndCoverFill`, used by all three paths, so they can't drift apart. When #899 lands, `ModifyZones` can call `ApplyZoneContourAndCoverFill` too.
- New example `Examples/zone_contour_and_cover_fill.py`.

The issue's bonus (cover fill) is included. `use3DHatching` and the cover fill orientation (`useLocalOrigo`, `locOrigo`, `fillAngle`) are left out to keep this small.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS), 14/14

- existing zones of a real project return both objects
- `CreateZones` with contour (on, pen 3, a line type) and cover fill (on, a fill, pens 5/0): read back exactly
- `CreateZones` without them: tool defaults, both objects present
- `SetDetailsOfElements` with only `contourLine.pen`: pen changed. Line type, cover fill, name, category, stamp position and polygon unchanged.
- line type, contour off, another fill and a background pen in one call: all applied
- cover fill off: applied, the fill stays
- unknown line type id together with a new pen: the item fails and the pen is **not** changed
- unknown fill id in `SetDetailsOfElements` and in `CreateZones`: error, no zone created
- contour pen 0 and background pen 256: refused. Background pen 0 (transparent): accepted.
- round trip: writing back what `GetDetailsOfElements` returned succeeds and changes nothing
- the example runs

`Test/ExpectedOutputs/get_and_set_details_of_elements.py.output` contains zone details and will now differ by the two new objects. It needs to be re-recorded against `TestProject.pla`, which I haven't done.

title: CreateWalls, CreateSlabs, CreateColumns, CreateBeams: optional layerIndex
body:
Fixes #1043

`CreateWalls`, `CreateSlabs`, `CreateColumns` and `CreateBeams` take an optional `layerIndex` per item, as `CreatePolylines` and the other 2D create commands already do. A new element goes straight onto its layer, without a second `SetDetailsOfElements` call.

## Design

The issue bot didn't build this because putting it in the shared create loop (`CreateElementsCommandBase::Execute`) is treated as crash-sensitive. This PR leaves the loop alone:

- One small helper, `ApplyLayerIndexFromParameters` (`ElementCreationCommands.cpp/.hpp`), is called at the start of each of the four `SetTypeSpecificParameters`. That is the same place `CreatePolylines` sets its layer.
- `SetTypeSpecificParameters` runs after the favorite (`favoriteName`) or the tool defaults have been applied, so an explicit `layerIndex` wins over the favorite's layer.
- On the open question from the issue: the helper checks that the layer exists and is not locked, with the same messages as `GetErrorIfLayerNotUsable` in `MEPCommands.cpp`. A bad layer fails only that item, with a clear error, instead of Archicad's generic create failure or an element on an unexpected layer.
- Without `layerIndex` nothing changes. The schema property has `minimum: 1`.
- New example `Examples/create_elements_on_layer.py`.

The other commands the issue lists in brackets (Zones, Objects, Meshes, Roofs, Morphs) can use the same helper in a follow-up. I kept this PR to the four in the title.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS), 20/20

For each of Walls, Slabs, Columns and Beams:
- with `layerIndex` of a test layer: `GetDetailsOfElements` returns that `layerIndex`
- without `layerIndex`: the tool default's layer, as before
- a layer index that doesn't exist: "The 'layerIndex' parameter does not refer to an existing layer.", nothing created
- a locked layer: "The layer given by the 'layerIndex' parameter is locked.", nothing created

Also:
- `layerIndex: 0` is refused by the schema
- a mixed call (valid / unknown layer / no `layerIndex`): only the item with the unknown layer fails, the other two are created
- `favoriteName` of a wall favorite together with `layerIndex`: the element is on the given layer, not on the favorite's
- the example runs

title: CreateWalls/ModifyWalls: no way to set flipped, so a read wall cannot be rebuilt as it was
body:
## Summary

`GetDetailsOfElements` reports a wall's `flipped`, but no command writes it: `CreateWalls`, `ModifyWalls` and `SetDetailsOfElements` have no `flipped` input. A new wall takes `flipped` from the Wall tool default. For a complex-profile wall that mirrors the whole cross section across the reference line, so the caller cannot rebuild a profile wall it has just read.

## Repro (Archicad 30 build 3001 ITA, Tapir 1.7.3, Windows 11)

1. Take any straight complex-profile wall with `flipped: false` (here one created by the IFC import, profile 827 × 2690 mm).
2. Read it with `GetDetailsOfElements`, and its profile with `GetProfiles`.
3. Rebuild the profile with `CreateProfiles` (`newSkins` from the read `outlineCoords`), then create the wall with `CreateWalls`: the same `begCoordinate`, `endCoordinate`, `height`, `referenceLineLocation`, `offset`, plus `structureType: "Profile"` and the new `profileId`.
4. Compare the two with `Get3DBoundingBoxes`.

**Expected:** the same wall, `flipped: false`.
**Actual:** `flipped: true` (from the tool default). The bounding box is mirrored and off by the full profile width (827 mm).

Workaround: swap `begCoordinate` and `endCoordinate`. The geometry then matches (0.0 mm off), but `flipped` still reads `true`, so a read → write round trip does not reproduce the element.

## Request

Accept an optional `flipped` (boolean) in `CreateWalls` and `ModifyWalls`, and in the wall case of `SetDetailsOfElements` if that fits better. This is `API_WallType::flipped` with its mask bit; it applies to every wall type, not only complex-profile walls. Same spirit as #531: an explicit parameter should not be overridden by the tool default.

title: SetDetailsOfElements: "Failed to change element" for every element in a Worksheet (same call works on the Floor Plan)
body:
**Environment:** Archicad 29 (Windows), Tapir 1.7.3.

**Steps**
1. `CreateWorksheets` creates a new independent worksheet.
2. `ChangeWindow` with its `navigatorItemId`; `GetCurrentWindowType` returns `Worksheet`.
3. `CreateHatches` / `CreatePolylines` create elements in the worksheet (confirmed with `GetElementsByType` + `databases`).
4. `SetDetailsOfElements` on those elements, with any change:
   - hatch: `{"layerIndex": <index>}`
   - hatch: `typeSpecificDetails: {"fillPenIndex": 3}`
   - hatch: new `coordinates` + `holes`
   - polyline: `typeSpecificDetails: {"linePenIndex": 3}`

**Result:** every call returns `-2130312912 "Failed to change element"`. `DeleteElements` on the same elements, with the worksheet active, works.

**Expected:** the same behavior as on the Floor Plan, where the identical hatch call (`coordinates` + `holes`) succeeds and `GetDetailsOfElements` returns the hole.

**Impact:** `SetDetailsOfElements` is currently the only way to give a hatch holes, so hatches with holes cannot be created in worksheets or other 2D databases.
author: cmartif

title: CreateHatches: accept "holes" (same format SetDetailsOfElements already accepts for hatches)
body:
`SetDetailsOfElements` already sets hatch holes (`holes: [{polygonOutline, polygonArcs}]`, PR #484), and `GetDetailsOfElements` returns them. `CreateHatches` still always creates a single contour (`nSubPolys = 1` in `CreateHatchesCommand::SetTypeSpecificParameters`).

Accepting the same optional `holes` array in each `hatchesData` item would make create and modify symmetric, and would avoid a second call per hatch when creating many hatches.
author: cmartif

title: 2D creation commands: optional databaseId to create elements in a given Worksheet/Detail without changing the active window
body:
**Problem**
2D creation commands always create elements in the current database, so creating content in a worksheet or detail requires activating its window first.

**Observed** (Archicad 29, Tapir 1.7.3)
- `CreateWorksheets` returns only a `databaseId`.
- `ChangeWindow` with `{"windowType": "Worksheet", "databaseId": <that id>}` fails with -2130313110 "Failed to change current database". This looks like the never-opened-window case fixed for elevations in #995.
- `ChangeWindow` with the `navigatorItemId` works, but obtaining that id requires reading the whole Project Map with `GetNavigatorItemTree`, which is very large on big projects.
- `GetElementsByType` with `"databases": [<same id>]` works, so the id itself is valid.

**Proposal**
1. An optional top-level `databaseId` on the 2D creation commands (CreatePolylines, CreateHatches, CreateTexts, CreateLineElements, CreateArcs, CreateCircles, CreateSplines, CreateLabels, CreateHotspots). The command would switch to that database, create, and switch back, as `ExecuteActionForEachDatabase` already does for commands that take `databases`.
2. `CreateWorksheets` and `CreateDetails` also returning each new `navigatorItemId` (as #1039 expected), so the new item can be opened or placed with CreateDrawings directly.

Related: #819 (copy 2D elements between databases).

title: Add CreateRailings and the Railing case of GetDetailsOfElements
body:
Part of #897: parts (1) and (2) of the split the bot proposed in the issue. `templateElementId` and `ModifyRailings` are left for follow-ups.

## What it adds

- **`CreateRailings`** (`railingsData[]`): `coordinates` (2D reference polyline, at least 2 points), optional `floorIndex`, `bottomOffset`, `height`, plus `favoriteName` and `id` from `CreateElementsCommandBase`. The posts, rails, handrails, toprails, panels and balusters come from the favorite or the Railing tool defaults.
- **`GetDetailsOfElements` for `Railing`** (`RailingDetails`): `referenceLine`, `bottomOffset`, `zCoordinate`, `height` (the default segment) and `segmentHeights` (one per generated segment).
- New example `Examples/create_railings.py`.

## Answers to the open points in the issue (AC29 DevKit + live)

1. **Reference line:** `memo.coords` from index 1 plus `memo.polyZCoords` (one value per vertex), with `API_RailingType::nVertices`. That is exactly what the DevKit's `Element_Test` (`Do_CreateRailing`) does.
2. **Tree generation:** `ACAPI_Element_Create` accepts the defaults' memo with only a new reference line, and builds the whole tree itself from `defNode` / `defSegment`. A 3-segment polyline came back with 4 nodes, 3 segments, 4 posts, 3 toprails and 3 panels. Nothing is cloned or re-indexed by the add-on.
3. **Field names:** `API_RailingType::bottomOffset`. The height is `defSegment.height`, a per-segment setting, and each generated segment's height is in `memo.railingSegments[i].height`.
4. **Two traps, both handled:**
   - `polyZCoords` is the **elevation** of each vertex. Archicad takes the base from it and derives `bottomOffset` from it. With zeros, the given `bottomOffset` was ignored, so every vertex gets `level(home story) + bottomOffset`.
   - `ACAPI_Element_Create` homes a railing on the **active** story, whatever `header.floorInd` says. With the basement active, `floorIndex` 0 and 1 both gave a railing homed on the basement. So, as `CreateZones` does for automatic zones (#853), items on another story are created in groups with that story made active (`APIStory_GoTo`), and the previously active story is restored. A call that stays on the active story runs through the base class unchanged.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS), 14/14

- railing along a 3-segment polyline (`floorIndex` 0, `bottomOffset` 0, `height` 1.1):
  - `referenceLine` reads back exactly as given
  - 3 segments of 1.1
  - home story 0, `zCoordinate` 0
  - 3D bodies span x 399.99–405.01 and z 0–1.1
- coordinates only: tool defaults, 1 segment
- `floorIndex` 1, `bottomOffset` 0.2, `height` 0.9: home story 1, `bottomOffset` 0.2, `zCoordinate` = level + 0.2
- one call with items on stories 0, 1, 0: the response order and the stories are right, and the active story is restored
- three railings in one call
- with a railing favorite: created from the favorite, 2 segments
- a zero-length segment fails that item, and nothing is created
- one coordinate is refused by the schema
- the example runs

**Note on reading 3D:** Archicad builds a railing's 3D bodies only when the 3D model is updated. Right after creation, `Get3DGeometryOfElements` returns no bodies and `Get3DBoundingBoxes` an internal error for the railing. After the 3D window has been opened once, the bodies are there. This isn't specific to this PR, but it's worth knowing for the setback checks mentioned in the issue.

title: Feature request: dimensioning new section/elevation views programmatically (SectElem GUIDs, level dimensions)
body:
Dear Developer Team,
Environment: Archicad 29 (HUN, build 5101), Tapir 1.5.9, Windows Server (multi-user RDP). Commands sent through the Archicad JSON API (`API.ExecuteAddOnCommand`).
Use case
We use Archicad for formwork drawings (zsaluterv). Every load-bearing wall gets its own wall-elevation section (hundreds per project). We create the sections with `CreateSections` successfully, but we cannot dimension them automatically. Four gaps block the workflow:
1. Real SectElem GUIDs are not obtainable for a section view
`CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection` requires `sectionElementId`(s) — the GUID of the section element (SectElem) in the section database. In a newly created section:
`GetElementsByType` with `elementType: "SectElem"` (current section window, or with `databases` set to the section's database) returns the GUIDs of the parent model elements (walls, slabs, openings…), not the SectElem GUIDs.
`GetSelectedElements` after Ctrl+A in the section window also returns the parent model GUIDs.
Passing those GUIDs to `CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection` fails: "The referenced 'sectionElementId' is not a valid section element." (code −2130313112).
`CreateAssociativeDimensions` with the parent GUID and `nodeType` 130/430 (as seen in existing section dimensions) fails: "Failed to create associative dimension."
The real SectElem GUIDs only become visible indirectly: after a user places a dimension manually, `GetDimensionData` shows them as `witnessPoints\[].baseElementId`. With those GUIDs, `CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection` works perfectly (tested: `SlabCompositeFaces` preset on two slabs). `GetDetailsOfElements` also works on them (`type: "SectElem"`, with section-plane polygons).
The SectElem GUIDs are not derivable from the parent GUID (we compared two parent/SectElem pairs; no constant relation).
Request: one of the following:
make `GetElementsByType("SectElem")` return the real SectElem GUIDs (optionally with the parent element GUID), or
a command that maps parent element GUID + section database → SectElem GUID(s), or
let `CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection` accept a parent element GUID together with the section database.
2. Elevation-type (level) linear dimensions cannot be created
Our level dimensions in sections are linear dimensions in elevation mode (`Dimension` element; `GetDimensionData` returns the absolute elevation as `dimensionValue`, e.g. −0.80 / −0.50 / 3.66 / 3.88 …). We can create the linear dimension chains, but not in elevation mode:
`CreateAssociativeDimensions` always creates a normal linear dimension (values are segment lengths).
`CreateFavoritesFromElements` / `UpdateFavoritesFromElements` from an elevation-mode dimension succeeds, but `ApplyFavoritesToElements` on a linear dimension does not switch it to elevation mode.
`ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults` with that favorite before `CreateAssociativeDimensions` does not help either: the new dimension is still linear (`dimensionValue` = segment length).
Request: a parameter on `CreateAssociativeDimensions` (and `CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection`) to create the dimension in elevation mode (or to respect the dimension tool defaults / a favorite name), and/or a `SetDetailsOfElements` field for the dimension type. A separate `CreateLevelDimensions` (the Level Dimension tool) would also be welcome.
3. "Explode into Current View" is not available
Our workaround for #1 is: explode the section into 2D (Edit → Reshape → Explode into Current View), move the 2D copy beside the view, and dimension the 2D hatches/polylines (this works well: `CreateAssociativeDimensions` binds to hatch/polyline vertices via `inIndex`/`nodeId`). The explode step itself still needs a manual menu click per section.
Request: a command to explode selected/all elements of the current (section) view into 2D drawing elements, optionally keeping the originals, returning the GUIDs of the new elements.
4. Geometry of existing sections / openings is not readable
`GetDetailsOfElements` on `CutPlane` (section markers on the plan): "Not yet supported element type"; `API.Get2DBoundingBoxes` on them: "Element not supported". We cannot read the start/end point, depth or direction of existing sections.
`GetDetailsOfElements` on `Opening` elements: "Not yet supported element type"; `API.Get3DBoundingBoxes` on them: Internal error (6000).
Request: details (geometry) for `CutPlane` (start/end, depth, direction/marker side, vertical range) and for `Opening` (position, size, host element).
Notes
`CreateSections`: the view direction is to the left of the start→end direction. It would help to document this, and to allow passing a favorite (section settings) at creation time.
Thank you for Tapir — it already covers most of our workflow (section creation, associative dimensions, favorites, layers, navigator).
thank you very mutch in advance, best regards,
Istvan

title: GetAllProperties: optional filter to read the expressions of specific properties
body:
Since #321, `GetAllProperties` returns `isExpressionBased` and `expressions`, and `UpdatePropertyDefinitions` rewrites them in place (GUID kept, order preserved). Thanks — the read/modify/write cycle works (tested with 1.7.3 on Archicad 29).

The remaining problem is size. `GetAllProperties` takes no parameters, so reading the expressions of one property means downloading every built-in and custom property with its full availability list. In a large template a single 100-property page of the response can exceed 2 MB (#1292 measured ~600k tokens for a full dump), which is impractical for scripts and MCP clients.

Any of these would solve it:
1. Optional `propertyIds` parameter in `GetAllProperties`, returning only those definitions.
2. Optional `propertyType` (`UserDefined` / `BuiltIn`) and `includeAvailability: false`.
3. Or `isExpressionBased` + `expressions` in a details command that takes property GUIDs.

Related: #1145 / #1146 (`CheckPropertyExpressions`, `GetPropertyExpressionReferences`) would complete the workflow:
- validate each expression before `UpdatePropertyDefinitions`, which today returns a generic "inconsistent definition" error for the whole list without saying which expression failed;
- build `###Property:<GUID>###` references from a property id. Name-based references (`{Property:Group/Name}`, `###Property:Group/Name###`) are rejected on write.
author: cmartif

title: Openings: direction vectors in GetOpeningDetails, working GetOpeningTransformations
body:
Fixes #1562
Fixes #1563

Both issues needed the DevKit and a live Archicad, so here is what they show (Archicad 29, macOS) and what this changes.

## #1562: axes of `GetOpeningDetails`

`OpeningGeometry::GetVectorX ()`, `GetVectorY ()` and `GetExtrusionDirection ()` return the axes **moved by the origin of the host's coordinate system**, as if they were points. I measured it on four fresh openings:

| host | raw xAxis | raw yAxis | raw extrusion | host origin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| wall along +x, story 0 | (401, 0, 0) | (400, 0, 1) | (400, 1, 0) | (400, 0, 0), wall start |
| wall along −x, story 0 | (415, 5, 0) | (416, 5, 1) | (416, 4, 0) | (416, 5, 0), wall start |
| diagonal wall, story 1 (level 4) | (420.71, 0.71, 4) | (420, 0, 5) | (419.29, 0.71, 4) | (420, 0, 4), wall start |
| slab, level 0 | (431, 10, 0) | (430, 11, 0) | (430, 10, −1) | (430, 10, 0), first vertex |

In every case the axes are orthonormal and extrusion = −(x × y). The bot pointed out that the origin can't be told apart from its mirror image without fixing the handedness. With the handedness fixed this way, the origin is the centroid of the three points plus a third of (Y − X) × (E − X), and subtracting it gives the direction vectors. That is `GetOpeningAxes` in `ExtendedElementCommands.cpp`. If the API ever returns plain vectors, the same formula gives a zero origin and leaves them as they are.

After the fix, the four openings read x (1,0,0) / (−1,0,0) / (0.707,0.707,0) / (1,0,0) with matching y and extrusion, as expected for each host.

(The anchor point of a wall opening comes back 1 m above the `basePoint` given to `CreateOpenings`, as noted in #1562. That isn't touched here.)

## #1563: `GetOpeningTransformations`

- **Why it always failed:** `ACAPI_Element_GetOpeningTransformation` is for the openings of the classic API: windows, doors and skylights. The DevKit's own `Element_Test` (`Do_GetFirstWindowPosition`) calls it on a window. For an element of the Opening tool it answers `APIERR_BADID` (−2130313115), which is exactly the error in the issue, while the command only let `API_OpeningID` through.
- **Windows, doors and skylights** now go to that call.
- **Opening elements** (Archicad 29 and later) get their placement built from the geometry: origin at the anchor point, the corrected X and Y axes, and Z = X × Y (right-handed, so Z points against the extrusion direction). On AC27/28, an Opening element gets a clear `APIERR_NOTSUPPORTED` item.
- **Matrix direction:** the DevKit text calls the returned matrix global-to-local, but it is local-to-global. For a window 4.5 m along a wall at x = 400 with a 0.9 m sill, its translation is (404.5, 0, 0.9), and `Element_Test` uses it that way too. Before this change, the command inverted it and reported the origin at (404.5, −0.9, 0). Now `localToGlobal` is the returned matrix and `globalToLocal` its inverse, so `origin` is the window's position.
- Since every supported element now always has an invertible matrix, `localToGlobal` and the derived `origin` and axes are always present (added to `required`). If a matrix can't be inverted, that item becomes an error instead.

The response keys are unchanged. Before this PR, the command only ever returned errors for both Opening elements and windows, so no existing result changes.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS), 18/18

- **4 openings** (wall +x, wall −x, diagonal wall on story 1, slab):
  - `GetOpeningDetails` gives the expected unit axes
  - `GetOpeningTransformations` gives `origin` = `anchorPoint`, the same X/Y axes, Z = −extrusion, determinant 1, not mirrored
- **Window:**
  - `origin` = (404.5, 0, 0.9), its center at sill height
  - `zAxis` is perpendicular to the wall, not mirrored
  - `globalToLocal` maps `origin` to (0, 0, 0)
- **Wall instead of an opening:** "Element is not an Opening, Window, Door or Skylight"
- The updated example (all Openings and Windows of a real project) runs.

title: Walls: a profile tool default no longer overrides a requested Basic or Composite structure
body:
Fixes #531

## What I found (Archicad 29, macOS, current `main`)

I set a complex-profile wall as the Wall tool default, through a favorite of a profile wall and `ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults`. Then I called `CreateWalls`:

| request | before this PR | after |
|---|---|---|
| `structureType: "Basic"`, `thickness` 0.333, `height` 1.111 | `structureType: "Profile"`, `profileId` 00000000…, `profileType: "Poly"` | Basic, 0.333 × 1.111 |
| `structureType: "Composite"` + `compositeId` | Profile, null `profileId` | Composite |
| `structureType: "Profile"` + another `profileId` | that profile | that profile |
| no `structureType` | the default's profile (documented: the default's structure is kept) | unchanged |

On current `main` the requested thickness and height already reach the wall, so the unconditional Basic from the issue is gone. What remains is the structure: the wall still comes out as a profile wall **without a profile**, the null-guid case from the report.

## Cause

It isn't the memo. I first dropped the whole defaults memo with `ACAPI_DisposeElemMemoHdls` (the DevKit's Element_Test creates walls without a memo) and the result was the same. The details of the bad wall show `profileType: "Poly"`. `ApplyWallStructure` sets `modelElemStructureType` but leaves the cross section `profileType` on `APISect_Poly` from the profile default, so Archicad keeps a profiled cross section with no profile attribute.

So the profile memo the review comment pointed to doesn't need freeing. Nothing in the create path deletes anything.

## Change

In `ApplyWallStructure`, which `CreateWalls` and `ModifyWalls` share:
- Basic and Composite set `profileType` back to `APISect_Normal` when it is `APISect_Poly`. Slanted and Trapez cross sections are kept, since they are valid for these structures.
- Profile sets `profileType = APISect_Poly`.
- The mask now includes `profileType`, so `ModifyWalls` gets the same fix.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS), 7/7

- Basic default: Profile + profile A gives a profile wall with profile A
- `ModifyWalls` on a profile wall with `structureType: "Basic"`, `thickness` 0.25 → Basic, 0.25 thick, `profileType` Normal
- profile default: the four cases in the table above
- The project was saved before and reopened without saving afterwards, so the changed tool default and the test favorite were gone.

Beams and columns weren't part of this. They keep their structure per segment (`memo.beamSegments` / `columnSegments`), and the create commands already set it there.

title: CreateFills: percent of Solid fills is ignored
body:
**Environment:** Archicad 29 (build 3200, German), macOS, Tapir 1.7.3

**What happens**

`CreateFills` with `subType: "Solid"` and a `percent` below 1 creates the fill with `percent` 1.0 (a full solid fill).
The same happens with `overwriteExisting: true` on an existing percentage fill: the percent is reset to 1.0.

`GetFills` reads the percent of existing percentage fills correctly (e.g. 0.05, 0.25, 0.95 for Archicad's
5 % … 95 % fills), so reading and writing are not symmetric: a fill copied with GetFills → CreateFills
loses its percentage.

**Expected**

The fill is created (or overwritten) with the given `percent`, as the schema describes
("Translucency percentage [0..1] (gradient and some Solid fills)").

**How to reproduce**

```python
fill = {"name": "Test 25 %", "subType": "Solid", "percent": 0.25}
CreateFills {"fillDataArray": [fill]}
GetFills {"attributeIds": [<new id>], "fields": ["subType", "percent"]}
# -> subType "Solid", percent 1.0   (expected 0.25)
```

Same result for 0.05 … 0.95, on create and on overwrite.

**Note**

`CreateFillsCommand` does read the value (`data.Get ("percent", fill.filltype.percent)`), so Archicad
probably overwrites or ignores `filltype.percent` on create/modify for this subtype. Maybe the percentage has
to be set in another field or in `API_AttributeDefExt` for Solid fills.
author: Kappa-lo

title: GetFills / CreateFills: symbol fills lose their offsets and solid parts (copies draw wrong)
body:
**Environment:** Archicad 29 (build 3200, German), macOS, Tapir 1.7.3

**What happens**

Symbol fills copied with `GetFills` → `CreateFills` (all fields, same file or another file) are created but draw wrong: the pattern is all black or broken. In our test all 17 symbol fills we copied came out wrong, although `GetFills` on the new fill returns the same data as on the original.

Also, two *different* symbol fills can return identical `GetFills` data, so the read data is not the full definition.

**Likely cause (from the source)**

`GetFills` / `CreateFills` leave out two parts of a symbol fill's definition:

1. **The symbol offsets `c1` / `c2`** (X1/Y1 and X2/Y2 in the Fill Types dialog, which say how the motif repeats). `GetFills` only returns `filltype.c1/c2` as `gradientStart` / `gradientEnd` for gradient fills, so for symbol fills they are never read. On create they stay (0,0) unless `gradientStart/End` are passed, so all copies of the motif sit on top of each other.
2. **The solid fill items of the motif** (`sfill_SolidFills`, `sfill_FillCoords`, `sfill_SubPolys`, `sfill_PolyArcs`, count in `filNumb`). The comment in `CreateFillsCommand` says they are not supported. Symbol fills with filled shapes lose them.

**Expected**

`GetFills` returns, and `CreateFills` accepts, the complete symbol fill definition: e.g. `symbolOffset1` / `symbolOffset2` (c1/c2) and `symbolSolidFills` (polygons with holes and arcs), so a symbol fill can be copied 1:1.

**How to reproduce**

1. In a project with a symbol fill (e.g. one of Archicad's insulation fills), read it with `GetFills` with all fields.
2. `CreateFills` with that data and a new name.
3. Draw a hatch with each fill: the copy looks different (black or broken pattern).

title: Import attributes from another project file (append / overwrite like the Attribute Manager) and export them to a file
body:
**Environment:** Archicad 29 (build 3200, German), macOS, Tapir 1.7.3

**Use case**

We maintain an office template and several project files that must share the same attributes (surfaces, fills, building materials, composites, line types, layers). Today the only scripted way to bring an attribute from one file into another is: read it (`GetAttributesFromProject` or `GetFills`/`GetSurfaces`/... in the source file) and recreate it with `Create*` in the target. That is slow and loses information:

- the attribute gets a new GUID, so files no longer match by GUID;
- some data cannot be recreated at all: symbol fills (#1614), percentage fills (#1613);
- references between attributes (a composite's building materials, a building material's fill and surface) have to be remapped by hand.

Archicad's own Attribute Manager does this in one step ("Append" / "Overwrite", matched by name or by index), and can save attributes to a file and load them from one.

**Request**

Follow-up to #1216 / #1221, where `load: true` was left for a maintainer decision:

1. **Import:** `ImportAttributesFromProject` (or `GetAttributesFromProject` with `load: true`) from a .pln / .tpl (and .aat if the API allows it):
   - `attributes`: by type + name, index or GUID (or "all of type")
   - `mode`: `append` (new only), `overwriteByName`, `overwriteByIndex`, like the Attribute Manager
   - dependent attributes brought along or mapped to existing ones by name, with a report of what was created, overwritten, mapped or skipped
   - a `dryRun` that returns that report without changing anything
2. **Export:** write selected attributes of the open project to a file (.aat, or a .pln/.tpl), so a curated set can be kept as one source file.
3. If `ACAPI_Attribute_GetAttributesFromProject` + `CreateExt` is the only route: keep the full `API_AttributeDefExt` from the source file, so symbol fills, percentages and the like come over complete, even if the GUID can't be kept.

Related: #1582 (`GetAttributesFromProject` returns empty lists for Layer, BuildingMaterial and Surface).

Happy to test on AC29 (macOS) with a template and a project file.
author: Kappa-lo

title: IFC import translators: list them and choose one for IFCFileOperation merge/open
body:
**Environment:** Archicad 29 (build 3200, German), macOS, Tapir 1.7.3

**Use case**

We merge consultants' IFC files into reference files every day by script (`IFCFileOperation` with `method: merge`). The result depends heavily on the import translator (geometry conversion: Morphs, Objects or MEP elements; layer and property mapping). Export translators can already be listed and chosen (`GetIFCExportTranslators`, `translatorName` on save — thanks!). For import there is nothing yet.

**What happens today**

- `IFCFileOperation merge` / `open` take no translator. The merge does not use the project's default import translator: it uses **the translator of the last manual merge in the current Archicad session**.
- `OpenProject` resets that. Even a project-default import translator set in the IFC Translators dialog did not help: after `OpenProject` the next scripted merge came in with different geometry (native MEP elements instead of Morphs).
- So a reliable scripted build must start with one manual merge of a tiny IFC and then never reopen the project.
- Also worth a note in the docs: without the dialog, the IFC's first storey is placed on the **active** storey of the floor plan. We call `ChangeWindow` to storey 0 before every merge.

**Request**

1. `GetIFCImportTranslators`: list the import translators of the project (name, which one is the default).
2. `translatorName` for `IFCFileOperation` with `method: merge` and `open` (like `save` already has).
3. If the API allows it: read (and ideally set) the main settings of a translator: geometry conversion per element type, layer mapping, property mapping file. Even read-only would let us check a file before merging.
4. Optional: a `targetStoryIndex` (or "keep IFC levels") for merge, so the result does not depend on the active storey.

Happy to test on AC29 (macOS).

title: SetDetailsOfElements: say why Archicad refused the element (hidden or locked layer)
body:
Part of #1600

## What the code in the report means

`-2130312912` is `APIERR_HIDDENLAY`: Archicad refused `ACAPI_Element_Change` because the element's layer is hidden. `SetDetailsOfElements` only said "Failed to change element", so it looked like bad input. This PR doesn't make hidden-layer elements editable, since Archicad doesn't allow that by hand either. It makes the result say why.

## Change

- New `DescribeElementEditRefusal (err, elemHead)` in `CommandBase`. It returns the reason from the error code and the layer flags:
  - its layer is hidden
  - its layer is locked
  - it is not reserved by you in the Teamwork project
  - it is not editable (locked with Edit > Locking, or not reserved in Teamwork)

  For any other cause it returns an empty string, so those messages stay as they were.
- `SetDetailsOfElements` adds the reason to "Failed to change element", and to the id write, which fails first when `id` is given.
- `SetGDLParametersOfElements` already had this check in `GetElementChangeFailureMessage`, but without the hidden layer. It now uses the shared helper.
- The command description and the docs now say so. In the golden of `get_and_set_details_of_elements.py`, the one line for the hidden-layer element changes. The 20 `APIERR_BADPARS` results there keep "Failed to change element".

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS), 6/6

A hatch on a new test layer on the floor plan:

| layer | `SetDetailsOfElements` result |
|---|---|
| visible | success |
| hidden | `-2130312912` "Failed to change element, because its layer is hidden" |
| hidden, with `id` | `-2130312912` "Failed to set the id of the element, because its layer is hidden; no other details were changed" |
| locked | `-2130312913` "Failed to change element, because its layer is locked" |
| visible again | success |

`SetGDLParametersOfElements` on an object moved to the hidden layer returns "The parameters of element with guid … were not changed, because its layer is hidden".

The project was saved before and reopened without saving afterwards.

For #1600 this means the worksheet hatches sit on a layer that is hidden while the call runs. Why they end up there is still open, so this PR doesn't close the issue.

title: Add ImportAttributesFromProject (lines, fills, zone categories, pen tables, operation profiles)
body:
Part of #1615

Adds `ImportAttributesFromProject`. It imports attributes from another project or template file into the open project with their complete definition, like Append or Overwrite by name in the Attribute Manager. This is item 3 of the request, scoped the way the bot suggested in its reply.

## Command

```json
{
  "projectFilePath": "/path/to/template.pln",
  "attributeTypes": ["Fill", "Line", "ZoneCategory", "PenTable", "OperationProfile"],
  "attributeNames": ["optional", "filter"],
  "overwriteExisting": false,
  "dryRun": false
}
```

Each attribute of the source file gets one result item: `name`, `sourceIndex`, `result` (`created` / `overwritten` / `skipped` / `failed`), `attributeId` in the open project, and `error` when it failed.

- The attribute is read with `ACAPI_Attribute_GetAttributesFromProject` and written with `ACAPI_Attribute_CreateExt` / `ModifyExt`, passing the `API_AttributeDefExt` exactly as it was read. Symbol fills, percent fills and image fills arrive complete. That covers what `GetFills` → `CreateFills` loses today (#1613, #1614).
- Attributes are matched by name, the same lookup the `Create*` commands use with `overwriteExisting`. An existing name is `skipped` by default. With `overwriteExisting: true` it is overwritten in place and keeps its index and guid, so the elements that use it are not affected.
- `dryRun` reports the same results without changing anything.
- Only Line, Fill, ZoneCategory, PenTable and OperationProfile can be imported. Other types return an `APIERR_NOTSUPPORTED` error item:
  - Layer, Surface, BuildingMaterial and MEPSystem: Archicad returns none of them from a closed file (#1582, #1595).
  - Composite, Profile and LayerCombination: they refer to building materials, fills or layers by their index in the source file, and those indexes would point at unrelated attributes in the open project.

## The guid can't be kept

`ACAPI_Attribute_GetAttributesFromProject` returns a **different guid on every read**. I read the same 338 fills twice and none of the guids matched, and none matched the guids `GetAttributesFromProject` returned either. So:
- a new attribute gets a new guid from Archicad (`APINULLGuid` on create),
- the result identifies the source attribute by `sourceIndex`, not by a guid,
- the description of `GetAttributesFromProject` now says that its `attributeId` is not the guid stored in the file.

Matching the two files by guid, as the issue asked, isn't possible this way.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS), 18/18

Source: a template with 109 line types, 338 fills, 13 zone categories, 9 pen tables and 33 operation profiles. Target: a project made from that template. A first `dryRun` reported all 502 attributes as `skipped`, so name matching works, including names with ä, ö, ü and ß.

For each case, the attribute was deleted in the target, a `dryRun` reported `created` without creating anything, and the import then created it. Afterwards I compared the `Get*` definition with the one read before deleting:

| type | attribute | result |
|---|---|---|
| Fill | symbol fill | same definition |
| Fill | solid fill, 75 % | same definition |
| Fill | vector fill, name with umlaut | same definition |
| Fill | image fill | same definition, texture included |
| Line | symbol line, name with ß | same definition |
| ZoneCategory | name with umlaut | same definition |
| OperationProfile | name with umlaut | created (Tapir has no reader for its details) |

The one difference: a non-image fill comes back with texture size 1 × 1 instead of 0 × 0. `CreateFills` gives a new fill the same 1 × 1, so it's Archicad's own default on create, and the texture is only used by image fills.

Also tested:
- An existing pen table: `skipped` by default. With `overwriteExisting` it is `overwritten`, guid and index stay the same, and the pens are unchanged.
- A symbol fill that `CreateFills` had changed to a solid fill was restored by `overwriteExisting`, with the same guid and index.
- Composite, Layer, BuildingMaterial, Profile and LayerCombination each return the `APIERR_NOTSUPPORTED` error item.
- An `attributeNames` filter that matches nothing returns an empty list.

The target project was saved before the test and reopened without saving afterwards.

## Not in this PR

- Export to a file (item 2): the DevKit has no API that writes attributes to a file.
- The types the API can't read from a closed file, and bringing dependent attributes along (item 1, dependencies): they would need a way to read Layer, Surface and BuildingMaterial from a closed file.

title: Hatch fill orientation in Get/SetDetailsOfElements
body:
## What changes

- **`GetDetailsOfElements`** returns a Hatch's fill orientation as `fillOrientation` (the existing `HatchOrientation` schema: type, origin, matrix, inner radius), like the Slab's `floorFill.orientation`.
- **`SetDetailsOfElements`** accepts `fillOrientation` for Hatches, merged onto the current orientation (omitted fields keep their values).
- Two things are needed for the values to reach Archicad:
  1. `ACAPI_ELEMENT_MASK_SET` marks only the first byte of a field (`*((char *) &((typ *) &rec)->varnam) = -1`), so masking the whole `API_HatchOrientation` let only its `type` through. Every member is masked on its own (`TAPIR_MASK_SET_HATCH_ORIENTATION` in `CommandBase.hpp`).
  2. Archicad ignores the origin while the fill is snapped to the project origin (`APIHatchOrinFlag_GlobalOrigo`). A given origin clears that flag, and a `Global` fill becomes `Rotated` unless a `type` is sent as well.
- Archicad ignores the orientation of Solid fills (there is no pattern); the schema says so.

## Not in this PR

The Slab floor fill (#662): with the same per-member mask and flag, Archicad still takes only the `type` there, not the origin or the matrix (tested by @Cri5chan). The Slab code is left as it is on `main`.

## Test

`archicad-addon/Examples/test_hatch_fill_orientation.py` creates a hatch with a Vector fill, writes origin / type / matrix, reads them back and deletes the hatch. Tested by @Cri5chan on Archicad 29 (macOS): Vector and Symbol fills ✅, Solid fills ignored by Archicad.

title: [2/2] GetFills/CreateFills: filled polygons of Symbol fills (builds on #1617, fixes #1614)
body:
Part 2 of #1614. **Builds on #1617** (symbol offsets): this branch contains #1617's commit plus one commit of its own, so after #1617 is merged only that commit remains.

## What changes

`GetFills` returns and `CreateFills` accepts `symbolSolidFills`: the filled polygons of a symbol fill's pattern (`sfill_SolidFills`, `sfill_FillCoords`, `sfill_SubPolys`, `sfill_PolyArcs`, counted by `filltype.filNumb`). New schema `FillSymbolSolidFill`: `coordinates`, `subPolygons`, `arcs` (`PolyArc`).

## The open questions from #1614, from the DevKit headers (`APIdefs_Attributes.h`, `APIdefs_Base.h`)

1. There is no `API_SFill_SolidFill`. `sfill_SolidFills` is `API_Polygon**`, and `API_Polygon` holds only counts: `nCoords`, `nSubPolys`, `nArcs`. The header says the polygons' data is *"stored sequentially"* in `sfill_FillCoords` (`API_Coord**`), `sfill_SubPolys` (`Int32**`) and `sfill_PolyArcs` (`API_PolyArc**`), so polygon *i*'s range starts after the counts of polygons 0..i-1.
2. Index conventions (slot 0, closing points, arc indices relative to what): **this PR does not interpret them.** Each polygon's slices are returned and written back unchanged, in the same order. A GetFills -> CreateFills round trip therefore writes exactly what Archicad stored, whatever the convention is. The schema description says to pass the arrays back as read, not to author them.
3. `filNumb` is set to the number of polygons, and the three handles are allocated to the sums of the counts, so counts and handle sizes always match. On overwrite without `symbolSolidFills`, the existing polygons are kept (as for the other symbol geometry); with it, they are replaced as a whole.

## Test

`archicad-addon/Examples/test_symbol_fill_copy.py` copies every Symbol fill of the open project, compares each copy with its original field by field (including `symbolSolidFills`) and deletes the copies (`KEEP_COPIES = True` keeps them to compare in a hatch).

Still a draft: I'll run it on this PR's AC29 build (macOS), together with the #1617 test, and report here before marking it ready.

title: CreateFills: keep the percent of a Solid fill (isPercentFill)
body:
Fixes #1613

## Cause

Archicad keeps the percent of a Solid fill only when `API_FilltypeType::isPercentFill` is set. The DevKit calls the field *"output-only; detected from the bitmap pattern"*, but `ACAPI_Attribute_CreateExt` and `ModifyExt` do read it. `CreateFills` never set it, so every Solid fill came out as a full Solid fill with percent 1.

The bit pattern doesn't do it, so the earlier idea in the issue isn't enough. I tested each variant with `CreateFills` (Solid, `percent` 0.25) on Archicad 29:

| also sent | percent read back |
|---|---|
| nothing | 1 |
| the original `bitPattern` of the 25 % fill | 1 |
| the original header flags | 1 |
| `isPercentFill` | **0.25** |
| `isPercentFill` + original `bitPattern` | **0.25**, same pattern as the original |

Several percents also share one pattern: 10, 15, 20, 30 and 35 % all have `00AA00AA00AA00AA`, and 5 % has an empty pattern. So the pattern alone could not tell the percent apart.

## Change

- `CreateFills` sets `isPercentFill` for a Solid fill whose `percent` is below 1, on create and with `overwriteExisting`. A Solid fill with percent 1 stays a full Solid fill.
- `GetFills` returns `bitPattern` for Solid fills too, not only for Vector fills. Then a fill read with `GetFills` can be passed to `CreateFills` unchanged and keeps its pattern.
- The description of `percent` in the `CreateFills` schema now says how it works for Solid fills.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS), 9/9

- The repro from the issue: `CreateFills` with Solid and `percent` 0.05, 0.25 and 0.95 reads back 0.05, 0.25 and 0.95.
- Round trip `GetFills` → `CreateFills` (as a copy) for all 23 Solid fills of a project, including the 5 % … 95 % fills, 100 % and a pattern fill imported from IFC: `percent` and `bitPattern` come back identical. The only change is texture size 0 → 1, which `CreateFills` sets on every new fill and which only image fills use.
- `overwriteExisting` on a 25 % fill: 0.6 → 0.6, 1.0 → 1 (full Solid fill), 0.1 → 0.1.
- `GetFills` returns `bitPattern` for all Solid fills.
- The project was saved before and reopened without saving afterwards.

Not changed: gradient fills still come back with `percent` 0, as noted in `Examples/test_all_attributes.py`. `isPercentFill` is only set for Solid fills.

title: Steward: push-merge fails at "Create the App token" (Invalid keyData), so conflict fixes are never pushed
body:
Since 05:39 UTC today, every steward run that merges `main` into a bot PR fails in the `push-merge` job at **Create the App token**:

```
Failed to create token for "tapir-archicad-automation" (attempt 1): Invalid keyData
DOMException [DataError]: Invalid keyData
    at importDerKey (node:internal/crypto/webcrypto_util:136:11)
```

Example: https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/actions/runs/40723856465 (Fix bot PR #1494, job `push-merge`).

`actions/create-github-app-token` cannot read the private key in `TAPIR_BOT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`. The `app-id` input is there, so the secrets exist, but the key is not a usable PEM. Common causes are a truncated paste, lost line breaks, or a value that is not the `.pem` file GitHub generated for the App.

**Effect**
- Today 318 "Fix bot PR" runs ended in failure. Of the 171 fix runs between the merge of #1447 and today, `push-merge` ran 10 times and failed every time; I found none where it succeeded, so the key may never have worked.
- In each one the `fix` job runs the model and resolves the conflict, but nothing is pushed. The PR stays in conflict, and the bot still writes its "fixed" comment. #1293 and #1547 have had the same conflict "fixed" several times today with no new commit.
- The steward starts the next round an hour later, so each of these runs uses a model run from the usage limit (#977) and achieves nothing.

**Suggested fix** (needs a maintainer, the bot can't change secrets):
1. Generate a new private key in the App's settings and store the whole `.pem` file content, including the `-----BEGIN … KEY-----` and `-----END … KEY-----` lines, as `TAPIR_BOT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`.
2. Until the key works, setting `BOT_PR_STEWARD=false` pauses the steward and stops the runs that have no effect.

A follow-up could be to write the "fixed" comment only after `push-merge` succeeded, so that a failed push shows up on the PR.

title: GetAttributesByType: return the attribute folder path (replaces #1026)
body:
Part 3 of #925. Replaces #1026.

#1026 by the issue bot is stuck: it has the `needs-maintainer` label, one blocking finding and conflicts with `main`. This PR is its change on current `main`, with the blocking finding fixed and tested in Archicad. #1026 can be closed when this one is merged.

## What it does

`GetAttributesByType` returns `folderPath` on every attribute: the attribute folder names from the first level below the root folder down to the folder that holds the attribute. It is empty for the root folder, and always empty on Archicad 25. The folder tree of the type is walked once per call. Everything else is as described in #1026: the schema, the description, the example check, the goldens with `"folderPath": []`, and the Grasshopper `FolderPaths` output.

## Changes against #1026

- **The root folder is left out of the path** (the blocking finding on #1026). Archicad returns the root folder with its localized name as its path (`Ebenen` in a German Archicad), and every subfolder with that name in front. `rootFolder.path.Clear ()` before the walk fixes this. Every subfolder is then rebuilt from its parent by the existing check.
- **Merged with current `main`:**
  - the `GetAttributesByType` registration keeps main's `creationInfo` text and adds the folder path sentence;
  - the `GetAttributesFromProject` registration stays;
  - the example checks both the folder paths and the creation info;
  - the golden has both lines.
- **Grasshopper:** `FolderPaths` is **appended** after main's five creation outputs (index 9, not 4 as in #1026), because saved definitions find outputs by position.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS, German UI), 18/18

The test project was saved before and reopened without saving afterwards.

- Every layer has `folderPath`. A layer in the root folder has `[]`.
- A test layer moved into `TapirTest/A/B` has `["TapirTest", "A", "B"]` (on #1026: `["Ebenen", "TapirTest", "A", "B"]`).
- After a move into `TapirTest/C` it has `["TapirTest", "C"]`. Moving it back with the path read before as `targetFolder` of `MoveAttributesAndFolders` works.
- The project's 226 surfaces in folders and its layer folders come back without the root name.
- `Examples/get_attributes_by_type.py` prints `all attributes have a folder path: True`.

Not checked:

title: MoveAttributesAndFolders: already in the target folder counts as moved; requested paths in folder messages
body:
Two small fixes to the attribute folder commands from #925. I came across both while testing #1026 / #1624.

## 1. Already in the target folder counts as moved

`MoveAttributesAndFolders` reported `"Failed to move the attribute."` when the attribute was already in the target folder. `ACAPI_Attribute_Move` fails in that case. The same happened for a folder that was already directly in the target. That makes it hard to run a script that applies a folder layout (for example from a template) a second time.

Now, when the move fails, the command reads the content of the target folder. If the attribute or folder is already directly in it, the result is a success, because nothing needed to change. Any other failure is still reported. The content is only read after a failed move, so a normal move costs nothing extra. For the root folder Archicad reports no guid, so the target is read again with `ACAPI_Attribute_GetFolder` first, the way #1624 reads the root folder.

## 2. The folder paths in messages and in the "into itself" check

`ACAPI_Attribute_GetFolder` (`FindAttributeFolder`) writes the found folder's full path back, with the localized root folder name in front. That is the same behaviour #1624 fixes for `folderPath`. As a result:
- messages after a lookup named `'Ebenen/TapirTest/A'` instead of the path that was sent (Delete, Rename, Move);
- the "cannot be moved into itself or one of its subfolders" check of `MoveAttributesAndFolders` compared the requested folder path with the *found* target path (`["Ebenen", "TapirTest", "A", "B"]`). It never matched, so Archicad's general error came back instead of the explaining one.

The commands now keep the requested path for their messages and for that check. The API calls still get the found folder as before.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS, German UI), 11/11

The project was saved before and reopened without saving afterwards.

| call | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| layer moved into `TapirTest/A`, then into `TapirTest/A` again | 2nd call fails | success |
| layer moved into the root folder twice | 2nd call fails | success |
| folder `TapirTest/B` moved into `TapirTest`, where it already is | fails | success |
| folder `TapirTest/A/B` moved into `TapirTest/A` (already there) | fails | success |
| folder `TapirTest/A` moved into `TapirTest/A/B` | Archicad's error, `'Ebenen/TapirTest/A'` | `Attribute folder 'TapirTest/A' cannot be moved into itself or one of its subfolders.` |
| delete a missing folder | | `'TapirTest/gibt es nicht' not found` |

Also tested:
- A real move (folder `B` into `A`) still works.
- A building material moved into a layer folder still fails.
- `Examples/attribute_folders.py` (with a new "move again" step) prints `Moved again into the root folder they are in: 1`. The example has no golden.
