title: DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItems: fail for a path that is not in the embedded library
body:
Follow-up to #1366 and #677. No issue was open for this.

## What the result meant

`DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItems` answers `{"success": true}` for a path that is not in the embedded library, so a script can't tell a deleted item from a typo, a bare file name or a part that is already gone. We hit it with a few thousand paths that all came back as deleted while the embedded library was unchanged.

In `DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItemsCommand::Execute`, every item first gets `CreateSuccessfulExecutionResult ()`. An item whose location doesn't exist (`ItemExists` is false) then went to `DeleteOneByOne`, which only replaces the result when `ACAPI_LibraryManagement_DeleteEmbeddedLibItem` returns an error. For a location that isn't there it returns `NoError`, so the success stayed. The batch call had the same gap: when `ACAPI_LibraryManagement_DeleteEmbeddedLibItems` returns `NoError`, nothing checked that the items were gone.

## Change

- An item whose path doesn't exist in the embedded library is now a failed result: `APIERR_BADPARS`, "No item at the given path in the embedded library." It is no longer passed to the API.
- After the batch call, every item that is still there is tried one by one, whatever the batch call returned (before, only when it returned an error).
- After the one-by-one call, an item that is still there is a failed result ("The embedded library item is still there after the deletion."), also when the API returned `NoError`.
- Paths that exist behave as before: one batch call, success when the item is gone.
- New check `archicad-addon/Test/checks/delete_embedded_library_items_missing_path.json` for the community test runner. It creates `TapirCheck/DeleteMe` with `CreateFolderInEmbeddedLibrary`, deletes it together with a bare file name and a missing folder path, deletes it again, and removes `TapirCheck` in teardown. It needs no empty project (`requiresEmpty: []`), since it creates no elements.

## Tested on Archicad 27 (macOS)

Run with `tools/community-test-runner` (`check`) on an untitled project: before, one that already held other test elements (the check only uses its own); after, a new empty one.

| | check result |
|---|---|
| Tapir 1.7.3 (release), before | 3/6: the bare file name, the missing folder and the second delete of the same folder all answer `success: true` |
| this branch (build check artifact "Tapir Add-On AC27 Mac", reports 1.7.4) | **6/6**; a bare file name now answers `APIERR_BADPARS` "No item at the given path in the embedded library." |

title: GetElementTrims: answer for walls, slabs and columns instead of an error item
body:
Follow-up to #625. No issue was open for this.

## What the error means

`GetElementTrims` answers every wall, slab and column with an error item:

```json
{"error": {"code": -2130313103, "message": "Failed to read the elements this element trims."}}
```

On a project with about 5,500 walls, 7,000 slabs and 1,250 columns, all of them came back like that; only the roofs answered.

`-2130313103` is `APIERR_BADELEMENTTYPE`. The DevKit documents it for `ACAPI_Element_Trim_GetTrimmedElements` as "The given element is not Roof or Shell element." `GetElementTrimsCommand::Execute` reads `trimmedBy` first (`ACAPI_Element_Trim_GetTrimmingElements`, `ACAPI_Element_Trim_GetTrimType`), then calls `ACAPI_Element_Trim_GetTrimmedElements` for `trims`. For anything that isn't a roof or shell that call returns `APIERR_BADELEMENTTYPE`, and the error replaced the whole item, so the `trimmedBy` already read was lost.

This also happens for walls that **are** trimmed. A wall trimmed by a roof with `TrimElements` gets the same error item, while the roof correctly lists the wall in its `trims`. So the repository's own `Examples/trim_elements.py` can't get the answer its golden output expects (`trimmedBy` with the roof and `trims: []`) on Archicad 27; it ends at `item['trimmedBy']`.

## Change

- In `GetElementTrimsCommand::Execute`, `APIERR_BADELEMENTTYPE` from `ACAPI_Element_Trim_GetTrimmedElements` now means "trims nothing": the item keeps its `trimmedBy` list and gets an empty `trims` list.
- Every other error is still an error item, and so is an unknown or deleted element (that fails earlier, in `ACAPI_Element_Trim_GetTrimmingElements`), as the response schema promises.
- New check `archicad-addon/Test/checks/get_element_trims_walls_and_slabs.json` for the community test runner: two walls trimmed by a roof, one wall and one slab apart, then `GetElementTrims` on [trimmed wall, untrimmed wall, slab, roof, bogus guid].

## Tested on Archicad 27 (macOS)

Run with `tools/community-test-runner` (`check`) on an untitled project: before, one that already held other test elements (the check only uses its own); after, a new empty one.

| | check result |
|---|---|
| Tapir 1.7.3 (release), before | 4/11: the trimmed wall, the untrimmed wall and the slab are error items; the roof (`trims` with both walls) and the bogus guid (error) pass |
| this branch (build check artifact "Tapir Add-On AC27 Mac", reports 1.7.4) | **11/11**; a new column also answers `{"trimmedBy": [], "trims": []}` |

title: CreateStairs: allow landings on multi-segment baselines (per-edge segment type, per-vertex turn type, landing edge offset)
body:
Environment: Archicad 29 JPN, Tapir 1.7.3, Windows 11.

Since #445, multi-segment (L/U) baselines work in CreateStairs. But we found no way to say that a turn should be a **landing**. When we create a U-shaped stair from a 4-point baseline, the solver turns the middle turn into winders. The textbook we follow (and most real two-flight stairs) needs a landing there, so today we create these stairs by hand.

Request: let CreateStairs (and later ModifyStairs, #824) take:
- per baseline edge: `segmentType` (flight / landing, i.e. `APIST_LandingSegment`)
- per baseline vertex: `turnType` (e.g. `APIST_LandingTurn`)
- the landing edge offsets (`currLandingStartEdgeOffset` and related fields in `API_StairPolylineEdgeData`), so the landing depth can be set

Our case: width 1150, riser 153.8, tread 240, baseline on the left. Baseline (mm): (2520,24250) → (5400,24250) → (5400,24490) → (2520,24490). The middle turn should be a landing with its edge offset by 50, giving a landing depth of 1350.

The tread depth side of the same case (we asked for 240 and got 292) is already tracked in #425 / #750, so this issue is only about landings. As noted in #425, the landing position is what decides whether a two-flight stair fits its stairwell.

Related: #425, #444/#445 (multi-segment baselines), #824 (ModifyStairs), #1210 (SolveStair), #1558 (SolveStairBaseline crash), #1561 (stair read-back). The DevKit sample Element_Test creates stairs and could serve as a reference. Happy to test a build on Archicad 29 JPN.

title: ModifySlabs: report a floor fill origin or matrix that Archicad ignored (#662)
body:
Follow-up to #662. The issue was closed when #676 fixed the merge of a partial `floorFill.orientation`, but the origin it reports as ignored is still ignored.

## What Archicad does with a Slab's cover fill orientation

Of `slab.hatchOrientation`, `ACAPI_Element_Change` applies **only the type**:
- the origin and the distortion matrix are reset (origin `(0, 0)`, identity matrix);
- `version` is reset to 0;
- the flags are normalized (0 for Rotated/Distorted, 11 for Global).

It still returns `NoError`.

I tested it with a probe build of `main` on Archicad 29. Each variant used a new slab on a visible layer, with a Vector cover fill and `use3DHatching` off. Every variant gave the same result:

| variant | type | origin / matrix |
|---|---|---|
| mask the whole struct (as `main` does) | applied | reset |
| mask every member (`type`, `version`, `flags`, `origo`, `matrix*`, `innerRadius`) | applied | reset |
| mask every byte of the struct (`memset 0xFF`) | applied | reset |
| flags cleared / `GlobalOrientation` kept | applied | reset |
| `version` 1, 2, 3 | applied (version back to 0) | reset |
| `Distorted` with origin and matrix | applied | reset |

The mask does reach Archicad, because the flags change. Hatch elements behave differently: there the same orientation sticks (#1620). The origin in #662 was set in the UI and read back correctly, so it is stored. It just cannot be written through `ACAPI_Element_Change`. I found no other API for it in the DevKit.

## Change

So `ModifySlabs` no longer reports success for something Archicad dropped. This is the read-back approach `SetDetailsOfElements` uses for a Drawing's `drawingScale` (#1476):

- When `floorFill.orientation` is given, the slab is read back after the change. A given `origin` or `matrix00`…`matrix11` that differs from what Archicad kept gets a failed execution result that names it, for example: `Archicad did not apply floorFill.orientation origin (it stayed 0, 0): on a Slab it applies only the orientation type through the API. The other details given were applied.`
- The type, the other floor fill fields and the geometry of the same call are still applied, as the message says. A value that already matches what is stored counts as a success.
- The `FloorFill.orientation` schema description and the `ModifySlabs` description say so.
- `Examples/test_modify_slabs_floorfill_orientation.py` (from #676) expected the matrix to be applied, which it is not on Archicad 29. It now checks:
  - that the type is applied and merged (type and `use` survive an origin-only call);
  - that the ignored origin and matrix are reported.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS), 7/7 + the example 6/6

The project was saved before and reopened without saving afterwards.

| call | result |
|---|---|
| floor fill without orientation | success, as before |
| type only | success, type applied |
| origin equal to the stored one | success |
| `fillId` + origin | failure naming the origin; the fill was set |

title: CreateClassificationSystems/Items: one result per input, and the new ids
body:
No issue was open for this.

## What the results meant

A script that creates a classification system with items, and then assigns them to elements, needs to know which creation failed and the new GUIDs. Both commands fall short:

1. **`CreateClassificationSystems` drops the result of a system without items.** In `CreateClassificationSystemsCommand::Execute`, a system with no `classificationItems` hits the `continue` before `executionResults (CreateSuccessfulExecutionResult ())`. Two systems in, one without items, gives one result, so the results no longer line up with the input:

   ```json
   {"executionResults": [{"success": true}]}
   ```

2. **`CreateClassificationItems` answers an empty list for items it created.** In `CreateClassificationItemsCommand::Execute` the loop only pushes failures; after a successful `ACAPI_Classification_CreateClassificationItem` nothing is pushed:

   ```json
   {"executionResults": []}
   ```

3. **Errors of nested children are dropped.** `CreateClassificationItemsRecursively` ignores the result of its own recursive call, and `CreateClassificationItems` ignores the result for the `children` of each item.
4. **Neither command returns the new GUIDs**, although `apiClassificationSystem.guid` and `apiClassificationItem.guid` are filled at that point. Today a script has to read everything back with `API.GetAllClassificationSystems` / `API.GetAllClassificationsInSystem` and match by name.

## Change

- One execution result per input, in input order, for both commands. A system or item whose children fail gets a failed result ("Failed to create items into classification system" / "Failed to create child classification items").
- `CreateClassificationItemsRecursively` returns the error of a nested child.
- New lists next to `executionResults`, aligned with the input, the way `CreatePropertyDefinitions` returns `propertyIds`:
  - `CreateClassificationSystems` → `classificationSystemIds`: `{"classificationSystemId": {"guid": "..."}}` or an error item.
  - `CreateClassificationItems` → `classificationItemIds`: `{"classificationItemId": {"guid": "..."}}` or an error item.

  A system or item that was created but whose children failed is still listed with its id, since it exists; its execution result carries the error.
- `executionResults` stays, so existing scripts and the Grasshopper components (which read only `executionResults`) keep working.
- `CommonSchemaDefinitions.json`: `ClassificationSystemIdOrError`, `ClassificationSystemIdsOrErrors`, `ClassificationItemIdOrError`, `ClassificationItemIdsOrErrors`, built from the existing `...IdArrayItem` definitions and `ErrorItem`.
- Golden output of `create_classifications.py`: the response now also has `classificationSystemIds`.
- New check `archicad-addon/Test/checks/create_classification_systems_and_items_return_ids.json`: two systems (one without items), an item with a child into the first, a read-back with `API.GetAllClassificationsInSystem`, an item into a system that doesn't exist, then `DeleteClassificationSystems`.

Out of scope: the ids of child items created through `children`. They would need a nested structure in the response; happy to add it in a follow-up if wanted.

## Tested on Archicad 27 (macOS)

Run with `tools/community-test-runner` (`check`) on an untitled project.

| | check result |
|---|---|
| Tapir 1.7.3 (release), before | stops at the first step: two systems in, one result out (`{"executionResults": [{"success": true}]}`), no ids |
| this branch (build check artifact "Tapir Add-On AC27 Mac", reports 1.7.4) | **14/14** |

`Examples/create_classifications.py` on the branch build gives exactly the updated golden response (with `classificationSystemIds`). Build check green on the fork for all Archicad versions, Windows and Mac.

title: Describe zCoordinate, offset and anchorPoint of CreateBeams, and the stair baseline
body:
Related: #1043, #1597 (layer on create; not part of this). No issue was open for this.

## Why

Creating beams and stairs from geometry read elsewhere (IFC axes, another application's model), we had to find out by trial where they land:

- In `CreateBeams`, `zCoordinate` and `offset` have no description, and `anchorPoint` only says "Anchor point of the beam cross section on a 3x3 grid", not that it decides where the beam sits relative to `zCoordinate`. The code puts `zCoordinate` into `element.beam.level`, the reference line's height. `CreateColumns` and `CreateSlabs` already say what their `zCoordinate` refers to; beams were the odd one out.
- In `CreateStairs`, `baseLinePoints` says "2D coordinates defining the stair baseline polyline", not which side the flight is on.

## Measured in Archicad 27 (macOS), Tapir 1.7.3

Beams from (900, y) to (904, y), `zCoordinate: 10`, `height: 0.1`, `width: 0.2`, read with `Get3DBoundingBoxes`:

| anchorPoint | z | across the axis (+ = left, looking from beg to end) |
|---|---|---|
| (none; the template's default) | 9.90 to 10.00 | −0.10 to +0.10 |
| `TopCenter` | 9.90 to 10.00 | −0.10 to +0.10 |
| `Center` | 9.95 to 10.05 | −0.10 to +0.10 |
| `BottomCenter` | 10.00 to 10.10 | −0.10 to +0.10 |
| `TopLeft` | 9.90 to 10.00 | −0.20 to 0.00 |
| `TopRight` | 9.90 to 10.00 | 0.00 to +0.20 |
| `TopCenter`, `offset: 0.3` | 9.90 to 10.00 | +0.20 to +0.40 |

Straight stairs, `zCoordinate: 0`, `flightWidth: 1.2`, `totalHeight: 2.8`, baseline 4 m long along +x, −x and +y, Stair tool defaults of the template: in all three the flight lies to the **right** of the baseline, looking from the first point to the last (e.g. along +x from (930, 900): y 898.8 to 900.0). The first point stays where it was given; the solver set the baseline to 4.69 m (17 risers at the tool's going), so the flight ends beyond the last point given.

The side is not fixed, though: the stair in #1561 (Archicad 29, another template) lies on the other side of its baseline. `API_StairType` has `baselinePosition` (`APILP_Left`, `APILP_Right`, `APILP_Center`, `APILP_Auto`), which `CreateStairs` doesn't set, so the side follows the Stair tool defaults or the favorite. With our template the baseline is on the left edge.

## Change

Descriptions only, in `ExtendedElementCommands.cpp`:

- `CreateBeams` `zCoordinate`: absolute Z of the reference line; which point of the cross section lies on it is set by `anchorPoint` (Top hangs below, `MiddleLeft`/`Center`/`MiddleRight` center, Bottom stands on top), with the 10 / 0.1 → 9.9 to 10 example; home story as for columns and slabs.
- `CreateBeams` `offset`: horizontal distance from the reference line, positive to the left looking from `begCoordinate` to `endCoordinate`.
- `CreateBeams` `anchorPoint`: the point of the cross section on the reference line, height and left/right edge as measured above.
- `CreateStairs` and `SolveStairBaseline` (which takes the same fields) `baseLinePoints`: the baseline runs along the left edge, the right edge or the center of the flight as set by the Stair tool's baseline position (tool defaults or `favoriteName`); with the baseline on the left edge the flight lies to the right; the first point is kept and the length comes from the risers.

A `baselinePosition` input for `CreateStairs` would make this explicit; that's a feature, not part of this PR.

The generated docs under `docs/` are left to the release, which regenerates them.

Seen while measuring, not changed here: `GetDetailsOfElements` returns a stair's `baseLinePoints` relative to its first point (`[{"x": 0, "y": 0}, {"x": 4.69, "y": 0}]` for the stair above that starts at (930, 900)), and `treadDepth` 0. Both are already reported in #1561.

## Tested

Build check green on the fork (all Archicad versions, Windows and Mac). No behaviour change, so no check file.

title: SetStories: set every story's level directly with SetElevation
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution -->
_Requested by **Ádám**_

## What goes wrong

`SetStories` anchored the story ladder on the active story and set the distances with `APIStory_SetHeight`. Which side of a boundary `SetHeight` moves differs between Archicad versions: on Archicad 27 it moves the active story below the boundary (the comment in the code measured the opposite on Archicad 28).

Reproduced on Archicad 27.0.0 R1 (5060), Windows: a project with one unnamed story at −1.09 m (3.39 m tall), and `SetStories` with `[{index: -1, level: -6}, {index: 0, level: 0}]`.

1. The new story is inserted below with a height of 6, so it lands at −7.09 m.
2. The level pass makes story −1 active, sets its elevation to −6, then sets its height to 6 so that story 0 follows to 0.
3. On Archicad 27 that `SetHeight` moves story −1 (the active one) back down instead of story 0 up.

Result: `Failed to set the level of story -1: requested -6.0000, got -7.0900 (active story: -1)`, with story 0 still at −1.09 m.

## The change

Every story that is off its requested level becomes the active story (`APIStory_GoTo`) and gets its level with `APIStory_SetElevation`, which moves the story it names and nothing else. Heights are no longer used in the level pass. The stories that go down are moved first, bottom up, then the stories that go up, top down, so no story crosses a neighbour. The previously active story is restored afterwards, and the final check of every level stays as it was.

## Tested

The Archicad 27 Windows build of this commit, on the project above: the levels come out as −6 m and 0 m, and the same project then exports to IFC with the right storeys. The build check passes for Archicad 25 to 30.

title: IFCFileOperation: storyIndex for merge, so the IFC's storeys no longer follow the active story (#1616)
body:
Part of #1616 (item 4).

## The problem

Without a dialog, `IFCFileOperation` with `method: merge` puts the **first storey of the IFC file on the active story** of the floor plan. The next IFC storeys go on the stories above it. So the result of a scripted merge depends on which story someone last looked at. Today a script has to call `ChangeWindow` with a `storyIndex` before every merge.

I checked this on Archicad 29 with a small IFC file (storeys EG and 1.OG; 4 walls, a door and a column on EG, the slab on 1.OG):

| active story | walls, door, column | slab |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | story 0 | story 1 |
| 2 | story 2 | story 3 |

## Change

`IFCFileOperation` gets an optional `storyIndex`, only for the merge method:
- The given story is made the active one, the same way `ChangeWindow` does it: floor plan window, then `APIStory_GoTo`.
- When the merge is done, the previous active story and the previous window are restored. This runs in a `GS::OnExit`, so it also runs after a failed merge, but I didn't test a failing merge. The previous window is restored like `SaveProject` does it (#681).
- An index outside `GetStories` and `storyIndex` with `open` or `save` are refused before anything changes.
- Without `storyIndex`, nothing changes.

Also:
- the schema description and the description in `AddOnMain.cpp`;
- `Examples/ifc_file_operations.py` has an extra merge with `storyIndex: 0`. I added that call to its golden by hand, as the merge before it: `success: true`;
- Grasshopper: `IFCFileOperation` gets a `StoryIndex` input, **appended** as the last input (index 5) and optional. It has no default value, so an unconnected input keeps the old behaviour.

## Not possible: items 1–3 of #1616

I checked the Archicad 29 DevKit, as the bot's answer on the issue asked:
- There is only `ACAPI_IFC_GetIFCExportTranslatorsList`.
- `API_IOParams`, which the merge hands to the IFC add-on, and `API_FileOpenPars` have no field for an import translator.
- The `IFCInOutAPI` module only covers properties, assignments and export hooks.

So an import translator cannot be listed or chosen. I don't have the AC30 DevKit, so I did not check it.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS), 11/11

The project was saved before and reopened without saving afterwards.

| call | result |
|---|---|
| floor plan on story -1, merge with `storyIndex` 0 | IFC storeys on 0 and 1; afterwards story -1 is active again, floor plan |
| 3D window (story 1 active), merge with `storyIndex` 2 | IFC storeys on 2 and 3; afterwards the 3D window and story 1 are back |
| story 0 active, merge with `storyIndex` -1 | IFC storeys on -1 and 0; afterwards story 0 is active |
| `storyIndex` equal to the active story | IFC storeys on 0 and 1 |
| merge without `storyIndex` (story 1 active) | IFC storeys on 1 and 2, as before |
| `storyIndex` 99 | `storyIndex is out of range…`, nothing merged, active story unchanged |
| `storyIndex` with `open` / with `save` | `storyIndex is only valid with the merge method` |

Not checked:
- **The Grasshopper change**: I couldn't build it here, so the CI build check covers it.
- **The example against `TestProject.pla`**: I didn't run it.

title: Add ReindexLayers: move layers to new indices without losing their elements (#1388)
body:
Part of #1388: layers. parikshit99 handed it over in the issue. It follows the move-then-delete plan posted there.

## What `ReindexLayers` does

Archicad has no API call that renumbers an attribute, and deleting a layer deletes every element on it. So for each requested layer (`attributeId`, `newIndex`):

1. **Checks:**
   - `newIndex` must be free;
   - index 1 (the Archicad Layer) can't be moved or used;
   - an element from a hotlinked module blocks the move before anything changes.
2. **Fill the gaps:** every free index below `newIndex` gets a temporary placeholder layer, because Archicad gives a new layer the lowest free index. A layer that needs more than `maxPlaceholders` (default 1000) is refused before anything changes, so a typo like `60000` can't freeze Archicad.
3. **Create the new layer** as a copy of the old one, on `newIndex`, then delete the placeholders. If Archicad puts the copy anywhere else, the move stops.
4. **Copy the state into every layer combination:** hidden, locked, wireframe and intersection group are copied from the old layer to the new one.
5. **Move the elements:** every element of the old layer goes to the new one, in the floor plan and in every section, elevation, interior elevation, detail, worksheet, 3D document, layout and master layout. While they move, the old layer is shown and unlocked.
6. **Scan again:** only when no element is left on the old layer anywhere are the tool defaults on that layer switched over and the old layer deleted.
7. **Finish:** the new layer gets the old name, flags and attribute folder.

**Rollback:** if an element can't be moved (locked, or not reserved in Teamwork), or anything is left after the move, everything for that layer is undone: the elements go back, and the copy and the placeholders are deleted (the copy only when it is empty). The old layer then keeps its id, index, flags and elements.

**Result:** per layer, either an error or:
- `attributeId`: the new layer's id;
- `oldIndex`, `newIndex`;
- `placeholders`: the number of temporary layers needed;
- `elements`: the moved elements;
- `toolDefaults`: the element types whose tool default was on the layer;
- `viewsToRebuild`: see below;
- `warnings`, only when restoring the name and flags or the move into the folder failed after the layer was already moved.

**`dryRun`** returns the same lists without changing anything, plus `blockedElements`.

**Undo:** the whole call is one undo step.

## Section elements (`API_SectElemID`)

Sections, elevations, interior elevations and 3D documents show model elements as section elements. Their layer can't be changed: `ACAPI_Element_Change` reports success but keeps the old layer. A rebuild recreates them from the element they show, on that element's layer. In the first test they were the only thing left on the old layer, so the check in step 6 stopped the move, as it should.

So section elements are not moved and are not counted in step 6. When the old layer is deleted they are deleted with it, and they come back on the new layer when the view is rebuilt:
- **Automatic rebuild:** Archicad does that when the view is opened, unless it is set to rebuild manually.
- **Rebuild from a script:** `viewsToRebuild` lists those views, so a script can rebuild them with `ChangeWindow` + `RebuildCurrentDatabase`.
- **Why the command doesn't rebuild them itself:** `ACAPI_Database_RebuildCurrentDatabase` did not recreate them, neither inside the undoable command nor in the background afterwards. It worked only with the view as the front window, and switching windows from the command would open every one of those views.

## Limits (also in the description)

- The new layer is a new attribute with a new id. Favorites that use the layer are not updated.
- Archicad keeps a layer's shown, locked and wireframe state **per open window**. The new layer gets the old one's state in the current window and in every layer combination, and starts shown and unlocked in the other open windows. Applying a layer combination sets it everywhere.
- Archicad 27 and newer, because before 27 layer combinations store their states differently. Archicad 25 and 26 return `APIERR_NOTSUPPORTED`.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS, German UI), 29/29

I used a project with 174 layers (highest index 600, 426 free indices), 57 layer combinations and layers in attribute folders. It was saved before and reopened without saving afterwards.

| case | result |
|---|---|
| wall layer (179 elements: walls, doors, objects; tool default Wall) to the first free index | moved; same name, flags, folder; state in all 57 combinations the same; Wall tool default on the new layer |
| same move: section elements | `viewsToRebuild` names the one section; after rebuilding it: 70 section elements on the new layer, 0 on the old one |
| hidden layer with 8 elements on master layouts, to highest index + 3 (428 placeholders) | moved, 7.2 s; still hidden; no placeholder left |
| hidden **and** locked layer (77 elements) | moved; still hidden and locked |
| layer with one locked element | error naming the locked elements; old layer unchanged (id, index, flags, folder, combinations, elements, tool defaults), no new layer |
| `newIndex` used by another layer | error naming that layer |
| `dryRun` to highest index + 3 | `placeholders`: 428 |
| the same with `maxPlaceholders: 10` | error naming the count, nothing changed |
| the Archicad Layer | error |
| `dryRun` over all 173 layers | 8.4 s, nothing changed |

Also:
- After all cases the project had 174 layers again, with no placeholder left.
- `Examples/reindex_layers.py` (new; creates its own layer and column and deletes them again) prints `Moved to the requested index: True` and `Column on the new layer: True`. It has no golden.

Not checked:
- **Teamwork:** not checked; reservation errors should take the rollback path.
- **Hotlinked elements:** only the check is there; the test project has no hotlinks.
- **Archicad's Undo** after the call.
- **The `warnings` path:** I couldn't make the rename or the folder move fail on purpose.
- **Archicad 27, 28, 30:** I didn't build or run those, so the CI build checks cover them.

Other attribute types (fills, surfaces, building materials, line types), as Kappa-lo asked in the issue, would need every reference rewritten and are not part of this PR.

title: SetProjectNotes: no longer duplicates architect and draftsmen (#1559)
body:
Fixes #1559.

## Cause

`architect` and `draftsmen` in the Project Notes are the full names of two Project Info persons (`CONTACT_*` and `CAD_TECHNICIAN_*`). Archicad keeps each as name parts: title prefix, given, middle and family name, title suffix.

`ACAPI_ProjectSetting_ChangeProjectNotes` writes the full name it gets into the **given name** and keeps the other parts. `SetProjectNotes` writes the whole struct back, as the API needs, so every write added a copy. Even a new name only got the old parts behind it.

This matches the field mapping thespatialist posted. I reproduced it on Archicad 29 with the released code:

| call | `architect` | `draftsmen` |
|---|---|---|
| start (prefix `Dr.` + middle name `Planer` / given `Ida` + family `Muster`) | `Dr. Planer` | `Ida Muster` |
| `{"notes": "x"}` | `Planer Planer` | `Ida Muster Muster` |
| then `{"architect": "Neu Name"}` | `Neu Name Planer` | `Ida Muster Muster Muster` |

## Change

`SetProjectNotes` reads the name parts (autotexts) before the write and sets them afterwards:
- **Not given, or unchanged:** a name that was not given, or was sent back unchanged (for example a whole `GetProjectNotes` result), gets its parts back exactly as they were.
- **New name:** it goes into the given name and the other parts are cleared, so `GetProjectNotes` returns exactly the text that was written. The parts can still be set one by one with `SetProjectInfoField`.
- **Comparison and characters:** whether a name changed is decided on the stored text. The new name is taken from the request, so non-ASCII names come out right; the project notes struct holds 8-bit text.

Also:
- the `architect`/`draftsmen` schema descriptions and the `SetProjectNotes` description;
- `Examples/project_notes.py` now prints that architect and draftsmen are unchanged after a write without them, and that the original notes are restored. It has no golden.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS, German UI), 8/8

The project was saved before and reopened without saving afterwards. Starting from the names above, `GetProjectInfoFields` was compared before and after each call:

| call | result |
|---|---|
| `{"notes": "x"}` | names unchanged; only `NOTES` changed |
| `{"notes": ""}` (second write) | nothing doubled; every field back as at the start |
| the whole `GetProjectNotes` result sent back | no field changed |
| `{"architect": "Neu Name"}` | reads `Neu Name`; given name `Neu Name`, prefix and middle name cleared; only `CONTACT_*` name fields changed; `draftsmen` unchanged |
| `{"architect": "Jürgen Müller-Weiß"}` | reads the same, also `CONTACT_FULLNAME` |
| then `{"notes": "y"}` | the name stays; only `NOTES` changed |
| `{"draftsmen": ""}` | `draftsmen` and `CAD_TECHNICIAN_FULLNAME` empty; `architect` unchanged |

The extended `Examples/project_notes.py` prints `Architect and draftsmen unchanged: True` and `Restored: True`.

Not checked:
- **Archicad 25–28 and 30:** not run here. The fix only touches the name parts that `ACAPI_AutoText_GetAutoTexts` lists, so a version without those ids is left as before.
- **Undo:** not tested. The name parts are set after the undoable step, so Undo may cover only the project notes.

title: Dimensions: textFrame on the creation commands, text settings in GetDimensionData (replaces #1593)
body:
Fixes #1592. Replaces #1593.

#1593 by the issue bot is stuck with `needs-maintainer`: every build failed on `API_NoteType::noteFrame`, and the bot could not look up the real member without the DevKit. This PR is its change on current `main` with the member fixed and tested in Archicad. #1593 can be closed when this one is merged.

## What it does

- **`textFrame` on the creation commands** (from #1593): `CreateAssociativeDimensions`, `CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection` and `CreateWallThicknessDimensions` take an optional boolean `textFrame`. It is applied with `textHeight` and `textPen` to `defNote`, which both creation paths copy into every witness point. Without it, the Dimension tool's setting is used.
- **The member name:** in the AC29 DevKit (`APIdefs_Elements.h`), the frame of `API_NoteType` is `bool frame` ("The note has frame"), next to `framePen`. #1593 used `noteFrame`, which doesn't exist. That one line is the only change to the bot's code.
- **New: read back in `GetDimensionData`.** Each witness point now also returns:
  - `textHeight` (`note.noteSize`, mm);
  - `textPen`;
  - `textFrame` (`note.frame`).

  The texts couldn't be read back so far (`GetDetailsOfElements` doesn't support dimensions). So a dimension's text settings can now be checked, and copied to a new dimension.
- **Schema, descriptions and examples:**
  - schema for the new witness point fields in `CommonSchemaDefinitions.json`, and the `GetDimensionData` description;
  - `Examples/create_dimensions_from_favorite.py` (from #1593) sets `textFrame` on the wall thickness dimension;
  - `Examples/get_dimension_data.py` prints the text settings and rebuilds the dimension with them, framed.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS, German UI), 7/7

The project was saved before and reopened without saving afterwards. Two walls were used; `GetDimensionData` read back each witness point.

| call | read back on every witness point |
|---|---|
| `CreateAssociativeDimensions`, `textFrame: true`, `textHeight: 4` | frame `true`, height 4 |
| same, `textFrame: false` | frame `false` |
| same without `textFrame` | the tool's setting (`false` in this project) |
| `CreateWallThicknessDimensions`, `textFrame: true` | frame `true` |
| `textFrame: "ja"` | rejected by the schema |

Also:
- `Examples/get_dimension_data.py`: `rebuilt dimension measures the same: True`, `rebuilt dimension texts are framed: True`.
- `Examples/create_dimensions_from_favorite.py`: `4 passed, 0 failed`.

Neither example has a golden.

Not checked:
- **`CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection`:** not run. It takes `textFrame` through the same `DimensionDefaults::Read` as the other two.
- **A tool default with a frame:** the project's Dimension tool has no frame, so "without `textFrame`" and `false` look the same here.
- **Archicad 25–28 and 30:** not run, so the CI builds cover them. `frame` is in the AC29 header; the bot's build log shows only `noteFrame` missing, so the member should exist in all versions.

## Added after review: the look of the dimension line

Asked for in the comments: `GetDimensionData` also returns `linePen`, the `marker` (`type` and `pen`) and `defaultWitnessForm` / `defaultWitnessVal`. Checked on Archicad 29 against the Dimension Settings dialog, 6/6: two favorites, a dimension already in the project, and `Examples/get_dimension_data.py`.

title: RenameNavigatorItem: also rename the Drawing of a Layout Book drawing item (replaces #1489)
body:
Fixes #1479. Replaces #1489.

#1489 by the issue bot is stuck with `needs-maintainer` and conflicts with `main`. Its review asked for one check in Archicad: is the Layout Book `DrawingItem` guid the guid of the Drawing element? On Archicad 29 it is **not**. So #1489 silently fell back to its old behaviour: the item was renamed, the Drawing was not, and it reported success. This PR keeps its approach and fixes how the Drawing is found.

## What links a Layout Book drawing item to its Drawing (Archicad 29)

I measured this with a temporary probe build:

| | value |
|---|---|
| `DrawingItem` guid | its own guid, not the Drawing element's guid |
| Drawing `drawingGuid` ("for identification by autotext") | a third guid, not the item's either |
| `API_NavigatorItem::db` of the drawing item | empty (`typeID` 0), `ACAPI_Window_GetDatabaseInfo` fails |
| parent item (`ACAPI_Navigator_GetNavigatorParentItem`) | the layout, with a valid layout database |
| item `sourceGuid` | **equals** the Drawing's `linkGuid` from `ACAPI_Drawing_GetDrawingLink` (the view it shows) |

## Change

`RenameNavigatorItem` with `newName` on a Layout Book drawing item renames the item, as before. It then also sets the Drawing's custom name (`nameType` CustomName), as renaming it in the Navigator does in Archicad.

**How the Drawing is found:** in the database of the item's parent layout, as the Drawing whose `linkGuid` is the item's `sourceGuid`.

**Two Drawings of the same view on one layout:**
- **Names differ:** the one whose custom name is the item's old name is taken.

**Unchanged:**
- A Drawing that is not found this way keeps its name, and the call succeeds as before. That covers an item without a `sourceGuid`, which I expect for images and PDFs but didn't test.
- Layouts and every other item are not affected.

**From #1489:**
- the description;
- the read-back check after the change (now with `strcmp` on the stored 8-bit name);
- the failure message when Archicad refuses the name;
- `Examples/rename_layout_book_drawing.py`, without its "guid of the item / guid of the Drawing" line, which suggested they belong together.

title: SetPropertyValueOfAttributes, clearer results of SetPropertyValuesOfAttributes (replaces #1365)
body:
Part 3 of #1318. Replaces #1365.

#1365 by the issue bot is stuck with `needs-maintainer`. Its builds are green; what was missing is the test in Archicad that its description and reviews ask for:
- all or nothing;
- `ACAPI_Attribute_ModifyPropertyValue` at runtime;
- the changed results of `SetPropertyValuesOfAttributes`.

This PR is its change on current `main` (part 1, #1333, is already there), tested on Archicad 29. #1365 can be closed when this one is merged.

## What it does (from #1365)

- **New `SetPropertyValueOfAttributes`:**
  - Input: `{"propertyId", "propertyValue": {"value"}, "attributeIds"}`; result: one `ExecutionResult`.
  - It sets one value on all given attributes in one undoable command, with `ACAPI_Attribute_ModifyPropertyValue` (AC27+) or `ACAPI_AttributeList_ModifyPropertyValue` (AC25–26).
  - If the property is not available for one of the attributes, no attribute is changed.
  - A value that can't be converted to the property's type is refused before anything is written.
- **`SetPropertyValuesOfAttributes`** still sets each value with `ACAPI_Attribute_SetProperty`, as on `main`. A failed entry no longer gets an empty result:
  - an unknown attribute gives `Attribute not found`;
  - a failed read gives `Failed to get property values for attribute`;
  - a property that isn't available for the attribute gives `The property is not available for the attribute`;
  - the same attribute and property given twice fail for the second entry.

## Changes against #1365

- **Version:** registered with `1.7.4`, the version `main` carries now (#1365 had 1.7.3).
- **Example:** `Examples/audit_building_material_properties.py` is merged with `main`'s version, which now has the `AddPropertyToAttributes`/`RemovePropertyFromAttributes` steps from part 4. The new `SetPropertyValueOfAttributes` step runs before the property is removed again: it sets `Audited` on the Building Materials that have the property and reads it back.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS, German UI), 11/11

The project was saved before and reopened without saving afterwards. It has 123 Building Materials:
- a text property that is available for 120 of them;
- an integer property and a single-choice list property, available for 94.

| call | result |
|---|---|
| `SetPropertyValueOfAttributes`, text value on the 120 Building Materials | success, all 120 read back the value |
| 5 Building Materials with the property + 1 without | failure *"no attribute was changed"*; the 5 keep their value |
| integer property, `"abc"` | failure *"cannot be converted"* |
| integer property, `"50"` on 94 | success, all read back 50 |
| list property, one of its values on 94 | success |
| list property, a value it doesn't have | failure *"cannot be converted"* |
| unknown attribute | `Attribute not found` |
| `SetPropertyValuesOfAttributes` with 2 valid entries, a repeated entry, a Building Material without the property and an unknown attribute | 2 values set; then *"given more than once"*, *"not available"*, `Attribute not found` |

The two examples ran in this project as a temporary copy, with an existing property in place of `Tapir Custom`:
- `audit_building_material_properties.py`: `SetPropertyValueOfAttributes` returned success, and every Building Material with the property read back `Audited`.
- `get_and_set_properties_for_attributes.py`: ran without errors.

Not checked:
- **The examples' golden outputs against `TestProject.pla`:** I didn't have the file here.
- **Undo** through Archicad.
- **Archicad 25–28 and 30:** not run. In particular `ACAPI_AttributeList_ModifyPropertyValue` on AC25–26 is only covered by the green builds of #1365.

title: Add SetMarkerLibraryPartOfElements: switch the marker of windows and doors (replaces #1383)
body:
Fixes #1382. Replaces #1383.

#1383 by the issue bot is stuck with `needs-maintainer` and conflicts with `main`. Its open point was a maintainer decision: any library part with the given name was accepted as a marker. It dropped its `typeID` filter because every marker part reports `APILib_ObjectID`. This PR is its command on current `main`, next to the newer `ChangeLibraryPartOfElements`, with a real marker check, tested on Archicad 29.

## What it does

`SetMarkerLibraryPartOfElements` changes which library part the marker of a window or door uses:

```json
{"elementsWithMarkerLibraryPart": [{"elementId": {"guid": "..."}, "libraryPartName": "Door Marker 27"}]}
```

From #1383:
- The new part is found by name.
- The marker gets the new part's default parameters; `SetMarkerParametersOfElements` changes them afterwards.
- The same part as now changes nothing.
- One `executionResult` per item.

## The marker check (new)

The library part has to be a marker for the opening's type:
- either Archicad's marker parent for windows or doors (`ACAPI_LibraryPart_GetMarkerParent`, the part Archicad itself uses as their marker ancestor);
- or a part derived from it (`ACAPI_LibraryPart_CheckLibPartSubtypeOf`).

Anything else is refused with *"'…' is not a marker library part for the Door of element …"*.

I measured the ancestry on Archicad 29:
- the doors' marker parent is the "Door Marker" library part, the parent of the default door stamp;
- the default window stamp derives from "Window Marker";
- an older door/window stamp from a previous library derives from "Label".

That's why a window stamp and that old stamp are refused for a door.

**AC25 and AC26:** they use the older names (`ACAPI_Goodies_GetMarkerParent`/`ACAPI_Goodies (APIAny_GetMarkerParentID, …)`, as in `ExtendedElementCommands.cpp`, and the same pattern for `CheckLibPartSubtypeOf`).

**Also changed:**
- registered with 1.7.4 (#1383 had 1.7.3);
- the `libraryPartName` description says which parts are accepted;
- `Examples/set_marker_library_part.py` from #1383, unchanged.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS, German UI), 12/12

The project was saved before and reopened without saving afterwards. It has 86 doors and 173 windows.

| call | result |
|---|---|
| door, the part it already uses | success, parameters unchanged |
| door → another door marker from a template library | success, `GetMarkerParametersOfElements` shows the new part |
| door → a chair group object, a section marker, a zone stamp | refused, marker unchanged |
| door → the default window stamp | refused (it derives from "Window Marker") |
| door → an older stamp derived from "Label" | refused |
| door → unknown name | *"Not found marker library part…"* |
| door back to its own stamp | success |
| window → a window marker from the template library | success |
| window → chair group | refused (*"…for the Window…"*) |
| a wall | *"…is not a window or a door…"* |

`Examples/set_marker_library_part.py` runs through: 259 of 259 openings succeed, no errors.

Not checked:
- **Archicad 25–28 and 30:** not run, so the CI builds cover them. In particular the AC25/26 names of the two library part functions.
- **Skylights:** `GetWindowOrDoorWithMarker` takes only windows and doors, as in #1383. I didn't try a skylight.

title: DeleteNavigatorItems: say why an item was not deleted (replaces #1419)
body:
Fixes #1418. Replaces #1419.

#1419 by the issue bot is stuck with `needs-maintainer` (8 reviews without a verdict) and conflicts with `main`. It had two parts:
- **The `MoveNavigatorItem` read-back:** `main` already has it, in a more thorough form, so it is left out here.
- **A clearer message in `DeleteNavigatorItems`:** that is this PR, extended with what I measured on Archicad 29.

## What Archicad 29 does

On `main`, every `APIERR_NOTSUPPORTED` is reported as *"Deleting layout subsets is not supported by the ArchiCAD API."*, and every other failure as *"Failed to delete navigator item."*. Measured in a project with 63 View Map folders, 53 layout subsets and a full Project Map:

| item | Archicad's result |
|---|---|
| layout subset | `APIERR_NOTSUPPORTED` (Tapir refuses it itself) |
| View Map folder that holds views or folders | `APIERR_NOTSUPPORTED` from `ACAPI_Navigator_DeleteNavigatorView` |
| empty View Map folder | deleted |
| Project Map index (TOC), schedule, story, section | another error (`APIERR_BADID`); nothing deleted |
| independent worksheet, layout | deleted |

So the "layout subsets" message also came for a folder. The issue saw that for folders and TOC items on Archicad 27. A folder can be deleted, it just has to be empty first.

## Change

Each case gets its own message:
- **Folder that isn't empty:** *"Archicad deletes a View Map folder only when it is empty: delete or move the views and folders in it first."*
- **Any other `APIERR_NOTSUPPORTED`** (layout subsets): *"Archicad does not support deleting this type of navigator item (SubSetItem) through its API."* This is #1419's message, with the type.
- **A Project Map item other than an independent worksheet or detail:** *"Project Map items cannot be deleted (ScheduleItem); only independent worksheets and details can."*
- **Everything else:** as before.

The command's description now lists these cases too.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS, German UI), 9/9

The project was saved before and reopened without saving afterwards.

| call | result |
|---|---|
| View Map folder with views in it | folder message; folder still there |
| empty View Map folder | deleted |
| layout subset | message naming `SubSetItem` |
| Project Map TOC item, schedule, story, section | Project Map message with the type; item still there |
| independent worksheet | deleted |
| layout | deleted |

Not checked:
- **Archicad 25–28 and 30:** not run, so the CI builds cover them. The issue's Archicad 27 result for TOC items (`APIERR_NOTSUPPORTED`) gets the type message there.
- **Teamwork:** not checked. Its existing message for an item that was not deleted is unchanged.

title: CreateStairs: landings and winders per baseline edge and point
body:
Fixes #1628.

`CreateStairs` can now say which baseline edge is a landing and which turn is a landing or winder turn. So a U-shaped stair gets a real half landing. Until now Archicad decided the segments itself: on the issue's U baseline it put steps along the short middle edge.

The issue bot left this for a maintainer: the array sizes and index base were unknown, and wrong guesses could crash Archicad. I measured them on Archicad 29, then built and tested the input path.

## What Archicad 29 stores (measured)

I added a read-back to `GetDetailsOfElements` first and read stairs that Archicad had filled in itself:

| | value |
|---|---|
| `stairBaseLine.edgeData`, `vertexData` | `nCoords + 1` entries each, slot 0 unused, like `coords`; entry i belongs to point i, edge i runs from point i to point i + 1 |
| derived `segmentType` | `APIST_StepsSegment` on every edge, also on the short middle edge of a U |
| derived `turnType` | `APIST_LandingTurn` on every point, the first and last included |
| derived winder settings | `winderStepNumBackward/Forward` 1, `innerWidthOffsetType` Min, `numOfWindersType` Min, `dividedLandingNumOfWindersType` Optimal, `dividedLandingFixedNumOfSteps` 2, `winderType` SIP |
| `currLandingStartEdgeOffset`/`EndEdgeOffset` | calculated by Archicad; an input value is overwritten |
| `minLandingStartEdgeOffset`/`EndEdgeOffset` | kept as given; the calculated offset is at least this much |

**Why #444 failed:** it filled every edge as steps and left every turn at `APIST_NoTurn`. With a landing or winder turn at each inner point, Archicad accepts filled arrays. Winder turns also need the winder settings: left at 0, every winder failed with `-2130313215`.

## Change

**`CreateStairs`, two new optional arrays per `stairsData` item:**
- **`baseLineEdges`:** one item per edge, `{"segmentType": "Flight" | "Landing" | "DividedLanding"}`.
- **`baseLineVertices`:** one item per point:
  - `turnType`: `"None" | "Landing" | "Winder" | "DividedLanding"`;
  - optionally `minLandingStartEdgeOffset` and `minLandingEndEdgeOffset`, to make a landing longer.

  This follows the correction in the issue thread: the offsets belong to the vertex, and only the minimal ones are input.

**When the arrays are used:**
- Only when one of them is given are `edgeData`/`vertexData` filled, in the measured layout. Without them nothing changes, and Archicad still derives the arrays (#444).
- Edges that aren't given are flights. Points that aren't given get no turn at the ends and a landing turn inside.
- A length mismatch is refused before anything is allocated.

**`GetDetailsOfElements`:** stairs now also return `baseLineEdges` and `baseLineVertices`, aligned with `baseLinePoints`. They include the calculated and the minimal landing offsets.

**Other files:**
- **Example:** `Examples/create_stairs_with_landings.py`: a U stair with a half landing, the same with a longer landing, and an L stair with winders.
- **Version check:** none needed. The fields and enums are already in the older DevKit headers I checked, so no gate.

The issue's U case: baseline (2520,24250) → (5400,24250) → (5400,24490) → (2520,24490), "on the left". `CreateStairs` places the baseline at the stair's centre (the tool default), so I used the centre line of the same stair: two 1.15 m flights with the 0.24 m well, 18 risers of 153.8 mm.

```json
{"baseLinePoints": [{"x": 0, "y": 0}, {"x": 3.455, "y": 0}, {"x": 3.455, "y": 1.39}, {"x": 0, "y": 1.39}],
 "baseLineEdges": [{"segmentType": "Flight"}, {"segmentType": "Landing"}, {"segmentType": "Flight"}],
 "baseLineVertices": [{"turnType": "None"}, {"turnType": "Landing"}, {"turnType": "Landing"}, {"turnType": "None"}],
 "zCoordinate": 0, "flightWidth": 1.15, "riserHeight": 0.1538, "treadDepth": 0.24, "totalHeight": 2.7684}
```

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS, German UI), 12/12

The project was saved before and reopened without saving afterwards. I checked each stair in the 3D window.

| call | result |
|---|---|
| U baseline without the arrays | created as before; read back as Flight ×3, Landing ×4; steps along the middle edge |
| U with Flight/Landing/Flight, landing turns | created; one flat half landing across the turn |
| the same with `minLandingStartEdgeOffset`/`minLandingEndEdgeOffset` 0.6 | min offsets read back 0.6, calculated 0.917 and 0.6; landing visibly longer |
| U with only `baseLineEdges` | turns None/Landing/Landing/None |
| L with a winder turn | created with winders |
| L with a landing turn | created with a landing |
| U with two winder turns | not created, `-2130313215` like any invalid stair; Archicad keeps running |
| straight stair, None/None | created |
| 2 edges or 3 points for a 4-point baseline | refused with the length message |
| unknown `turnType` | refused by the schema |

`Examples/create_stairs_with_landings.py` runs through and prints the three stairs' edges and turns.

Not checked:
- **`DividedLanding`:** a U with divided landing turns and a DividedLanding middle edge is created. Its 3D looked odd: a wedge sticks out at the turn. I didn't compare it with one drawn in the UI. It is passed through like the other values.
- **`ModifyStairs` (#824) and `SolveStairBaseline`:** they don't take the arrays yet. `SolveStairBaseline`'s schema refuses them, and it still fills the arrays its own way.
- **Archicad 25–28 and 30:** not run, so the CI builds cover them.

**Separately:** `SolveStairBaseline` on the straight stair of its own example (`(0,0)` → `(0,5)`, `totalHeight` 3.0, `flightWidth` 1.2) closed Archicad 29 here. It did the same with this branch's change set aside, so it's on `main`, not caused by this PR. I'll look at it separately.

This branch includes the build fix from #1647, because `main` doesn't compile without it; that commit drops out once #1647 is merged.

title: SolveStairBaseline: run the stair solver inside an undoable command
body:
Follow-up to #1558 and #1560: `SolveStairBaseline` still crashed Archicad 29.

#1560 fills `stairBaseLine.edgeData`/`vertexData` before the solver runs. On current `main` (with #1560), `SolveStairBaseline` still closed Archicad 29 for the straight stair of its own example (`Examples/solve_stair_baseline.py`, `(0,0)` → `(0,5)`) and for both inputs from #1558. The memo isn't the cause.

## What I measured (Archicad 29, macOS)

I added a temporary step log to the command, written to a file before and after each call. It always stopped right before `ACAPI_HierarchicalEditing_SolveStair` returned.

| attempt | result |
|---|---|
| #1560's fill (nCoords edge entries, no turns) | crash |
| fill in the layout Archicad itself stores (nCoords + 1 entries, landing turns, its winder settings; read back from created stairs for #1628) | crash |
| the same plus a walking line | crash |
| **the complete memo of a stair Archicad had created itself** (`ACAPI_Element_GetMemo`, `APIMemoMask_All`: baseline, walking line, both boundaries) | **crash** |
| that memo, solver called inside `ACAPI_CallUndoableCommand` | `Correct`, no crash |
| the memo `SolveStairBaseline` builds, without any fill, inside `ACAPI_CallUndoableCommand` | answers for every case, no crash |

So the solver crashes when it is called outside an undoable command, whatever the memo holds.

## Change

- **Undoable command:** `ACAPI_HierarchicalEditing_SolveStair` now runs inside `ACAPI_CallUndoableCommand`. The command returns `APIERR_CANCEL`, so nothing is changed or put on the undo stack. If the command doesn't run, the item fails instead of reporting `NotSolved`.
- **The #1560 fill is removed**, because it wasn't the cause. The solver now gets the same memo `CreateStairs` creates from, as the command's comment always said.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS, German UI), 15/15

The project was saved before the `CreateStairs` part and reopened without saving afterwards.

| call | result |
|---|---|
| the example's straight stair `(0,0)` → `(0,5)` | `Correct`, Archicad keeps running |
| the same at x = 400 | `Correct` |
| #1558's straight stair `(110,0)` → `(114.2,0)`, 16 risers | `Correct` |
| #1558's 1 m case `(110,5)` → `(111,5)` | `Correct` |
| the example's L | `Correct` |
| L with riser and tread depth given | `Correct` |
| a U (3.5 / 2.4 / 3.5 m) | structured error `-2130313215` *"Failed to solve the stair baseline."*, Archicad keeps running |
| number of stairs before and after the solver calls | unchanged; nothing is created |
| `CreateStairs` with each solved baseline | created |

`Examples/solve_stair_baseline.py` runs through.

Not checked:
- **Windows, Archicad 27, 28 and 30:** not run, so the CI builds cover them. #1558 was on Windows.
- **The solver's verdicts:** the 1 m case comes back `Correct` although 16 treads of 0.28 m don't fit. The solver seems to check the baseline shape, not whether the steps fit. I didn't change that.

This branch includes the build fix from #1647, because `main` doesn't compile without it; that commit drops out once #1647 is merged.

title: `SetLayoutSettings`: allow changing the master layout of an existing layout
body:
`CreateLayout` accepts a master (by id or name) when creating a layout, but there is no command to change the master of an existing layout. `SetLayoutSettings` has size, margins, numbering and `showMasterBelow`, but no master reference.

Use case: a new master layout was created with the API; all existing layouts of a subset should be switched to it.

Proposal: add `masterNavigatorItemId` / `masterLayoutName` to `LayoutSettingsData`.

Related: #1423, #1498.
author: cichym

title: `CreateLayout`: option to exclude the new layout from numbering (and document that custom numbers still shift the sequence)
body:
Steps:
1. A subset has layouts numbered `PK-01 … PK-09` (custom ID prefix `PK`).
2. `CreateLayout` with `parentNavigatorItemId` = the subset and `layoutParameters: {customLayoutNumbering: true, customLayoutNumber: "PK-03N"}`.

Result: the new layout is inserted at the top of the subset and every following layout is renumbered (`PK-01` became `PK-03`, and so on).

Workaround: `SetLayoutSettings` with `doNotIncludeInNumbering: true` and `MoveNavigatorItem` to the end.

Proposal: accept `doNotIncludeInNumbering` in `CreateLayout`'s `layoutParameters`, and/or insert the new layout at the end of the parent by default. Please document the numbering behaviour.
author: cichym

title: `GetAutoTextKeys`: list the autotext keys for Project Info, Layout, Drawing and View (only element property keys are returned)
body:
`GetAutoTextKeys` (also with `elementId` of a Text placed on a Master Layout) returns only element property keys (`PROPERTY-<guid>`). Project Info keys are discoverable only via `GetProjectInfoFields` (`PROJECTNAME`, `autotext-CLIENT-1`, …), and layout keys (`LAYOUTNAME`, `LAYOUTID`) are not listed at all.

They do work when typed as `<KEY>` in `CreateTexts`/`ModifyTexts` (read-back resolves e.g. `<SITEADDRESS1>, <SITECITY>` to `<street>, <city>`; on a master `<LAYOUTNAME>` reads back as `#Nazwa arkusza`), but this had to be found by trial and error.

Proposal:
- return all autotext categories (Project Info, Layout/Master, Drawing, View, Date, Revision) with name and key
- on Text read, expose that a run contains an autotext reference (currently `effectProtected` stays false)

Related: #1096, #1166, #1168.
author: cichym

title: `CreateDrawings`: resulting `pos` differs from the given `position`, `MoveElements` moves the clip polygon with the drawing, and there is no `ModifyDrawings`
body:
Steps:
1. `CreateDrawings` with `position = (-0.000575, -9.252056)`, `drawingScale = 0.01`, a `clipPolygon` in layout coordinates.
2. `GetDetailsOfElements` returns `pos = (0.249606, -18.497868)` for that drawing (offset about `(+0.25, -9.25)` m), apparently caused by the stored zoom box of the source view. The meaning of `position` is not documented (model origin vs. drawing box origin).
3. `MoveElements` on the drawing succeeds and moves `pos` and `clipPolygon` together, so the drawing cannot be repositioned inside its clip.

Workaround: delete and recreate with a corrected `position`.

Proposal: document `position`, accept an option "position of the model origin", and add `ModifyDrawings` (pos, clipPolygon, scale, name) so the clip and the content can be changed independently.

Related: #1476, #1477.
author: cichym

title: `Get2DBoundingBoxes` returns error 7203 for Hatch, Text, Drawing and PolyLine

title: `GetElementsByType`: filter by layer (and story) and return them in the list
body:
The element lists return only guids. To find the ~50 polylines on one layer among 400 (mostly hotlinked site data) I had to fetch the layer of each element in separate calls.

Proposal: optional `layerIndex` / `layerName` and `floorIndex` filters; flag or filter for hotlink content (`hotlinkId` is returned only in `GetDetailsOfElements`).
author: cichym

title: OpenProject: say that unsaved changes are discarded without asking
body:
Part of #1381.

The issue asked for a `hasUnsavedChanges` field in `GetProjectInfo` and whether `OpenProject` silently discards changes. The issue bot left both open: it couldn't check the DevKit, and a guessed flag would be worse than none. I checked both on Archicad 29.

## `hasUnsavedChanges`: not reliable, so not added

The DevKit has no query for unsaved changes. The only candidate is `API_ProjectInfo::modiStamp` ("Modification stamp of project"). I built a temporary version that recorded it on Archicad's project events (`APINotify_Open`, `APINotify_Save`, …), logged every event with the stamp, and compared it in `GetProjectInfo`.

| step (no change in between unless stated) | `modiStamp` |
|---|---|
| reading it twice | unchanged |
| `APINotify_Open` and `APINotify_AllInputFinished` | same value |
| right after opening, no further event | +7,700 to +9,400 |
| `ChangeWindow` to the floor plan | +3,573 |
| zoom | +6 |
| `APINotify_Save`, then reading again | +3 |
| drawing one polyline | +92 |
| selecting it / deselecting | +2 / +9 |

So there is no point after opening or saving where the stamp settles: the flag would say "unsaved" almost always. Ordinary changes and view changes look the same. `APINotify_ChangeProjectDB` and `APINotify_ChangeWindow` didn't fire at all for these changes made through the API. I didn't add the field. That matches the bot's concern that a guessed flag can mislead.

## `OpenProject`: discards without asking, now said in its description

The DevKit states it for `ACAPI_ProjectOperation_Open` (and `NewProject`): *"If the plan is not saved, any modifications made will be lost."* On Archicad 25–28 `OpenProject` also sets `enableSaveAlert = false`; Archicad 29 has no such field and behaves the same.

`NewProject`'s description already says *"The unsaved changes of the open project are discarded, as with OpenProject."*, but `OpenProject`'s own description said nothing. It now reads:

> Opens the given project. The unsaved changes of the open project are discarded without asking: Archicad has no query for them, so call SaveProject first when they must be kept.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS, German UI), 5/5

The project was saved first, so only the test changes were discarded.

| call | result |
|---|---|
| draw a polyline, don't save | it exists |
| `OpenProject` with the same file | success after 14 s, no dialog |
| the polyline | gone |
| draw another one, `NewProject` | success, no dialog, new untitled project |
| `OpenProject` back | the second polyline is gone too |

Not checked:
- **`CloseProject` and `QuitArchicad`:** I didn't test them with unsaved changes; the DevKit says nothing about them.
- **Archicad 25–28 and 30:** not run.

This branch includes the build fix from #1647, because `main` doesn't compile without it; that commit drops out once #1647 is merged.

title: Section dimensioning: Opening preset, target database for creation commands, elevation-mode dimensions
body:
Follow-up to #1607. With `GetSectionElements` we can now dimension walls and slabs in section views fully automatically. Three gaps remain before our wall-elevation drawings can be produced without any manual step (Tapir 1.7.3, Archicad 29 HUN build 5101):

1. Opening (Opening tool) preset for `CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection`

Our wall openings are `Opening` elements. `GetSectionElements` lists them (`ownerElementType: "Opening"`), but `DoorWindowWallHoleCorners` rejects them ("requires a door or window section element"), and we could not find witness codes for opening edges with `CreateAssociativeDimensions` (dimensions created with guessed codes are dropped immediately). Request: an Opening preset (e.g. `OpeningCorners` / `OpeningEdges`: left/right edges for horizontal chains, bottom/top for vertical chains), or documentation of the witness codes for Opening section elements.

2. Target database (view) for creation commands

`CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection`, `CreateAssociativeDimensions`, `CreateTexts`, `CreatePolylines`, `CreateLevelDimensions` always create in the frontmost window. Read commands (`GetElementsByType`, `GetSectionElements`) already accept `databases`. Request: an optional `databaseId` on the creation commands (the API seems to allow switching the current database without UI), or a command to open/activate a navigator item. Then a whole set of wall elevations can be created and dimensioned in one run, while the user keeps working on the floor plan.

3. Elevation-mode linear dimensions (from #1607, point 2)

If a maintainer can let `favoriteName` or the tool defaults decide the dimension appearance (instead of forcing `APIApp_Normal`), or add an explicit parameter, our level marks in sections could be associative too.

We are happy to test builds on real projects (hundreds of wall elevations per project). Thank you!

title: Shell support in GetDetailsOfElements and a ModifyShells command
body:
GetDetailsOfElements currently returns "error": "Not yet supported element type" for Shell
elements, and there is no command to modify them.

Request:
1. Support Shell in GetDetailsOfElements, returning at least structureType (Basic/Composite),

2. A ModifyShells command accepting structureType, buildingMaterialId and compositeId per

Use case: scripts that read or change the structure of construction elements in bulk
currently have to skip shells.

title: CreateDrawings: a clipPolygon no longer moves the drawing's content
body:
Fixes #1654.

`CreateDrawings` with a `clipPolygon` put the Drawing's content somewhere other than `position`. This is the offset from the issue. The issue bot asked for measurements before documenting or fixing anything; I measured it on Archicad 29 and fixed it.

## What Archicad 29 does (measured)

I created Drawings of a floor plan and a section on a layout and read them back with `GetDetailsOfElements`.

| case | stored `pos` |
|---|---|
| no `clipPolygon` | exactly `position`: the lower left corner of the Drawing |
| with `clipPolygon` | `position − scale · R(angle) · clipMin`, where clipMin is the lower left corner of the clip polygon's bounding box |
| with `clipPolygon` and `modelOffset` | as above, plus `scale · R(angle) · drawingScale · modelOffset` |

The clip polygon itself stays where it is given, in layout coordinates. So the content moved by `clipMin` against the clip. With a clip at (0.3, 0.42), the clip window showed nothing at all.

Measured examples (position (0, 0)):
- a clip from (0.1, 0.1): `pos` (−0.1, −0.1);
- the same with `scale` 2: (−0.2, −0.2);
- the same with `angle` 90°: (0.1, −0.1).

Further findings:
- **What `pos` means for a clipped Drawing:** the point where the source view's origin lands. To check this, I drew a cross at the project origin in the floor plan. With the fix, the cross sits exactly at `position`, in the middle of the clip window, also with `scale` 2 and 30°. In a section the origin is level 0, so a section with a basement has its content 3.6 m × 1:100 above the lower edge.
- **`drawingScale` is ignored:** 0.02 came back as 0.005, the scale of the view. The DevKit marks `API_DrawingType::drawingScale` "output only".
- **`modelOffset`:**
  - It is ignored without a clip.
  - With a clip it is in model meters: 1 m moves `pos` by 5 mm at 1:200.
  - When another Drawing was created later, Archicad sometimes recalculated an existing Drawing's `pos` without the modelOffset part, while `modelOffset` itself stayed.
- **`ChangeDrawingLink` moved clipped Drawings:** it passes the old `pos` back in as `position`, so every relink shifted the Drawing by its clip corner. Measured: (0.945, −0.08) → (0.845, −0.18).

## Change

- **`CreateDrawings`:** with a `clipPolygon`, `clipMin` (times scale, rotated by angle) is added to `pos` before `ACAPI_Element_Create`. Archicad takes it off again, so `pos` is `position`. Without a clip nothing changes.
- **`ChangeDrawingLink`:** for a clipped Drawing it also takes the model offset part off the old `pos`, because Archicad adds it again. The new Drawing gets the old `pos` when both sources have the same scale.
- **Descriptions:**
  - `CreateDrawings`: `position` with and without a clip, `drawingScale` ignored, `modelOffset` in model meters and only used with a clip.
  - Shared schema: `pos`, `modelOffset` and `drawingScale` in the Drawing details and settings.
- **Example:** `Examples/test_drawing_clip.py` now checks that `pos` is the given position.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS, German UI), 12/12

The project was saved first and reopened without saving afterwards.

| call | result |
|---|---|
| floor plan without clip, position (0.3, 0.2) | `pos` (0.3, 0.2), as before |
| floor plan with clip (0.42…0.58, 0.24…0.36), position (0.5, 0.3) | `pos` (0.5, 0.3); before the fix this was position − clip corner |
| clip read back | as given |
| with clip, `scale` 2, `angle` 30° | `pos` = position |
| section with clip | `pos` = position |
| with clip and `modelOffset` (1, 0) | `pos` = position + (0.005, 0), Archicad's own offset |
| `drawingScale` 0.02 | ignored, 0.005 |
| `ChangeDrawingLink`, clipped | `pos` and clip unchanged |
| `ChangeDrawingLink`, clipped with `modelOffset` | `pos` unchanged |
| `ChangeDrawingLink`, not clipped | `pos` unchanged, as before |
| `SetDetailsOfElements` `pos` on a clipped Drawing | set exactly, as before |

`Examples/test_drawing_clip.py` runs through.

Not checked:
- **Which part of a section is its origin in x:** I only measured the vertical offset.
- **Hidden state after a `modelOffset`:** once a clipped Drawing with a non-zero `modelOffset` has been created in a session, later clipped Drawings got an extra offset of about that `modelOffset` (minus the drawing scale part), even with `modelOffset` 0. The values the API reads didn't show it. I couldn't find what holds it, so this PR doesn't change it.
- **Windows, Archicad 25–28 and 30:** not run, so the CI builds cover them.

@cichym the formula above should explain your numbers: `pos − position` was about (0.25, −9.25), so your clip polygon's lower left corner was probably around (−0.25, 9.25). If not, the hidden state after a `modelOffset` may be involved.

This branch includes the build fix from #1647, because `main` doesn't compile without it; that commit drops out once #1647 is merged.

title: Dimensions: appearance (Cumulative, Baseline, Elevation) and elevationOrigin on the creation commands
body:
Part of #1662 (point 3).

The dimension creation commands always made linear dimensions, so level marks in sections couldn't be associative. The issue bot left two options for a maintainer: let the favorite or the tool defaults decide, which would change existing scripts, or add an explicit parameter. It couldn't check the values against `API_AppearID` in the DevKit. I added the explicit parameter and tested it on Archicad 29.

## Change

`CreateAssociativeDimensions`, `CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection` and `CreateWallThicknessDimensions` take two new optional fields per item:
- **`appearance`:** `"Linear"`, `"Cumulative"`, `"Baseline"` or `"Elevation"`. These are the four values of `API_AppearID` (`APIApp_Normal`, `APIApp_Cumu`, `APIApp_CumuSv`, `APIApp_Elev`) under the names the Dimension Settings use. [Graphisoft's help](https://help.graphisoft.com/AC/21/INT/AC21Help/Appendix_Tools/Appendix_Tools-66.htm) says Baseline measures the same distances as Cumulative without marking the zero point. The created dimensions show exactly that: `APIApp_Cumu` has the origin circle, `APIApp_CumuSv` doesn't.
- **`elevationOrigin`:** the existing `DimensionOrigin` of `CreateLevelDimensions` (`"ProjectZero"`, `"ReferenceLevel1"`, `"ReferenceLevel2"`, `"StoredOrigin"` or `"Altitude"`), read and written with its helpers `ParseDimensionOriginString` / `DimensionOriginToString`. It sets the level an Elevation dimension measures from. Without it, the origin of `favoriteName` or the tool defaults is kept.
- **Unknown values:** an unknown `elevationOrigin` gets an error item (*"Unknown 'elevationOrigin' value: …"*), as `CreateLevelDimensions` does for `origin`, because the schema doesn't check an enum behind `$ref`. The same applies to an unknown `appearance`; the schema already rejects that one.

Without `appearance` the dimensions stay linear, whatever the favorite or the tool defaults say, so existing scripts are not affected. `GetDimensionData` now also returns `appearance` and `elevationOrigin`.

Other files:
- **Example:** `Examples/get_section_elements.py` adds the slab chain a second time as level marks.
- **Descriptions:** the two associative commands' descriptions mention the types.
- **Version check:** none added. The fields are old ones (`APIDimOrigin_Altitude` is marked "New in API 16"); the CI builds for Archicad 25–30 check the rest.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS, German UI), 13/13

The project was saved first and reopened without saving afterwards. The chain is all slabs of a section, with `SlabCompositeFaces`.

| call | result |
|---|---|
| section chain without `appearance` | Linear, as before: 0.30, 3.15, 0.25, 3.75 … |
| `Cumulative` | running totals 0 … 14.30, origin circle |
| `Baseline` | the same totals, no origin circle |
| `Elevation`, `ProjectZero` | level marks −3.85, −3.55, −0.40, −0.15, 3.60 … 10.45; span = the Cumulative total |
| `Elevation`, `Altitude` / `StoredOrigin` / `ReferenceLevel1` | origin stored and read back |
| `elevationOrigin` `SeaLevel` (an earlier name) | error item *"Unknown 'elevationOrigin' value: SeaLevel"*, nothing created |
| unknown `appearance` | refused by the schema |
| `CreateAssociativeDimensions`, 3 static points, `Cumulative` | 0 / 2 / 5 |
| `CreateWallThicknessDimensions`, `Baseline` | created, Baseline |
| `CreateWallThicknessDimensions` without `appearance` | Linear, as before |

`Examples/get_section_elements.py` runs through.

Not checked:
- **Other origins:** `Altitude`, `StoredOrigin` and `ReferenceLevel1` showed the same values as `ProjectZero` in this project. I couldn't tell whether its sea level and reference level 1 are at project zero, so I only checked that the origin is stored.
- **Point 1 (an Opening preset):** not in this PR. It needs the witness codes of a dimension placed by hand, as the bot said.
- **Windows, Archicad 25–28 and 30:** not run.

This branch includes the build fix from #1647, because `main` doesn't compile without it; that commit drops out once #1647 is merged.

title: FilterElements: fromHotlink and hotlinkIds criteria
body:
Fixes #1657.

The issue's layer and story filters already exist in `FilterElements`, as the issue bot showed. What was missing is a way to leave out the elements that came in through placed hotlinks (in the issue, hotlinked site data). The bot proposed a `hotlinkIds` or `excludeHotlinked` criterion and left the decision to a maintainer. This PR adds both, as two optional criteria.

## Change

`FilterElements` takes two new optional criteria. Like the layer, story and type criteria, they are checked on the element header (`API_Elem_Head::hotlinkGuid`, *"the identifier of the hotlink instance the element belongs to"*):
- **`fromHotlink`:** `true` keeps only the elements from a placed hotlink, `false` only the project's own elements.
- **`hotlinkIds`:** keeps the elements of the given placed hotlink instances. These are the `hotlinkId` field of `GetDetailsOfElements`, and the instances `GetHotlinks` lists.

Both combine with the other criteria. So the issue's case is one call:

```json
{"elements": [...], "fromHotlink": false, "elementTypes": ["Polyline"], "layerIndices": [12]}
```

`IsEditable` is no substitute, as the bot already warned. In the test it kept only 627 of the 731 own elements, because it also drops elements on locked layers, and in Teamwork elements that are not reserved.

Other files:
- **Example:** `Examples/filter_hotlinked_elements.py` compares both criteria with the `hotlinkId` field of `GetDetailsOfElements`.
- **Description:** the command's description mentions the new criteria.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS, German UI), 11/11

The project was saved first. Two instances of another project were placed as hotlinks (636 elements each), and the project was reopened without saving afterwards.

| call | result |
|---|---|
| `fromHotlink: true` | 1272 elements, exactly those with a `hotlinkId` |
| `fromHotlink: false` | 731 elements, exactly the own ones |
| both together | 1272 + 731 = all 2003 |
| `hotlinkIds` with instance 1 | its 636 elements only |
| `hotlinkIds` with both instances | 1272 |
| `fromHotlink: false` + `elementTypes: ["Wall"]` | the 146 own walls |
| unknown hotlink id | empty |
| instance 1 + `fromHotlink: false` | empty |
| no criterion at all | the existing error, unchanged |
| `filters: ["IsEditable"]` | 627, no hotlinked elements, unchanged |

`Examples/filter_hotlinked_elements.py` runs through, all comparisons match.

Not checked:
- **Nested hotlinks:** a hotlink inside a hotlink. The DevKit calls `hotlinkGuid` "the hotlink instance the element belongs to"; I didn't check whether that is the inner or the outer instance.
- **Windows, Archicad 25–28 and 30:** not run, so the CI builds cover them.

This branch includes the build fix from #1647, because `main` doesn't compile without it; that commit drops out once #1647 is merged.
