title: CreateHotlinkInstances: place on the Archicad layer when the default layer was deleted
body:
`CreateHotlinkInstances` without `layerIndex` failed in one of my projects for every node, with only *"Failed to place the hotlink instance"* (`APIERR_BADINDEX`). There's no issue for it yet.

## Cause (measured on Archicad 29)

I logged the element before `ACAPI_Element_Create`: the hotlink tool's default layer was index 25, and the project no longer has that layer (`ACAPI_Attribute_Get` answers `APIERR_BADINDEX`). A tool default can still name a layer that was deleted later. With any existing `layerIndex` the same call worked. The story (`floorIndex`) had no influence.

## Change

- **`CreateHotlinkInstances`, without `layerIndex`:** when the default layer no longer exists, the instance goes onto the built-in Archicad layer (index 1), which cannot be deleted. When the default layer exists, nothing changes.
- **`CreateHotlinkInstances` and `ChangeHotlinkInstances`, with a `layerIndex` that is not a layer of the project:** refused with *"layerIndex N is not a layer of the project."* instead of the bare error.
- **Descriptions:** both `layerIndex` descriptions say this.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS, German UI), 8/8

The project's default hotlink layer had been deleted. It was saved first and reopened without saving afterwards.

| call | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| `CreateHotlinkInstances` without `layerIndex` | `APIERR_BADINDEX` | placed on layer 1 |
| only `floorIndex` | `APIERR_BADINDEX` | placed |
| `layerIndex` 2 | placed | placed on layer 2 |
| `layerIndex` 999 | "Failed to place the hotlink instance" | "layerIndex 999 is not a layer of the project." |
| `layerIndex` 25 (the deleted layer) | "Failed to place …" | "layerIndex 25 is not a layer of the project." |
| `ChangeHotlinkInstances` `layerIndex` 999 | "Failed to change …" | refused with the message, layer unchanged |
| `ChangeHotlinkInstances` `layerIndex` 2 | moved | moved |
| `Examples/hotlink_instances.py` with `TAPIR_HOTLINK_SOURCE` | placement failed | places, changes |

Not checked:
- **A project whose default hotlink layer exists:** that code path is unchanged.
- **Windows, Archicad 25–28 and 30:** not run, so the CI builds cover them.

**Separately:** the last step of `Examples/hotlink_instances.py`, `DeleteElements` on the instance, failed here with *"Failed to delete the element."*. It failed the same way for an instance placed with an explicit, editable `layerIndex`, so this PR doesn't cause it. The CI example never reaches that step, because `TestProject.pla` has no hotlink source set. I'll look at it in a separate PR.

This branch includes the build fix from #1647, because `main` doesn't compile without it; that commit drops out once #1647 is merged.

title: API Coverage: no longer run on pull requests
body:
API Coverage ran on `pull_request_target` only to refresh the coverage checklist. As a check on a pull request it tested nothing of the change, and with `cancel-in-progress` on one shared group it is cancelled by every newer event. So pull requests carried a cancelled or skipped `update` check and never showed all green.

## Changes
- `api_coverage.yml`: the `pull_request_target` trigger is removed. It still runs on pushes to `main`, published releases, issue events, hourly and by hand. The hourly run still reads the open pull requests through the API, so "in an open PR" items are updated within the hour instead of within minutes. Header comment updated.
- `claude_auto_merge.yml`: comment only. It keeps ignoring API Coverage, because heads pushed before this still carry the old check.
- `CLAUDE.md`: the `api_coverage.yml` description is updated.

## Notes
- Pull request heads pushed before this merges keep their old cancelled `update` check until their next push.
- This touches `.github/`, so auto-merge leaves it to a maintainer.
- YAML parses; not run on Actions yet.

title: Add Get2DBoundingBoxes: 2D boxes of texts, hatches, drawings and polylines on any database
body:
Fixes #1655.

Graphisoft's `API.Get2DBoundingBoxes` refuses Hatch, Text, Drawing and PolyLine with error 7203. Those are the elements placed on layouts and masters, so their placement couldn't be checked through the API. The issue bot left two design questions for a maintainer:
- which Archicad call gives a reliable 2D extent for texts and drawings;
- whether the command should switch databases itself.

I measured both on Archicad 29 and added a Tapir `Get2DBoundingBoxes`.

## Which call

`ACAPI_Element_CalcBounds` already returns the drawn 2D extent of 2D elements. Its DevKit note says it can be used for 2D elements and leaves the vertical part unfilled. To check it, I compared it with the extent of every drawing primitive `ACAPI_DrawingPrimitive_ShapePrimsExt` sends for the same element (lines, arcs, polygons, texts, pictures). The two were equal for:
- Polyline, Hatch and Wall;
- a Text, also when rotated: the box covers the whole drawn line, not only the anchor point;
- a Drawing, with one difference: CalcBounds gives exactly the `bounds` of `GetDetailsOfElements`, its frame including the title. The primitives started 1 cm further right; I didn't find out why. Top, bottom and right edges were equal.

So the command uses `ACAPI_Element_CalcBounds` alone.

## Which database

`ACAPI_Element_CalcBounds` only works on elements of the current database. The command reads each element's database with `ACAPI_Database_GetContainingDatabase`, switches to it when it differs, and puts the starting database back at the end. A script can therefore ask for elements on layouts, sections and the floor plan in one call, whichever window is open. The boxes are in the coordinates of the element's own database: meters on the sheet for a layout.

**Slabs:** they don't go through `ACAPI_Element_CalcBounds`, because it crashes Archicad for a Slab that is not drawn in the current window (#686). They take the plan view of their 3D body, as `Get3DBoundingBoxes` does.

## Change

- **`Get2DBoundingBoxes` (new, element commands):** takes `elements` and returns `boundingBoxes2D`, one item per element, each either `boundingBox2D` (`xMin`, `yMin`, `xMax`, `yMax`) or an error item. It has the same shape as `Get3DBoundingBoxes`. An unknown element gets *"Failed to find element in Archicad"*.
- **Schemas:** `BoundingBoxes2D`, `BoundingBox2DOrError` and `BoundingBox2DArrayItem`. They reuse the existing `BoundingBox2D`.
- **Example:** `Examples/get_2d_bounding_boxes.py` creates a polyline and a text on the floor plan and a text on the first layout, if there is one. It reads the boxes while the floor plan is open, then deletes the elements again. The text widths depend on the machine's fonts, so the example prints only their relations.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS, German UI), 18/18

The project was saved first and reopened without saving afterwards.

| element | open window | result |
|---|---|---|
| Polyline, Hatch (floor plan) | floor plan | exactly their points |
| Text, 5 mm, left | floor plan | from the anchor point to the end of the line, top at the anchor |
| Text rotated 30° | floor plan | box of the rotated line |
| Arc 0–90°, r 2 | floor plan | (120, 100) – (122, 102) |
| Circle r 1.5 | floor plan | (128.5, 98.5) – (131.5, 101.5) |
| Linear dimension 140–145 | floor plan | witness points plus dimension line and text |
| Polyline, Hatch (layout) | floor plan | layout coordinates |
| Text (layout) | floor plan | 5 mm high, the whole line, in meters on the sheet |
| Drawing (layout) | floor plan | = `bounds` of `GetDetailsOfElements` |
| Polyline (section) | layout | section coordinates |
| 3 elements from three databases + one unknown | layout | aligned with the input, the unknown one is an error item |
| current database after the call | layout | still the layout |
| Wall | layout | = plan view of `Get3DBoundingBoxes` |
| Slab | layout | no crash, = plan view of `Get3DBoundingBoxes` (floor plan open) |
| Zone, Object | layout | box, no crash |

`Examples/get_2d_bounding_boxes.py` runs through.

**Found on the way:** `Get3DBoundingBoxes` fails for Slabs and Zones while a layout is open (*"Failed to get the 3D bounding box"*). With the floor plan open it works. That's a separate fix.

Not checked:
- **Labels, master layout elements, worksheets and details:** not tested. The databases they live in are switched the same way.
- **Hotlinked elements, and elements on other stories than the shown one:** apart from the Slab, not tested.
- **Windows, Archicad 25–28 and 30:** not run, so the CI builds cover them.

This branch includes the build fix from #1647, because `main` doesn't compile without it; that commit drops out once #1647 is merged.

title: Grasshopper: graphic override, Teamwork and solid operation commands
body:
Part of covering every Tapir command, with its parameters, in Grasshopper. This PR covers the 25 commands of this area that had no component.

## Components
- **Graphic override rules:** GetGraphicOverrideRules, GetGraphicOverrideRulesByName, CreateGraphicOverrideRules, ModifyGraphicOverrideRules, DeleteGraphicOverrideRules, MoveGraphicOverrideRules.
- **Graphic override combinations:** GetGraphicOverrideCombinations, CreateGraphicOverrideCombinations, ModifyGraphicOverrideCombinations, DeleteGraphicOverrideCombinations.
- **Rule groups:** CreateGraphicOverrideRuleGroups, GetGraphicOverrideRuleGroups, SetGraphicOverrideRuleOrder, RenameGraphicOverrideRuleGroups, DeleteGraphicOverrideRuleGroups.
- **Older single-item commands:** CreateGraphicalOverrideRule, GetGraphicalOverrideRules, CreateGraphicalOverrideCombination.
- **Teamwork:** GetTeamworkStatus, UploadLibrariesToBIMcloud, RemoveLibrariesFromBIMcloud.
- **Solid operations:** CreateSolidOperations, MergeElements, UnmergeElements, GetMergedElements.

## Design
- The graphic override components are in the Attributes group, because the commands are registered as Attribute Commands.

title: Get3DBoundingBoxes: work for Slabs and Zones while a layout or a section is open
body:
`Get3DBoundingBoxes` fails for Slabs and Zones while a layout or a section is the open window. I found this while testing #1675.

## Before

In a test project on Archicad 29 with Tapir 1.7.4, I asked for one element of each type and switched the open window between calls:

| open window | Wall, Object, Door, Window, Morph | Slab, Zone |
|---|---|---|
| floor plan | box | box |
| 3D | box | box |
| layout | box | *"Failed to get the 3D bounding box"* |
| section | box | *"Failed to get the 3D bounding box"* |

Slabs, Zones and Roofs are read from their 3D model (`ACAPI_ModelAccess_Get3DInfo`). Slabs are read that way to avoid the crash in #686. That call fails while a layout or a section is the current database. The other elements go through `ACAPI_Element_CalcBounds`, which works there.

## Change

- **Database switch:** before each element, `Get3DBoundingBoxes` makes the element's database current: the floor plan for model elements, the layout or section for 2D elements. It puts the starting database back after the last element. For this it uses the helper `ChangeToContainingDatabase` from #1675, moved up above `Get3DBoundingBoxes`.
- **Unknown element:** like before, an unknown element still gets *"Failed to find element in Archicad"*.
- **Description:** the registered description now says the current window doesn't need to show the element.

This branch builds on #1675, which adds the helper; please merge that one first. Like #1675, it also carries the build fix from #1647, because `main` doesn't compile without it. Both commits drop out of this diff once those PRs are merged.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS, German UI), 12/12

The project was saved first and reopened without saving afterwards. I compared 104 elements: a new single-plane Roof, a new Stair, all 96 Slabs of the project, and one Zone, Wall, Object, Door, Window and Morph. The reference was each box with the 3D window open.

| check | result |
|---|---|
| 3D window open | every element has a box (reference) |
| floor plan open | all 104 boxes = reference |
| another story open | all 104 = reference |
| layout open | all 104 = reference (Slab and Zone failed before) |
| section open | all 104 = reference (Slab and Zone failed before) |
| Stair, 3.25 m | 0.00 – 3.25 |
| Roof, 6 × 4 m at 3 m, 0.5 rad | covers the polygon, top above 3 m |
| current database after the call | still the layout |
| unknown element and a just-deleted polyline, in a list | aligned with the input, both *"Failed to find element in Archicad"* |
| polyline on a layout, floor plan open | box in layout coordinates |
| `Examples/get_3d_bounding_box_of_stairs.py` | runs through, 3.25 m |

Not checked:
- **Roof and Stair before the fix:** the project had none when I measured the old build, so the before table has no row for them. They take the same 3D model path as the Slab.
- **Worksheets, details, master layouts, interior elevations and the 3D document:** not tested.
- **Windows, Archicad 25–28 and 30:** not run, so the CI builds cover them.

title: CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection: OpeningEdges preset for Opening tool elements
body:
Part of #1662 (point 1).

Openings made with the Opening tool show up in `GetSectionElements`, but no preset of `CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection` takes them. The bot asked for the witness codes of a dimension placed by hand first.

## What a hand-placed dimension gets

On Archicad 29 I placed a test Opening in a section, both in a wall the section sees and in a wall it cuts, and dimensioned its edges by hand. The edges of both Openings, left and right and bottom and top, were snapped to.
- **Opening:** Archicad stored every point as a **fixed point**: no base element, node type 0. The same happened in the cut wall.
- **Window in the same section:** the points are associated (node type 2100, node status 3, 8 and 9).

So Archicad has no associative points on Opening section elements, which is why dimensions with guessed codes are dropped. There are no witness codes to put into a preset.

## Change

`CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection` gets a preset **`OpeningEdges`** that does what Archicad does by hand: it places **fixed** points at the edges of the Opening.
- **Where the edges come from:** `ACAPI_Element_CalcBounds` of the Opening's section element. In the section it is the opening as the section draws it, in the section's coordinates. For a seen wall that is the opening rectangle; for a cut wall it is the reveal across the wall thickness.
- **Horizontal chain (default):** left and right edge.
- **Vertical chain (`direction` with a larger y):** bottom and top edge.
- **Several Openings:** with `sectionElementIds`, they make one chain, as with the other presets.
- **Fixed, not associated:** the points don't follow the Opening when it changes. The schema description says so.
- **Current window:** the section of the Opening must be the current window, because the points are in its coordinates. Otherwise the item gets an error instead of a misplaced dimension.
- **Wrong section element:** the item gets *"The 'OpeningEdges' preset requires an opening section element."*

The command's registered description now names doors and windows for the existing presets and mentions `OpeningEdges`.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS, German UI), 8/8

I placed two test Openings: 1.2 × 1.0 m in a wall the section sees, 1.0 × 1.0 m in a wall it cuts. The project was reopened without saving afterwards.

| call | result |
|---|---|
| seen Opening, horizontal | fixed points at x 68.90 / 70.10 (1.20) |
| seen Opening, vertical | y 1.50 / 2.50 (1.00) |
| cut Opening, horizontal | the reveal, x 35.925 / 36.075 |
| cut Opening, vertical | y 1.50 / 2.50 |
| both Openings in one chain | 4 points |
| a Window with `OpeningEdges` | error item |
| a Window with `DoorWindowWallHoleCorners` | created as before |
| floor plan as current window | error item, nothing created |

The values are exactly where the hand-placed fixed points lay.

To place the test Openings I used `PlaceOpenings`, which crashes Archicad 29 too without the fix of #1666 (#1665). I applied #1666 only to my test build; it is not part of this PR.

Not checked:
- **Polygonal and circular Openings:** the points go on the bounding box of what the section draws.
- **Elevations, interior elevations, worksheets:** not tested.
- **Windows OS, Archicad 25–28 and 30:** not run, so the CI builds cover them.

This branch starts from the build fix that was merged as #1647, so that commit is already on `main`; the branch merges cleanly with `main`.

title: SetZoom resets a rotated floor plan to zero, even with the identical zoomBox
body:
Archicad **29** AUT build3200, Windows, released Tapir1.7.3. Related to #1313 / merged #1324.

A script records the current 2D zoom before temporary operations and restores the box afterwards. On a rotated floor plan, SetZoom also changes the orientation, although no rotation was requested. PR #1324 explicitly says that omitting tranmat should leave the rotation unchanged.

Reproduction in a disposable project, FloorPlan / story0:

1. `SaveCurrentWindowAsImage` returns this metadata:

```json
{"zoom":{"xMin":44.927934864,"yMin":-12.621140739,"xMax":82.029589926,"yMax":11.009080045},"rotation":-1.655666095}
```

2. Call SetZoom with **exactly that box**, without changing its size or position:

```json
{"zoomBox":{"xMin":44.927934864,"yMin":-12.621140739,"xMax":82.029589926,"yMax":11.009080045}}
```

Response: `{"success":true}`.

3. The next image-export metadata has the identical zoom bounds but **rotation0**. It was -1.655666095rad (equivalent4.627519212rad) immediately before the call. The same side effect had also been observed during the preceding independent restoration sequence, which prompted this isolated same-box test.

Expected: preserve the existing 2D rotation when SetZoom only receives zoomBox. If zero rotation is intentional, document the side effect and expose a reliable preserve/rotation option so a caller can restore the recorded view safely.

Current main's SetZoom Execute still calls `ACAPI_View_SetZoom(&zoomBox)` without an explicit transformation. Whether the missing transformation is interpreted as identity by Archicad is a cause to confirm, not a native API claim established here. No proposed fix or PR build tested.

Workaround used for cleanup: prepare a disposable saved floor-plan view with the original zoom and rotation, activate it, return ignoreSavedZoom to the original state via a disposable view, and remove all temporary views/folders. The final complete floor-plan settings, zoom and rotation equal the initial snapshots. The test project was saved before testing and after verified cleanup; no original saved view was edited.

title: Feature request: inspect custom GDL settings pages in their real element context, if supported
body:
Archicad 29 AUT build3200 / Windows / released Tapir1.7.3. Feature/feasibility request for our own editable GDL parts, not a claim that the native UI is broken.

Two use cases:

- **IS_Schichtlistenetikett:** six UI_PAGE pages, conditional controls and UI_FUNCTION insert/delete buttons. We manually displayed all six pages, inserted before model layer2, deleted the extra row and checked conditional controls. API readback confirmed committed parameter changes. A drawing export does not verify this dialog.
- **Planrahmen_IS:** a simpler sheet-frame object with four hierarchical settings pages, pictures and native text controls. During its development, real Archicad screenshots exposed three problems that our mock-up renderer missed: transparent UI_PICT areas became black until mask1 was used; controls over a picture were not editable; lower rows were clipped because the actual visible panel was about266px high rather than the assumed296px. These were local object-development issues, not demonstrated Tapir bugs.

**Existing local workaround:** we now have Windows UI helpers that open the actual settings dialog, capture its image/control list and close it with Escape, restoring the selected page. The Planrahmen four-page workflow was checked locally. This still drives the native Windows UI and requires the proper window/context; it is not an exposed Tapir renderer. Drawing screenshots already work and are not requested again.

If the Archicad API supports it, could Tapir expose an image of a specified custom settings page for a loaded part/placed instance, evaluated at the actual panel size and with its parameters/parent context? Page identity, part identity and image size should accompany it. Control rectangles, where available, would help identify overlaps and cut-off rows; a screenshot alone cannot prove clickability.

Optionally, keep UI_FUNCTION action invocation separate and return the resulting parameter changes. Assigning the parameters directly is not equivalent to exercising a UI button. A concrete manually verified example is insert-before-layer2 → inspect updated table → delete → inspect original rows.

Avoid leaving a blocking dialog or undocumented tool/default changes. Native rendering/action feasibility is not established: if unavailable, an explicit documented limitation and feasible inspection alternative would help. Interface-script writing/UI metadata already covered by merged #1468 is a different capability.

title: CreateWindows, CreateDoors: create without a marker when the marker defaults cannot be read
body:
When the Window or Door tool's Dimension Marker is set to "No Marker", or the marker's library part isn't in the loaded libraries, `CreateWindows` and `CreateDoors` fail for every element with "Failed to prepare window defaults." / "Failed to prepare door defaults.". The reason is that `ACAPI_Element_GetDefaultsExt` can't return a main marker in that state, and `PrepareWindowOrDoorDefaults` treated that as fatal. Archicad itself just places the opening without a marker.

With this change, `PrepareWindowOrDoorDefaults` first tries to read the defaults with the marker, as before (that code is unchanged and renamed `PrepareWindowOrDoorDefaultsWithMarker`). If that fails, it frees the handles and reads the tool defaults without a marker (`ACAPI_Element_GetDefaults`). It then tells the caller which case it was, and the caller creates the opening with `ACAPI_Element_CreateExt` (with the marker) or with `ACAPI_Element_Create` (without one). Nothing changes when the marker defaults can be read.

I also added `archicad-addon/Test/checks/create_windows_doors_keep_marker.json`, a regression check that a window and a door created with the template's tool defaults still get their marker. I couldn't find a way to put the tool into the "No Marker" state through Tapir, so the no-marker path itself has no check.

## Verification

- Built for Archicad 30 on Windows (AC30 DevKit 30.3000, MSVC toolset v143, RelWithDebInfo) with no errors. I haven't built the other versions locally.
- I have not run this in Archicad yet, and the new check hasn't been run against a live Archicad either.

Steps to try it in Archicad:

1. In a project with a straight wall, open Window Tool Settings, set Dimension Marker to "No Marker" and click OK.
2. Run `CreateWindows` with `{"windowsData": [{"ownerWallId": {"guid": "<wall guid>"}, "centerOffset": 1.0}]}`. Before this change it returns "Failed to prepare window defaults."; with it, the window is created and has no marker on the floor plan.
3. Do the same with the Door tool and `CreateDoors` (`doorsData`).
4. Set a marker again and create a window and a door: both should get the marker with the tool's settings, as before.
author: bimgeek

title: Add CreateRailingsFromPolyline: railings along a 3D polyline with arcs
body:
Part of #897

Adds `CreateRailingsFromPolyline`, which creates Railings along a reference polyline where every node has its own elevation and segments can be arcs. That covers railings along ramps, stair edges and sloped terrain, and curved balconies or terraces.

## What it adds

- **`CreateRailingsFromPolyline`** (`railingsData[]`):
  - `polylineCoordinates`: at least 2 `Coordinate3D` points. `z` is the elevation of the node relative to the floor level of the home story.
  - `polylineArcs`: optional `PolyArc`s, with indices into `polylineCoordinates`. An arc must join two consecutive points.
  - `floorIndex`, `height`, `favoriteName` and `id`: same as in `CreateRailings`.
- An example, `Examples/create_railings_polyline.py`.
- A runner check, `Test/checks/create_railings_from_polyline.json`.

## How it differs from CreateRailings

`CreateRailings` (#1606) takes 2D `coordinates` with straight segments and one `bottomOffset` for the whole railing. This command takes 3D points, so each node gets its own elevation, plus arc segments. Posts, rails, panels and balusters come from the favorite or the tool defaults in both.

I kept it as a separate command so the released `CreateRailings` schema and behaviour stay exactly as they are. Everything except the reference line is the same, though. I'd be happy to fold this into `CreateRailings` as optional `arcs` and a per-point `z` instead (with `z` taking precedence over `bottomOffset`), if you prefer one railing command.

## Design notes

- The class derives from `CreateRailingsCommand`, but only to reuse its `Execute`. That `Execute` creates each railing with its home story made active, because `ACAPI_Element_Create` ignores `header.floorInd` for railings (found in #1606). `CreateRailings` itself is unchanged. The new class overrides `GetName` instead of passing a name to a constructor, which keeps `tools/generate_addon_docs.py` working.
- `polyZCoords` holds absolute vertex elevations, as #1606 found. So each `z` is added to the level of the home story. A railing on story 1 with `z = 0.5` sits 0.5 above that story's floor, the same as on story 0.
- Only the reference line is written to the defaults' memo: `coords`, `parcs` and `polyZCoords` from index 1, plus `nVertices`. Archicad generates the nodes, segments, posts and rails, as in `CreateRailings` and the DevKit's `Do_CreateRailing`.
- An item fails with a clear error when two consecutive points have the same x and y, or when an arc doesn't join consecutive points. The other items in the call are still created.

## Verification

Built for Archicad 30 on Windows (DevKit 30.3000, Visual Studio 2026 with the v143 toolset, RelWithDebInfo). It compiles without errors, and `tools/generate_addon_docs.py` picks up the new command. I haven't run it in Archicad yet, and the new check hasn't been run against a live Archicad either.

To test:

1. Load the add-on in an empty project and run `archicad-addon/Examples/create_railings_polyline.py`.
   - Two railings should appear at x = 140 to 148.
   - The first stays flat for 4 m, then rises 1 m over its second segment, with segments 1.1 high.
   - The second ends in a quarter arc.
   - `GetDetailsOfElements` should return their reference lines and segment heights.
2. Create a railing with `floorIndex` set to an upper story whose level isn't 0, and all `z` values set to 0.5. It should be homed on that story, with `bottomOffset` 0.5 (not 0.5 minus the story level). The previously active story should be active again afterwards.
3. Pass `favoriteName` with a Railing favorite. Posts, rails and panels should come from the favorite.
4. Check that these items fail and nothing is created for them: one point, two consecutive points with the same x and y, and an arc with `endIndex` not equal to `begIndex + 1`.
5. `python tools/community-test-runner/tapir_test_runner.py check archicad-addon/Test/checks/create_railings_from_polyline.json` covers steps 2 and 4.
6. `Examples/create_railings.py` should behave as before.
author: bimgeek

title: Add CreateShells: extruded, revolved and ruled shells
body:
Adds a `CreateShells` command for creating Shell elements, which Tapir couldn't do until now. Related to #1663, which asks for shell support in `GetDetailsOfElements` and a `ModifyShells` command. This PR doesn't cover either of those; it only adds creation.

## What it does

`CreateShells` takes a `shellsData` array, like the other create commands. Each item can name a `favoriteName` and an `id`, and gets back either the new element's guid or an error. An item that fails doesn't stop the others.

Each item picks a `shellClass`:

- **Extruded**: the `profile` polyline is swept along `extrusionVector`, which is required. Optional: `extrusionStart`, `slantAngle`, `shapePlaneTilt`, `begPlaneTilt`, `endPlaneTilt`.
- **Revolved**: the `profile` is turned around `axis` through `revolutionAngle`. Defaults are a full turn around the base plane's Y axis. Optional: `beginAngle`, `slantAngle`, `distortionAngle` (pi/2, no shear, by default) and `segmentsByCircle`. The default base plane of a revolved shell stands upright, so the profile's x is the radius and its y is the height. This is the same setup the DevKit's revolved shell sample uses.
- **Ruled**: a surface between `profile` and `secondProfile`. Each profile lies in its own plane, given by `profilePlane` and `secondProfilePlane`. All three are required. `morphingRule` is `Paired` or `Smooth`.

### Profiles
A profile is a list of 2D `coordinates` with optional `arcs`, using the same `PolyArc` format as the other polygon inputs. `closed` says whether the segment from the last point back to the first is part of the surface; profiles are open by default. Archicad stores every profile as a closed polygon whose per-edge body flags mark which edges produce a surface, so an open profile is a closed polygon with the closing edge's flag off.

### Placement and structure
- `basePlane` sets an origin and/or axes in project coordinates. Profiles, vectors, the axis and the cut polygons are all given in this plane. The three axes must be given together or not at all; a partial set is refused rather than guessed.
- `floorIndex` sets the story.
- `thickness` and `isFlipped` work as in the Shell tool.
- `structureType`, `buildingMaterialId` and `compositeId` work exactly as they do for roofs.

### Clipping contour and holes
`contour` is an optional clipping polygon: only the part of the shell inside it is kept. `holes` is a list of polygons, each extruded `depth` along the Z axis of its own `plane`, which defaults to the base plane. With a separate plane per hole you can, for example, cut a horizontal oculus into a dome whose base plane is vertical.

### Edge trims
`begShapeEdgeTrim`, `endShapeEdgeTrim`, `begSideEdgeTrim` and `endSideEdgeTrim` each take a `trimType` of `Vertical`, `Perpendicular`, `Horizontal` or `CustomAngle`, plus an `angle` for `CustomAngle`.

When a trim isn't given, it defaults to Perpendicular at pi/2. That is what the Archicad 30 Shell tool stores for a shell drawn by hand, while the tool defaults read through the API hold Vertical at 1 degree. Without this default, shells created through the API looked different from hand-drawn ones. The default also applies when a favorite is given.

New shared schema definitions: `CoordinateSystem3D`, `ShellProfile`, `ShellCutPolygon` and `ShellEdgeTrim`.

## Refactor: ApplyShellBaseStructure

Roofs and shells share `API_ShellBaseType`, so the Basic/Composite structure part of `ApplyRoofStructure` moves into an `ApplyShellBaseStructure` helper that both use. Roofs behave the same as before. The only difference is in the profile-structure branch: it no longer sets the roof's structure masks, but roofs already reject a profile structure in `ParseStructureSelection` before reaching that branch.

## Example and check

- `Examples/Element/CreateShells.py` creates three shells:
  - an extruded barrel vault with a square opening cut through it
  - a revolved dome with a circular oculus
  - a ruled shell between a straight edge and an arched one
- `Test/checks/create_shells.json`:
  - creates the same three kinds of shell, with edge trims on the vault, and checks that `GetElementsByType` finds three shells
  - sends four incomplete items: an extruded shell without `extrusionVector`, a ruled shell without `secondProfile`, a base plane with a single axis, and an arc index outside the profile
  - checks that each of these returns an error and that no shell is created

## Verification

I built this for Archicad 30 on Windows with the AC30 DevKit and MSVC v143 (Visual Studio 2026). It compiles with no warnings. I haven't run it against Archicad yet, so the example and the check are untested. I validated the check's parameters against the command's input schema.

To try it:

1. Load the built add-on in Archicad 30 (or 25–29) on an empty project.
2. Run `python archicad-addon/Examples/Element/CreateShells.py`.
3. In the 3D window, you should see:
   - a barrel vault at the origin, 6 m wide and 8 m long, with a 2 x 2 m opening in its top
   - a 4 m radius dome around (15, 4) with a 1 m oculus
   - a ruled shell starting at x = 25, from a straight edge at y = 0 to an arched edge at y = 6
4. Open each shell's settings: thickness and structure should match the input, and the edges should show Perpendicular trims.
5. Run the check with the community test runner: `python tools/community-test-runner/tapir_test_runner.py check archicad-addon/Test/checks/create_shells.json`.

title: UpdateZones: optional list of the Zones to update
body:
Fixes #894. Replaces #900, which can't work as it is (see below).

`UpdateZones` updates the selected Zones, or every Zone when nothing is selected. #894 asks for an optional list, so a script no longer depends on the selection and never updates every Zone by accident.

## What Archicad does

I measured `APIInternal_UpdateRoomsID` on Archicad 29 with test Zones far from the model.
- **Deferred:** it never updates during the command. The Zones change about 0.3 s after the JSON command has returned. That is the same inside an undoable command, outside one, and when the call is made from Archicad's main event loop (`ACAPI_AddOnAddOnCommunication_CallFromEventLoop`): in all three cases a Zone's polygon read right after the call is still the old one.
- **Selection at that moment:** it updates the Zones that are selected when it runs. If the next JSON command changes the selection first, the new selection is updated. With nothing selected, every Zone is updated.
- **Afterwards:** Archicad clears the selection itself.
- **Other stories:** Zones on a story that is not the active one can be selected, and they are updated too.
- **Reference point:** setting it with `SetDetailsOfElements` does not recalculate an automatic Zone, so that is no way around it.

That is why #900 updates the wrong Zones (my test report there): it selects the listed Zones, calls the update and puts the previous selection back, and the update then runs on that previous selection. The bot came to the same conclusion; the only working form is to leave the listed Zones selected.

## Change

`UpdateZones` takes an optional **`zones`** (`Elements`):
- **Check first:** every item must be an existing Zone, listed once, on a visible and unlocked layer, and editable (the checks of `MoveElements`). If one fails, the command returns a failed result naming each bad Zone and its reason, and nothing is selected or updated. The previous selection stays.
- **Select exactly the list:** the selection is replaced by the listed Zones, on any story, and read back. Only when it is exactly the list does the update go ahead.
- **Leave it selected:** the update runs right after the command returns, on these Zones. The schema and the registered description say so: don't change the selection until then, and read the new geometry with a later command.
- **Empty list:** `zones: []` succeeds and updates nothing; it does not mean "all".
- **Without `zones`:** unchanged.

The result stays an `ExecutionResult`. New areas can't be part of it, because the update hasn't run yet when the command returns.

**Example:** `Examples/update_given_zones.py` builds two automatic Zones next to each other, moves the wall between them, updates the left one, waits a second and prints that only the left one changed. It deletes everything afterwards. No golden output, because it waits for Archicad.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS, German UI), 12/12

Test Zones in pairs (two automatic Zones, the wall between them moved by 1 m: 21.16 / 22.08 m², up to date 25.76 / 17.48 m²). The project was saved first and reopened without saving afterwards.

| call | result |
|---|---|
| `zones: [A]`, B selected before | success, the selection is A; only A updated; afterwards the selection is empty |
| `zones: [E]`, E on story 1, story 0 active | only E updated |
| one Zone from story 0 and one from story 1 | both updated, their neighbours not |
| a Wall in the list | failed, "the element is not a Zone"; selection unchanged, nothing updated |
| a Zone listed twice | failed, nothing updated |
| a Zone on a hidden layer | failed, "its layer is hidden", nothing updated |
| `zones: []` | success, selection unchanged, nothing updated |
| no `zones`, B selected | B updated, as before |
| every Zone of the project | polygons unchanged |
| `Examples/update_given_zones.py` | runs through |

Not checked:
- **Teamwork reservations and locked elements:** handled by the same check, but not tested.
- **Windows, Archicad 25–28 and 30:** not run, so the CI builds cover them.

This branch starts from the build fix that was merged as #1647; it merges cleanly with `main`.

## Added after review: the Grasshopper input

The `UpdateZones` component gets an optional `Zones` input, appended after the three existing ones, so saved definitions keep their inputs. A connected input never falls back to the selection or every Zone, also when its list is empty, so a filter that finds no Zones updates nothing. Without the input the component works as before. The Grasshopper coverage now counts 4/4 parameters for `UpdateZones`.

Not built or run here: no .NET SDK on this machine, so the Grasshopper build check covers the compile, and the component was not tried in Grasshopper.

title: Open/activate the Session Report and read its plain text through the API
body:
### Use case
After placing or rebuilding GDL objects, an automation needs to inspect Archicad's existing Session Report (Session-Protokoll) for runtime/conversion messages without Windows UI automation.

### Reproduced
Archicad 29 AUT, build 3200, Windows, released Tapir 1.7.3. Tested in an isolated test PLN.

| Input | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `ChangeWindow` with the Project Map Info > Protokoll item's navigatorItemId | Error -2130313112: `navigatorItemId must be a view or viewpoint; got a container or folder` |
| Same with Info > Projektnotizen | Same error |
| `ChangeWindow {"windowType":"Report"}` | Error -2130313109: `Failed to change the window!` |
| Open Session-Protokoll using Archicad's menu, then `GetCurrentWindowType` | `{"currentWindowType":"Report"}` |
| Return to the floor plan, then try `ChangeWindow {"windowType":"Report"}` while the Report tab already exists | Same -2130313109 error; the floor plan remains active |

`Report` is an allowed value in the installed WindowType schema. Current main also maps it in the window-type conversion. This is therefore not a request to accept an undocumented enum value.

### Request
1. A supported way to open/activate the Session Report through Tapir, or an explicit documented limitation if Archicad cannot support this.
2. A getter returning the existing report's plain text. An optional incremental cursor/offset would help repeated polling, with defined behavior when the report is cleared or a project/session changes.

The exposed command catalog/current main contains no report-text getter that we could find. Our local workaround invokes the menu and reads the report's rich-edit control from outside Archicad; it is Windows-only and fragile across versions.

Related: #1400 requests structured GDL diagnostics. This request concerns the already existing report text, not per-library-part script checking or structured compiler messages. It does not assume that all GDL errors appear in the report.

We have not established whether the public native SDK supports reading this text; please assess feasibility rather than treating the UI workaround as proof of a portable native implementation.
author: thespatialist

title: Return the active window's database/view identity, not only its type
body:
### Use case
Scripts temporarily switch to a layout, worksheet or report, then need to restore the user's original window/view reliably. A window type alone cannot identify the previous database or saved view. Matching tab titles against View Map names is ambiguous when several views have the same name.

### Reproduced
Archicad 29 AUT, build 3200, Windows, released Tapir 1.7.3. In an isolated test PLN, we opened a known saved floor-plan view, a disposable layout and an independent worksheet using their known navigator/database identifiers, then queried `GetCurrentWindowType`:

| Active context | Complete returned object |
| --- | --- |
| Saved floor-plan view | `{"currentWindowType":"FloorPlan"}` |
| Layout | `{"currentWindowType":"Layout"}` |
| Worksheet | `{"currentWindowType":"Worksheet"}` |

None returns a databaseId or navigatorItemId. Supplying a known ID to open a context is a control for this test, not a way to discover an unknown user's starting context.

### Request
Extend this getter, or add a `GetCurrentWindow` command, to return:
- the active window type;
- its `databaseId`, where applicable;
- the actual opened View Map `navigatorItemId`, where it can be resolved reliably.

Please return an explicit unknown/null for unavailable identity, rather than selecting the first view with a matching name. Several saved views can share the same source database but different settings. A Report or other non-model window may have no corresponding database/view.

The result should describe the visibly active window, not silently return a background working database. Document any cases where the exact saved view cannot be recovered.

### Implementation pointer / limitation
Current main already calls `ACAPI_Window_GetCurrentWindow` into `API_WindowInfo` in `GetCurrentWindowTypeCommand::Execute`, then serializes only typeID. The available window info and possibly `ACAPI_Database_GetCurrentDatabase` may help with database identity; this is not evidence that either call always identifies the actual opened View Map item.

Our current Windows-specific workaround reads tab titles and searches the View Map. It is unreliable with duplicate names and does not provide a robust cross-platform restoration token. `GetDatabaseOfElements` maps supplied elements to a database; it does not discover the active window/view.
author: thespatialist

title: CreateOpenings: put the bottom edge on basePoint.z on every Archicad 29 build
body:
On Archicad 29 build 3000, `CreateOpenings` places every opening a full height too high: `basePoint.z` 1.5 with `height` 1.0 gives an opening at 2.5–3.5.

## Cause

The AC29 branch raises the placement point by the height before `PlacePolygonal`. That was right for the builds measured in #533, where `PlacePolygonal` hung the polygon below the point, with the bottom at `z - height`. #848 found that Archicad 30 already puts the bottom on the given Z, and limited the raise to Archicad 29 with `#ifndef ServerMainVers_3000`.

Archicad 29 build 3000 behaves like Archicad 30. So the raise now overshoots there too. A compile-time guard can't tell the builds apart, because both are compiled against the same AC29 DevKit.

## Change

`CreateOpenings` on Archicad 29 and 30 now does this:
- **Placement:** places the opening at `basePoint` without the raise.
- **Read back:** reads the placed opening back and computes where its anchor should be: the requested bottom above the opening's home story, plus the anchor's offset above the bottom. This is the same formula the pre-AC29 branch already uses (`GetAnchorHeightOffset`, now shared).
- **Correct:** only if the anchor altitude differs does it set it with `Opening::Modify`. On a build like 3000 nothing is changed; on the older AC29 builds the opening is moved down onto `basePoint.z`.
- **On failure:** if the correction fails, the opening is deleted again and the item gets an error. An opening at the wrong height is never returned as a success.
- **Free / ForcedVertical constraint:** such an opening has no anchor altitude and is left as placed, as before.

## Tested on Archicad 29 build 3000 (macOS, German UI), 9/9

The project was saved first and reopened without saving afterwards.

| call | result |
|---|---|
| wall that a section cuts, `z` 1.5, `height` 1.0 | anchor altitude 1.50; the section draws the opening at 1.50–2.50 (before: 2.50–3.50) |
| `z` 1.0 / `height` 1.2, `z` 0.0 / 2.1, `z` 2.0 / 0.6 | bottom at 1.00, 0.00, 2.00 |
| wall on an upper story (level 4.00), `z` 4.90 | bottom 0.90 above that story |
| unknown owner | error item as before |
| openings in the project | exactly the 5 new ones, nothing duplicated |

I also ran the same 9 checks on a build that deliberately places the opening a full height too high, which is the behaviour of the builds from #533. The correction moved all of them onto `basePoint.z`, and the section again drew the first one at 1.50–2.50. That build was only for testing and is not part of this PR.

Not checked:
- **Archicad 30:** not run here. The code path is the same, and the read-back only changes something when the bottom is off.
- **Older Archicad 29 builds:** checked only through the simulated build above.
- **Undo:** not checked by hand. The correction runs inside the command's undo step.
- **Windows, Archicad 25–28:** not run, so the CI builds cover them. The pre-AC29 branch is unchanged.

This branch starts from the build fix that was merged as #1647; it merges cleanly with `main`.

title: Add ReindexAttributes: move fills, line types, surfaces and building materials to new indices
body:
Part of #1388. Stacked on #1635 (`ReindexLayers`): the branch is based on it, so the diff shows that PR's commits until it is merged; only the last commit (`fe632235`) belongs to this PR. It follows `ReindexLayers` for the attribute types that reserved index ranges in templates are usually planned for (@Kappa-lo's use case on #1388).

Archicad cannot renumber an attribute, so the command recreates the attribute at the new index and rewrites every reference to the old index, then deletes the old attribute:

1. A copy of the attribute (fields, definition, name under a temporary name) is created at `newIndex`; free indices below it are filled with temporary attributes first, which are deleted again (`placeholders` in the response, `maxPlaceholders` as a limit).
2. Every reference is rewritten to the new index:
   - the fields of the elements in the floor plan and in every section, elevation, interior elevation, detail, worksheet, 3D document, layout and master layout (a table of the `API_AttributeIndex` / `API_OverriddenAttribute` fields of `API_Element`, per element type),
   - the library part parameters of fill, line type, surface and building material type, single values and arrays (objects, lamps, windows, doors, skylights, labels, zone stamps, interior elevation markers),
   - memo data: cutting planes (walls, columns, beams), slab and roof side surfaces, multi-plane roof levels, morph face surfaces (the body and its material map table written back with `APIMemoMask_All`, as `ModifyMorphs` does), and the sub-elements kept in a memo (column and beam segments, curtain wall frames and panels with their defaults, stair structures), so tool defaults and Favorites of these types are covered,
   - the Opening element: its floor plan line types and cover fill, through the `API_Element` fields before Archicad 29 and through `ACAPI::Element::Opening` / `OpeningDefault` from Archicad 29,
   - the tool defaults, the Favorites (element, memo and sub-elements; a curtain wall Favorite is left as it is and named in `warnings`, because `ACAPI_Favorite_Change` answers NoError without taking its frame and panel classes; every other Favorite is read back after the change to make sure it took),
   - the other attributes: composites (skins, separators), building materials (cut fill, cut surface), surfaces (hatching fill), MEP systems (fill), profiles (skins and edges),
   - the graphic override rules (line type, fill, surface).
3. The old attribute is deleted, the copy gets the real name and is moved into the old attribute's folder.

Elements on a hidden or locked layer cannot be changed, so those layers are shown and unlocked for the move and put back afterwards (as `ReindexLayers` does for the moved layer). If an element still cannot be changed (locked itself, not reserved in Teamwork), everything is put back and the attribute is not moved. Elements from hotlinked modules cannot be changed: they are listed (`hotlinkElements`, plus a warning) and the module file has to be reindexed on its own. `dryRun` lists every reference without changing anything. The whole call is one undo step. Available from Archicad 27 (same guard as `ReindexLayers`).

Compiled locally against the AC27 and AC29 DevKits (`extrusionMaterial` of beam segments exists from Archicad 28 only).

Not in this PR: pens (fixed 1–255) and the other attribute types; indices typed into GDL scripts (not findable); a Favorite's marker element; the frame and panel classes of curtain wall Favorites (see above) and of the Curtain Wall tool default (it would need `ACAPI_Element_GetDefaultsExt` with sub-elements).

**Attribute id:** the new attribute has a new id. Archicad does not keep a guid given in `API_Attr_Head` on `ACAPI_Attribute_CreateExt` (tested on Archicad 29: the attribute is created, with a different guid), so there is no way to keep it. Between files Archicad matches attributes by name, so hotlinks and merges are not affected.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS), 28/28 checks

Live test on a real project (339 fills, 110 line types, 227 surfaces, 124 building materials): own test attributes with a hatch, a line, a wall, a composite (skin + separators), a building material (cut fill + cut surface), an object with a surface parameter, a Favorite and a graphic override rule; then a project surface used by 173 elements, 6 Favorites and a tool default, moved into a gap in 2.2 s. Checked after each move: the attribute at the new index with its name, every reference (`GetDetailsOfElements`, `GetComposites`, `GetBuildingMaterials`, `GetGDLParametersOfElements`, `GetGraphicOverrideRules`, a second `dryRun` on the moved attribute) and the attribute counts (no placeholder left). Error cases: used index, locked element (rollback, nothing changed), `maxPlaceholders`, same index.

Not tested here: hotlinks, Teamwork, Archicad's Undo after the call, roofs with multi-plane levels and morphs with face surfaces (the code paths exist, the test project has no such reference to a moved surface).

title: GetDetailsOfElements: read Elevation markers like sections
body:
Follow-up to #1608 (#1607), which reads the geometry of sections. Elevation markers still answered `"Not yet supported element type"`, so the start of an elevation line couldn't be read, and an elevation's own 2D content (x along the view, y = height) couldn't be placed back into the model.

## What changes

In the DevKit, `API_ElevationType` is `API_CutPlaneType` (`using API_ElevationType = API_CutPlaneType;`), and an elevation keeps its line and depth line in the same memo fields as a section (`sectionSegmentMainCoords`, `sectionSegmentDepthCoords`). So the reader from #1608 applies as it is:

- `GetDetailsOfElements` gets a `case API_ElevationID` next to `API_CutPlaneID`, with `elem.elevation.segment` instead of `elem.cutPlane.segment`: `name`, `idStr`, `mainCoordinates`, `depthCoordinates`, `startCoordinate`, `endCoordinate`, `depth`, `viewDirection`.
- The details reuse `SectionDetails`. A second definition with the same shape would make the `oneOf` of `TypeSpecificDetails` ambiguous. Its descriptions now say "section or elevation".
- `Examples/get_section_details.py` reads elevations too.

Not covered: interior elevations. They keep several segments (`intElevSegments`), not one, so they would need their own reader.

## Tested on Archicad 27 (macOS)

No command creates elevations, so an elevation and a section were drawn by hand in a test project.

| | Tapir 1.7.3 (release) | this branch (build check artifact "Tapir Add-On AC27 Mac") |
|---|---|---|
| Elevation | `"Not yet supported element type"` | name "Ansicht Nord", idStr "A-01", line (1.34, −4.46) → (8.98, −4.46), depth line 6.08 away, `viewDirection` (0, 1), towards the depth line |
| Section | `"Not yet supported element type"` (#1608 is not in 1.7.3) | read as in #1608, unchanged |

`Examples/get_section_details.py` lists both markers. Build check green on the fork (14/14 jobs, all Archicad versions, Windows and Mac).

title: Curtain wall segments, frames and panels: homeStoryLevel, and say what their z is measured from
body:
No issue was open for this. #1561 reports the same kind of thing for stairs.

## What the values meant

In `GetDetailsOfElements`, the z values of curtain wall parts are measured from the **curtain wall's home story**, while the curtain wall's own 3D box, and every other element's height, is absolute:

- segments: `begCoordinate.z`, `endCoordinate.z`, `gridOrigin.z`;
- frames: `begCoordinate.z`, `endCoordinate.z`;
- panels: the z of `polygonCoordinates`.

Nothing in the response or the schema says so, and the story isn't in the details either. A script that rebuilds curtain walls in another application put every curtain wall above the ground floor too low by its story's level.

Measured on Archicad 27 with Tapir 1.7.3: two curtain walls 3 m high, made with `CreateCurtainWalls`, one on story 0 and one on story 1 (level 3 m):

| | story 0 | story 1 (level 3) |
|---|---|---|
| curtain wall `Get3DBoundingBoxes` z | 0 → 3 | **3 → 6** |
| segment `begCoordinate.z` / `endCoordinate.z` / `gridOrigin.z` | 0 / 0 / 0 | **0 / 0 / 0** |
| frames z | 0 → 3 | **0 → 3** |
| panel polygon z | 0 → 3 | **0 → 3** |

## Change

- The values stay as they are: scripts that already add the level keep working.
- Segment, frame and panel details get **`homeStoryLevel`** as their last field: the absolute level of the curtain wall's home story (`GetZPos (owner's floorInd, 0, stories)`, the owner from `cwSegment.owner`, `cwFrame.owner`, `cwPanel.owner`). Adding it gives absolute z. One helper, `AddCurtainWallHomeStoryLevel`, is called from the three cases.
- Schema: `homeStoryLevel` in `CurtainWallSegmentDetails`, `CurtainWallFrameDetails` and `CurtainWallPanelDetails`, and descriptions on the fields above that say what they are measured from.
- Golden output of `get_and_set_details_of_elements.py`: `"homeStoryLevel": 0` on its 48 curtain wall items (one segment, its frames and panels, all on story 0). I couldn't run `test_examples.py` here (`TestProject.pla` is an LFS file I didn't download), so this assumes story 0 of the test project is at level 0. Please check if it isn't.

## Tested on Archicad 27 (macOS)

| | Tapir 1.7.3 (release) | this branch (build check artifact "Tapir Add-On AC27 Mac", reports 1.7.4) |
|---|---|---|
| story 1 curtain wall | z 0 → 3 everywhere, no way to tell the story | z unchanged, `homeStoryLevel: 3` on the segment, all frames and all panels: 0 → 3 + 3 = 3 → 6, the 3D box |
| story 0 curtain wall | z 0 → 3 | z unchanged, `homeStoryLevel: 0` |

Edge cases, each checked by adding the story level (and on this branch `homeStoryLevel`) to every segment, frame and panel z and comparing with the curtain wall's `Get3DBoundingBoxes`:

| curtain wall | story level | parts z | + level | 3D box | `homeStoryLevel` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| on UG | −3 | 0 → 3 | −3 → 0 | −3 → 0 | −3 |
| on OG, base at 4.5 (1.5 above the story) | 3 | 1.5 → 3.5 | 4.5 → 6.5 | 4.5 → 6.5 | 3 |
| on OG, two segments (L-shaped) | 3 | 0 → 3 | 3 → 6 | 3 → 6 | 3 on both segments |
| the same after `SetStories` moved OG to 3.5 | 3.5 | unchanged | 3.5 → 6.5 / 5 → 7 | moved with the story | 3.5 |

So the parts' z already include the curtain wall's offset from its story, and z + `homeStoryLevel` is absolute in every case. Not tested: arc segments (`CreateCurtainWalls` can't make them).

Build check green on the fork (14/14 jobs, all Archicad versions, Windows and Mac).

Seen while measuring, not changed here: `Get3DBoundingBoxes` of a **panel** on the story 1 curtain wall also answered story-relative z (1.03 → 2.95), while the curtain wall, its segment and its frames answered absolute z. That's in another command; happy to open an issue for it.

author: Gigiasso

title: Get3DBoundingBoxes: real height of Opening elements
body:
`Get3DBoundingBoxes` returns `zMin` = `zMax` = 0 for every Opening element: an opening 1.0 high in a wall comes back as a flat box at height 0. X and Y are right, so the box looks plausible in plan. `API.Get3DBoundingBoxes` answers with an internal error for the same element.

## Cause

`ACAPI_Element_CalcBounds` doesn't give an Opening element any height. An Opening element only cuts other elements.

## Change

For Opening elements (Archicad 29 and later), `Get3DBoundingBoxes` computes the box from the opening's geometry:
- **Outline:** the size of the outline, placed around the anchor point by the opening's anchor. Measured live: this holds for polygonal openings too. A polygon around the origin with a `BottomCenter` anchor still has its bottom edge on the anchor point, as the section shows.
- **Extrusion:** the outline is extruded along the extrusion direction, from `extrusionStartOffset`, over `finiteBodyLength` for a `Finite` opening and without end for `HalfInfinite`.
- **Infinite ends:** an `Infinite` or `HalfInfinite` extrusion is limited to the solid bodies of the elements the opening cuts. The vertices are used, not the bounding box, so an opening in a diagonal wall gets the hole's box and not the wall's. The result is also clipped to those bodies' bounding box, because the opening has no effect beyond them.
- **Cuts nothing:** an opening whose infinite extrusion doesn't reach any of its elements returns the existing error item ("Failed to get the 3D bounding box").
- **Finite openings:** the box is that of the finite body, as for any element. It is not clipped to the cut elements.

The geometry is read in `ExtendedElementCommands.cpp`, next to `GetOpeningAxes` (`GetOpeningExtrusionBody`). `Get3DBoundingBoxes` has a new branch for `API_OpeningID`. Other element types are unchanged.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS, German UI), 11/11

The truth is the hole itself: its vertices in the 3D mesh of the cut element (`Get3DGeometryOfElements`), plus one opening in an existing section. Every opening was made with `CreateOpenings` and changed with `SetOpeningDetails`. The project was saved first and reopened without saving afterwards.

| opening | result |
|---|---|
| polygonal 1.0 × 1.2 in a wall, infinite | equal to the hole (before: z 0–0) |
| `Finite`, offset 0.05, length 0.06 (a niche inside the wall) | equal to the niche, 0.05–0.11 into the wall |
| `HalfInfinite`, offset −0.05 | equal to the hole |
| `Rectangular` 0.6 × 0.3, anchor `Center` | equal to the hole |
| `Rectangular` 0.5 × 0.4, anchor `TopRight` | equal to the hole |
| `Circular` Ø 0.5 | equal to the hole (within the mesh's polygon approximation) |
| polygonal 1.0 × 0.6 in a slab | equal to the hole, z = the slab's thickness |
| in a diagonal wall on an upper story | equal to the hole, not the wall's whole box |
| in a wall a section cuts | the same height as the opening in the section |
| `HalfInfinite` that starts outside the wall | error item, no box |
| the wall itself | unchanged |

Not checked:
- **Archicad 30:** not run here. It uses the same Opening API.
- **One opening cutting several elements:** the code uses all of them, but every opening in the test cut a single element.
- **`Free` constraint:** not tested.
- **Windows, Archicad 25–28:** not run, so the CI builds cover them. Before Archicad 29, Openings still go to `ACAPI_Element_CalcBounds` as before.

This branch starts from #1611 (merged), which added `GetOpeningAxes`. It merges cleanly with `main`, and with my open #1686 (same command) and #1711 (`CreateOpenings`).

title: Add DeselectAll, GetMarquee and SetMarquee (replaces #963)
body:
Adds the add-on commands `DeselectAll`, `GetMarquee` and `SetMarquee` from #934. It replaces #963, the issue bot's part 1, which has been waiting for a maintainer since October. I took its code, tested it in Archicad 29 and fixed two bugs the test showed.

The Grasshopper components from part 2 (#1031: `DeselectAll`, `GetMarquee`, `SetMarquee`) are already merged and call these three commands. Until now they had nothing to call.

## Commands

- **`DeselectAll`:** no input. Clears the selection of the current window.
- **`GetMarquee`:** returns `type` (`none`, `rectangle`, `rotatedRectangle`, `polygon`), `multiStory`, the `box` and `rotationAngle` for the rectangles, and the outline as `polygon`.
- **`SetMarquee`:** takes `polygon` or `box` (with an optional `rotationAngle`), plus `multiStory`. Without either it removes the marquee.

The schemas, the example and the `MigrationHelper` mapping for `ACAPI_Selection_DeselectAll` on Archicad 25/26 are taken over from #963. So is the handle `GetSelectedElements` never freed.

## Fixed compared with #963

- **Polygon marquees are 0-based.** Unlike memo polygons, `API_Region::coords` holds `nCoords` vertices from index 0, the last one repeating the first. #963 wrote and read them 1-based. Every polygon marquee therefore also contained vertex 0, the project origin: a marquee over a 4 × 2 m rectangle also took a thin wedge from the origin to its corner into the selection. Reading 1-based gave back exactly the polygon that was written, so the round trip hid it.
- **Rotated rectangles get an outline.** Archicad stores a rotated rectangle without `coords`, also when the user draws it by hand, so `GetMarquee` returned no `polygon` for it. The Grasshopper component then had no outline to show. Measured: the `box` lies in the coordinate system rotated by `rotationAngle` around the project origin, not around the box. `GetMarquee` now returns the box's corners rotated that way as `polygon`. The descriptions of `box` and `rotationAngle` say how the box is meant, in both commands.
- **`rotationAngle` without `box`** is now rejected instead of being ignored.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS, German UI), 15/15

The truth is which elements the marquee takes into the selection. A grid of 576 probe columns was placed for this, and `GetSelectedElements` was compared with the outline. The project was saved first and reopened without saving afterwards.

| call | result |
|---|---|
| 5 walls selected, `DeselectAll` | 0 selected |
| `GetMarquee` without a marquee | `type: none` |
| `box`, `multiStory: true` | `rectangle`, the box, its 4 corners, `multiStory: true`; selects exactly the columns inside |
| L-shaped `polygon` | `polygon` with exactly its 6 vertices; selects exactly the columns inside (with #963: also a wedge to the origin) |
| the same polygon with the first vertex repeated | the same vertices and columns |
| `box` with `rotationAngle` 30° | `rotatedRectangle`, the box and angle as given, its 4 corners on the plan; selects exactly the columns inside those corners |
| `SetMarquee {}` | marquee removed |
| polygon and box together, box without width, 2-point polygon, `rotationAngle` without box | failed result each, marquee unchanged |
| rectangle in a section window | set and read back |

A rotated marquee drawn by hand from the origin was checked by reading it back: the same form (box with one corner at 0/0, angle, no `coords`). The elements it covered came back from `GetSelectedElements`. A rotated marquee set through the API was checked visually, where it appears on the plan: rotated around the origin.

Not checked:
- **Archicad 25–28 and 30, Windows:** not run here, so the CI builds cover them. The code is the same for every version apart from the `DeselectAll` name.
- **The Grasshopper components:** not run here, but they read and send exactly these fields.

#963 can be closed when this is merged. This branch starts from the build fix that was merged as #1647. It merges cleanly with `main`.

title: Add GetAttributeIndexes; mark GetCurrentAttributeSetReader as not applicable
body:
Covers the remaining open items of the Attribute group in the API coverage list. `ACAPI_Attribute_ModifyPen` is left out here because #975 (`ModifyPens`) already changes single pens.

## `GetAttributeIndexes` (new)

Uses `ACAPI_Attribute_EnumerateAttributesByType` and `ACAPI_Attribute_GetFirstValidAttribute`. For each given attribute type it reports:
- `count`: the number of attributes;
- `firstIndex`: the first valid index, as Archicad reports it;
- `lastIndex`: the highest index in use;
- `freeIndexes`: the indexes in between that no attribute uses, for example those of deleted attributes.

Up to now a script had to read every attribute with `GetAttributesByType` and work this out itself. It is useful before creating attributes (where they go), and with index-based workflows such as reindexing. An unknown type gives an error item for that type only. Available from Archicad 27, where both functions start; older versions get an error.

Measured while testing: a new Layer takes the lowest free index, not the one after the highest. Three new Layers took 15, 25 and 28 in a project whose Layers go up to 600, and after one was deleted the next new Layer took its index again. The `freeIndexes` description says this for Layers.

The Surface texture location is the one member of `API_Attribute` that is allocated for the caller (`DisposeAttribute`). The enumeration callback frees it and sets it to null, so it is released exactly once whether or not the enumeration frees it as well.

## `ACAPI_Attribute_GetCurrentAttributeSetReader` → `notApplicable`

It returns a C++ `Modeler::IAttributeReader` that an add-on passes to its own 3D model export (`EXPGetModel`). What the reader can read the attribute commands already return: surface colors and textures, pens, fills, line types and building materials. Its texture data holds only the image name, not the picture. So there is nothing new a JSON command could return. It goes into the `notApplicable` items of `tools/api_coverage_rules.json` with that reason.

## Tested on Archicad 29 (macOS, German UI), 17/17

The truth is `GetAttributesByType`. The project was saved first and reopened without saving afterwards.

| call | result |
|---|---|
| all 12 attribute types in one call | one item per type, in the order asked |
| each type (Layer, Line, Fill, Composite, Surface, LayerCombination, ZoneCategory, Profile, PenTable, MEPSystem, OperationProfile, BuildingMaterial) | count, first and highest index and the free indexes equal what `GetAttributesByType` gives (for example Layers: 174, 1–600, 426 free) |
| 3 new Layers | they took the 3 lowest free indexes |
| the middle one deleted | its index is free again, count +2, highest index unchanged |
| one more new Layer | it took the freed index |
| `["Fill", "Quatsch", "Line"]` | an error item for the unknown type only |

Not checked:
- **Archicad 27, 28 and 30, Windows:** not run here, so the CI builds cover them.
- **Archicad 25/26:** they return the "needs Archicad 27" error by design.
- **Which index new attributes of the other types take:** measured for Layers only.

Also includes the example `get_attribute_indexes.py`. This branch starts from the build fix that was merged as #1647. It merges cleanly with `main`.

title: ModifyMEPRoutingElements, CreateMEPRoutingElements: an unresolved mepSystemId answers success and clears the route's MEP system
body:
`ModifyMEPRoutingElements` and `CreateMEPRoutingElements` answer success when `mepSystemId` doesn't name an MEP system attribute, and they leave the route with no MEP system at all.

Tested on AC29 (5101, Mac) with 1.7.4 plus some open PRs. The code involved is the same on `main`. I used a piping route on Cold Water:

| `mepSystemId` passed | Reply | System read back with `GetMEPRoutingElements` |
|---|---|---|
| `{"guid": "<Hot Water guid>"}` | success | Hot Water (correct) |
| `{"attributeId": {"guid": "<Hot Water guid>"}}` | success | `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` |
| `{"guid": "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555"}` | success | `00000000-…` |
| `CreateMEPRoutingElements` with `{"attributeId": {"guid": …}}` | placed | `00000000-…` |

The wrapped form is easy to send by mistake, because it's the shape `GetMEPRoutingElements` returns for `mepSystemId`. The schema (`#/AttributeId`) doesn't allow it, but the input isn't rejected. `GetGuidFromObjectState` then finds no `guid` and gives `APINULLGuid`. `GetAttributeIndexFromGuid` returns index -1, and `SetMEPSystem` is called with it anyway (`MEPCommands.cpp`, `ModifyMEPRoutingElementsCommand::Execute` and `CreateMEPRoutingElementsCommand::Execute`).

`CreateMEPPhysicalSystems` and `ModifyMEPPhysicalSystems` already guard against this:

```cpp
if (mepSystemId != nullptr && systemCategory == ACAPI_CreateAttributeIndex (-1)) {
    executionResults (CreateFailedExecutionResult (APIERR_BADID, "The 'mepSystemId' is not an MEP system attribute."));
    continue;
}
```

The same check before `SetMEPSystem`, in both routing commands, would give a failed result and leave the route unchanged. In `CreateMEPRoutingElements` it would need to come before `Place`.
author: BenTristem

title: PR review: allow Write of the summary file, by relative and absolute path
body:
Five reviews of fork pull requests (#1711, #1703, #1702, #1649, #1634) ended without a summary comment, so no verdict was recorded. The review's own log says why: its Write of `.review-context/summary.md` was refused, and the prompt only allows posting the summary from that file. The fallback step then had no file to post. The allowed tools named only `Edit(./.review-context/summary.md)`.

It is frequent. Of 8 reviews I dispatched by hand on 2026-11-01 (#1711, #1703, #1702, #1649, #1634, #1668, #1624, #1573), 5 hit it (#1703, #1702, #1634, #1668, #1573) on both sonnet and opus. Each run's final message says the Write was refused and contains the finished review text, which was lost. Bot pull requests suffer too: the steward counts each such run as an empty review and hands the pull request over after `BOT_PR_MAX_EMPTY_REVIEWS` (#837 got `needs-maintainer` that way).

This change:
- adds `Write(./.review-context/summary.md)` to the allowed tools;
- adds both `Edit` and `Write` for the file's absolute path under `${{ github.workspace }}` (`//` absolute form), in case the model writes by absolute path;
- asks for the relative path in the prompt.

All four rules name that one file only, so the review gets no wider write access.

It touches `.github/`, so it needs a maintainer merge.

title: CreateMEPRoutingElements, CreateMEPElements: no way to set the home story; elements land on the active story plus a per-file offset
body:
`CreateMEPRoutingElements` and `CreateMEPElements` have no `floorIndex`, and the home story they pick doesn't follow z. It follows the active story, shifted by an offset that differs from file to file. So you can't put MEP elements on the right story without first measuring that offset per file.

Tested on AC30 (3001, Mac) with 1.7.0 and on AC29 (5101, Mac) with 1.5.9. Read back with `GetDetailsOfElements.floorIndex`. Routes and terminals behave the same.

**AC30, project from an office template, stories -15…17.** After `ChangeWindow {"windowType":"FloorPlan","storyIndex":N}` (confirmed with `GetStories.actStory`):

| Active story N | z of nodes / position | Home story read back |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 3.0 and 20.0 | -6 |
| 2 | 3.0 and 20.0 | -4 |
| 3 | 3.0 | -3 |
| 5 | 3.0 and 20.0 | -1 |
| 9 | 3.0 | 3 |

With the 3D window in front and story 1 active, the same calls gave story 1.

**AC29, a different file, stories -2…6.** With the 3D window in front and story 1 active, every route and terminal landed on story 5.

z doesn't change the home story. Polylines read back z exactly as sent, so I couldn't tell whether z is stored as absolute or relative to the home story. `Get3DBoundingBoxes` gives a degenerate box for MEP elements, with z = the story level.

**Request:** an optional `floorIndex` on `CreateMEPRoutingElements` and `CreateMEPElements`, with z kept absolute like the other non-wall create commands (#448). Or failing that, the home story chosen from z. The home story and story offset should also come back somewhere (`GetMEPRoutingElements` / `GetMEPElementDetails`).

Workaround for now: per file, place one probe after `ChangeWindow`, read `floorIndex`, compute the offset, then set active story = target − offset before each storey's batch.
author: UGEFONTAN

title: ConnectMEPElements: tees only work with the main as routingElementId and the branch node exactly on the main's centreline; document it and report why
body:
Tees with `ConnectMEPElements` do work, but only under two conditions that the schema doesn't mention. Breaking either one gives the same generic error (`-2130313112 "Failed to connect the elements."`), so it looks as if branches aren't supported.

Tested on AC29 (5101) with 1.5.9 and on AC30 (3001) with 1.7.0, ventilation and piping routes.

**1. Direction.** The command calls `ConnectLogically` on `routingElementId`, with `connectToId` as the parameter. Graphisoft's docs for `RoutingElement::Modifier::ConnectLogically` say the begin or end node of the *parameter* route must lie on the *caller* route. So for a tee the main must be `routingElementId` and the branch `connectToId`:

| `routingElementId` | `connectToId` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| branch | main | error, in every geometry tried |
| main | branch | `splitRoutingElementId` + `createdBranchId` (tee with 3 physically connected ports) |

The current field descriptions ("The routing element to connect." / "The MEP element or routing element to connect to.") read naturally the wrong way round for a tee.

**2. Precision.** The branch node has to lie exactly on the main's centreline. On a diagonal main, a branch start rounded to 0.1 mm sat 0.019 mm off the line and the connect failed. The same branch with an unrounded, projected start point connected. The branch angle didn't need to be exactly 90°.

**Requests:**
- State the direction in the schema descriptions. Something like: "for a tee pass the main route as `routingElementId` and the branch route as `connectToId`; the branch's first or last node must lie on the main".
- When `ConnectLogically` fails, say which condition failed (domain, MEP system, no intersection), or at least mention the direction.
- Optionally snap a node that lies within a small tolerance (e.g. 0.1 mm) onto the target segment before connecting. Coordinates from IFC/CSV sources are rarely exact.
author: UGEFONTAN

title: Add CreateMEPTakeOffs: place Take-Offs on routing segments (TakeOffDefault::Place)
body:
There's no way to place MEP **Take-Offs**: a grille, or a small branch, tapped straight into the side of a duct or pipe segment. `GetMEPElements` already reports the type (`"TakeOff"`), but no create command exists.

The C++ API has it: `ACAPI::MEP::CreateTakeOffDefault (Domain)` and `TakeOffDefault::Place (segmentId, distanceFromSegmentBegin, rotationAngle)`. See the Take-Off-Placement-Example in the DevKit's `MEP_Test` example, `PlaceElements.cpp`.

**Use case:** rebuilding a Revit MEP model (IFC2x3) as native Archicad MEP. In one model, 31 duct segments carry a third port, where a grille or a small branch sits directly on the segment without a tee. Without Take-Offs these can only be modelled as a full tee with a separate stub, which is bulkier and isn't what the source model has. Or left for manual work.

**Request:** a `CreateMEPTakeOffs` command, e.g.
`takeOffsData[]: { segmentId: ElementId, distance: number, rotationAngle?: number, domain?, crossSectionWidth?, crossSectionHeight?, crossSectionShape? }` → `elements: ElementIdsOrErrors`.
`ConnectMEPElements` / `GetMEPPorts` should then work on the Take-Off's free port, so a terminal or a branch route can be attached to it.
author: UGEFONTAN

title: CreateMEPElements: choose the library part (or favorite), size and MEP system for terminals, accessories and equipment
body:
`CreateMEPElements` can only place the tool-default object for `Terminal`, `Accessory`, `Equipment` and `Fitting`. There's no way to choose the library part, its size, or its MEP system. With many terminals or pieces of equipment, every one has to be swapped by hand afterwards.

Observed on AC29 (5101) with 1.5.9 and AC30 (3001) with 1.7.0. A ventilation `Terminal` always comes out as the default diffuser: one round Ø200 port and a footprint of about 0.72 m. Its port reads the default system (`Fresh Air [Ductwork]`) through `GetMEPPorts`. The input on `main` has `type`, `domain`, `position`, the orientation vectors and `defaults` (insulation only). There's no `mepSystemId`, `libraryPartName`/`favoriteName` or size.

**Use case:** a Revit MEP model with 346 air terminals (grilles, nozzles, perforated diffusers of several sizes), 174 valves and manifolds, and about 280 pieces of equipment (fan coils, fire dampers, pumps, AHUs). Position and orientation can be matched through the API, but not the product or the connection size.

**Requests (any of these helps):**
- `favoriteName` on `CreateMEPElements`, the same as the other create commands since #529, so office favorites carry the library part and size.
- Optional `libraryPartName` (or the library part's GUID) plus GDL parameter overrides.
- Optional `mepSystemId` (plain `{guid}`), applied to the element's ports. Or document `ModifyMEPPorts` as the way to do it.
- Optional port size for the connection (`width`/`height`/`shape`).
