title: Set the reference ID of sections: CreateSections id/favoriteName, ModifySections (#1662)
body:
Part of #1662: the section reference ID requested in [this comment](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/issues/1662), in the split the issue bot proposed there.

## What changes

**`CreateSections`**
- `id` (optional) is the reference ID shown in the section marker and in the Project Map. A `/` splits it between the start and the end marker, as in the Section settings. Without it, a section keeps taking the ID of the Section tool defaults, as before.
- `favoriteName` (optional) bases the new section on a Section favorite, marker included. Fields given explicitly (`name`, `id`, `depth`, `floorIndex`) override the favorite. Afterwards the Section tool defaults are restored, so the next section placed by hand is not affected. A favorite of another element type, or an unknown name, gives an error for that item only.

**`ModifySections`** (new) changes `name` and/or `id` of existing Sections **and Elevations** by `elementId`. Only the fields given are written. Each item gets its own result: an error for a hidden or locked layer, for an element that is not a section or elevation, for an unknown GUID, or when neither field is given.

**`RenameNavigatorItem` fix**: renaming a section or elevation through its Project Map item currently fails on Archicad 29 with "Archicad did not apply the new name".

**Grasshopper**: the `CreateSections` component gets `IDs` and `FavoriteNames` inputs. They are appended after the existing inputs, so saved definitions keep their wiring.

## Why `ACAPI_Element_ChangeParameters`
On Archicad 29, `ACAPI_Element_Change` returns `NoError` for `cutPlane.segment.cutPlName` / `cutPlIdStr` but leaves both unchanged. That is why `RenameNavigatorItem`'s read-back reported a refused rename.

The DevKit's own `Element_Test` (`Element_Modify_ChangeParameters.cpp`) changes the ID of sections and elevations with `ACAPI_Element_ChangeParameters`, and that does apply them. `ModifySections` uses it and reads the values back, so an unapplied value is reported instead of a false success. `RenameViewpointElement` uses it for sections and elevations. Details and worksheets keep `ACAPI_Element_Change`.

`ChangeParameters` also returns `NoError` on a hidden or locked layer, so `ModifySections` checks the layer first.

## Notes
- **No reference ID in a Section favorite.** A favorite (from the palette or from `CreateFavoritesFromElements`) carries no reference ID. After `ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults` a new section has an empty ID; this is the "no ID at all" case reported in the issue. With `favoriteName`, pass `id` as well.
- **Applying the favorite.** The favorite goes through the same helper as for doors and windows (`ChangeDefaultsExt` with the marker). That alone put the section on layer 1 instead of the favorite's layer, so for sections the favorite is applied once more the way `ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults` does it. The resulting layer and ID now match that path exactly; the test checks this.
- **Version.** New command registered with `1.8.1`, the version `main` carries after this week's 1.8.0 release.

## Tested
Archicad 29 (macOS, AC29 build), live, 26/26 checks:

| Area | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| CreateSections `id` | IDs arrive in `GetDetailsOfElements` (`idStr`) and the Project Map (`prefix`) | ✅ |
| | without `id`: ID of the tool defaults as before | ✅ |
| | `id` with `/` is stored | ✅ |
| ModifySections | name + id, only id (name kept), only name (id kept), Project Map updated | ✅ |
| | hidden layer: "The section was not changed, because its layer is hidden." | ✅ |
| | nothing to change / wall / unknown GUID: error for that item only, the next item succeeds | ✅ |
| RenameNavigatorItem | section renamed through its Project Map item (failed before) | ✅ |
| CreateSections `favoriteName` | favorite applied; same layer and ID as `ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults` | ✅ |
| | `favoriteName` + `id`: own ID | ✅ |
| | next item without favorite gets the tool defaults; defaults restored after the command | ✅ |
| | wall favorite / unknown favorite: error for that item only, defaults unchanged | ✅ |
| Example | `Examples/modify_sections.py` runs | ✅ |

Not tested: Elevations (the test project has none; the code path is the same segment), Windows build (CI), and the Grasshopper inputs (no .NET SDK here; CI builds the plugin).

@kipisti, could you test this on your elevation run?

title: Align property reads and writes for numeric round-tripping
body:
Aligns the property getter’s output with the setter’s expected input, allowing numeric values to be read, transformed, and written back without project-unit conversion or locale normalization.

Adds optional useSIUnits to GetPropertyValuesOfElements, defaulting to false to preserve existing behavior.

When enabled, numeric scalars and list items return locale-independent decimal strings without project display rounding, grouping separators, suffixes, or scientific notation. Measurements use SI units, with degrees for angles to match the existing setter. The response structure remains unchanged.

Extends SetPropertyValuesOfElements to accept semicolon-separated numberList and integerList values, preserving order and duplicates. Empty strings produce empty lists. Invalid items, integer overflow, and non-finite values reject the property write without partially applying the list.

Handle failed property reads before result lookup, preventing crashes for invalid property IDs and reject non-editable properties before parsing or writing, across all property types.

Text, boolean, enumeration, and measured-list setter behavior remains unchanged. Read-only properties remain read-only.

The macOS add-on builds of the 1.8.0 release failed twice in `Code sign and notarize` after Apple had already accepted the notarization: `xcrun stapler staple` lost its connection to Apple while downloading the ticket (`NSURLErrorDomain Code=-1005 "The network connection was lost."`, `The staple and validate action failed! title: Walls / Walls_API GH components: every element fails with "elementId is missing"
body:
# Walls / Walls_API components: every element fails with "elementId is missing"

## Problem
The Walls and Walls_API Grasshopper components (Design Tools) report
"elementId is missing" for every element when Refresh is pressed.
Execute and Create show the same message, because both re-read the elements at the end.

## Cause
`ElementToolComponent.ReadDetails` and `ElementToolComponent.KeepElementsOfTool`
(`grasshopper-plugin/TapirGrasshopperPlugin/Components/DesignToolsComponents/ElementToolComponent.cs`)
call `GetDetailsOfElements` with:

```json
"elements": [ { "guid": "..." } ]
```

The command expects:

```json
"elements": [ { "elementId": { "guid": "..." } } ]
```

`GetDetailsOfElementsCommand::Execute` (`archicad-addon/Sources/ElementCommands.cpp`) does
`element.Get ("elementId")`, gets null, and answers each entry with
`APIERR_BADPARS` "elementId is missing".

The other calls in the same file (Modify command, `SetDetailsOfElements`,
`SetPropertyValuesOfElements`) already wrap the guid in `elementId` correctly.

## Proposed fix
In both places (`ReadDetails`, `KeepElementsOfTool`) build each item as
`{ "elementId": { "guid": ... } }` instead of `{ "guid": ... }`.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Place a Walls (or Walls_API) component.
2. Connect `ElementGuid` to an existing wall.
3. Press Refresh.
4. The `Errors` output and the component message show "elementId is missing".

## Expected
The wall's settings are read into the JSON outputs and `Errors` is empty.

title: GetReservationStatusOfElements says "Free" even for elements I reserved

title: SetMEPPreferenceTableRows, AddMEPPreferenceTableRows: branch row values land on the first row with the same reference ids, ignoring branchAxisAngle
body:
On a branch (tee) table, `SetMEPPreferenceTableRows` writes the values to the wrong row whenever two rows share the reference ids and differ only in the angle. The values land on the first row with those reference ids, and the reply is still `{"success": true}`. `AddMEPPreferenceTableRows` with `values` does the same: it adds the row, then writes the values to the older row. Elbow tables are fine.

Tested on AC29 (5101, Mac) with 1.8.1. I used the stock Piping branch table "Sewage Inside" of the default template, which has rows `{100, 50, 45°}` (index 12) and `{100, 50, 87°}` (index 16):

```json
{"tableId": {"guid": "<Sewage Inside>"},
 "rows": [{"key": {"mainAxisReferenceId": 100, "branchAxisReferenceId": 50, "branchAxisAngle": 87},
           "values": {"description": "probe", "length": 0.151}}]}
```

| Row | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 12 (45°) | length 0.17, description "" | length **0.151**, description **"probe"** |
| 16 (87°) | length 0.15, description "" | unchanged |

- **Reading works:** `GetMEPPreferenceTableRows` with the same keys reads each row correctly, and so does the row list of `GetMEPPreferenceTables`.
- **Deleting works:** `DeleteMEPPreferenceTableRows` with the 87° key removes the 87° row.
- **Adding:** `AddMEPPreferenceTableRows` with the 87° key and values added the row at index 16 with all values 0, and wrote the values to the 45° row.

**Cause:** Tapir builds the same `Key`, with `branchAxisAngle`, for the getter and the setter. So it looks like `PipeBranchPreferenceTable::Modifier::Set…ByKey` ignores `branchAxisAngle` in AC29, while `Get…ByKey`, `IsRowValidByKey` and `DeleteRowByKey` honour it. `MEPDuctBranchPreferenceTable.hpp` has the same `…ByKey` setters; I haven't tested them.

**Proposed fix:** for branch tables, find the row's index the way `GetExactPreferenceTableRowAngle` already does (main and branch reference ids plus angle). Then call the index setters of the Modifier: `SetMainAxisDiameter (index, …)`, `SetBranchAxisDiameter`, `SetLength`, `SetBranchOffset`, `SetConnectionLength` and `SetDescription`. They exist in the AC29 DevKit. `AddMEPPreferenceTableRows` can use the index that `AddNewRow` returns. If no row matches, give a failed result for that row.
author: BenTristem

title: ModifyMEPRoutingElements: set the connection style before the flange size
body:
Found while testing the MEP routing commands on Archicad 29 for macOS (DevKit 29.3000, Tapir 1.8.1).

**The bug.** I ran `ModifyMEPRoutingElements` with `{"connectionStyle": "Flanged", "flangeSize": 0.03}` on a pipe route whose style was SimpleBody. It returned "Failed to modify the routing element.", and `GetMEPRoutingElements` then read `connectionStyle: "Flanged"` with `flangeSize: 0`. `SetFlangeSize` runs before `SetConnectionStyle`, and the DevKit refuses a flange size unless the segment is already Flanged. This PR sets the style first.

**Two description fixes, from the same tests:**
- `flangeSize`: Archicad 29 returns it for every connection style (0 on a SimpleBody pipe, 0.03 on a SimpleBody duct), not only on flanged segments.
- `MEPConnectionStyle`: the pipe settings dialog shows SimpleBody as "Welded", and `"Welded"` is refused on a pipe route. A pipe set to Welded in the dialog therefore reads SimpleBody.

So far this has only been built on macOS (AC29, Xcode). I'll add the Archicad test result here once it's run.

title: Columns: read and write the veneer of the segments (#1044)
body:
Closes #1044.

## What changes
The veneer of a column lives on its **segments** (`API_ColumnSegmentType::venType`, `venThick`, `venBuildingMaterial`; the same in the AC25–AC30 DevKits), so it is read and written there.

- **`GetDetailsOfElements`**
  - A Column's `segments` each get a `veneer` object: `{type, thickness, buildingMaterialId}`.
  - A `ColumnSegment`'s own details get the same object.
  - `type` is `Core`, `Finish` or `Other` (`API_VeneerTypeID`; there is no `Insulation`).
  - `buildingMaterialId` is reported only for a segment whose cross section is a building material, because Archicad uses it only then (DevKit comment).
- **`CreateColumns` / `ModifyColumns`**
  - Both take an optional `veneer` object (new shared schema `ColumnVeneer`).
  - It is applied to all segments, like the existing cross-section fields (`width`, `depth`, `buildingMaterialId`, …).
  - Only the given fields change, and `thickness: 0` removes the veneer.
- **Errors:** an unknown `type` or `buildingMaterialId` fails that item before anything changes. `ModifyColumns` checks it before it touches the column.
- `SetDetailsOfElements` is not extended: `ModifyColumns` is the column modifier, and the Grasshopper `CreateColumns`/`ModifyColumns` components already pass extra keys through their JSON input.
- New example `Examples/column_veneer.py`.

## Tested
Archicad 29 (macOS), live, in a project whose column layer is hidden; all layers were shown for the test.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `CreateColumns` with `veneer: {Other, 0.10, buildingMaterialId}` → read back identical (the acceptance case of the issue) | ✅ |
| Archicad computes it: `GetQuantitiesOfElements` `veneerVolume` 0.48 m³ | ✅ |
| `ColumnSegment` details show the veneer | ✅ |
| `ModifyColumns` type + thickness (building material kept), building material only | ✅ |
| `thickness: 0` removes the veneer, `veneerVolume` back to 0 | ✅ |
| Unknown type: error, the `height` in the same item is not applied; unknown building material: error | ✅ |
| `CreateColumns` with an unknown type: error for that item | ✅ |
| `Examples/column_veneer.py` | ✅ |

Not tested: multi-segment columns (the loop is the same as for the cross-section fields), Windows (CI).

Note for testing: on a hidden or locked layer `ModifyColumns` fails as before ("Failed to modify column …"), not specific to the veneer.

title: Place Detail and Worksheet markers, change their name, ID and clip polygon (#1377)
body:
Part of #1377: parts 1 and 2 (placing markers, changing their settings). Part 3, a stricter result of `SetDetailsOfElements`, is a maintainer decision and is left out.

## What changes
New commands, in the shape of `CreateSections` (which places a Section marker together with its viewpoint):

- **`CreateDetailMarkers` / `CreateWorksheetMarkers`**
  - Place a Detail or Worksheet marker in the current floor plan, section or elevation, with `linkData.sourceMarker`, so Archicad creates the new Detail or Worksheet viewpoint with it, as the tools do.
  - Per item:
    - `clipPolygon` (required, ≥3 points) with optional `clipPolygonArcs`.
    - `markerCoordinate`: where the marker symbol goes; default is the first polygon point.
    - Optional `angle`, `name`, `id` (a `/` splits it over the marker's two lines) and `floorIndex`.
  - Defaults come from the tool settings (`ACAPI_Element_GetDefaultsExt` with the main marker), as in the DevKit's `Element_Test` (`Do_CreateDetail`, `Do_CreateWorksheet`).
- **`ModifyDetailMarkers`** changes `name`, `id` and `clipPolygon` of existing Detail and Worksheet markers:
  - **Name and ID** go through `ACAPI_Element_ChangeParameters`, as `Element_Test` does for Details and Worksheets. `ACAPI_Element_Change` returns `NoError` for them but leaves them unchanged (Archicad 29), the same finding as for sections in #1731.
  - **Clip polygon** goes through `ACAPI_Element_Change` with the polygon memo.
  - **Layer check:** both calls return `NoError` on a hidden or locked layer and change nothing, so the layer is checked first. The error names it ("… because its layer is hidden").
  - **Read-back:** a value Archicad did not take is reported instead of a success.
- **`GetDetailsOfElements`: Worksheet ID fixed.** A Worksheet element reports an empty `detailIdStr` while its viewpoint has the ID, so `detailName`/`detailIdStr` of Details and Worksheets are now read from the viewpoint's database (`ACAPI_Window_GetDatabaseInfo`), falling back to the element.
- **No `basePoint`.** Archicad puts the base point (the origin of the new viewpoint) at the center of the clip polygon's bounding box whatever `pos` is given, so it is not offered as an input.
- New example `Examples/detail_markers.py`.

`RenameNavigatorItem` had the same Element_Change problem for Details and Worksheets. That fix is in #1731, next to the same fix for Sections and Elevations.

## Tested
Archicad 29 (macOS), live, in a project whose Detail/Worksheet tool layers are hidden.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Hidden tool layer: `ModifyDetailMarkers` → "The marker was not changed, because its layer is hidden." | ✅ |
| `CreateDetailMarkers`: name, ID, clip polygon, base point = center, `linkData.referredPMViewPoint` | ✅ |
| Project Map: new Detail item with name and ID | ✅ |
| `CreateWorksheetMarkers`: name, ID, angle; marker symbol at `markerCoordinate` | ✅ |
| Project Map: new Worksheet item | ✅ |
| `ModifyDetailMarkers` name + ID / ID only, read back and in the Project Map | ✅ |
| `ModifyDetailMarkers` clip polygon (4 → 5 points) | ✅ |
| Nothing to change / a column: error for that item only, the next item succeeds | ✅ |
| `Examples/detail_markers.py` | ✅ |

Not tested: markers placed in a section or elevation window (the code does not depend on the window type), Windows (CI). No Grasshopper components yet.

title: CopyElementsToDatabase: copy 2D elements into another database (#819)
body:
Part of #819: 2D elements; Drawings are left out (see below).

## What changes
New command **`CopyElementsToDatabase`**, in the design from the issue:

- **Parameters:**
  - `elements` and `targetDatabaseId` (a worksheet, detail or layout; see `GetDatabases`).
  - Optional `sourceDatabaseId`; default is the current database.
  - Optional `offset` (`x`, `y`).
- **Response:** one `elementId` or error per input element, in order (`ElementIdsOrErrors`).
- **How it copies:**
  - Each element is read with `ACAPI_Element_Get` and `ACAPI_Element_GetMemo (APIMemoMask_All)` in the source database, then created from that data with `ACAPI_Element_Create` in the target. So every field is kept without per-type code.
  - The offset is applied afterwards with the drag `MoveElements` uses.
  - All of this runs in one undoable command, and the starting database is restored.
- **Supported types:** Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hotspot, Text, Hatch, and Labels not associated with an element.
  - Associated labels, dimensions and all other types are refused per element ("cannot be copied to another database").
- **Databases never opened:** a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened (e.g. one just made by `CreateWorksheets`) cannot be made the current database (`APIERR_BADDATABASE`). Such a database is opened once through its Project Map item, as `ChangeWindow` does it (#1602), and the starting window is brought back.
- **Drawings are not copied.** Created from their own data, a copied Drawing lost the link to its source view: `drawingScale` 1 instead of 0.005. `CreateDrawings` notes that a wrong `drawingGuid` can terminate Archicad during creation. So a Drawing is refused like the other unsupported types. Copying Drawings needs the `CreateDrawings`/`ChangeDrawingLink` path and is a follow-up.

## Tested
Archicad 29 (macOS), live.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| 2 new worksheets (target never opened); polyline, text, hatch and circle copied with offset (10, 0) | ✅ |
| Copies are in the target worksheet; geometry moved by the offset; text content kept | ✅ |
| Originals unchanged; the current window is still the floor plan afterwards | ✅ |
| Without `sourceDatabaseId` and `offset`: copied in place; unknown GUID: error for that item only | ✅ |
| Wall: "Elements of type Wall cannot be copied to another database." | ✅ |
| Drawing (layout → layout): refused, nothing created | ✅ |

Not tested: labels, splines and hotspots (same generic path), Windows (CI). No Grasshopper component yet.

title: Fields with a $ref schema aren't validated: a wrapped preference table guid is ignored with success
body:
Tested on Archicad 29 for macOS (DevKit 29.3000) with Tapir 1.8.1 (main at 537ca638).

**What happens.** A preference table id sent as `{"guid": "…"}` instead of a bare string is accepted. The command answers success and the id is ignored:
- `CreateMEPRoutingElements`, with `preferenceTableId` and `defaults.routingNode.elbow.preferenceTableId` wrapped: the route is placed with the tool's default segment and elbow tables. The same call with bare strings uses the tables given.
- `ModifyMEPRoutingElements`, with `branchPreferenceTableId` wrapped: success, and the branch table stays as it was.

**Why it gets through.** Archicad doesn't seem to validate fields whose schema is a `$ref` to the common definitions; inline schemas are validated. Probes with `GetMEPPreferenceTables` and `GetMEPRoutingElements`:

| Input | Schema | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `"includeFittingTables": "yes"` | inline `boolean` | rejected (4002, rule `type`) |
| `"domain": "NotADomain"` | `$ref` enum | accepted; the command's own check reports it |
| `"elements": [{"elementId": "not-an-object"}]` | `$ref` ElementId | accepted |
| `{"elementId": {"guid": "…", "x": 1}}` | `$ref` with `additionalProperties: false` | accepted |

A command that reads such a field with `os.Get (name, string)` takes the failed `Get` as "not given", so the wrong shape is ignored without an error. The wrapped `mepSystemId` in #1718 (PR #1719) is the same pattern.

**Suggestion:** where a command reads a `$ref`'d field, treat "present but unreadable" as an error for that item. Or check the shared shapes (Guid, ElementId, AttributeId) in one helper in `CommandBase`. Accepting both the bare and the wrapped guid would also be friendly, since the wrapped form mirrors `elementId` and `mepSystemId`.
author: BenTristem

title: Roofs: read and set the planes of each pivot polygon edge (#569)
body:
Part of #569: the per-edge roof planes asked for in [this comment](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/issues/569), now read **and** written. The rest of the issue, the Roof case of `GetDetailsOfElements`, is already on `main`.

## What changes
**Reading:** `GetDetailsOfElements` reports for a multi-plane roof a new `pivotEdges` array:
- One item per edge of the pivot polygon; item i belongs to the edge from vertex i to vertex i + 1 of `pivotPolygonOutline`.
- Each item has `levels`, the roof plane of that edge on each level, with `angle`, `eavesOverhang` and `angleType` (`Sloped` or `Gable`, from `API_RoofSegmentData::angleType`).

**Writing:** `ModifyRoofs` takes `pivotEdges` in the same shape:
- Only the given fields change, and an item without `levels` keeps its edge.
- Errors, where an invalid item changes no edge: a wrong item count, more levels than the roof has, or `pivotEdges` together with `polygonOutline` (which makes new edges).
- The Grasshopper `ModifyRoofs` component passes it through its `AdditionalSettings` input; its description now says so.
- New example `Examples/roof_gables.py` turns a hip roof into a gable roof. `Examples/roof_details.py` prints the `angleType` of each edge.

Notes from the DevKit and from testing:
- **Indexing:** `memo.pivotPolyEdges` is indexed like the pivot polygon's coords, as the DevKit's `Plan_Dump` reads it. So index 0 and the closing vertex of each contour carry no edge (`GetPivotEdgeIndices`, shared by both sides). Read as a plain array, it gave an empty first item and a duplicated last one.
- **The closing vertex holds a copy of the first edge, and Archicad takes that copy.** A gable written only to the first edge was not applied, while edges 2–4 worked. The first edge of each contour is now mirrored to its closing vertex, and every combination applies.
- **Memo mask:** the DevKit comment names a memo mask `APIMemoMask_PivotPolygon`, but that mask is not defined. The edges come with `APIMemoMask_AdditionalPolygon`.
- **Left out: `memo.roofEdgeTypes`.** Archicad 29 returned `Undefined` for every edge of every roof tried, so it would not tell gables apart.

## Tested
Archicad 29 (macOS), live, 15/15:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Hip roof (6 × 5 m, 25°, overhang 0.45): exactly 4 `pivotEdges`, 1 level each, 25° / 0.45 / `Sloped` | ✅ |
| Single-plane roof: no `pivotEdges` | ✅ |
| `ModifyRoofs`: edge 1 → `Gable`, edge 3 → 35° / 0.6; read back, edges 2 and 4 unchanged | ✅ |
| Archicad changes the roof: volume 8.98 → 9.44 m³ | ✅ |
| Gable on each edge alone and in combinations: applied | ✅ |
| Right edge: gable on the long bottom edge raises the roof to 1.51 m (limited by the 3 m hips), on the short right edge it stays 1.28 m | ✅ |
| Wrong item count / more levels than the roof / with `polygonOutline` / unknown `angleType` (schema) / single-plane roof: errors, nothing changed | ✅ |
| `Examples/roof_gables.py` → Sloped, Gable, Sloped, Gable; `Examples/roof_details.py` | ✅ |

Not tested: roofs with more than one level, and pivot polygons with holes (the edge mapping follows the pends, as in `Plan_Dump`).

@NavyBlueCanoe, this should let you read and set gable edges without marking them by hand. Could you try it on one of your roofs?

title: ModifyMEPPreferenceTables: add anglesToAdd; read whole-number angles
body:
Elbow and branch rows can only use an angle that is in the domain's angle set. `ModifyMEPPreferenceTables` could delete angles but not add them. This adds `anglesToAdd` (Archicad 29+), which runs before the tables are changed so that new rows can use the new angles. The result is reported as `addedAngles`.

It also fixes angle lists given as whole numbers: `[87]` read as 0 and was refused, while `[87.0]` worked. The reader that handles both, `GetDoubleList`, moves from `ElementCreationCommands.cpp` to `CommandBase`, where the curtain wall patterns also use it.

**Tested** in Archicad 29 on macOS (DevKit 29.3000):
- `anglesToAdd: [72]` adds the angle.
- `anglesToAdd: [87.5, 67.5]` adds both; elbow rows at 87.5 were then set and read back.
- `anglesToDelete` removes an angle again.
- `CreateCurtainWalls` with whole-number pattern sizes still works.
author: BenTristem

title: SetMEPRoutingParameters: make route preference table changes stick
body:
In Archicad 29, the preference table setters of a route's segment and node defaults answer OK, and inside the command the new table even reads back. Once the command ends, though, the route's segments and nodes can keep their old tables, so `SetMEPRoutingParameters` reported success for a change that never happened. Seen with elbow, transition and segment tables.

This sets a changed table on the route's defaults and on each segment and node, injects it into them, and then reads it back. An item whose segments or nodes still have the old table now fails with a message saying so, and setter errors carry Archicad's own text.

**Tested** in Archicad 29 on macOS (DevKit 29.3000), on a fresh route and on routes in a real project where the previous build answered success but kept the old table:
- An elbow table and a segment table change read back on the route and on every node.
- A transition table change on a four-node route read back on the route and all four nodes, minutes later too. Archicad replaced the fittings to match the new table.

title: Expose publisher set output path: read it, and change it without publishing
body:
### API functions

ACAPI_Navigator_GetNavigatorSet

### What should Tapir let you do?

I keep one project per building and need each publisher set to point to that building's folder, so that later publishing from Archicad goes to the right place.

1. **Read:** a command that returns each publisher set's saved output (`name`, `path`, `host`, `dirName`) through `API_NavigatorSet` with `wantsExtraInfo`.

__APIEXPORT GSErrCode ACAPI_Navigator_GetNavigatorSet (API_NavigatorSet* navigatorSet, Int32* index = nullptr);

title: Favorites: apply and read Drawing favorites, whose settings Archicad refuses to give out (#652)
body:
Fixes #652.

## What Archicad does

`ACAPI_Favorite_Get` refuses every Drawing favorite. Tested live on Archicad 29 with a favorite made from a Drawing by `CreateFavoritesFromElements`:

- **Every request is refused.** I tried all 64 combinations of the optional fields (memo, properties, classifications, category values, marker, sub-elements), including none at all. Each one returns `APIERR_REFUSEDCMD`, and Archicad still fills in the element type as Drawing. A Wall favorite works in the same session.
- **The error code.** `-2130312312` is `APIERR_REFUSEDCMD` (`APIErrorStart + 904`), not `APIERR_REFUSEDPAR` (905) as decoded in the issue.
- **The C++ Favorite manager can't build an element either.** For the same favorite, `GetOldElementDefault`, `GetMemo`, `GetElementMarker`, `GetMemoMarker` and `GetSubElements` all fail with "Failed to create API_Element".
- **What the Favorite manager does give (Archicad 29 and newer):**
  - `GetElementType`, `GetProperties`, `GetClassifications`, `GetElemCategoryValues` and `GetParentFolder` all work.
  - `GetElementDefault().SetAsArchicadDefault()` works. It is what `ApplyFavoriteToToolDefault` already uses, and a Drawing placed afterwards takes over the favorite's settings.

## What this changes

When `ACAPI_Favorite_Get` returns `APIERR_REFUSEDCMD`, a new helper, `GetFavoriteWithoutElementSettings`, fills what the Favorite manager gives: the element type, folder, properties, classifications and category values. The element settings and memos stay empty. Before Archicad 29 nothing changes.

- **`ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults`** makes such a favorite the tool's defaults through `ElementDefault::SetAsArchicadDefault`. It then applies classifications, category values and properties as before.
- **`GetFavoriteDetails`** returns the element type, classifications, properties and category values.
- **`GetFavoriteSettings`** returns the element type and folder, with empty `parameters` and `subElements`.
- **`ApplyFavoritesToElements`** can't apply such a favorite to elements, because there are no element settings to apply. It now says so and points to `ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults`, instead of "Failed to get favorite".

There are no schema changes, and the code changes are all in `FavoritesCommands.cpp`.

New example: `drawing_favorite_defaults.py`. It captures a Drawing turned by 30° as a favorite, applies it to the defaults, and places a Drawing without an angle, which comes out at 30°.

## Tests

Live on Archicad 29 (macOS), with two Drawing favorites made from Drawings turned by 0.5 rad and 0, one of them in a folder:

| # | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `CreateFavoritesFromElements` from two Drawings, one into folder `TapirTest/Sub` | ok |
| 2 | `ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults` with favorite A → a new Drawing without an angle is turned by 0.5 | ok |
| 3 | Same with favorite B → 0 | ok |
| 4 | B and A in one call → both succeed, the new Drawing is turned by 0.5 | ok |
| 5 | A Wall favorite and a Drawing favorite in one call | ok |
| 6 | `GetFavoriteDetails` of a Drawing and a Wall favorite | ok |
| 7 | `GetFavoriteSettings` of the Drawing favorite: elementType `Drawing`, folder `["TapirTest", "Sub"]` | ok |
| 8 | `ApplyFavoritesToElements` with a Drawing favorite → the new message | ok |
| 9 | An unknown favorite still fails with its own error (`APIERR_BADNAME`) | ok |
| 10 | `DeleteFavorites` cleans up | ok |

10/10. The new example also ran live and prints 30.0 degrees.

title: Version fixes after 1.8.0: GetElementsInDrawOrder check from 1.8.1, review reads main's version
body:
Two small fixes for problems that came from 1.7.4 shipping as **1.8.0** (the month's first release).

## 1. Run the GetElementsInDrawOrder check from 1.8.1

#1571 fixes the `GetElementsInDrawOrder` crash and sets `minTapir` of its runner check to 1.7.4. But 1.7.4 shipped as 1.8.0 before #1571 was merged, so the released 1.8.0 still has the crash and the fix first ships in 1.8.1. This raises `minTapir` in `archicad-addon/Test/checks/get_elements_in_draw_order.json` to `1.8.1`, so the community test runner doesn't crash testers' Archicad on 1.8.0 add-ons.

## 2. The review checks the registered version against `main`'s `package_info.json`

`claude_pr_review.yml` checks out the pull request's base commit, which is the base of its last update and can be weeks older than `main`. Its `tools/package_info.json` then names a version that has already shipped, and the review asks for that version. After the 1.8.0 release this sent #1094, #1517 and #963 to `needs-maintainer`: the review asked for 1.7.4, and the fix run (correctly) kept `main`'s 1.8.1.

The context step now fetches `main` and saves its current `tools/package_info.json` as `.review-context/main_package_info.json`, and logs the version. The prompt's version rule and its rule for judging the steward's replies point the review at that file instead of the checked-out copy. The review still never checks out or runs the pull request's code. The YAML parses.

This touches `.github/`, so a maintainer has to merge it.

title: ImportFavorites returns success but changes nothing in a Teamwork project (Tapir 1.8.0 / 1.8.1, Archicad 28)
body:
**Environment**
- Archicad 28 (Windows 11), Tapir add-on 1.8.0. Re-tested with the 1.8.1 test build from PR #1739: same result.
- Project: Teamwork (BIMcloud). The same steps on a solo project work as expected.

**Steps**
1. Reserve the Favorites set: `ReserveLockableObjectSet` with `objectSetName: "Favorites"`.
   `GetLockableObjectSetStatus` then reports `Editable`.
2. `ExportFavorites` with `{"path": "<folder>"}` (default "prefs" format). This works: one XML per favorite plus an `AddPars` folder.
3. Copy one exported favorite (its XML and its AddPars files) to a new folder and change one value, e.g. `<OffsetX>2.18</OffsetX>` → `3.30`.
4. Run `ImportFavorites` with `{"path": "<that folder>", "targetFolder": [<original folder names>], "conflictPolicy": "Overwrite"}`.
5. Run `ExportFavorites` again and compare.

**Expected**
The favorite is overwritten. The new value shows in the export and in the Favorites palette.

**Actual**
- `ImportFavorites` returns `{}` with no error.
- The favorite is unchanged: the value is still 2.18, and the number of favorites is the same as before.
- These variants give the same result:
  - without `targetFolder`;
  - with `importFolders: true`.
- `format: "xml"` is refused: "The xml format requires Archicad 29 or newer."

**Solo project comparison**
With the same steps and the same call on a solo (non-Teamwork) project in the same Archicad session:
- the value changes as expected;
- importing the original file restores it.

**Notes / questions**
- Is importing favorites into a Teamwork project supported with the "prefs" format on Archicad 28?
- If the import is skipped, could the command return an error (or a list of skipped/imported items) instead of an empty success? That would let scripts detect it without re-exporting.
author: Hcf-Archi

title: Fix leaks, overflows and missing undo scopes found by a DevKit review
body:
I compared the API calls of the existing commands with Graphisoft's example add-ons (`Examples/` of the AC30 DevKit) and with the header remarks of every supported DevKit (AC25–30). This PR fixes the clear deviations. Each fix is small and leaves the commands' JSON interface unchanged. Things that need Archicad to confirm are not changed here; they are listed for the maintainer separately.

## Memory the API allocates that was never freed
- **Surface texture locations.** `ACAPI_Attribute_Get` allocates `material.texture.fileLoc` for `API_MaterialID` (AC30 `ACAPinc.h` remarks; `Attribute_Test.cpp:34`, `Override_Test.cpp:832`). These places now call `DisposeAttribute` (MigrationHelper):
  - `GetAttributeGuidFromIndex` / `GetAttributeIndexFromGuid` (CommandBase.cpp)
  - `GetAttributeIdFromIndex` / `GetAttributeIndexFromAttributeId`, `GetSurfaces` and `CreateAttributesCommandBase::Execute` (AttributeCommands.cpp)
  - the two `ResolveAttributeIndex` helpers (ExtendedElementCommands.cpp, ElementCreationCommands.cpp)
- **3D surface components.** `CollectSolidBodies` (ElementCommands.cpp) now deletes `umat.mater.texture.fileLoc` of the `API_UmatID` components it reads.
- **Library part location.** `ACAPI_LibraryPart_Get` allocates `location`; `AddLibPartBasedElementDetails` (GetDetailsOfElements) now deletes it.
- **GDL parameters.** `GetGDLParametersOfElements` used the `ACAPI_LibraryPart_GetParams` handle without checking the result. It indexed the handle past its size and never disposed of it. It now initializes the variables, checks the result, bounds the index, and calls `ACAPI_DisposeAddParHdl` (as `Element_Basics.cpp:438` does).
- **Line and fill definitions.** When CreateLines / CreateFills overwrite an existing attribute with new items, the handle taken from `ACAPI_Attribute_GetDef(Ext)` was replaced without being freed. It is now freed first, as CreateFills already did for `sfill_SolidFills`.
- **Model view options.** `GetModelViewOptions` and `FindModelViewOption` now free `gdlOptions` after each Get with `ACAPI_FreeGDLModelViewOptionsPtr` (`Environment_Control.c:1592`).
- **Navigator views.** `GetViewSettings`, `SetViewSettings` and `SetViewRotation` now free what `ACAPI_Navigator_GetNavigatorView` allocates for views with custom settings. They use the existing `FreeNavigatorView` helper (`APIdefs_Navigator.h` remarks; `NavigatorPalette.cpp:507`).

## Buffer overflows on long input strings
User strings were copied unbounded into fixed `[API_UniLongNameLen]` arrays. They are now truncated the way the code already does elsewhere (`CopySectionString`). The places:
- `docu_UName` in CreateWindows/CreateDoors, CreateObjects/CreateLamps and the marker library part search
- `cutPlName` / `cutPlIdStr` in CreateInteriorElevations
- `SetParamValueString` wrote its terminator one past `uStr[API_UAddParStrLen]`

## Writes outside an undo scope
`CreateGraphicalOverrideRule` and `CreateGraphicalOverrideCombination` changed the override rules and combinations without an undo scope. Both now run in one `ACAPI_CallUndoableCommand`, as `Override_Test.cpp:979` and the newer `GraphicOverrideCommands.cpp` do. Responses and error messages are unchanged.

## Ignored error
`SetGeoLocation` writes back the struct it read. When `ACAPI_GeoLocation_GetGeoLocation` failed, it would have overwritten every field not given with zeros. It now returns a failed result.

## Verification
Nothing was compiled locally; the build checks compile every Archicad version. In Archicad:
- run GetSurfaces, GetDetailsOfElements, GetGDLParametersOfElements, GetViewSettings and GetModelViewOptions repeatedly: same output as before, without memory growth;
- run CreateGraphicalOverrideRule: Edit > Undo now removes the rule;
- run GetViewSettings on a view with custom layers and a custom pen set. This is the case to watch: `FreeNavigatorView` also frees `layerStats` and `pens`, which the DevKit doesn't document as caller-owned.

title: API coverage: IFC classification details, GetFavoriteDefaults, Teamwork online status
body:
Part of #1538.

## What changes

### GetIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements (Archicad 28+): more fields
- `referencedSource` now also has `editionDate`, `description` and `location` on Archicad 28+, from `IFCAPI::Classification::GetEditionDate`, `GetDescription` and `GetLocation`. Until now these were only returned on Archicad 25–27.
- New `relAssociatesClassificationName` on each reference (Archicad 28+, `ClassificationReference::GetIfcRelAssociatesClassificationName`). It is left out when empty.
- New `sort` on each reference (Archicad 29+, `ClassificationReference::GetSort`).
- The shared schema `ElementIFCClassificationReference` and the registered description are updated to match.
- Grasshopper: the component gets new `Sorts` and `RelationNames` outputs, appended after `ErrorMessages` so saved definitions keep their wires. The edition date, description and location outputs no longer say "Archicad 25–27 only".

### New command GetFavoriteDefaults {favorites} (Archicad 29+)
- Reads the element default stored in each Favorite through `ACAPI::Favorite::Favorite`: `GetOldElementDefault`, `GetMemo`, `GetElementMarker`, `GetMemoMarker` and `GetSubElements`.
- For each Favorite it returns:
  - `elementType`, `layerIndex` and `elementId` (the ID stored in the memo);
  - `folder`, `libPart` and `parameters`;
  - `marker`, for every element type that has one;
  - `subElements`: each with `elementType`, `libPart`, `parameters` and `subTypes` (the names of the `API_SubElementType` flags set).
- A Favorite that is not found, or whose default can't be read, gets an error item. The memos are disposed as `Favorite_Test` does.
- `GetFavoriteSettings` is not touched; #1753 and #1557 change it.
- Archicad 25–28 get "This command requires Archicad 29 or newer."
- Grasshopper: new `GetFavoriteDefaults` component in Favorites. Example: `Examples/get_favorite_defaults.py`.

### GetTeamworkProjectInfo / GetTeamworkStatus: `isOnline` fix
`isOnline` now comes from `ACAPI_Teamwork_IsOnline`. Before, it came from `ACAPI_Teamwork_HasConnection`, which the DevKit documents as "is a Teamwork project", so an offline Teamwork project was reported as online. Archicad 25–26 use `ACAPI_TeamworkControl_IsOnline` through a new `MigrationHelper.hpp` define.

## Not done, and why
These go to the coverage rules file in a separate PR:
- `ACAPI_Property_CheckPropertyExpressionString`: it crashes Archicad 29 on an unknown function name and gives wrong results. It was tested and removed from #1146 before that PR was merged.
- `ACAPI_Element_ChangeMore` (#1226): a measured test there showed no speed gain over the Modify*/SetDetailsOfElements commands. It also returns one error code for the whole batch.
- `FavoriteManager::RenameFavorite` and `Favorite::GetPreviewImage`: maintainers deliberately kept `RenameFavorites` and `GetFavoritePreviewImage` on the C API (8dbbe7b9).
- `ACAPI_Teamwork_SendReleaseCommentMail`: needs the ids of a Teamwork reserve interface that the add-on registered for its own dialog.
- `APIIo_AreCuttingPlanesVisibleID`: `Get3DCutawayStatus` already reads this flag through `ACAPI::CuttingPlane::AreCuttingPlanesVisible` (AC28+) and the C API (AC25–27).
- `ACAPI::ElementBase::GetElemId`: Tapir always gets ids from its input, so using this would be a fake use.
- `ACAPI_AddOnObject_CreateUniqueObject` / `ExistsObject`: `SetProjectData` creates its objects in one batch with `CreateUniqueObjectMore`, and the lookups by name already report missing objects.
- `ACAPI_Database_GetDatabasesForType(s)`: they return the same lists `GetDatabases` already reads per type, and `GetDatabasesForTypes` loses each database's type.

## To verify in Archicad
- **IFC (Archicad 28, 29, 30):** run `Examples/get_ifc_classification_references_of_elements.py` on a project with classified elements.
  - Compare `editionDate`, `description`, `location` and `sort` (29+) with the IFC Project Manager.
  - Check that `relAssociatesClassificationName` is what you expect.
- **Favorites (Archicad 29, 30):** run `Examples/get_favorite_defaults.py` with Window, Curtain Wall and Stair favorites.
  - Check `layerIndex` and `elementId` against the Favorite's settings.
  - The Window favorite should have its `marker`, and the curtain wall's sub-elements should list frames and panels.
  - Watch for crashes: the memo handles come from the Favorite manager.
- **Teamwork:** in a Teamwork project, run `Examples/teamwork_project_info.py` and `Examples/teamwork_status_and_rights.py` once online and once offline. `isOnline` should be false when offline.

Every call was checked against the AC25–30 headers and the DevKit's `Favorite_Test`. Nothing was compiled locally; the build checks compile every version. `tools/generate_addon_docs.py` parses every schema.

title: Add CreateLibraryPartFromElements, InterpretGDLScript3D and GetGDLUserGlobals
body:
Part of #1538 and #1580 (section 4, `CreateLibraryPartFromElements`). Also covers #1400 in the smaller form described there: the API gives no line-level diagnostics.

Fixes #1400

The three new commands are in a new `LibraryPartCreationCommands.cpp`, so this doesn't conflict with the open PRs that edit `LibraryCommands.cpp`; CMake picks the file up with its GLOB_RECURSE. They are registered with version 1.8.1. Each has an example (`Examples/<CommandName>.py`) and a Grasshopper component in the Library group.

### `CreateLibraryPartFromElements` (Archicad 25–30)
Input: `{name, elements, parentId?/parentName?, folder?, libraryFolder?, overwrite?, placeable?, scripts?: {master?, 2D?, 3D?, parameter?}, comment?, keywords?}`

It makes a new library part whose 2D symbol is a copy of the given 2D drawing elements. The steps follow the DevKit's `LibPart_Test` example:
1. Each element is read with `ACAPI_Element_Get` + `ACAPI_Element_GetMemo`. Only lines, polylines, arcs, circles, splines, fills, texts and hotspots are accepted: the DevKit allows only 2D drawing elements in a symbol.
2. Inside one `ACAPI_CallUndoableCommand`: `ACAPI_LibraryPart_SetUpSect_2DDrawHdl`, then `ACAPI_Element_Create` for each copy, with its guid, group guid and hotlink guid cleared.
3. `ACAPI_LibraryPart_GetSect_2DDrawHdl` is always called once SetUpSect has succeeded, even after a failed create.
4. `ACAPI_LibraryManagement_OverwriteLibPart (overwrite)`, `ACAPI_LibraryPart_Create`, then `OverwriteLibPart (false)`.
5. The text sections are written with `NewSection` / `WriteSection` / `EndSection`:
   - the comment and the keywords;
   - the master script, always, even when empty;
   - the 2D, 3D and parameter scripts.
6. `AddSection (API_Sect2DDraw)` adds the symbol.
7. A and B are calculated from the symbol, as the header says happens when the 2D drawing handle is given:
   - `GetSect_ParamDef` is called with the 2D drawing handle;
   - then `SetDetails_ParamDef` with `fixSize = false` and `autoHotspot = true`;
   - then `AddSection (API_SectParamDef)`.
8. `ACAPI_LibraryPart_Save`. The location is deleted before and after Save, as the example does.

Every memo and handle is disposed on every path. After a failed section the part is still saved, as the DevKit requires, and the error says so.

**Where the part is saved:**
- By default in the embedded library, optionally in a subfolder `folder`.
- Or in `libraryFolder`, an absolute path. If that folder isn't a loaded library, it is added with `ACAPI_LibraryManagement_AddLibraries` first, and it stays added.
- Without `overwrite`, Archicad gives the part a unique name, and the response returns the real one.

Response: `{name, fileName, unId, guid, index, a, b}`.

**Differences from the issue's design:**
- It also takes `parentId` / `parentName`, like `CreateLibraryParts`. The DevKit example finds the Model Element parent through the `BuiltInLibrary` module, and it couldn't be confirmed that the add-on can link that module.
- A and B come from the 2D drawing handle, not from a bounding box computed by hand.
- Text that isn't pure ASCII is written with `AddSection (UniString)`, because the DevKit doesn't say how `WriteSection` encodes non-ASCII bytes.

### `InterpretGDLScript3D` (Archicad 25–30)
Input: `{script?, libraryPartName?}`. It uses `ACAPI_LibraryManagement_InterpretGDLScript3D`, and `APIAny_InterpretGDLScript3DID` on AC25/26.
- It runs the given script, or a loaded part's master script followed by its 3D script.
- With `libraryPartName`, the part's default parameters are used (`ACAPI_LibraryPart_GetParams`).
- Response: `{success, error?, elementCount, boundingBox3D}`.
- The API gives only an error code, with no GDL message or line number. `elementCount` tells a script that ran but produced nothing apart from one that built a model.

### `GetGDLUserGlobals` (Archicad 28+)
It copies the GDL globals with `ACAPI_LibraryManagement_CreateCopyOfGdlUserGlobalsHandle`, lists them (name, type, value) with the existing `GDLParametersToObjectStates`, and destroys the copy with `DestroyCopyOfGdlUserGlobalsHandle`. That helper exists only from AC28, so the command needs AC28; Archicad 25–27 get a "requires Archicad 28" error.

### Not done, and why
These go to the coverage rules file:
- `ACAPI_Element_SetEmptyHoleUnId`: it takes the signature of a library part subtype the add-on registers itself, and Tapir registers none.
- `ACAPI_LibraryPart_GetBuiltInLibpartUnId`: it returns the id of a library part compiled into the calling add-on, and Tapir has none.
- `ACAPI_LibraryPart_RegisterAll`: `ACAPI_LibraryPart_Save` already registers the parts it creates.
- `APIDo_LoadLibrariesID` (AC25/26): `SetLibraries` / `AddLibraries` already set the library list on AC25/26 through `APIEnv_SetLibrariesID`.

### Please verify in Archicad
- **`Examples/CreateLibraryPartFromElements.py`:**
  - the object appears in the embedded library under `TapirExamples`, and its 2D symbol shows the square and the circle;
  - A and B are about 1 × 1, and placing the object works;
  - run it a second time to check that `overwrite` replaces the part;

- **Undo after `CreateLibraryPartFromElements`:** check whether it leaves an empty undo step or touches the plan.
- **`libraryFolder`:** with a folder that isn't loaded yet, it is added and the part ends up in it.

- **`Examples/GetGDLUserGlobals.py`** on AC28+.

title: API coverage: SetPens, module data, shape primitives, spline distances, 3D style, view settings, image conversion
body:
Uses the Archicad C API functions the API coverage checklist still listed as unused. Every new command:
- is registered with version 1.8.1;
- has an example `Examples/<CommandName>.py`;
- has a Grasshopper component, which reuses an existing icon.

### New commands
- **SetPens** (Attribute, AC27+, `ACAPI_Attribute_ModifyPen`): the writing twin of GetPens.
  - Changes the color, width and description of the given pens in effect in the current window.
  - Each pen is read with `ACAPI_Attribute_GetPen`, and only the given fields change.
  - One execution result per pen, all in one undo step.
  - In Teamwork the PenTables set must be reserved first.
  - GH: `SetPens` (Attributes).
- **GetShapePrimitivesOfElements** (Element, AC25+): uses `ACAPI_DrawingPrimitive_ShapePrims` (`ACAPI_Element_ShapePrims` on AC25/26), plus `ACAPI_Drawing_IsMarkerDrawingEnabled` / `ChangeMarkerDrawingEnabled`.
  - Same output as GetDrawingPrimitivesOfElements, but drawn with plain ShapePrims instead of ShapePrimsExt with dontClip/allStories.
  - The optional `includeMarkers` draws or leaves out window/door markers, drawing titles and the like. Archicad's own setting is restored afterwards.
  - Needs the floor plan as the current database.
  - GH: `GetShapePrimitivesOfElements` (Element Details).
- **GetModulData / StoreModulData / DeleteModulData** (Project Data, AC25+, `ACAPI_ModulData_GetList/GetInfo/Get/Store/Delete`): named UTF-8 text blobs saved in the project under Tapir's MDID, each with a `dataVersion`.
  - The empty name is the default section.
  - GetModulData without `names` lists everything, and with `includeContent: false` it reads only the info.
  - The API documents Store as a non-undoable modifier, so these commands open no undo step.
  - GH: `GetModulData`, `StoreModulData`, `DeleteModulData` (Project).
- **GetSplineMaxDistances** (Element, AC25+, `ACAPI_ProjectSetting_GetSplineMaxDist`): the largest distance of given 2D coordinates from segment `segmentIndex` (0-based) of a Spline element.
  - It uses the spline's fit points and Bezier handles from its memo, as the DevKit's Goodie_Functions example does.
  - GH: `GetSplineMaxDistances` (Element Details): a points tree, one branch per spline.
- **SetCurrent3DStyle** (Navigator, AC25+, `ACAPI_View_SetCurrent3DStyle`): makes a style listed by Get3DStyles the current one.
  - The name is checked first, and the change runs in an undoable command, like Change3DStyles.
  - GH: `SetCurrent3DStyle` (Navigator).
- **StoreViewSettings** (Navigator, AC25+, `ACAPI_View_StoreViewSettings`): `action: Store | Restore`.
  - The two calls must come in pairs and can't be stacked.
  - GH: `StoreViewSettings` (Navigator).
- **ConvertImages** (Application, AC25+, `ACAPI_Conversion_ConvertPicture` / `ConvertMimePicture`): converts base64 images.
  - Bitmap, GIF, TIFF, JPEG and PNG on both sides go through ConvertPicture.
  - If either side is a MIME type, both are passed as MIME types to ConvertMimePicture.
  - GH: `ConvertImages` (Utilities).

### Changed command
**GetCutPolygonsOfElements** used to return "not supported" before AC28. It now has an AC25–27 path:
- The element's bodies come from `ACAPI_ModelAccess_Get3DInfo` (fbody..lbody); `bodyIndex` is the index within the element.
- Each body is cut with `ACAPI_CuttingPlane_GetCutPolygonInfo` (`ACAPI_3D_GetCutPolygonInfo` on AC25/26).
- Building materials are left out on that path; the schema already allows that.
- The current database is switched to the floor plan when needed, as Get3DGeometryOfElements does.
- The AC28+ path and the schema are unchanged.

The AC25/26 mappings of the new calls are in `MigrationHelper.hpp` (pre-27 block), following the AC27 `ACAPI_MigrationHeader.hpp`.

### Not done, and why
These go to the coverage rules file:
- `ACAPI_Element_GetPropertyValue`: GetPropertyValuesOfElements already uses `ACAPI_Element_GetPropertyValuesByGuid`.
- `ACAPI_Database_GetDBUnIdFromGuid` / `GetGuidFromDBUnId`: they convert to the old userId/databaseId pair, which no JSON command or official command takes.
- `ACAPI_Body_AddPolyNormal`: `ACAPI_Body_AddPolygon` computes the normal when 0 is passed, as the morph body builder does.
- The AC25–27-only items:
  - the AC25 analytical load geometry and profile vector image (AC25 loads are a different element model);
  - the drawing link ids and `UnIdToGuid` (AC25/26);
  - the IFC difference generator, removed in AC28, whose state can't pass between JSON calls.
- `GetCurrentAttributeSetReader` (#1717 marks it skipped), `GetComponents_Obsolete` (replaced by #1019) and `ElemComponent_GetPropertyValue(s)` (AC25/26; #1019 adds the component commands).

### Overlap with open PRs
- #1754 (schema refactor) touches the same .cpp files. This PR only adds new code there. `GetShapePrimitivesOfElements` builds its response from the static `DrawingPrimitiveSchema`, which #1754 replaces with `#/DrawingPrimitive`, so whichever merges second must switch to the `$ref`.
- The new registrations in `AddOnMain.cpp` and the `MigrationHelper.hpp` block may conflict textually with other branches.

### Please verify in Archicad
- **SetPens (AC27+):**
  - pen 5 changes and is restored, and index 1000 gives an error item only;
  - check Undo;
  - in Teamwork, check with and without the reservation.
- **GetShapePrimitivesOfElements:**

title: MEP: ports and tool defaults on Archicad 27, flexible segment polylines, new ModifyMEPElements
body:
Part of #1538. Uses most of the Archicad MEP C++ API that Tapir didn't use yet: new optional inputs and outputs on existing commands, plus one new command. It covers the items #1538 planned that its merged parts (#1539–#1542) left out.

### `GetMEPPorts` (now Archicad 27+)
- **Archicad 27 (new):** each port is read through the port class of its domain, including `CableCarrierPort::Get` for cable carrier ports. It returns `isConnected` (`PortBase::IsConnected`), plus the outer diameter and wall thickness of piping and ventilation ports.
- **Archicad 30:** the ports are listed with `ElementBase::GetPorts`, and `portId` comes from `PortBase::GetElemId`.
- **Archicad 28–29:** unchanged. The port reading moved into a helper, `CreateMEPPortDetails`.
- **Schema:** `isPhysicallyConnected` is no longer required, because Archicad 27 doesn't report it.

### `GetMEPToolDefaults` (now Archicad 27+)
- **Archicad 27 (new):**
  - Route default: built from `CreateRoutingElementDefault`, `CreateRoutingSegmentDefault`, `CreateRoutingNodeDefault`, `CreateBendDefault` (the elbow's radius factor) and `CreateTransitionDefault`.
  - Flexible segment default: Ventilation only.
  - Terminal, accessory, fitting and equipment defaults: library part and insulation; for ports, only the index and the shape (`ElementDefault::GetShapeOfPort`).
- **Every version:**
  - New `rigidSegment` (`CreateRigidSegmentDefault`). Shape and size only on Archicad 27–28, because Archicad 29 removed those getters; insulation on every version.
  - New `branch` (`CreateBranchDefault`).
  - `insulationThickness` on all element defaults.
- **Archicad 30:** new top-level `electricalPanel`: library part, panel name, circuit name prefix, circuit id style and `circuitDefaultCount` (`ElectricalPanelDefault::GetCircuitDefaultCount`).

### `PlaceMEPFlexibleSegments` (Archicad 28+)
- New `polyline` input, used instead of `controlPoints`: alternating `{type: "Line", begin, end}` and `{type: "Spline", controlPoints}` parts, with optional `startDirection` and `endDirection`.
- It goes through `FlexibleSegmentDefault::PlacePolyline`. Archicad places polylines in the Piping domain only.
- `controlPoints` is no longer required.
- The new shared schema `MEPFlexibleSegmentPolyline` describes the parts.

### `GetMEPElementDetails` (Archicad 28+)
Flexible segments also return their `polyline` (`FlexibleSegment::GetPolyline`).

### New `ModifyMEPElements` (Archicad 27+)
Input: `{elements: [{elementId, anchorPoint?, orientation?, libraryPartId?, controlPoints?, polyline?, width?, height?}]}`
- **Placement** of terminals, accessories, equipment, fittings and flexible segments: anchor point, orientation and library part, through `ModifiableElement::Get`.
- **Flexible segments:** control points (`FlexibleSegment::Modifier::SetControlPoints`), polyline (`SetPolyline`, Archicad 28+), width and height.
- **Errors and undo:**
  - The whole call is one undo step, with one execution result per element.
  - Each item's fields are checked against its element before anything changes, so an item with a field that doesn't fit its element changes nothing.
  - The one exception: Archicad shows that it didn't find a `libraryPartId` only after the placement changed. That item's error says the element keeps its library part and that its other changes were made.
- **No elbow radius factor:** the first version of this PR also set the elbow radius factor on Archicad 27 through `Bend::Modify`. That call doesn't compile against the Archicad 27 DevKit, because its `Bend::Modifier` doesn't derive from `ACAPI::ModifierBase`. So it's not part of the command. From Archicad 29 the radius factor is set with `SetMEPRoutingParameters`.

### Grasshopper
- New `ModifyMEPElements` component in the MEP group, covering all 9 parameters of the command. It reuses the `ModifyMEPRoutingElements` icon. `ControlPoints` is a point tree with one branch per element, and `Polylines` are JSON texts.
- The `GetMEPPorts` component's `IsConnected` output falls back to `isConnected` on Archicad 27.
- #1764 adds the `PlaceMEPFlexibleSegments` and `GetMEPToolDefaults` components. Whichever of the two PRs merges second should name the new `polyline` input in that component.

### Example
`archicad-addon/Examples/ModifyMEPElements.py` (new).

### Not done, and why
These are in the coverage rules file (#1768):
- The 8 `Duct/PipeBranchPreferenceTable::Modifier::Set…ByKey` setters (AC29/30): #1740 (b2640243) found that they ignore the branch angle and change the first row with the same reference ids. That is why `SetMEPPreferenceTableRows` sets branch rows by index.
- `ACAPI::MEP::PhysicalSystem::Create` (AC29/30): it gives no id for the new system. `SystemGroup::Modifier::Add`, which `main` already uses, returns the new id directly.
- `ACAPI::MEP::Bend::Modify` (AC27 only): it doesn't compile against the Archicad 27 DevKit (see above).

### Overlap
No function that #1728 or #1747 edits is touched: `ApplyRoutingNodeDefaults`, `CreateMEPRoutingElements`, `ModifyMEPRoutingElements`, `CreateMEPElements` and the routing parameter file. The new command is appended at the end of `MEPCommands.cpp/.hpp`.

### Please verify in Archicad
- **Archicad 27:**
  - select a flexible segment and a terminal, then run `ModifyMEPElements.py`;
  - check that `GetMEPPorts` gives `isConnected`, and that `GetMEPToolDefaults` gives the route, elbow, rigid segment, branch and port shapes;
  - `width` 0.3 changes the flexible segment.
- **Archicad 28–30:** run `ModifyMEPElements.py`:
  - the terminal moves and its ports are listed;
  - the ventilation flexible segment takes the new control points and width;
  - the Piping polyline segment is placed, its `polyline` is read back, and the modified polyline is applied;
  - `GetMEPToolDefaults` gives `rigidSegment` and `branch`, and on Archicad 30 also `electricalPanel.circuitDefaultCount`.
- **Archicad 30:** `GetMEPPorts` still lists the same ports, now through `ElementBase::GetPorts`.
- **Open question:** whether `GetPolyline` returns anything for a flexible segment placed with control points only. The code leaves `polyline` out when the call fails.

Nothing was compiled locally; the build checks compile every version.

title: Examples: one clean script per command, in a folder per command group; tests and workflows moved out; examples in the docs
body:
`archicad-addon/Examples/` mixed simple examples with long workflows and tests. This PR makes it one short, clean example per Tapir command, moves the tests and workflows into their own folders, and shows each command's example in the command reference.

## New layout
- **`archicad-addon/Examples/<Group>/<CommandName>.py`:** exactly one example per registered command (701, all but the developer command `GenerateDocumentation`), in one folder per command group, named as in the docs.
  - The 23 folders: Application, Project, CustomData, Element, ElementGrouping, Favorites, Property, Classification, Attribute, IFC, Library, Teamwork, Navigator, GraphicOverride, IssueManagement, RevisionManagement, DesignOptions, Keynote, ProjectData, MEP, Analytical, SolidElementOperation, ScriptUI.
  - The two MEP groups share `MEP/`.
  - Each folder has a small `aclib.py` that loads the shared `Examples/aclib`, so `python Examples/MEP/GetMEPPorts.py` works.
- **Each example:**
  - starts with a docstring: what it does, what the project needs, and the Archicad version where the command has one;
  - is short top-level code using `aclib` only;
  - takes ids from the open project instead of hard-coded GUIDs;
  - for Set commands, reads the old value, sets, reads back and restores;
  - deletes what it created, and writes files only to temporary folders.
- **`archicad-addon/Workflows/`:** 18 multi-command task scripts, moved unchanged with `git mv` (e.g. `sync_attributes_gui.py`, `zone_clip.py`, `create_library_parts.py`, `detail_markers.py`).
- **`archicad-addon/Test/Scripts/`:** 141 test scripts, moved unchanged. This includes every script that has a recorded output in `Test/ExpectedOutputs/`, under the same name, so the regression tests keep their goldens. `Examples/manual_tests/` became `Test/Scripts/manual/`.
- **Deleted:** 286 old single-command scripts without recorded outputs, which the new examples replace. They stay in git history.
- **Clean-up:** 14 hard-coded `sys.path.insert(r"D:\ONEDRIVE\...")` lines from one developer's machine are gone. The repository root path in `generate_documentation.py` is fixed for its new depth.

## Examples in the docs
Each command of the reference (`docs/archicad-addon`) gets a collapsed **Example** section.
- When opened, it fetches `archicad-addon/Examples/<Group>/<CommandName>.py` from `main` on raw.githubusercontent.com.
- It shows the script's docstring as the description (escaped) and the rest highlighted with the page's bundled highlight.js, with a "View on GitHub" link.
- A command without an example shows "No example yet."
- Nothing of the scripts is copied into the docs. Only `renderer.js` and `style.css` change; the generated `command_definitions.js` is untouched.

## Tooling
- **`tools/check_examples.py` (new):** checks that every registered command has its example at the right path, that each example starts with a docstring and calls its own command, that every folder has its `aclib.py`, and that nothing else is in `Examples/`. `--report` prints counts. It passes on this branch: 701 of 701.
- **`tools/new_command.py`:** writes the starter example to `Examples/<Group>/<CommandName>.py` with a docstring, finding the group's name from `AddOnMain.cpp`.
- **`Test/test_examples.py`:**
  - runs `Test/Scripts/*.py` against their goldens as before;
  - smoke-runs every example, with goldens recorded on the first run in `ExpectedOutputs/Examples/<Group>/`;
  - skips the examples that can't run unattended on the test project, listed in `EXAMPLES_NOT_SMOKE_TESTED`: interactive input, project open/close/new/save, printing, publishing and rendering, consolidation dialogs, Teamwork and BIMcloud, the GDL editor, and the notification server;
  - keeps the quit script last;
  - no longer stops at a script that fails or times out;
  - runs only the scripts given on the command line, when names are given.
  - `record_expected_output.py` looks in both places.
- **Docs:** `CLAUDE.md` (layout, adding a command, testing), `archicad-addon/README.md`, the root `README.md`, and new READMEs in `Examples/`, `Workflows/` and `Test/Scripts/`.

## Please note
- **Not run in Archicad.** None of the 701 examples has run in Archicad yet. Each was checked statically: it compiles, and every property name in every command call exists in that command's resolved input schema. Please run `Test/test_examples.py` once; the first run records the example goldens.
- **Examples that leave something in the project** (their docstrings say so):
  - **Create examples whose element has no delete command:** `CreateLayoutSubset`, `Create3DStyles`, `CreateAddOnViewpoints`, the MEP system group and preference table examples.
  - **Changes with no way to read back the old value:** `SetAnalyticalGenerationSettingsToNoRule`, and `SetDefaultDesignOption`, which ends with the Main Model as default.
  - **Irreversible or needing extra files:** `DeleteGhostRecords` can't be undone. `ImportMarkupsFromPDF` and the project import examples need a file and stop with a message without one.
- **Open PRs that still add old-style examples** (`Examples/some_name.py`): `tools/check_examples.py` lists them, and they should be renamed to `Examples/<Group>/<CommandName>.py` with a docstring when they are merged.
- **Issue bot prompts:** `.github/workflows/claude_issue_triage.yml` (lines 329 and 786) still says "add a Python example under archicad-addon/Examples". That stays true, but it could point to `Examples/<Group>/<CommandName>.py` and `tools/check_examples.py`. I didn't change `.github/`.

Touches `tools/` and the docs viewer, so it needs a maintainer merge.

title: Run check_examples.py in the build check and point the bots to the new example layout
body:
Follow-up of #1769, built on its branch, so this diff only shows the follow-up. Once #1769 is merged, I'll retarget this PR to `main`.

The review of #1769 noted that nothing enforces the new layout. The issue bot would keep adding examples at the top of `Examples/`, and the test runner now ignores those silently. This PR closes that gap:

- **`archicad_addon_build_check.yml`:** the `generate_docs` job gets a step that runs `python3 tools/check_examples.py`. A PR fails the build check if it adds a command without `Examples/<Group>/<CommandName>.py`, an example without a docstring or that doesn't call its command, or any other script directly in `Examples/`. It is a step in an existing job, so the required check names don't change.
- **`claude_issue_triage.yml`** (the fix and next-part prompts): "add a Python example under archicad-addon/Examples" becomes "add its example as `archicad-addon/Examples/<Group>/<CommandName>.py` (a module docstring first, then short aclib code; `tools/check_examples.py` checks it and the build check runs it)".
- **`claude_pr_review.yml`:** the consistency rule names the example path.
- **`CLAUDE.md`:** the CI section mentions the new check, and the golden file name is corrected to `ExpectedOutputs/<name>.py.output` (the nit from #1769's review).

**Effect on open PRs:** after this merges, an open PR that still adds an old-style example (`Examples/some_name.py`) fails `generate_docs` until the example is renamed to `Examples/<Group>/<CommandName>.py`. For the issue bot's PRs, the steward's fix run does that from the failed check and the updated prompt. The `tools/check_examples.py` output says what to rename.

title: Examples: aclib prints nothing by default, no more debug = False in the examples
body:
The examples passed `debug = False` on 465 lookup calls, because `aclib.RunTapirCommand` printed every command, its parameters and its response by default. This makes quiet the default and removes the parameter from the examples.

### aclib (`archicad-addon/Examples/aclib/__init__.py`)
- `RunTapirCommand (command, parameters = None, debug = None)`: with no `debug`, it follows the module's new `printCommands`, which is `False`. `debug = True` still prints everything for one call. Errors are still printed, as before.
- New `aclib.PrintJson (value)`: prints a response as indented JSON, the format the old default used.
- `RunCommand` is unchanged: it was quiet by default already.

### Examples (701 files)
- All `debug = False` arguments are gone.
- An example whose main command relied on the old default to show its response now prints it: `aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('X', {...}))` (695 calls), or `aclib.PrintJson (x)` after `x = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('X', ...)` (34).
- Where the script already prints that result in its own words, nothing is added (36 places, plus 3 loops that print each item). For example, `GetAddOnVersion.py` is now `aclib.PrintJson (aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetAddOnVersion'))`.
- Lookup calls (finding a wall, reading a value to restore) print nothing, so running an example shows the result of its own command.

### Test scripts and workflows: output unchanged
`Test/Scripts/aclib.py` and `Workflows/aclib.py` set `printCommands = True` after loading aclib. These scripts keep printing every command as before, so the 76 recorded outputs in `Test/ExpectedOutputs/` still match. `Test/Scripts/manual/` uses the `Test/Scripts` loader. The examples' smoke outputs have not been recorded yet, so the first run records them in the new form.

### Keeping it clean
- `tools/check_examples.py` reports an example that passes `debug` to aclib.
- `tools/new_command.py` writes the starter example with `aclib.PrintJson`.
- `Examples/README.md` describes the quiet default.

### Checked
- `tools/check_examples.py` passes: 701 of 701.
- All examples compile.
- Against a mock Archicad:
  - `Application/GetAddOnVersion.py` prints just the response JSON;
  - a `Test/Scripts` script still prints `Command:` / `Parameters:` / `Response:` for every call.
- Not run in Archicad.

Open PRs that add examples with `debug = False` (#1761, #1765, #1766, #1767) will get the same clean-up when they're updated with `main`. `tools/check_examples.py` points those out.

Touches `tools/`, so it needs a maintainer merge.

title: Add the Complex Element Finder built-in script
body:
A new built-in script for the Tapir palette: `builtin-scripts/ComplexElementFinder.py`. It finds the elements that make a project heavy, highlights them, and can reduce the points of the ones it is able to rewrite.

## Finding
- **Outline points:** polylines, fills, slabs, roofs, meshes, zones and splines with more points than a limit (default 500), counted over the outline plus its holes. Read with `GetDetailsOfElements` (fields `id`, `type`, `floorIndex`, `details`).
- **3D polygons:** any element whose 3D model has more polygons than a limit (default 20,000), such as imported objects, morphs or detailed library parts. Read with `Get3DGeometryOfElements`, 20 elements per call, with progress in the status line. This check can be switched off because it is slow on large projects.
- **Scope:** current story, whole project or the selection, limited to elements whose layer is visible.
- **List:** Element ID, type, story, points, 3D polygons, and whether the element can be simplified. The worst offenders come first, ranked by how many times they are over the limit.
- **Highlight and select:** the found elements are highlighted in red and the rest dimmed, as in `OrthoWallFinder`; the highlight is cleared when the window closes. *Select in Archicad* selects the chosen rows, or all of them; a double-click selects one element.

## Simplifying (polylines, fills, slabs)
- **Algorithm:** Douglas-Peucker with a tolerance in mm (default 10), so no outline moves by more than the tolerance.
  - The ends of arcs, the ends of open polylines and at least three points of each ring are always kept.
  - Arc indices are remapped, including an arc on the closing edge.
  - A closed polyline stays closed.
- **Check before writing:** each simplified slab or fill outline goes through `RegularizePolygons` first. A shape that would no longer be exactly one polygon with the same number of holes, for example because it now crosses itself, is left unchanged and counted in the result.
- **Confirmation:** shows "from N to M points", says how far the outline may move, and warns that custom settings of removed slab edges are lost.
- **Writing:**
  - polylines and fills: `SetDetailsOfElements` (`coordinates`, `arcs`, `holes`);
  - slabs: `ModifySlabs` (`polygonOutline`, `polygonArcs`, `holes`).

  Both can be undone in Archicad. The list is refreshed afterwards.
- **Other element types** can only be found and selected. The script description says to reduce their curved-surface resolution or remodel them. Roofs are left alone because `ModifyRoofs` writes only the pivot polygon of multi-plane roofs. Zones are left alone because no command writes their outline.
- **Older add-ons:** the 3D count needs Tapir 1.7.2 and the slab and fill check needs 1.7.3. On older add-ons the script says so instead of failing.

## Testing
- **Geometry, no Archicad:**
  - a 2,000-point circle at 10 mm becomes 64 points (largest deviation 6.3 mm), and its hole loses its collinear point;
  - a 5,000-point near-straight polyline becomes 2 points;
  - a closed polyline with an arc in the middle and one on its closing edge keeps both arcs and stays closed;
  - duplicate points are removed;
  - a thin sliver never drops below 3 points.
- **The window, no Archicad:** run under Xvfb with Python 3.12 / Tk 9, with a fake Archicad answering the commands. *Refresh* lists 5 elements; *Simplify* writes the polyline and the fill with `SetDetailsOfElements` and the slab with `ModifySlabs` (9,000 → 130 points); the next refresh no longer lists them.
- **Not tested in Archicad.** Two things need a real Archicad: that `ModifySlabs` and `SetDetailsOfElements` accept the simplified outlines (slab with holes and arcs, fill with holes), and that `Get3DGeometryOfElements` is fast enough on a large project.

title: Add ModifyStairs: change the settings of existing stairs
body:
Fixes #824

## What it adds

`ModifyStairs`, a new command in Element Commands (registered as 1.8.1, Archicad 25–30). It changes existing Stair elements in place:

```json
{"stairsWithDetails": [{
  "elementId": {"guid": "..."},
  "flightWidth": 1.4,
  "treads": [{"role": "Run", "visible": true, "thickness": 0.04}],
  "risers": [{"role": "Run", "crossSection": "Slanted", "angle": 1.2}],
  "structures": [{"role": "Run", "side": "UnderSide", "structureType": "Monolith", "bottomType": "Smooth", "thickness": 0.18}]
}]}
```

- **Stair level:** `flightWidth`, `totalHeight`, `stepNum`, `riserHeight`, `treadDepth`, `treadDepthLocked`, `totalHeightLocked`, `finishVisible`.
- **Per part (`role` Run/Landing):** for treads, `visible`, `thickness`, `offset`, `nosingType`, `nosingValue` and `nosingSlant`; for risers, `visible`, `thickness`, `offset`, `crossSection`, `angle` and `position`.
- **Structures, per part and `side` (LeftSide/RightSide/UnderSide):** `visible`, `structureType` (Side/Monolith/BeamSupport/CantileveredSupport), `bottomType` (Stepped/Flat/Smooth), `thickness` and `horizontalThickness`.
- Only the given fields are written: each one sets its bit in the element mask. `ACAPI_Element_Change` gets no memo, so the baseline and the position stay as they are. One undoable command for the call and one execution result per stair. A non-Stair element or an invalid enum value gets an error item.

The approach is the DevKit's own: `Element_Test` `Do_Stair_Edit` (`Element_Modify_ModelElements.cpp`) changes `flightWidth` and `riser[Run]`/`tread[Run]` fields the same way. `Do_Change_ElemParameters` changes `treadDepth`/`treadDepthLocked`. The fields and enums of `API_StairType`, `API_StairTreadType`, `API_StairRiserType` and `API_StairStructureType` are identical in the AC25–AC30 headers, so the command needs no version guard.

Example: `Examples/Element/ModifyStairs.py`. It creates a stair, makes its flights monolithic with a smooth underside, reads the stair back and deletes it.

## Needs a check in Archicad

Not built or run here. Please check:
- Whether Archicad keeps a stair in place when only `stepNum`/`riserHeight`/`treadDepth` change, and how it re-solves the dependent values. The description says to read them back with `GetDetailsOfElements`.
- Whether the tread, riser and structure changes show on the placed subelements. The DevKit example suggests they do; a stair with per-flight overrides may behave differently.

`GetDetailsOfElements` returns only the stair-level fields, so the tread, riser and structure settings can't be read back by a command yet.

title: CreateStairs: optional baselinePosition and baselineOffset
body:
Fixes #578

`CreateStairs` never set `API_StairType::baselinePosition`/`baselineOffset`, so which edge of the flight the baseline runs on always came from the Stair tool defaults. The reporter found that a multi-segment baseline turning to one side fails while its mirror image is created, and that the flights land on one side of the baseline. The DevKit's `Do_CreateStair` example (`Element_Test/Src/Element_Basics.cpp`) sets `element.stair.baselinePosition = APILP_Center` before `ACAPI_Element_Create`.

## Changes
- New optional `baselinePosition` (`Left`, `Right`, `Center`) and `baselineOffset` (number) on `CreateStairs` items. They are written to `element.stair.baselinePosition`/`baselineOffset` in `CreateStairsCommand::SetTypeSpecificParameters`. Without them the tool defaults (or the favorite) are kept, so existing calls don't change.
- The `baseLinePoints` description mentions the new field.
- `Examples/Element/CreateStairs.py`: the straight stair uses `baselinePosition: 'Center'`.

`API_LinePositionID` (`APILP_Left/Right/Center`) and both fields have the same declaration in the AC25–AC30 DevKits. `SolveStairBaseline` shares `SetTypeSpecificParameters`, but its schema is unchanged here because open PR #1557 moves that schema.
