title: 2D creation commands: optional databaseId to create in a worksheet, detail or layout without opening it
body:
Fixes #1602 (part 2 of its plan; part 1 was #1605).

## What it does
`CreatePolylines`, `CreateHatches`, `CreateTexts`, `CreateLineElements`, `CreateArcs`, `CreateCircles`, `CreateSplines`, `CreateLabels` and `CreateHotspots` take an optional top-level `databaseId`, the same `DatabaseId` object as `ChangeWindow`, `GetElementsByType`'s `databases` and `CopyElementsToDatabase`. The elements are then created in that database (a worksheet, a detail, a layout, ...), and the current database is switched back afterwards, so the front window stays.

It follows the design posted on the issue:
- **Only these nine commands** get the field. Every other `Create*` command still rejects it through its schema (`additionalProperties: false`). A call without `databaseId` runs the old code.
- **Database only, not the window.** The switch is `ACAPI_Database_ChangeCurrentDatabase`. The DevKit's remark on that function says all subsequent database-dependent calls work on that database, which answers the question the issue left for a maintainer. The switch runs inside the one undoable command, as `CopyElementsToDatabase` (#1745) does it, and the starting database is restored on every path.
- **A worksheet or detail whose window was never opened** is opened once through its Project Map item, and the front window is brought back (Archicad 27+). This is the same helper `CopyElementsToDatabase` uses.
- **A failed switch fails the whole call:** nothing is created, and the error suggests opening the database once with `ChangeWindow`.
- `favoriteName` and the tool defaults are global, so they work unchanged.

`ChangeCurrentDatabaseTo` and `OpenDatabaseIfNeverOpened` move from `ElementCommands.cpp` to `CommandBase`, so `CopyElementsToDatabase` and the create commands share them. The code is unchanged.

New workflow script: `Workflows/draw_in_worksheet_by_database_id.py` creates a worksheet, draws a polyline and a text in it from the floor plan, counts them, and deletes the worksheet again.

## Checks
- `tools/check_examples.py` passes; `tools/generate_addon_docs.py` runs and lists the new field for all nine commands.
- No local compiler: the build checks compile it for Archicad 25–30.
- **Not run in Archicad.** To check:
  - with the floor plan in front, run the workflow script: the polyline and the text should be in the new worksheet, and the floor plan should still be in front;
  - one Undo should remove them.

title: Add DeleteAndReplaceAttributes: delete attributes and replace them where they are used
body:
Fixes #298

New command **DeleteAndReplaceAttributes** (registered with 1.8.1, Archicad 27 and later), like Delete and Replace in the Attribute Manager:

```json
{
  "attributeType": "Fill" | "Line" | "Surface" | "BuildingMaterial",
  "attributes": [{"attributeId": {"guid": "..."}, "replacementAttributeId": {"guid": "..."}}],
  "dryRun": false
}
```

- It reuses the reference scan of `ReindexAttributes` (`ScanReferences`): element fields, library part parameters and memo data in the floor plan and every view/layout database, tool defaults, Favorites, other attributes (composites, building materials, surfaces, profiles, MEP systems) and graphic override rules.
- The replacement may already be used, so its references can't be told apart from the rewritten ones afterwards. The references therefore first go to a temporary copy of the deleted attribute. If an element can't be changed, they are moved back exactly and nothing is deleted. After the old attribute is deleted, they go on to the replacement and the copy is deleted.
- Hidden or locked layers of the affected elements are shown and unlocked for the change and restored afterwards, as `ReindexAttributes` does.
- The response per item has the same lists as `ReindexAttributes` (`elements`, `hotlinkElements`, `toolDefaults`, `favorites`, `attributes`, `overrideRules`, `layersShown`, `warnings`), or an error item. The whole call is one undo step.
- Example: `archicad-addon/Examples/Attribute/DeleteAndReplaceAttributes.py`.

Static checks: `tools/check_examples.py` passes and `tools/generate_addon_docs.py` runs. No local compiler, so it needs the build checks and a test in Archicad.

title: Add GetModelViewOptionDetails: read the settings of stored model view option combinations
body:
Fixes #781

## What it adds
**GetModelViewOptionDetails** (Navigator, registered with 1.8.1, Archicad 27+).
- Input: optional `modelViewOptions`, an array of `{modelViewOptionId}` or `{name}` items. When it is omitted, every combination is returned.
- Output: `modelViewOptionDetails`, one item per combination (or an error item when one is not found), with:
  - `index`, `modelViewOptionId`, `name`;
  - `modelViewOptions`: the fields of `API_ModelViewOptions` stored in the combination. These are the same fields as `GetViewOptions` returns for the current window, so the two outputs can be compared directly.
  - `gdlOptions`: the options library parts add to the combination (`name`, `guid`, `supersetGuid`), each with its GDL `parameters` in the `StoredGDLParameter` shape.
- How it works: every combination is read once with `ACAPI_Navigator_ModelViewOptions_GetNum` / `_Get`. `gdlOptions` is sized with `BMGetPtrSize` as the DevKit's Environment_Control example does, serialized with the existing `AddLibPartAndGDLParameters`, and freed with `ACAPI_FreeGDLModelViewOptionsPtr`.
- On AC25/26 it returns "Available from Archicad 27.", like `FindModelViewOption`.
- It is read-only. The AC27–AC30 headers have only `_Search`, `_GetNum` and `_Get` for stored combinations, so writing, renaming and creating combinations is not possible. `SetViewOptions` still changes only the current window.

## Other changes
- The model view option fields of `VisitViewOptions` were moved into a new `VisitModelViewOptions`. This is a pure move; `GetViewOptions` / `SetViewOptions` behave as before.
- New Grasshopper component `GetModelViewOptionDetails` (Navigator). It reuses the ModelViewOptions icon and has a new GUID.
- New example `Examples/Navigator/GetModelViewOptionDetails.py`.

## Checks
- `tools/check_examples.py`, `py_compile` and `tools/generate_addon_docs.py` pass. Both schemas parse as JSON.
- Not built here: there is no compiler on this runner. It needs a check in Archicad 27+ on a project whose library adds model view options, e.g. doors and windows of the standard library. The `gdlOptions` entries and their parameters should match what the Model View Options dialog shows.

title: MEP: CreateMEPTakeOffs and CreateMEPFlexibleSegments (renamed from Place...), take-off checks from #1728
body:
## Why
Tapir's creating commands are named `Create<Things>` (`CreateMEPElements`, `CreateMEPRoutingElements` and about 110 others). The two MEP commands added in 1.8.1 used `Place` instead. Issue #1724 asked for `CreateMEPTakeOffs` by name. Neither command has been released yet (both are registered as 1.8.1), so they are renamed with no alias. `PlaceOpenings` (1.8.0, released) stays as it is.

## What changed
**1. Rename** (`PlaceMEPTakeOffs` -> `CreateMEPTakeOffs`, `PlaceMEPFlexibleSegments` -> `CreateMEPFlexibleSegments`)
- C++ classes, `GetName`, registrations in `AddOnMain.cpp` (still "1.8.1"; descriptions now start with "Creates ..."), undo step names (`Create MEP Take-Offs`, `Create MEP Flexible Segments`) and a schema reference in `GetMEPElementDetails`.
- Examples moved with `git mv` to `Examples/MEP/CreateMEPTakeOffs.py` and `CreateMEPFlexibleSegments.py`. `ModifyMEPElements.py` now calls the new name.
- Grasshopper: `CreateMEPTakeOffsComponent` and `CreateMEPFlexibleSegmentsComponent`. The file, class, name/nickname and `CommandName` are renamed. **`ComponentGuid` and icon are unchanged.**

**2. Take-off checks taken from #1728** (main's parameter names kept)
- `domain` is now optional. Without it, the domain of the segment's routing element is used.
- `rotationAroundMainAxis` must be a multiple of pi/2, because Archicad places take-offs only at quarter turns. It is normalized into [0, 2*pi). The schema says which way 0, pi/2, pi and 3*pi/2 face.
- `distanceFromBeginning` may not be more than the segment length, which is computed from its begin and end node positions with a 1e-6 tolerance. The error message gives both lengths.
- `length` must be positive.
- New optional `defaults: {removeInsulation}`, applied with the existing `ApplyMEPElementDefaults`. `insulationThickness` is refused (with #1728's error text) because setting it stops Archicad with a fatal error.
- Every API call was checked in the AC28, AC29 and AC30 MEP headers. All of it is inside `#ifdef ServerMainVers_2800`.
- Grasshopper: the `Domains` input is now optional, and a new `RemoveInsulation` boolean input is added as the last input.
- The example leaves out the domain and uses a quarter turn and `removeInsulation`.

**3. Polyline inputs in the flexible-segment component** (matching #1767's `polyline`, `startDirection`, `endDirection`)
- Three new optional inputs, added last: `Polylines` (one curve per flexible segment), `PolylineStartDirections` and `PolylineEndDirections`.
- Straight curve segments become `Line` parts. A run of curved segments becomes one `Spline` part through points on the curve, as many as the segment has control points.
- `ControlPoints` is now optional. Give exactly one of `ControlPoints` or `Polylines`. Orientation inputs work only with control points, direction inputs only with polylines.

Thanks to #1728 (issue-bot PR) for the take-off checks. It will be closed in favour of this PR.

## Checks
- `tools/check_examples.py`: complete. `py_compile` passes on the touched examples.
- `tools/generate_addon_docs.py` runs.
- Neither old name remains outside `docs/` and `.github/`.
- `tools/generate_gh_coverage.py`: both commands are done, with 8/8 parameters covered.
- Not compiled locally (no MSVC, Xcode or dotnet here), so the PR build checks are the first compile.

Fixes #1724

title: Grasshopper ElementDetails: absolute Elevations output
body:

title: Community Archicad test results become a commit status that holds back the bot's auto-merge
body:
The approach agreed in #1577 (maintainer decision: yes).

**This touches release-critical workflows (`.github/workflows/claude_auto_merge.yml`, `claude_pr_review.yml`, a new workflow) and needs the maintainer's review.** Auto-merge never merges it by itself (gate 3).

- **New `archicad_test_status.yml`** (`issue_comment` created, PR conversations only, no model, never checks out the PR). For a comment whose body starts with `tapir-test: `:
  1. the author must be listed in the repository variable `ARCHICAD_TESTERS` (logins, spaces or commas) or have write access; this is checked before the comment is parsed;
  2. only the first line counts, and it must match the runner's format: `^tapir-test: AC(\d{2}) ([A-Za-z_-]{2,8} )?(PASS|FAIL) (\d+)/(\d+) build ([0-9a-f]{7,40}) ` (as `report()` in `tools/community-test-runner/tapir_test_runner.py` writes it, with or without the language);
  3. the sha must be a prefix of the PR's `headRefOid` read from the API, and the PR must be open;
  4. then it sets `archicad-test/AC<version>` on that head: `success` for PASS, `failure` for FAIL, description `PASS 12/12, tested by <login>`, linked to the comment. Only `statuses: write`, `pull-requests: read`, `contents: read`.
- **`claude_auto_merge.yml`**: a bot PR is skipped when the newest status (highest id) of any `archicad-test/*` context on its head is `failure` or `error`, so a later PASS on the same head unblocks it. No status means nobody tested it and does not block. Note: gate 2 (`gh pr checks`) already counts commit statuses, so a failed `archicad-test/*` status also holds back a human PR's auto-merge; the new check makes it explicit for bot PRs.
- **`claude_pr_review.yml`**: a conversation comment starting with `tapir-test:` no longer starts a re-review (saves a model run per result, #977). The status carries the result, and the review runs again on every new head.
- `tools/community-test-runner/README.md`: one paragraph about the status.

To use it, set the repository variable `ARCHICAD_TESTERS` (e.g. `weltmaister`). A new head (a push or the steward's merge of `main`) carries no status, so the test is repeated for it. The steward only reads check runs, so a failed status does not start a fix round (left for later, as discussed in #1577).

Checked statically: YAML parses, every `run:` script passes `bash -n`, the regex was tested against the runner's line formats, and the jq filter was tested on sample statuses.

Fixes #1577

title: Walls: Create updates the walls the component created before
body:
Part of #521: a re-run of *Create* no longer duplicates the elements. This PR covers the Walls tool component (`Walls` and `Walls_API`) only.

**What changes**
- The component remembers the walls its *Create* made, one per geometry item (StartPoint/EndPoint pair). It saves them in the .gh file through `Write`/`Read` overrides (`GH_IWriter`/`GH_IReader`).
- On the next *Create*, item *i* modifies the wall made from item *i* instead of creating a new one. It sends `ModifyWalls` with the new start and end point and the settings, `SetDetailsOfElements` for floor index, layer and draw order, and the Element ID property. Settings only `CreateWalls` takes (FavoriteName, the bottom elevation of a Refresh JSON) are left unchanged on those walls, and a remark says so.
- Items beyond the remembered walls are created and remembered. Remembered walls that no longer have a geometry item are left as they are (a remark gives their number). Deleting stays with `DeleteElements`.
- A remembered wall that was deleted (or is not a wall any more, or belongs to another project) gets an error in `Errors` and a null `ElementGuid`. It is **not** created again.
- Two component menu items: *Create Updates the Elements Created Here* (on by default) and *Forget the Elements Created Here (n)*. Both record a Grasshopper undo step. With updating off, each *Create* makes new walls and remembers only those.
- A copied or pasted component starts with no remembered walls (the list belongs to the component's instance id), so two components never drive the same walls.
- No inputs or outputs change, so saved definitions keep their wiring. Execute and Refresh behave as before. Execute's splitting of settings into Modify and SetDetailsOfElements items moved into `AddWriteItems`, which Create's update path reuses.

**How other tool components follow**
The mechanism lives in `ElementToolComponent` behind `protected virtual bool CanUpdateCreatedElements` (false by default). A tool sets it to true once its Modify command takes everything its Create writes, geometry included (the geometry keys from `TryGetGeometry` must be in `ModifyKeys`; a key that is not shows up as "can only be given when creating"). Railings can't opt in yet because there is no `ModifyRailings`. The old per-command Create* components are not changed: they are replaced by tool components over time.

**Notes for the maintainer**
- The remembered GUIDs change during a solve, which Grasshopper doesn't count as a document change. Save the .gh file after a *Create* to keep them.
- The CLAUDE.md section "Archicad tool components" says "*Create* makes new elements". You may want to add that Create updates the elements a tool component made when the tool opts in.

Needs a check in Archicad: place Walls, *Create* two walls, move the points and press *Create* again (the same two walls move). Save, reopen and repeat. Delete one wall in Archicad and press *Create* (an error for that item, no new wall). Copy the component and press *Create* on the copy (new walls).

title: Versioned installer assets in the release; the installer shows the installed Tapir version
body:
Maintainer decision on #1646: add a versioned copy of the installer to the release, and show the installed version using (b), a version resource in the add-on.

**This touches release paths (`.github/workflows/archicad_addon.yml`, `weekly_release.yml`, `archicad-addon/Tools/`, `archicad-addon/Installer/`) and needs the maintainer's review.** Auto-merge never merges it by itself.

**1. Versioned installer assets**
- `release_installer_win` also attaches the same file as `TapirInstaller_Win_<version>.exe`. The version comes from a new `version` output of `build_installer_win` (what `write_version_file.py` printed, checked as `N.N.N`). A copy keeps the embedded Authenticode signature.
- `build_installer_mac` also attaches `TapirInstaller_Mac_<version>.zip` on a tag, with the version from `tools/package_info.json`.
- The fixed names `TapirInstaller_Win.exe` / `TapirInstaller_Mac.zip` stay. The add-on (exact name match in `VersionChecker.cpp`), the legacy update script and the README links use them. The add-on assets are matched by `AC<v>_<Win|Mac>`, which the versioned names don't contain.
- `weekly_release.yml`: `EXPECTED_ASSETS` goes from `versions * 2 + 2` to `versions * 2 + 4`. Note: CLAUDE.md's CI section still says "two installers" for that count, so it needs a one-line update (I didn't edit CLAUDE.md).

**2. Version resource in the add-on (option b)**
- Windows: `CompileResources.py` writes `AddOnVersion.rc2` (a `VERSIONINFO`: FILEVERSION/PRODUCTVERSION `M,m,p,0`, ProductName `Tapir`, ProductVersion `M.m.p`, OriginalFilename `<addOnName>.apx`) into the ResourceObjects folder, using `ADDON_VERSION` from `Sources/AddOnVersion.hpp`. `RFIX.win/AddOnMain.rc2` includes it, and `rc` already has that folder on its include path. `AddOnVersion.hpp` is now a dependency of the resource step, so a version bump recompiles the resources.
- macOS: `CMakeCommon.cmake` reads `ADDON_VERSION` and sets `CFBundleShortVersionString` to it. Before, it held `<AC>.0.0.<GS build>`. `CFBundleVersion` stays the Archicad build. The header is a configure dependency.
- The installer reads it: `GetInstalledTapirVersion` takes the `.apx` ProductVersion via `version.dll` (ctypes) or the bundle's `Info.plist` (plistlib), and accepts only `N.N.N`. A row shows "Installed 1.8.1", and after an install it shows the version just installed. Add-ons built before this change show only "Installed", as before. The console listing adds ", Tapir <version> installed". Standard library only, and a failed read never breaks the installer.

**Checks done here (no compiler):** YAML parses, and the changed bash steps pass `bash -n`. I ran the CMake version extraction with `cmake -P` (gives `1.8.1`) and generated the `.rc2` from the real header. I tested the installer's detection with mock bundles (an old 4-part version shows "Installed", `1.8.1` shows "Installed 1.8.1"), and `test_update_mode.py` passes (67 tests). Still unchecked: the Windows `rc` build and the `.apx` ProductVersion. The build check compiles them, and someone should look at the file's Properties > Details on Windows and the row on both platforms.

Fixes #1646

title: Add ModifyRailings: height, bottom offset and home story of railings
body:
Part of #897

Maintainer decision: `ModifyRailings` starts small, with height, bottomOffset and floorIndex (home story) only. Reference line changes come later, after a test in Archicad. #897 stays open for the rest: the reference line and `templateElementId`.

**`ModifyRailings`** (registered with 1.8.1, `ExtendedElementCommands.cpp`)
- Input: `railingsWithDetails[]` with `elementId` and the optional `height` (> 0, applied to every segment), `bottomOffset` and `floorIndex`. The response is `executionResults`, one per item, like the other Modify commands. All items run in one undoable command.
- Only fields of the railing element change: `defSegment.height` (as the DevKit's `Element_Test` / `Do_Railing_Edit` does), `bottomOffset` and `header.floorInd`. The call passes no memo, so the reference line, nodes, segments, posts, rails and panels are not written.
- Checks before the change: the element is a Railing, `floorIndex` is a story of the project, and at least one field is given.
- After the change, each railing is read back: its home story, its bottom offset and the height of every segment (`memo.railingSegments`). A value Archicad did not apply gets a failed result (`APIERR_REFUSEDPAR`) that says what the railing has now. `CreateRailings` showed that Archicad can derive the base from the elevations of the reference line vertices, so this read-back is what tells whether a bottom offset or story change really applies.
- Example: `Examples/Element/ModifyRailings.py` creates a railing, sets height 1.2 and bottomOffset 0.15, and prints what `GetDetailsOfElements` reads back.

**What needs a check in Archicad:** the three fields on an existing railing, one at a time and together, and moving a railing to another story with `floorIndex`. Each item should succeed, and `GetDetailsOfElements` should show the new `height`, `segmentHeights`, `bottomOffset` and `floorIndex`. A failed item's message names the values Archicad did not apply.

Checks: `tools/check_examples.py` passes, and `tools/generate_addon_docs.py` runs (docs not committed). The C++ was checked against the AC25-AC30 headers (`API_RailingType` `defSegment`, `bottomOffset`, `nSegments`; `APIMemoMask_RailingSegment`). It has not been compiled locally; the PR build checks compile every version.

title: Add the export_obj.py workflow: export the 3D model to an OBJ file
body:
Part of #1051

Maintainer decision: the script route comes first. A workflow script writes OBJ from `Get3DGeometryOfElements`. A native `Export3DModel` command follows only if the script is too slow.

**`archicad-addon/Workflows/export_obj.py`** (standard library only, uses `aclib`; no add-on change)
```
python archicad-addon/Workflows/export_obj.py [<output.obj>] [--elementType Wall ...] [--selected]
    [--holes triangulate|bridge] [--zUp] [--batchSize 100] [--port 19723]
```
- **Elements:** every element visible in 3D (`GetAllElements` with `IsVisibleIn3D`). `--elementType` limits the export to the given types (repeatable), and `--selected` to the selection.
- **Geometry:** `Get3DGeometryOfElements` is read in batches of `--batchSize` elements. Each element becomes one OBJ object, `o <Type>_<Element ID>_<GUID>` (from `GetDetailsOfElements` with `fields: type, id`). Elements without a 3D body are skipped and counted.
- **Faces with holes:** OBJ faces have no holes.
  - First, each face is projected to its dominant plane and its holes are joined to the outline by seams; each hole is joined to the nearest vertex it can see.
  - By default the joined polygon is ear-clipped into triangles. `--holes bridge` writes it as one polygon with seams instead.
  - Faces without holes are written unchanged, and the winding of the faces is kept.
- **Camera note:** the camera of the 3D window (`Get3DProjectionSettings`: position, target, view cone, roll, azimuth, or the axonometry) is written as a comment at the top of the file. The comment also says how to read a saved view's camera: open it with `ChangeWindow`, then call the same command.
- **Axes and output:** the file is written Y up, as `(x, z, -y)`, which Blender's OBJ importer expects by default; `--zUp` keeps Archicad's axes. The output goes to the given path, or to `tapir_export_<timestamp>.obj` in the temp folder. The script prints the counts and the path.
- The Workflows README lists the script.

**Checks:**
- `py_compile` and `tools/check_examples.py` pass.
- The face code ran offline against a fake `aclib` with these faces:
  - a square with four holes (convex and concave, wound either way) in five orientations
  - a U-shaped outline with three holes
  - a 200-gon with 36 octagon holes
- For every face, the triangles (and the bridged polygon) add up to the outline's area minus the holes, with no inverted triangles. The large face took 0.1 s.

**Not verified:** a run against Archicad. The next step is to export a real project, import the file in Blender, and time a whole-model export.

title: Grasshopper: own icons for the 126 new components
body:
Gives each of the 126 recently added Grasshopper components its own icon. Until now they borrowed the icon of a related component. This PR combines the two icon branches `claude/gh-icons-part1` (68 components) and `claude/gh-icons-part2` (58 components) on top of current `main`.

## What the icons are
- **38 Archicad help icons.** They come from Graphisoft's Archicad 29 help (help.graphisoft.com): the toolbox, Info Box, toolbars, menus, window tabs, attribute managers, palettes and organizers. Each one is kept at its original pixels, with the screenshot background made transparent. All are credited in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, which now has one sorted list of 170 names. Tapir uses them with Graphisoft's permission, the same as the existing ones.
  - Examples: the Structural Analytical Model tools (supports, links, loads, releases), Grids & Background, the 3D visualization toolbar, Project Map / Navigator, the Take-off tool, Inject Parameters, Pens & Colors, the Favorites palette, Classification Manager, Action Center, Trace / Autogroup, Shell, Railing, Zone, Skylight, Curtain Wall, Opening and single-plane Roof.
- **88 drawn icons.** Each has an SVG source in `grasshopper-plugin/TapirGrasshopperPlugin/IconSource/`, rendered to a 24x24 PNG in `Resources/`. They cover the design options, general, IFC, project, teamwork, element, attribute, element set/group, favorite, property, library, navigator, analytical and MEP commands.

## Badges
Like the existing icons, a small badge in the corner shows what the component does. The badges are copied pixel for pixel from the existing badged icons:
- plus: create
- pencil: set or modify
- X: delete
- sheet: details

## Weak spots
- **ModifyShells:** the Shell help icon is 26 px wide and was scaled down to fit.
- **CreateMEPTakeOffs:** slightly soft, because the 27 px original was scaled down to 24 px.
- **GetPens:** the details badge covers much of the narrow pen nib, as on the existing ZoneDetails icon.
- **Classification systems icon:** the best match in the help was on 045_PropertiesClassifications-7.
- **Analytical link icons:** the Structural Link icon is faint, like the original.
- **3D Document icons:** they keep the original's very light grey fill.
- **Drawn on purpose instead of using a help icon:**
  - Insert Autotext and Hotlink Manager status: the help only has blurry or highlighted copies.
  - Groups: the help icons would look the same as each other.
  - ReindexLayers: it would look the same as SetLayers.
  - Flexible Segment: the help only labels it indirectly.
  - OpenLibraryPartInEditor: the help shows the same icon for two commands.
  - ModifyLibraryList: it would look the same as SetLibraries.

## Combining the two branches
- **MEP renames from #1780:** the icons follow the command names. `PlaceMEPTakeOffs` is now `CreateMEPTakeOffs` and `PlaceMEPFlexibleSegments` is now `CreateMEPFlexibleSegments` (PNG, SVG source, `.resx` entry, `Designer.cs` property and the component's `Icon`). No `PlaceMEP*Component.cs` file comes back.
- **Resource files:** `Resources.resx` and `Resources.Designer.cs` are `main` plus the block each branch appended.
- **Component files:** compared with `main`, each changes only its `Icon` line, plus the removal of the old "Shares the icon…" comments.

These were done by reading and with scripts, because nothing is compiled locally. The PR build check compiles the plugin.

- There are no duplicate resource names: 696 `.resx` entries and 696 `Designer.cs` properties.
- `Resources.resx` parses as XML, and the braces in `Designer.cs` are balanced.
- There are no conflict markers.
- 126 components have a new icon. Every name in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` has a PNG.
- `git diff main` touches only `Resources/`, `IconSource/`, the resource files, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and the `Icon` lines of the components.

title: ReserveElements reports success for GUIDs that are not elements, and nothing is reserved
body:
### Environment
Tapir 1.8.0, Archicad 29, Teamwork project.

### Steps
1. Pick a layout whose settings nobody has reserved.
2. `SetLayoutSettings` with its current `customData` fails: `"Failed to change layout settings."` (code -2130312909). Expected, since the layout settings are not reserved.
3. `ReserveElements` with the layout's navigator item GUID, or its database id (`GetDatabaseIdFromNavigatorItemId`), or the GUID of its Layout Book subset, or of the Layout Book root. Every call returns `{"executionResult": {"success": true}}` with no conflicts.
4. `SetLayoutSettings` still fails with the same error: nothing was reserved.
5. After reserving the layout settings by hand (Layout Book > Reserve Layout Settings), the same `SetLayoutSettings` call succeeds.

### Expected
`ReserveElements` should not report success for GUIDs that are not elements. A per-GUID result (for example, checking each GUID with `ACAPI_Element_GetHeader` first) would let scripts tell which items were actually reserved. Similar in spirit to #840.

### Context
The Archicad API does not seem to offer a way to reserve layout settings either (`ACAPI_Teamwork_GetTWOwner` only reads the owner). I asked about it in the Graphisoft Community: https://community.graphisoft.com/t5/Archicad-C-API/Reserve-and-release-navigator-items-layout-settings-views/m-p/719787

### Suggestions
- Document in `SetLayoutSettings` that, in Teamwork, the layout settings must be reserved first, and that `GetTeamworkOwnersOfDatabases` shows who holds them.
- If the Archicad API adds a way to reserve Layout Book items, expose it as commands (e.g. `ReserveLayoutSettings` / `ReleaseLayoutSettings`).

title: ModifyColumns / ModifyBeams: switching a profiled segment to Basic does not take effect
body:
**What happens**
`ModifyColumns` (and `ModifyBeams`) with `buildingMaterialId` on a column whose segments use a complex profile reports success, but the column keeps its profile: `GetDetailsOfElements` still returns the profile structure.

**Likely cause**
The command sets `assemblySegmentData.modelElemStructureType = API_BasicStructure` but leaves `assemblySegmentData.profileType` unchanged (`APISect_Poly`). It looks like the same issue as #531 for walls, fixed in #1612 by resetting `profileType`.

**Expected**
- `buildingMaterialId` switches the segments to a Basic rectangular/circular section, resetting `profileType` as #1612 does for walls.
- `profileId` sets `profileType` to `APISect_Poly`.

**Steps**
1. Place a column (or beam) with a complex profile.
2. `ModifyColumns` with `{ elementId, buildingMaterialId }` → success.
3. `GetDetailsOfElements` → still a profiled column.

title: Profiles: edit geometry without losing stretch zones, modifiers and edge flags
body:
Today the only way to change a Profile's geometry is `CreateProfiles` with `overwriteExisting` + `replaceSkins` + `newSkins`. By design this discards the stretch zones and the profile modifiers, and `edgeOverrides` cannot carry `isInnerLine` or `isCutEndLine`, so the rebuilt profile is no longer stretchable and some edge settings are lost.

**Use case**
Adjust the height of saved wall profiles (move the vertices of the top band by a given distance) while keeping them stretchable and keeping their modifiers.

**Proposal (either would work)**
1. A `ModifyProfileVertices` command that moves given vertices (by skin/contour/vertex, or every vertex above a height) by a vector, keeping the hatch topology so modifiers, stretch zones and edge data stay attached.
2. Or: `GetProfiles` returns the stretch zone limits, `CreateProfiles` accepts them back, and `edgeOverrides` accepts `isInnerLine` and `isCutEndLine`.

**API**
`ProfileVectorImage::GetStretchData / SetStretchData`, `AddProfileParameterDef / GetParameterDefs` (ProfileVectorImage.hpp), `ProfileEdgeData::SetInnerLine` (ProfileAdditionalInfo.hpp).

title: CreateAssociativeDimensions: position an associative witness point along the referenced edge
body:
A witness point is either associative (`elementId`, `line`, `inIndex`, ...) or static (`coordinate`). For an associative point on a wall edge Tapir leaves `API_DimBase.loc` empty, and Archicad puts the point at the middle of the edge. When the dimension line crosses a long or oblique wall face, that is not where the line crosses the face, so scripts fall back to static points that don't follow the wall.

Example (Archicad 30, Tapir 1.8.0): a dimension line at y = 4.88 crossing two vertical walls whose faces run from y = 0 to y = 10. `GetDimensionData` returns the associative witness points of both walls at y = 5.00, the middle of each face.

**Proposal**
Accept `coordinate` together with `elementId`, and fill `dimElem.base.loc` (and `pos`) with it, as the DevKit's Element_Test examples do for associative points (Element_Snippets.cpp sets `base.loc` together with `base.guid` and `inIndex`).

**To check**
Whether Archicad keeps `loc` for `line = true` bases (wall edges) or only for hotspot bases.

title: Project preferences: Reference Levels page and Floor Plan Cut Plane Settings
body:
`GetProjectPreferences` and `SetProjectPreferences` get two more pages: the reference levels and the floor plan cut plane.

## Why

- **Reference levels.** The Reference Levels page was part 1 of the plan in #929, but it isn't on `main`. The commands only have working units, dimensions, calculation units and zones. A template setup script can't name the levels or set their elevations, for example sea level for level dimensions.
- **Floor plan cut plane.** No command reads or writes the Floor Plan Cut Plane Settings yet. Scripts that draw or check the floor plan need the cut plane height and the shown range. Template setup scripts need to set them.

## What this adds

Both pages use the same pattern as the existing ones:
- `GetProjectPreferences` answers them by name, and every page when `preferenceTypes` is missing.
- `SetProjectPreferences` reads the page, changes only the given fields and writes it back in one undo step. It answers one execution result per page.

**`referenceLevels`** (`APIPrefs_ReferenceLevelsID`): `level1` and `level2`, each with `name` and `elevation` (from Project Zero, in meters).
- `ACAPI_ProjectSetting_GetPreferences` points the name fields to strings that Archicad keeps. The pointers are the same on every call, so they are only read and never freed, as in the DevKit's Environment_Control example.
- For a new name, the setter points to its own string, which lives until the page is written. An unchanged name keeps Archicad's pointer.

**`floorPlanCutPlane`** (`APIPrefs_FloorPlanCutPlaneDef`):
- `cutPlaneHeight`: from the current story.
- `topLevel` and `bottomLevel`: each with `relativeStory` (0 is the current story, 1 the story above, -1 the story below) and `offset`.
- `absoluteDisplayLimit`: from Project Zero.

A `relativeStory` outside the range of a `short` fails with a message.

Also in this PR:
- The registered descriptions name the new pages.
- The examples `GetProjectPreferences.py` and `SetProjectPreferences.py` use them.
- The Grasshopper `GetProjectPreferences` and `SetProjectPreferences` components get the two pages. They are appended after the existing inputs and outputs, so saved definitions keep their wiring.

There is no new command and no change to the existing pages.

## Tests

Live on Archicad 29 (macOS, build 5101), in a test project, which was reopened without saving afterwards:

| # | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `GetProjectPreferences` without `preferenceTypes` returns all six pages | ok |
| 2 | Set the name (with umlauts) and elevation of `level1`; `level2` unchanged | ok |
| 3 | Set only the elevation of `level2`: both names and `level1` unchanged | ok |
| 4 | Set only the name of `level2`: its elevation kept | ok |
| 5 | Set only `cutPlaneHeight`; the rest of the page unchanged | ok |
| 6 | Set `topLevel` (2, 0.5), `bottomLevel` (-1, -0.3) and `absoluteDisplayLimit` (-5); read back as given | ok |
| 7 | Set only `bottomLevel.offset`: its `relativeStory` kept | ok |
| 8 | `relativeStory` 40000 → failed result "topLevel.relativeStory is out of range." | ok |
| 9 | Empty `floorPlanCutPlane` → failed result "No field … given" | ok |
| 10 | Empty `referenceLevels` → failed result "No field … given" | ok |
| 11 | Unknown field in `floorPlanCutPlane` → schema error | ok |
| 12 | `workingUnits`, `floorPlanCutPlane` and `referenceLevels` in one call → one result each, all applied | ok |
| 13 | Round trip: the output of `GetProjectPreferences` written back restores every page | ok |
| 14 | Unknown preference type → schema error | ok |

14/14. Both examples also ran live. Built locally for Archicad 29 only. The other versions are left to CI.

title: GetGraphicOverrideRules: return the criterion as structured conditions too
body:
`CreateGraphicOverrideRules` / `ModifyGraphicOverrideRules` accept a structured `criterion`, but `GetGraphicOverrideRules` only returns `criterionXML`. To read a rule or change one value in it, a script has to parse Archicad's XML, and element type conditions are stored as internal ClassId GUIDs that the API doesn't map to element types (scripts create temporary rules just to learn that mapping).

**Proposal**
An option (e.g. `includeStructuredCriterion`) or a `ParseGraphicOverrideCriterion` command that returns the same shape the `criterion` input accepts: logical operators, element types by name, property conditions (id, name, operator, value), classification conditions. Parts it can't parse could come back as raw XML fragments so nothing is lost.

**Note**
Tapir already has the element type table it writes with (ElemRegistryRefId); the ClassIds could be resolved once per session from the XML Archicad stores for those.
author: cmartif

title: CreateMorphs: favoriteName, layerIndex and id like the other creation commands
body:
Most `Create...` commands accept `favoriteName`, `layerIndex` and `id` per item (#529); `CreateMorphs` only accepts `floorIndex`. Creating morphs with a favorite's look, on a given layer and with an Element ID now takes `ApplyFavoritesToElements`, then `MoveElements` (in tests the favorite moved the morph back to the story level), then `SetDetailsOfElements`.

**Proposal**
Add `favoriteName`, `layerIndex` and `id` to `morphsData`, applied before creation, keeping the given geometry and elevation.
author: cmartif

title: Script palette: let a script run detached (tool windows)
body:
The palette runs one script at a time, so a script that opens a tool window and stays open (for example a helper that follows the selection) blocks every other script until it is closed. The workaround is to relaunch itself as a detached process, which Tapir then doesn't track: it isn't stopped when Archicad quits and the Stop button doesn't reach it.

**Proposal**
An opt-in per script (e.g. a `# tapir: detached` comment, or a setting in the palette) to run it detached: the palette stays free, and Tapir still tracks the process and ends it on Stop or when Archicad quits (as #775 does for the processes `uv` starts).
author: cmartif

title: Run several commands as one undo step
body:
Each Tapir command is its own undo step. A script that builds one result with several calls (create hatches, polylines and texts; or modify rules and then combinations) leaves many Undo steps, and a failure halfway leaves a partial result.

**Proposal**
A command that runs a list of Tapir commands inside one `ACAPI_CallUndoableCommand` (e.g. `ExecuteCommands` with `[{ command, parameters }]` and a stop-on-error option). Commands open their own undoable scope today, so this probably needs an internal path for "already inside an undo scope".

title: Commands added after the 1.8.0 tag are registered with older versions (1.7.4, 1.7.3)
body:
28 commands that were not in the 1.8.0 release are registered on main with a version below 1.8.1:

- 1.7.4: ActivateLayerCombination, CompareLibraryPartUnIds, CreateElementsFromAnalyticalMembers, CreateRailingsFromPolyline, DeleteUserDataOfElements, ElevateElements, Get3DStyles, GetCalculatedParametersOfCurtainWallSubElements, GetCoordinateOrigins, GetDesignOptionCombinationOfViews, GetIFCAssignments, GetIFCSpatialStructure, GetLastValidEmbeddedLibraryPartName, GetLibraryPartIdentities, GetLibraryPartMetadata, GetMEPToolDefaults, GetPropertyEditability, GetPropertyValuesOfElementDefaults, GetRoofPlanes, GetTeamworkRightsOfObjects, ModifyOpenings, MoveProjectInfoFields, ReadFavoritesFile, RenameProjectInfoFields, SetDesignOptionCombinationOfViews, ShowElementsIn3D, TransferMEPSettings
- 1.7.3: ReorderNavigatorItems

They will first ship in 1.8.1, but the generated documentation will list them as available since 1.7.4 or 1.7.3. Scripts and tests that use the version to decide whether a command exists (like the `minTapir` fix in #1755) will be wrong for the 1.8.0 add-on.

**Proposal**
- Relabel these commands as 1.8.1 before the next release.
- Optionally, a CI check that fails when a command is registered with an already released version but was not in that release.
author: cmartif

title: fontName in CreateTexts, MeasureTexts and the other text commands: find fonts the way GetFontsByName does
body:
`GetFontsByName` finds fonts with Archicad's font search (`ACAPI_Font_SearchFont`), so a family name such as "Century Gothic" resolves to the font Archicad lists with its script on Windows ("Century Gothic Western", "Century Gothic Occidental" in Spanish). `CreateTexts`, `MeasureTexts` and the other commands that take `fontName` use `GetFontIndexFromName`, which only accepts the exact name or a case-insensitive match, so the same name fails there.

Archicad 30, Spanish Windows, Tapir 1.8.0:
- `GetFontsByName` with `"Century Gothic"` → `{"fontIndex": 510, "fontName": "Century Gothic Occidental"}`
- `MeasureTexts` with `"fontName": "Century Gothic"` → error -2130313113 "No loaded font is named 'Century Gothic'"

**Proposal**
In `GetFontIndexFromName`, after the exact and case-insensitive matches, fall back to `ACAPI_Font_SearchFont` (`ACAPI_Attribute_Search` before Archicad 27), as `GetFontsByName` does. Scripts could then give the family name without knowing the script suffix of the user's language.
author: cmartif

title: Element notifications: changes and deletions made by Tapir commands are not reported
body:
With a client registered with `SetElementNotificationClient` (`notifyOnNewElement` and `notifyOnModificationOfAnElement` true), on Archicad 30 with Tapir 1.8.0:

| Action | Notification |
|---|---|
| `CreateWalls` (Tapir) | `newElements` |
| `SetDetailsOfElements`, `SetPropertyValuesOfElements` (Tapir) | none |
| `DeleteElements` (Tapir) | none |
| `API.SetPropertyValuesOfElements` (Archicad's JSON API) | `changedElements` |
| Changing, moving and deleting the element by hand | `changedElements`, `deletedElements` |

New elements come from `ACAPI_Element_CatchNewElement`, which also reports Tapir's own creations. Changes and deletions come from the element observers, which don't seem to fire for changes made by the add-on that attached them. So a tool that follows changes misses everything that other Tapir scripts do.

**Proposal**
Report them from Tapir itself: the commands that modify or delete elements (`SetDetailsOfElements`, `Modify…`, `SetPropertyValuesOfElements`, `MoveElements`, `DeleteElements`…) could queue `changedElements` / `deletedElements` events for the elements they touched, through the same queue `ElementEventHandlerProc` uses. If that is not wanted, a note in the `SetElementNotificationClient` description would help.
author: cmartif

title: Delete the head branch of every merged pull request
body:
`claude_auto_merge.yml` already merges with `--delete-branch`. Pull requests merged on the web page or through the API keep their branch, though, and 43 such branches are left today. The coordinator session can't delete them, because its git proxy refuses branch deletions.

## New workflow: `.github/workflows/delete_merged_branches.yml`
- **When a pull request is merged** (`pull_request: closed`), however it was merged: it deletes the head branch if all of these hold:
  - it is a branch of this repository, not a fork's;
  - its tip is still the merged head commit, so nothing pushed after the merge is lost;
  - no open pull request uses it as head or base;
  - it isn't `main` or a `KEEP` branch: `api-coverage`, `gh-pages`, and the image branches `claude/pr-1773-screenshots` and `claude/gh-component-icons-sheets`.
- **Run by hand** (`workflow_dispatch`): it sweeps every branch with the same rules. It is a dry run by default, listing what it would delete; run it once with `dry_run` off to remove today's leftovers.
- **Security:** it runs no model and checks out nothing. It only reads pull request metadata and deletes refs through the API, with `contents: write`. A ruleset that protects a branch from deletion gives a warning, not a failure.
- **`CLAUDE.md`:** one entry in the CI section.

## Tested
The step's script was run locally against a fake `gh` serving the real pull request list (1,049) and branch list (118).
- **Result:** the dry run selects exactly the 43 branches found by hand, all from merged pull requests with their tip at the merged head.
- **Kept:**
  - the 44 branches with open pull requests;
  - 12 from closed, unmerged ones;
  - `claude/busy-johnson-6qseu0`, which has commits after its merge;
  - 17 branches with no pull request.

It touches `.github/`, so the maintainer merges it.

title: Criteria evaluator: accept the criterion of a graphic override rule
body:
Follow-up of my comment on #1292, which is out of scope there.

Once the criteria evaluator of #1292 is in, it could also take the criterion of a graphic override rule (the `criterionXML` that `GetGraphicOverrideRules` returns, optionally with some values replaced) and return the elements that match it.

**Use case**
Find which values of a property actually occur among the elements that match the rest of a rule's criterion (element types, classifications, other properties), without re-implementing Archicad's criteria in a script. The C++ API has no function to evaluate a criterion, so Tapir would be the only route for scripts.

**Related**
- #1292: the evaluator itself.
- #1816: reading a criterion as structured conditions. A parser written for it could feed the evaluator too.
author: cmartif

title: Get3DBoundingBoxes: measure Walls on their 3D model, with their connections
body:
`Get3DBoundingBoxes` now measures Walls on their 3D model, so a Wall's box includes its connections to other walls.

## The problem

Walls go through `ACAPI_Element_CalcBounds`, which measures a Wall along its reference line. At an L or T corner, though, the Wall's 3D body reaches up to half the wall thickness beyond the end of the reference line. So the box of a connected Wall is smaller than what the 3D window shows.

Example from a test project (Archicad 29): four 0.3 m walls form a closed 14 × 10 m rectangle.

| Wall | Reference line | Box on `main` | 3D body |
|---|---|---|---|
| bottom | (0, 0) → (14, 0) | x 0 … 14 | x −0.15 … 14.15 |
| right | (14, 0) → (14, 10) | y 0 … 10 | y 0.15 … 10.15 |

In that project every one of the 146 Walls differed from its 3D body. Scripts that build cut planes, views or simple 3D models from these boxes were off by up to half a wall thickness at every corner.

## What this changes

Walls now go through `CalculateSolidBodyBounds`, as Slabs, Roofs and Zones already do: the union of the bounding boxes of the Wall's solid bodies. A Wall without a solid body falls back to `ACAPI_Element_CalcBounds`, as Stairs do.

The registered description now says which types are measured on their 3D model. Nothing else changes, and no other element type is affected.

## Tests

Live on Archicad 29 (macOS, build 5101), in a test project, which was reopened without saving afterwards. "3D body" below means the minimum and maximum of the vertices that `Get3DGeometryOfElements` returns.

| # | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | All 146 Walls of the project: box = 3D body (1 mm) | ok |
| 2 | Boxes changed against `main`: 146 of 146 | ok |
| 3 | The bottom wall of the rectangle above: x −0.15 … 14.15 | ok |
| 4–9 | Slabs (96), Doors (86), Windows (173), Object, Zones (118), Morphs (13): boxes the same as on `main` | ok |
| 10–14 | New Walls: free-standing, diagonal, curved, and two forming an L corner: box = 3D body | ok |
| 15 | Curved Wall: the box includes the bulge of the arc | ok |
| 16 | A Wall on a hidden layer still has its 3D body, so it is measured the same way | ok |
| 17 | With a layout open: the same boxes | ok |

17/17. The fallback to `ACAPI_Element_CalcBounds` didn't run in these tests: even a Wall on a hidden layer kept its 3D body.

**Golden output.** `Test/ExpectedOutputs/set_cut_planes.py.output` holds the boxes of the Walls in `TestProject.pla`. I did not run it. If those Walls are connected, their boxes and the cut planes change, and the golden needs to be recorded again (`record_expected_output.py set_cut_planes.py`).

title: Checks: skip three files on Archicad versions without their commands (minArchicad)
body:
Three check files on `main` use commands that older Archicad versions don't have, but they carry no `minArchicad`. So they fail on every PR tested on such a version, whatever the PR changes:

| check | needs | answer on Archicad 26 |
|---|---|---|
| `graphic_override_criterion_fields.json` | 27 | "This command requires Archicad 27 or newer." (18 expectations fail) |
| `delete_embedded_library_items_missing_path.json` | 27 | "This command requires Archicad 27 or newer." (5 fail) |

This adds `minArchicad` to the three files, as #1572 did for `graphic_override_structured_criterion.json`. Since #1783, a failure posted by a tester holds the bot's auto-merge, so a version gap in a check would block PRs that are fine.

- AC26: all three skipped ("needs Archicad 27/28, running 26").
- AC28: PASS 32/32, so nothing changes where the commands exist.

That's the template's tool defaults, as BenTristem described in #1700 for Archicad 29 INT; on Archicad 26 GER the check passes. It needs a template whose Window and Door tools have a marker, or a different approach, which is for the check's author to decide.
- When every check of a run is skipped, the runner's verdict line reads `FAIL 0/0`. With #1783 that would become a failed status. I'll open a separate issue for it.

title: Test runner: a run where every check is skipped reports FAIL 0/0, which #1783 turns into a failed status
body:
When every check of a run is skipped (`minTapir`, `minArchicad`), `report()` in `tools/community-test-runner/tapir_test_runner.py` writes the verdict `FAIL 0/0`:

```
tapir-test: AC26 GER FAIL 0/0 build 7b8a626 tapir 1.8.1
| ... | - | `minArchicad` | skipped | skipped: needs Archicad 27, running 26 |
```

The cause is `verdict = "PASS" if scored and passed == len(scored) else "FAIL"`: with nothing scored, `scored` is empty, so the verdict is FAIL.

Since #1783 this matters. `archicad_test_status.yml` turns that line into a failed `archicad-test/AC26` status, and the bot's auto-merge stops, although nothing was tested. It happens for a PR whose only check needs a newer Archicad than the tester's, e.g. a PR that adds one AC27+ check and is tested on AC26 (with #1837, three of main's checks are such files).

Suggestion: when nothing is scored, write a verdict the status workflow ignores, e.g. `SKIP 0/0` (its pattern only accepts PASS or FAIL), or post no comment at all. The exit code is already 0 for "passed or skipped" according to the README.

A question about #1783 while I'm here: is `weltmaister` in `ARCHICAD_TESTERS`? The runner I use answers the bot's test requests on AC26 and AC28, and since #1783 those results only count as statuses for listed testers.

title: GetAllElements and GetElementsByType Object take minutes on large projects (sub-element object check)
body:
Since 1.7.3 (#1471), `GetAllElements` leaves out objects that belong to another element, as `GetElementsByType` already did for `Object`. To tell them apart, `IsSubElemObject` calls `ACAPI_Element_GetHeader` and then a full `ACAPI_Element_Get` for every object, and on a large project that check takes almost all the time.

Measured with Tapir 1.8.0 on Archicad 29 (5101), Windows, with the floor plan in front, in a project with 136,077 elements in the floor plan database (about 38,800 of them objects, most of them belonging to other elements):

| Command | Elements returned | Time |
|---|---|---|
| `API.GetAllElements` (Archicad's JSON API) | 9,771 | 0.3 s |
| `GetAllElements` with `IncludeSubElemObjects` | 136,077 | 2.1 s |
| `GetAllElements` | 99,640 | 183 s |
| `GetElementsByType` with `Object` | 2,335 | 184 s |

That is about 4.7 ms per object checked, with Archicad blocked for three minutes. On a small file (379 elements) the same commands take a fraction of a second, so it only shows on large projects.

Could the check use something lighter than reading the whole element, for example `ACAPI_HierarchicalEditing_GetHierarchicalElementOwner`?
author: cmartif

title: SetElementNotificationClient with modification notifications blocks Archicad for a long time on large projects
body:
With `notifyOnModificationOfAnElement`, registering the first such client attaches an observer to every element of the current database (`ACAPI_Element_AttachObserver` for each guid from `ACAPI_Element_GetElemList (API_ZombieElemID)`), and removing the last one detaches them all. Archicad is blocked meanwhile, and the time grows faster than the number of elements.

Measured with Tapir 1.8.0 on Archicad 30 (3001), Windows, with the floor plan in front, in a small file with lines added in steps. Each row is `SetElementNotificationClient` with modifications on, then `RemoveElementNotificationClient`; the element count is `GetAllElements` with `IncludeSubElemObjects`:

| Elements | Register | Remove |
|---|---|---|
| 379 | 4.5 s | 2.3 s |
| 879 | 4.9 s | 5.1 s |
| 1,379 | 9.1 s | 25.5 s |
| 2,379 | 19.8 s | 32.0 s |
| 5,379 | 73.7 s | 141.8 s |

Registering with only `notifyOnNewElement` takes 0.01 s on that file. On Archicad 29, in a project with 136,077 elements in the floor plan, registering with modifications had not finished after more than 30 minutes; at this rate it would take hours, and removing even longer. The loop only calls `ACAPI_Element_AttachObserver` and `ACAPI_Element_DetachObserver`, so the time seems to be spent in those calls.

So a client that wants change notifications can only use them on small projects. Some ideas:

- An optional list of element types to observe, so a client can leave out what it does not need. In large projects most elements are parts of curtain walls, stairs and railings.
- If the API allows it, attaching in smaller batches instead of all at once, so Archicad is not blocked in one go.
- A note in the description of `notifyOnModificationOfAnElement` about the cost, so clients know to count the elements first.
author: cmartif

title: ChangeSelectionOfElements: select the whole list in one API call
body:
`ChangeSelectionOfElements` calls `ACAPI_Selection_Select` once per element:

```cpp
for (const GS::ObjectState& element : addElementsToSelection) {
    ...
    const GSErrCode err = ACAPI_Selection_Select ({ API_Neig (GetGuidFromObjectState (*elementId)) }, true);
```

Each call is a selection transaction of its own, so the cost grows with the
selection instead of staying linear in the list. A few thousand elements take
minutes, and tens of thousands do not finish.

`ACAPI_Selection_Select` takes an array, so the whole list now goes in one
call. That call reports a single error code, which would lose the per-element
results the response promises, so on failure the elements are tried one by one
as before: that path says which element Archicad refused, and costs nothing
when the bulk call succeeds.

No schema change, and the response is unchanged.

### Measured

Archicad 27 on Windows, a survey project of about 29,000 elements, adding the
5,167 elements of two of its storeys to the selection in one command:

| | time |
| --- | --- |
| one call per element | did not return; the caller gave up after 15 minutes |
| one call for the list | 8 seconds |

The case behind it is an IFC export limited to chosen storeys, which selects
the elements of those storeys and saves with `SelectedElementsOnly`.

### Builds

`Archicad Add-On Build Check` is green on the branch for AC27 on both Windows
and macOS.
author: brncsk

title: SetPropertyValuesOfElements: write each element's values with one ACAPI_Element_SetProperties call
body:
`SetPropertyValuesOfElements` (`archicad-addon/Sources/PropertyCommands.cpp`) makes up to three API calls per value: `ACAPI_Element_IsPropertyDefinitionValueEditable`, `ACAPI_Property_SetPropertyValueFromString` and `ACAPI_Element_SetProperty`. Writing 10 properties on 1,000 elements is about 30,000 calls.

**Proposed change:** keep the per-value checks and conversions, then write each element's values with one `ACAPI_Element_SetProperties` call (Archicad 25–30) instead of one `ACAPI_Element_SetProperty` per value.

**Keep:**
- one execution result per input value, in input order
- a value that fails the editability check or the conversion still fails on its own, without blocking the element's other values
- the single undo step
- the input and response schemas unchanged

If `SetProperties` fails for an element, retry that element's values one by one with `SetProperty`, so each value still gets its own error.

**To verify in Archicad:** run `Examples/` scripts that use `SetPropertyValuesOfElements` and compare with the current results; time 10 properties on 1,000 elements before and after.

title: Send each command only the schema definitions it uses
body:
636 of the 731 commands use `CommonSchema::Used`, so `CommandBase::GetSchemaDefinitions` gives Archicad the whole `CommonSchemaDefinitions.json`: 674 definitions, 704 KB (143 KB in July). Following each command's `$ref`s, the median command needs 1.5 KB of it, and 603 of 614 commands need under 10 KB. Archicad checks requests and responses against these schemas, so a smaller schema should make every call cheaper.

**Proposed change** (in `archicad-addon/Sources`, `CommandBase` and `SchemaDefinitions`):
- give each command only the definitions its input and response schemas reference, following references inside definitions too
- work this out once per command and cache it
- if any reference cannot be found, return the whole file as today, so a command can never lose a definition it needs

Nothing else changes: same schemas, same validation, same responses.

**To verify in Archicad:** time `GetCurrentWindowType` (uses the shared schema) against `GetAddOnVersion` (does not) before and after, and run `Test/test_examples.py`.

A script or tool learns that a command is missing or needs a newer Archicad only by calling it: 244 registered descriptions state a version requirement in text, and those commands return `APIERR_NOTSUPPORTED`. `GenerateDocumentation` only writes developer files.

**Proposed change:** a `GetCommands` command (no input) that returns one item per registered command with its `name`, `group`, the `version` it was introduced in and its `description`, taken from the existing `RegisterCommand` calls in `AddOnMain.cpp`.

A follow-up can add each command's supported Archicad versions as data, so callers can check availability before calling.

title: CreateDoors with libraryPartName: parameters unreadable, and the Door tool defaults stay broken
body:
Tested on Archicad 29 INT for macOS (DevKit 29.3000) with Tapir 1.8.1, in a new project from the default template.

**Steps.** In a plain wall, run `CreateDoors` with `"libraryPartName": "Door"`, `width` 1.195 and `height` 1.987.

**What happens:**
- The door is placed, and `GetDetailsOfElements` reads the library part "Door" at the given width and height.
- `GetGDLParametersOfElements` on it fails: `-2130313215 Failed to get parameters of element`.
- `SetGDLParametersOfElements` fails with the same code.
- Its 3D frame keeps the part's own size instead of the given width and height.
- **The Door tool defaults stay broken afterwards:** a door placed next, *without* `libraryPartName`, has unreadable parameters too. Reopening the project without saving restores them.

The same call without `libraryPartName` gives a door with 810 readable parameters (`A` = 1.195, `B` = 1.987), and `favoriteName` also works.

**Likely cause.** `ApplyWindowOrDoorLibraryPartToDefaults` writes the part into the tool defaults with `ACAPI_Element_ChangeDefaults`:
- the mask holds only `openingBase.libInd`;
- `memo.params` comes from `ACAPI_LibraryPart_GetParams`;
- the call is not `ChangeDefaultsExt`, so no marker is written;
- the defaults are never put back, and `A`/`B` are not set from `width`/`height`.

The favorite path uses `ChangeDefaultsExt` with the full memo and doesn't show this.

**Suggestion.**
- Set the part with `ChangeDefaultsExt` (marker included), or skip the tool defaults and set `libInd` and `memo.params` (with `A`/`B` from `width`/`height`) on the element before `ACAPI_Element_CreateExt`.
- Put the tool defaults back afterwards, as `CreateSections favoriteName` does.

I can test a fix on macOS.

title: Drawing primitives: name the element a Ctrl_ElementRef item refers to
body:
`GetDrawingPrimitivesOfElements` and `GetShapePrimitivesOfElements` now say which element a `Ctrl_ElementRef` item refers to. `GetShapePrimitivesOfElements` also says why it fails for an element on another story.

## Ctrl_ElementRef

For `API_PrimCtrl_ElementRefID` Archicad passes the referenced element as `par1` (`API_PrimElemRef`). The collector didn't read it, so the item came back with only `type`, `pen`, `drwIndex` and `renovationStatus`, and a reader couldn't tell what it refers to.

The item now carries `referencedElement` with `elementId`, `type` and `drwIndex`, in both commands, since they share the collector and the primitive schema. Before Archicad 26, `API_PrimElemRef` has `typeID` instead of `type`, and the code reads that one there.

What this shows on Archicad 29:
- **A Wall's drawing ends with one `Ctrl_ElementRef` for each Window and Door in it.**
- **Windows and Doors give no primitives of their own**, only `Ctrl_Beg` and `Ctrl_End`, with and without `includeMarkers`.

So the references are the only link from the floor plan drawing to the openings. The registered description of `GetDrawingPrimitivesOfElements` now says both.

## GetShapePrimitivesOfElements on another story

`ACAPI_DrawingPrimitive_ShapePrims` draws on the current story only, and returns `APIERR_REFUSEDCMD` for an element of another story. The command answered that with "Failed to get the drawing primitives of the element". It now says "The element is not on the current story. Open its story first, or use GetDrawingPrimitivesOfElements, which draws on every story." The registered description mentions it too.

The example `GetShapePrimitivesOfElements.py` runs into this case whenever the first walls aren't on the current story, and now prints the new message.

There are no new commands, no change to the other primitives, and the Grasshopper components read the primitives as JSON, so the new key passes through.

## Tests

Live on Archicad 29 (macOS, build 5101), in a test project with 146 Walls, 86 Doors and 173 Windows on four stories. Nothing was changed in the project.

| # | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Every `Ctrl_ElementRef` in the drawings of all 146 Walls has `referencedElement` (259 items) | ok |
| 2 | `referencedElement` has `elementId`, `type` and `drwIndex` | ok |
| 3 | `type` is `Window` for the windows and `Door` for the doors | ok |
| 4 | Each reference is in the drawing of the Wall that owns the opening (`ownerElementId`) | ok |
| 5 | Every Door and Window of the project is referenced exactly once (86 + 173) | ok |
| 6 | `GetShapePrimitivesOfElements` on the Walls of the current story: the references are there too (93) | ok |
| 7 | `GetShapePrimitivesOfElements` on Walls of another story: the new message | ok |
| 8 | Doors and Windows: only `Ctrl_Beg` and `Ctrl_End` | ok |
| 9 | No other primitive has `referencedElement` | ok |

9/9. Both examples also ran live.

title: ModifyRoofs: change single-plane roofs (#1782)
body:
Fixes #1782.

`ModifyRoofs` now changes single-plane roofs too. Until now it refused them with "Only multi-plane roofs are supported."

**This PR is built on #1748** (pivot edges of multi-plane roofs), which changes the same `ModifyRoofsCommand::Execute`. Until #1748 is merged, the diff shows its commits as well. This PR's own commit is the last one, `ModifyRoofs: change single-plane roofs (#1782)`.

## What this changes

For a single-plane roof (`API_PlaneRoofID`), `ModifyRoofs` takes these fields:

- **`angle`**: written to `u.planeRoof.angle`.
- **`pivotLine`**: written to `u.planeRoof.baseLine`. The ends can be named `begCoordinate` / `endCoordinate`, as `CreateRoofs` names them, or `begin` / `end`, as `GetDetailsOfElements` reports them. So a roof that was read can be fed back as it is.
- **`polygonOutline`, `polygonArcs`, `holes`**: the plan outline. These were the tricky part:
  - A memo built from scratch, as `CreateRoofs` builds it, is refused with `APIERR_BADPOLY` whenever the point count changes. `ModifySlabs` hit the same problem in #452.
  - So the outline is edited in place with the polygon primitives that `ModifySlabs` uses (`ApplySlabPolygonChange`).
  - It is then written with `ACAPI_Element_ChangeMemo` the way the DevKit's `Element_Modify_Polygon` example writes a roof's polygon: only the polygon handles, with the roof's memo mask (`Polygon | EdgeTrims | SideMaterials | RoofEdgeTypes`). Passing the full memo from `ACAPI_Element_GetMemo` instead makes `ChangeMemo` answer `APIERR_BADPARS`. Dropping the vertex IDs or `RoofEdgeTypes` fails as well.
  - The other fields of the same item are applied first with `ACAPI_Element_Change`.
  - The edges keep their trim, side surface and edge type. Each new edge takes them from the old edge it lies on, or from the old edge at the same index when the point counts stay the same. Otherwise it gets the defaults of a new roof.
- **`level`, `thickness`, `structureType`, `buildingMaterialId`, `compositeId`**: as for multi-plane roofs.

Fields of the other roof class are refused per item, because they live in the other member of the roof's union:
- `levels`, `eavesOverhang` and `pivotEdges` for a single-plane roof.
- `angle` and `pivotLine` for a multi-plane roof.

Multi-plane roofs work as before.

Also in this PR:
- The input schema has `angle` and `pivotLine`, and `pivotEdges` now says it applies to multi-plane roofs only.
- The registered description names both roof classes.
- The example `ModifyRoofs.py` also creates and changes a single-plane roof.
- The Grasshopper `ModifyRoofs` component names both roof classes and lists `angle` and `pivotLine`. It has an `Angles` input after `AdditionalSettings`.

## Tests

Live on Archicad 29 (macOS, build 5101), in a test project on a test layer, which was reopened without saving afterwards:

| # | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | A single-plane roof made by `CreateRoofs` reads as `SinglePlane` | ok |
| 2 | `angle` 15° → 30° | ok |
| 3 | The steeper plane makes the 3D bounding box higher | ok |
| 4 | Changing `angle` leaves `pivotLine`, the outline, the level and the thickness unchanged | ok |
| 5 | `pivotLine` with `begCoordinate` / `endCoordinate`: moved to the opposite edge | ok |
| 6 | `pivotLine` as `GetDetailsOfElements` reports it (`begin` / `end`) fed back | ok |
| 7 | `polygonOutline` with 4 points plus one hole | ok |
| 8 | Outline changed to a triangle with `holes: []` | ok |
| 9 | An outline change keeps `angle` and `pivotLine` | ok |
| 10 | `level` (4.0 = the next story) and `thickness` | ok |
| 11 | `buildingMaterialId` | ok |
| 12–14 | Single-plane roof refuses `levels`, `eavesOverhang` and `pivotEdges` | ok |
| 15–16 | Multi-plane roof refuses `angle` and `pivotLine` | ok |
| 17 | A zero-length pivot line is refused | ok |
| 18 | A `pivotLine` without its second end is refused | ok |
| 19 | Multi-plane roof: `levels` and `eavesOverhang` still change | ok |
| 20 | Multi-plane roof: `pivotEdges` still change (first edge to Gable) | ok |
| 21 | A call with both roof classes: one result per roof, only the wrong one fails | ok |
| 22 | Round trip: `angle`, `pivotLine`, the outline, the holes, the level and the thickness from `GetDetailsOfElements`, fed back, leave the roof as it was | ok |
| 23 | `polygonOutline` without `holes` removes the holes, as `ModifySlabs` does | ok |

23/23. The example also ran live.

The edges were tested separately after the review: 14/14, listed in the review reply.

**Two behaviours shared with `ModifySlabs`:**
- When `holes` are given, Archicad stores the outline starting at another vertex. The polygon is the same, only its first point moves. A Slab does the same with the same helper, so tests 7 and 22 compare the outlines as rings.
- `polygonOutline` without `holes` removes the existing holes. A Slab does the same.

title: Set3DProjectionSettings: allow setting the sun position (date/time or custom azimuth/altitude)
body:
**What I'm trying to do**
Generate "Eye of the Sun" views for solar access compliance (NSW Apartment Design Guide): one saved perspective per time step on 21 June, with the camera placed on the sun's ray so anything visible is in direct sun. `Set3DProjectionSettings` + `CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap` already do this well – the camera sticks and each saved view keeps it.

**The gap**
Each perspective also has its own sun position (`API_PerspPars::sunAngSets`, `API_SunAngleSettings`), shown under *Sun Position* in the 3D Projection Settings dialog. `Set3DProjectionSettings` copies the current `sunAngSets` and has no way to change it. So every view saved from a script shows whatever date and time the 3D window had (in our case 20/08/2017 7:00 am), instead of 21/06 at that view's time. `SetPlaceSettings` changes the project location date, not this.

This matters because:
- reviewers check these views by opening the dialog and reading the date and time;
- 3D shading and shadows come from that sun, so they don't match the view.

**Request**
An optional `sun` object on the `perspective` input of `Set3DProjectionSettings`, mapping to `API_SunAngleSettings`, for example:

```json
"sun": {
  "sunPositionOption": "DateAndTime",
  "year": 2026, "month": 6, "day": 21, "hour": 13, "minute": 30, "second": 0,
  "summerTime": false
}
```
or
```json
"sun": { "sunPositionOption": "Custom", "sunAzimuth": 81.55, "sunAltitude": 28.65 }
```

Omitted, it keeps the current behaviour (current sun kept). Returning the sun settings in `Get3DProjectionSettings` too would let scripts verify it. The same option on `Set3DProjectionSettings`' axonometry branch would be nice to have.

**Environment**
Archicad 28 (Windows), Tapir 1.8.0.

title: GetUsedAttributes: send the JSON query as a JSON object (#1864)
body:
Fixes #1864.

`GetUsedAttributes` always failed with -7003. The cause is how the JSON query is sent. The same fix applies to `ConsolidateLines` and `ConsolidateFills`, which go through the same helper.

## Cause

The DevKit documents `ACAPI_Database_JsonQuery` with a table of query names (`"usedAttributes"`, `"getTopWindow"`, …), and Tapir passed that name as the query. Archicad, however, parses the query as JSON and runs the query named by its `name` key. A bare name is not JSON, so every query fails with -7003 (`GS::Error`), `"getTopWindow"` included.

How this was found, on Archicad 29 (macOS, build 5101):
- `"usedAttributes"`, `"getTopWindow"`, `"numberOfTraceReferences"`: -7003, the result string untouched.
- `{"usedAttributes": {}}`: Archicad terminated. Its crash report ends in an uncaught exception thrown from `APIJson::QueryMap::Query (const GS::ObjectState&)`, called by `APIJson_Query`. The key that function looks up is the C string `name`.
- `{"name": "getTopWindow"}`: no error, the title of the top window.
- `{"name": "usedAttributes"}`: no error, the report.

**A JSON object without a known `name` makes Archicad throw an exception it does not catch, and Archicad terminates.** `{"name": "numberOfTraceReferences"}` terminated it as well, which Tapir does not use. So the helper only ever sends the fixed names of these three commands, and the comment above it says why.

## What this changes

- `RunJsonQuery` sends `{"name": "<query>"}`.
- **The report is plain text,** not JSON: `"Layer: 16, LineType: 9, Fill: 17, BuildingMaterial: 9, Material: 29, CompWall: 3, ZoneCategory: 12"`. It is the number of attributes in use per attribute type.
- **`GetUsedAttributes` now returns:**
  - `raw`: the report as Archicad wrote it, always present
  - `usedAttributes`: the counts as integers. The keys are Tapir's attribute type names where they exist: `LineType` becomes `Line`, `CompWall` becomes `Composite`, `Material` becomes `Surface`, `LayerComb` becomes `LayerCombination`. Otherwise Archicad's own name is kept (`City`, `DimStand`, `MarkupStyle`, `GraphicOverride`, as listed in Archicad). It is left out when a part of the report does not read as `<type>: <count>`.
- The response schema, the registered description and the Grasshopper component say what the command returns. The old texts said the report could be a JSON object, and that it helps to find the attributes `DeleteAttributes` can remove. It only gives counts, not which attributes.

## Tests

Live on Archicad 29 (macOS, build 5101), in two test projects. The first was reopened without saving afterwards.

| # | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|

title: Fix switching model view option combinations (#1873)
body:
Fixes #1873.

This fixes three problems with switching the model view option combination of a window, and documents what the index does.

## What was wrong

**`SetViewOptions` with only `modelViewOptionIndex` always failed with `APIERR_BADPARS`.** It called `ACAPI_Navigator_ChangeViewOptions (nullptr, &index)`, and up to Archicad 29 the function rejects a null options pointer. It now always reads the current options and passes them along, with any given fields changed.

**`FindModelViewOption` by name did not work.** `ACAPI_Navigator_ModelViewOptions_Search` does not compare the name given in `uniStringNamePtr`. On Archicad 29 it failed for every name. Once the project had a combination with an empty name, it returned that combination for any name. Names are now looked up by walking the combinations, the way `GetModelViewOptions` and `GetModelViewOptionDetails` read them. The match ignores case. The guid search is unchanged.

**The index is not the position in `GetModelViewOptions`, and it can change.** The schemas said the index matches the order of `GetModelViewOptions`, starting from 1. In my test project the first combination has index 2. `GetModelViewOptions` lists names only and skips indices it cannot read.

Archicad may also renumber the combinations when the view options of a window change. In my project, after such a change:
- a combination with an empty name appeared at index 1
- index 2 could no longer be read
- every named combination moved up by one

Reopening the project restores the old numbering. This matches the report: an empty record on Nov 3 that was gone on Nov 4, and index 8 then switching to the neighbouring combination. It did not happen on every run, so an index read earlier is not safe to reuse.

## What this changes

- **`SetViewOptions`:** an index on its own works. The current options are always passed to `ACAPI_Navigator_ChangeViewOptions`.
- **`FindModelViewOption`:** name lookup walks the combinations, as described above.
- **`GetViewOptions` returns `modelViewOptionName`:** the name of the combination at `modelViewOptionIndex`, empty for Custom (index 0). A combination can be found again by name (`FindModelViewOption`) right before switching back to it.
- **Schemas, descriptions and Grasshopper components** now say what Archicad does:
  - The index is the one `GetViewOptions`, `FindModelViewOption` and `GetModelViewOptionDetails` return.
  - With an index, Archicad applies the model view options stored in the combination. Given `modelViewOptions` are not applied, given `onScreenViewOptions` are.
  - Without an index, the window uses Custom model view options (index 0), even when only on-screen options are given. This is the "association changed to Custom/index 0" from the report. To keep the combination, pass its index as well.
- **Grasshopper:** `GetViewOptions` gets a `ModelViewOptionName` output, added last so that existing definitions keep their wiring.
- **Examples:**
  - `SetViewOptions` switches the fill handles instead of Bold Cut Lines (see below). It restores the original combination by finding its index by name.
  - `FindModelViewOption` and `GetModelViewOptionDetails` use the first combination that has a name.

## Tests

Live on Archicad 29 (macOS, build 5101), in a test project with 13 combinations. The project was reopened before each run and reopened without saving afterwards. The whole suite passed 3 times in a row.

| # | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 0a | On-screen option only, no index: the option changes, the window is Custom (index 0) | ok |
| 0b | The same with the index found by name: the option changes back, the combination and its model options are restored | ok |
| 1 | `modelViewOptionName` is the name `GetModelViewOptionDetails` gives for that index | ok |
| 2 | `FindModelViewOption` by name returns the index of every combination | ok |
| 3 | The name match ignores case | ok |
| 4 | An unknown name fails with the same error as before | ok |
| 5 | Index-only switch succeeds (was `APIERR_BADPARS`) | ok |
| 6 | The window then applies the target combination, by name | ok |
| 7 | Its model options equal the stored ones of the target | ok |
| 8 | Switching back by the name read before | ok |
| 9 | All model options equal the original ones again | ok |
| 10 | Index plus fields: the stored model options apply, the on-screen field applies | ok |
| 11 | A model field without an index: Custom, index 0, empty name | ok |
| 12 | Unknown index fails | ok |
| 13 | No parameters fails | ok |
| 14 | The numbering did not change again after the first renumbering | ok |

The examples `GetViewOptions`, `SetViewOptions`, `FindModelViewOption` and `GetModelViewOptionDetails` also ran. `tools/check_examples.py` passes.

**Not changed, but found:**
- **`boldCutLines`:** on Archicad 29, `ACAPI_Navigator_ChangeViewOptions` never changes it, with or without an index. The other 11 on-screen switches change. This is why the example now uses the fill handles.
- **GUIDs:** on Archicad 29, `ACAPI_Navigator_ModelViewOptions_Get` returns a null guid for every combination. `FindModelViewOption` and `GetModelViewOptionDetails` by `modelViewOptionId` therefore cannot find anything there, and the second half of the `FindModelViewOption` example fails.
- **Builds:** not tested on Windows or Archicad 25–28. The Archicad 25/26 branch of `GetModelViewOptionName` reads the name the same way `GetModelViewOptions` does there.
