title: `GetLinkedPropertyObjectsOfElements` crashes Archicad 28 inside its JSON schema validation (EXC_BAD_ACCESS in `rapidjson::internal::Schema::StartObject`)
body:
## Environment

- Archicad 28.0.0, build 6003, AUT localization
- Tapir add-on 1.8.0 (`TapirAddOn_AC28_Mac`)
- macOS 15.8.1, Apple Silicon (ARM64)
- Local single-user copy of an office template, not Teamwork

## What happens

During a scripted run of many read-only commands, a call to `GetLinkedPropertyObjectsOfElements` made Archicad crash. The HTTP connection was closed without a response, every following request got "Connection refused".

**Honest status:** observed **once**, not repeated yet. I have not tried other element types, a plain wall in a new project, Archicad 27 or 29.

The request is not stored verbatim in my log (the script wrote it only after the call returned, and the call never returned). It is rebuilt from the script's deterministic parameter generator, which builds the request from the command's `inputScheme` (first alternative of every `oneOf`):

```json
{"command": "API.ExecuteAddOnCommand",
 "parameters": {"addOnCommandId": {"commandNamespace": "TapirCommand", "commandName": "GetLinkedPropertyObjectsOfElements"},
                "addOnCommandParameters": {"elements": [{"elementId": {"guid": "<GUID of an existing wall>"}}]}}}
```

The same generator built, one step earlier in the same run, the equivalent request for `GetDescriptorsOfElements` (by the same logic `{"elements": [{"elementId": {"guid": "<same wall>"}}]}`; that request is also not in the old log, I deduced it), and that call succeeded (`{"descriptorsOfElements": [{"descriptors": []}]}`).

## Crash report (macOS, excerpt)

```
Exception Type:  EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGSEGV)
Exception Codes: KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x0000000000000050
Crashed Thread:  0 (main thread)

0  APICommandJSONSchema  rapidjson::internal::Schema<...>::StartObject(SchemaValidationContext&) const + 20
1  APICommandJSONSchema  GenericSchemaValidator<...>::StartObject() + 52
2  APICommandJSONSchema  GenericSchemaValidator<...>::StartObject() + 108
3  APICommandJSONSchema  GenericValue<...>::Accept<GenericSchemaValidator<...>>   (nested, 3 levels:
4  APICommandJSONSchema  GenericValue<...>::Accept<GenericSchemaValidator<...>>    root object -> array ->
5  APICommandJSONSchema  GenericValue<...>::Accept<GenericSchemaValidator<...>>    item object)
6  APICommandJSONSchema  APICommand::JSON::SchemaDocument::Impl::ValidateValue
7  APICommandJSONSchema  APICommand::JSON::SchemaDocument::Validate(GS::ObjectState const&)
8  APICommandBridge      APICommand::ExecuteAddOnCommand::DoExecute
```

## Observation

The crash is in Archicad's own validation of the add-on command parameters against the command's input schema. It happens in `ExecuteAddOnCommand::DoExecute`, **before the add-on's command code runs**. The access address `0x50` looks like a null pointer plus a field offset (a schema node that was not resolved). The three nested `Accept` frames match the shape root object -> `elements` array -> item object.

## Schema excerpt (`GetLinkedPropertyObjectsOfElements`, 1.8.0 input scheme)

```json
{"type": "object",
 "properties": {
   "elements": {"type": "array",
     "items": {"oneOf": [
        {"$ref": "#/ElementIdArrayItem"},
        {"type": "object",
         "properties": {"elementType": {"$ref": "#/ElementType"}},
         "additionalProperties": false, "required": ["elementType"]}]}}},
 "additionalProperties": false, "required": ["elements"]}
```

## Comparison with a command that works

`GetDescriptorsOfElements` (also 1.8.0) takes the same element object, but its input scheme is `{"elements": {"$ref": "#/Elements"}}`, i.e. the items are `ElementIdArrayItem` directly, with no `oneOf`.

I compared the input schemas of all 641 commands in the 1.8.0 definition file: `GetLinkedPropertyObjectsOfElements` is the **only** one where a `oneOf`/`anyOf` inside the input scheme has a bare `$ref` as one of its alternatives. All other `oneOf`/`anyOf` nodes (for example `SetLinkedPropertyObjectsOfElements`, `GetClassificationItemVisibility`, `ChangeLibraryPartOfElements`) consist of inline objects or primitive types. This is a guess about the cause, not a proven one.

The input scheme in `archicad-addon/Sources/PropertyObjectCommands.cpp` on `main` (checked 2026-11-05) still has the same `oneOf` with the bare `$ref`.

## Expected behavior

Either a result, or an error object. Never a crash.

## Suspicion and request

I suspect the `$ref` alternative inside the `oneOf` is not resolved when Archicad builds its schema document, so a null schema node is dereferenced while an item object is validated. If so, inlining `ElementIdArrayItem` in that `oneOf` (or avoiding a `$ref` there) might avoid it, but I have not verified this.

Could someone please confirm whether this reproduces on your side (Archicad 28, and 27/29 if available)? Tapir's own example for this command sends `[element, {"elementType": "Wall"}]`; I did not send that form in the crashing call.

Keep that structure, every URL and every anchor; this issue changes the look and adds pages. A part that edits `docs/` starts after those three are merged, or is built on their branches as #2078 is on #2071's, so no two open PRs edit the same file. Two parts that both edit the header in every page are never open at once.

## 1. Brand

An architect's material board: warm cream paper, charcoal ink, moss and ochre accents. Light by default, dark under `prefers-color-scheme: dark`, plus a toggle that remembers the choice (`localStorage`, wrapped in try/catch; without JavaScript the system setting applies).

| Token | Hex | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Deep Charcoal | `#1C1E1F` | Text and headings; dark-mode page |
| Natural Cream | `#F4F1EA` | Light page; text on dark |
| Paper | `#FFFFFF` | Cards and code panels on cream |
| Jungle Moss | `#2D3A30` | Header, footer, feature bands, secondary buttons (cream text 10.6:1) |
| Earthy Ochre | `#BD8D53` | Primary buttons, badges, highlights. Text on it is always charcoal (5.7:1), never cream or white (2.6:1) |
| Deep Ochre | `#8A6235` | Links and ochre text on light backgrounds (4.8:1 on cream) |
| River Slate | `#707C80` | Icons, dividers, inactive states only (3.8:1 on cream, too light for text) |
| Deep Slate | `#5F6A6E` | Subtext and captions on light backgrounds (4.9:1) |
| Light Ochre | `#D4A876` | Links and highlights in dark mode (7.7:1 on charcoal) |

Dark mode: page `#1C1E1F`, cards `#262A2B`, text `#F4F1EA`, subtext `#97A2A6`, links `#D4A876`; primary buttons stay ochre with charcoal text.

- **Type** (Google Fonts): Fraunces 600–700 for headings, Inter 400–600 for text, JetBrains Mono for code and command names. Body 16 px, line height 1.6; headings 40/28/21/17 px, 32/24/19/17 on phones; text columns at most 72 characters.
- **Logo:** keep the tapir mark from `branding/logo/svg/` (single colour: charcoal on cream, cream on moss or charcoal, never ochre or slate). Wordmark = the mark + "Tapir" in Fraunces. An SVG favicon from the mark on moss.
- **Components:** primary button ochre with charcoal text, secondary moss outline, 8 px corners; cards paper on cream with a 1 px River Slate border at 25%, 12 px corners, no shadows; badges ochre tint with charcoal text; code blocks charcoal with cream text and a copy button; callouts with an icon and a word, never colour alone; real Archicad and Grasshopper screenshots, no stock images.
- **Voice:** for architects first. Plain words, short sentences, no hype; a real command or number rather than a claim; every page ends with one next step.
- **Accessibility:** every text pair at least WCAG AA; a visible 2 px focus ring (Deep Ochre, Light Ochre in dark mode); usable by keyboard; works at 360 px; no motion under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## 2. Pages

Header: logo, Get started, Docs (Commands, API coverage, Grasshopper coverage), Scripts, Community, and a Download button. Drop the "Website" link: this is the website. Discord: `https://discord.gg/NAnSennmpY`, as in the README.

| --- | --- |
| `/` | Becomes the full home page: what Tapir is in one sentence; Windows and macOS installer buttons (`releases/latest/download/TapirInstaller_Win.exe`, `…/TapirInstaller_Mac.zip`); three ways in (palette scripts, Python, Grasshopper); six use cases taken from the real built-in scripts and `archicad-addon/Workflows/`; the live numbers #2071 adds, plus the script count from the catalogue; tutorials and Discord. A code sample that really runs (standard library, port 19723); never `import tapir`. |
| `/start/` | Get started from #2071, in the new look. Step 3 points to the palette's Marketplace (below) instead of `localFolders`. |
| `/archicad-addon/`, `/api-coverage/`, `/gh-coverage/` | As in #2078 and #2084, in the new look. |
| `/grasshopper/` | What the components do, the tool components (Walls, Doors, Windows, Railings, Level Dimensions), installing the `tapir` package, a sample definition. |
| `/scripts/` | The marketplace: search, category and Archicad version filters, cards (name, summary, author, Archicad versions, "Changes the model" or "Read only"). |
| `/scripts/?s=<slug>` | One script: README, screenshots, versions, Archicad and Tapir versions, licence, code view, how to install it from the palette, "Report a problem". |
| `/scripts/share/` | How to share: the palette's Share button, Discord `#share-a-script`, or a pull request; what the AI changes; what review checks; the MIT terms. |
| `/ai/` | Using Tapir from Claude and other AI tools: list the Tapir MCP servers (SzamosiMate/tapir-archicad-MCP and its forks) without recommending one until #2070 decides; a working prompt. |
| `/tutorials/` | The YouTube playlist (https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLGc943dgyfjjqzeFglpYLIPrcn_HFicDn), grouped by topic. |
| `/community/` | Discord, how the bots work, how to report a bug, how to test a PR, and an activity chart drawn as inline SVG from `community.json` (below): counts per month only. |
| `/roadmap/` | How features are requested, links to open enhancement issues and to the releases. |
| `/404.html` | Links to the four sections. |

## 3. Script marketplace, inside this repo

Every shared script is a folder in `marketplace/`, reviewed like any code. Marketplace scripts are never added to `builtin-scripts/`; people choose what to install.

```
marketplace/<slug>/
  listing.json   name, summary, category, tags, author, licence, entry, versions
  <script>.py    with its # /// script (uv) header and the # /// tapir header (#1991)
  README.md      what it does, its settings, its limits, "Original by <author>"
  screenshots/   up to 5 PNG or JPG, at most 1 MB each
```

- **`listing.json` fields:** `slug` (= the folder name), `name` (≤ 60 characters), `summary` (≤ 160), `category`, `tags` (≤ 8), `author` (`name`, optional `github`, optional `discord`), `license` (an OSI licence, MIT by default), `entry` (the file the palette runs), `versions` (newest first: `version`, `archicadVersions`, `minTapirVersion`, `changelog`). No pricing: everything is free and open source.
- **Categories:** documentation-layouts, element-data-properties, modeling-geometry, zones-areas, import-export, quality-assurance, quantities-scheduling, libraries-objects, navigator-views, classification-attributes, batch-automation, utilities.
- **A new `changes` key in the `# /// tapir` header:** `model`, `read-only` or `files`. The site and the palette show it as "Changes the model" or "Read only".
- **`marketplace/README.md`** documents the format and the adaptation rules below. A short CLAUDE.md section points to it.
- **The pages read `catalogue.json` from the `site-data` branch** (raw.githubusercontent.com, never GitHub's API): `{"version": 1, "scripts": [{listing fields…, "versions": [{…, "commit", "url", "sha256"}]}]}`. Until it exists, `/scripts/` says the marketplace is opening and links to `/scripts/share/`.

## 4. Adapting a shared script for public use

Scripts arrive as issues labelled `script-share`, from the palette's Share button or from Discord, mostly from architects without a GitHub account. The issue bot turns each into one PR adding `marketplace/<slug>/`, keeping what the script does:

- **Security, removed or flagged in the PR:** network calls other than Archicad's local port; `subprocess`, `os.system`, `eval`, `exec`; `pip install` at run time; deleting or overwriting files, or writing outside the project folder and `Documents/Tapir`; passwords, tokens and keys; user names, `C:\Users\…` paths, and project, client or office names in code and comments.
- **Made to fit other offices:** hard-coded property names, layers, stories, paths and classification codes become settings at the top or a `ShowScriptUI` dialog. Built-in properties are found by ID, not by translated name. Metric and imperial units; Windows and macOS paths.
- **Safe to run:** it says what it will change, does nothing when nothing fits, makes its changes in one Undo step, and gives a clear message instead of crashing when a property or element type is missing.
- **Headers and README:** dependencies in `# /// script`; category, versions and `changes` in `# /// tapir`; a plain-words README crediting the author.
- **The PR lists every change in plain words** and asks the author to try the adapted version and confirm it still does what they meant.

## Not for the bot

Listed so no part attempts them:
- **Maintainers:**
  - a `site_data.yml` workflow and a `tools/build_site_data.py` that write `catalogue.json`, a search index and `community.json` (counts only, never message text) to the `site-data` branch, never to `main`;
  - `tools/check_marketplace.py`, a model-free checker of the folder format and the security list, whose findings send a listing to `needs-maintainer`;
  - the Discord bot's share mode for `#share-a-script`.
- **Project owners:** the share service at `share.archicad-api.com`, which turns a palette share into a `script-share` issue through a GitHub App. The add-on holds no token.
- **A separate issue:** the palette redesign, the palette's Marketplace window and the Share button.
- **Enzyme:** `docs/CNAME` and the DNS switch. Don't add `docs/CNAME` here. Enzyme also retires Tapir-Report-web; its `discord_data.json` holds the full text of Discord messages and should be deleted.
- **Script authors:** moving listings from tapir-marketplace.vercel.app needs each author's OK.

## Constraints

- No build step and no framework: static HTML, CSS and a little JavaScript.
- Page content readable without JavaScript.
- External scripts only from a CDN at an exact version.
- Never call GitHub's API from a page. A number or list that can't be read is left out, not shown wrong.
- English only, with all text in the HTML, so pages can be translated later.
- Nothing under `tools/`, `.github/` or `archicad-addon/`.
